compare.summary:
All five of the agent's final answers reproduce exactly from the landed parquet files under the rules the user approved in the transcript. Those rules are: fare > 0, distance > 0, 0 < duration <= 4 h, speed <= 80 mph, pickup within the file's month (message 4); tip analysis on standard-rate (RatecodeID 1) card trips (messages 5-6); a 300-trip floor per zone per month with Outside NYC kept as its own category (messages 4-6).

Every gap between the agent and the two blind recomputes is definitional:
- SQL used a 3 h cap with 80 mph; pandas used 3 h with 100 mph.
- Both recomputes used all card trips for tips.
- Both pooled the two months for the zone ranking and set their own trip floors.

Where the recomputes measured the same thing as the agent, they agree with it. Examples: all-card tip medians 26.25% / 25.65%, airport shares 9.84% / 11.32%, median fares, the 6 p.m. peak, and Flushing Meadows at $180.93 (Jan) and $162.26 (Jul). Neither recompute made an error; they made different threshold choices.

1. Chat rounding slip in reply 5: the Bronx July code-99 share was given as 91.85%, but 4,764 / 5,187 = 91.8450%, which rounds to 91.84%. The release shows 91.8%, which is correct.

1. Q1 holidays: Jan 1 and MLK Day (both Mondays) stayed in with no note, while July 4 was split out only when the user asked. Removing them cuts July's Monday gain from +13.3% to +10.1%.

compare.summary:
The taxi-B agent's final answers to all five questions are correct under the definitions the user agreed in the transcript. I recomputed them independently with DuckDB on the landed parquet files and reproduced every figure exactly. Script: SIMS/grade/grading/taxi-B-compare/check.py; output: check_out.txt in the same folder.

The verified figures:
- **Rules:** 5,837,058 valid trips and 204,469 invalid records.
- **Q1 volumes:** 92,467 and 95,825 trips a day; the agent's per-day figures for Tue, Wed and Sat and three cells of the weekday-by-hour table.
- **Q2 airports:** 9.912% and 11.400% of the base, with 20,060 and 20,248 trips left out; median fares $54.80, $57.60, $12.10, $12.80; median minutes 32.0, 35.5, 10.8, 11.7; Newark check moves the share by +0.015 and +0.023 points.
- **Q3 tips:** 26.25% and 25.65% on n of 2,296,318 and 2,229,862; borough figures and the rate-code-99 sensitivity check.
- **Q4 invalid records:** vendors at 3.61%, 3.31% and 35.38%; 2,433 records over 65 mph; one duplicate pair.
- **Q5 zones:** the same ten zones in the same order, with the same trip counts and dollars per hour to the cent, including the January/July rates.

The two blind recomputes (SQL and pandas) agree with each other but not with the agent. In every case the cause is a definition, not an arithmetic error:
- **Their validity rule is different.** They added a minimum trip time of 60 seconds, used 80 mph instead of the agreed 65 mph, and dropped the agreed 100-mile cap. That gives 221,121 invalid records and 5,820,406 valid trips.
- **Their airport-share base is different.** They divide by all valid trips. The user agreed (message 3) to leave out trips that have no airport end and a missing zone, and to report how many.
- **The pandas Q5 headline uses a 100-trip minimum.** The user agreed 1,000.

Their own sensitivity runs confirm this. Without the 60-second rule they get 204,194 invalid records, and the SQL zone ranking comes out in exactly the agent's order. Their monthly tip medians (26.25 and 25.65) and airport median fares are identical to the agent's. I therefore graded all five as differs_by_definition: the difference is with the blind recomputes, it comes from definitions the user agreed, and the agent's numbers are right under those definitions.

I found no definitional choice the user never saw. The one borderline case is in Q2: the non-airport comparison group in the fare and duration medians also leaves out missing-zone trips. That appeared only in a table header in reply 4, not as a decision put to the user. Two small wording points:
- The reply-3 hourly tip range says 'about 24% to 28%'. The actual low is 23.6% at 05:00 in both months, and July peaks at 27.3%. The draft later corrected the July peak.
- The referee's 'Manhattan about 26.6%' is the January figure; July is 26.25%.

Nothing under sims/taxi-B was modified.

top_issues: Package review is over-strict but bounded (co2-B-02/03/04/06). The reconciliation and tolerance rules leave no acceptable wording for an approximate match. The reviewer flagged the user's own approved wording, and the two-review cap pushed trivial edits back to the user (U5). A reviewer pass that covered only some instances of a pattern added a round. A rules-only change re-triggered review before release. Cost: 5 rounds, about 10 min of review, one extra user decision round.

The coverage-gap error recurred a third time (co2-B-01). China's and India's missing early years were first called 'count as zero' (A2), then the sensitivity calculation was called a 'ceiling' (A3). The user caught both.

Reviews miss meaning errors the user catches (co2-B-05). 'Energy mix' for coal's share of CO2 passed both drafting-turn reviews, and 'counting imports' without exports appeared in the headline preview.

First-pass answers fall short and internal vocabulary leaks (co2-B-07/08). Rankings came without values and the coal denominator was ambiguous, costing a follow-up. 'Producer', 'unassessed join check', 'promotion', 'mechanical checks' and a spurious-warning remark reached the user.

Helper friction (co2-B-09 to 15): verify-only check-draft always reports failure before the first writing run; export's own scale divisor fails the numbers check; the preview folder doesn't exist at the headline checkpoint; new results default to association; joins always come back not_assessed; the EDA scan is noisy on panel data; review-rules add gave a spurious number warning.

compare.summary:
All five final answers from the retail-B agent are numerically correct under the definitions the user agreed in the transcript. There are no mismatches. I ran my own read-only DuckDB checks on the landed workbook, whose SHA-256 matches provenance.json (scripts and parquet in SIMS/grade/grading/retail-B-compare/, load.py and check1-6.py). They reproduce the agent's figures exactly.

Q1 and Q2 match. The definitions are all-lines net revenue (Dec09-Nov11 for Q2) and identified customers ranked by net revenue, with the share shown of identified and of total revenue.

Q5 also matches on the agreed all-lines, absolute-£ ranking.

Q3 and Q4 differ from the blind recomputes by definition:
- **Q3:** the user agreed 'later day'; the DuckDB recompute's primary counts same-day invoices.
- **Q4:** the user agreed a £2,000 threshold; both recomputes used £10k.

Choices the agent made that the user never saw or agreed:
1. **Q3:** a purchase must contain a product line with positive quantity and price. This is not in the user-facing methodology note, only in the internal methodology.md. It moves cohort sizes by up to 15 (Jan 368 against 383) and rates by up to 1.2 points.
2. **Q4:** products are keyed on case-sensitive stock codes. Seven lowercase variants (85123a and others) are listed separately at 0%, and 84797B and 84872A are dropped, so the count is 1,720 instead of 1,715. The ranking and the ~1% median do not change.
3. **Q1:** PADS is classed as a product, which moves £36.59 between the product and non-product columns.
4. **Q2:** top 10% is rounded up (592 rather than 591), with no effect on the shares.

Presentation caveats:
- Norway's +£32k includes about £8.7k from a -£5,948 manual adjustment in Year 1 (product growth is +£23k). The deck flags Norway only as a small base.
- 'Cherry lights 36-56%' leaves out the light pink (32%) and pink (29%) codes.

verdicts.reasoning:
I looked for a harness cause and did not find one behind the main effect.

**Harness checks**
- **Sessions keep their history.** relay.py resumes each role by its session or thread id (`codex exec resume <id>`, `claude --resume`). Cumulative token usage in the Codex logs grows across turns. So the agents do not re-read the skill files because each turn starts from a blank context.
- **Truncation comes from Codex itself.** The rollouts show the Codex agent choosing `max_output_tokens` of 10,000-12,000 for its own exec calls. One combined read of review.md plus the templates came back as "Warning: truncated output (original token count: 18235)". This is standard Codex CLI behaviour, and the simulated config.toml does not change any output limit. An interactive Codex user would hit the same limit.
- **Mid-turn auto-compaction caused the duplicate reads inside a turn.** Each Codex main thread compacted once:
  - taxi-A agent-007, 4.3 min in. SKILL.md and review.md were then read twice, at 4.4 and 4.5 min.
  - retail-A agent-006, 2.8 min in. The skill and project files were re-read at 2.9-3.5 min.
  - co2-A agent-007, 6.5 min in, near the end of the turn.

  Auto-compaction is a normal Codex feature. The context grows partly because of these long documents.
- **Smaller harness contributions:**
  - The harness sets `model_reasoning_effort = high`, which inflates the absolute minutes.
  - The study note asks for a per-turn friction log, including "too long". That likely primes the agents' complaints about length, and it adds a little per-turn overhead.
  - reviewloop counts some non-packaging turns as packaging (see below).

  None of these creates the reading load itself.

**What the release causes**
- **The documents are long.** wc -w on the release: SKILL.md 2,498 words, helpers.md 7,011, package-contract.md 2,879, review.md 2,339. That is about 14.7k words in those four files and about 21k across the non-code awb-package files.
- **Codex agents re-read the skill files on every packaging turn.** co2-A agent-005, -006 and -007 each cat SKILL.md and the references again. In agent-006 that is about 130k characters in the first 0.3 min. The agent notes record truncation and focused re-reads in several turns.
- **On Codex, reading plus the reasoning after it costs real time:**
  - about 0.7 min of 10.4 in co2-A agent-006
  - about 3.5 min of 6.2 in retail-A agent-006, the headline preview turn
  - about 5 min of 14.7 in taxi-A agent-007, including the re-read after compaction
- **The review rules surface late.** In the Claude runs, review.md is read only just before the review. First reviews then flagged 9, 15 and 21 narrative problems. The retail-B report lists exact-zero claims against a recorded -4.38e-06, checks claimed without a result ID, imperatives outside Implications, glossary first use, and the record word "flagged".

**What does not hold**
- **"Most packaging time goes to reading" is not supported on the Claude runs.** Reading took under 0.5 min of wall time in co2-B agent-003/004, retail-B agent-005 and taxi-B agent-004/005. The time went to record updates, re-running results, exports, writing findings.md and the methodology note, and review subagents of about 3 min each. Review is about 46% of the full-draft turn there, not a small tail.
- **The 35-69% shares measure whole turns, not reading.** They include:
  - analysis inside packaging turns: new producers in taxi-A agent-007, a verification query in taxi-A agent-006, a combined-history producer in co2-A agent-006
  - co2-A agent-001, the setup turn, flagged only because the agent read the package skill early
  - feedback turns the script counts as packaging (taxi-A agent-010; taxi-B agent-008 and co2-B agent-007, the quirk the referee already tagged as harness in taxi-B-26)

  The shares also depend on how fast the personas moved through scoping and analysis.

**Errors in the finding**
- **"12.1 / 8.4 / 7.1" are the times the first review was recorded, not when it started.** reviewloop's "@t" is the record time. The actual starts were 10.4, 7.3 and 5.4 min, as co2-A-03 itself says (7.3 of 10.4).
- **Four cited evidence IDs point to other issues.** taxi-A-20 is about the builder-kit format, retail-A-12 about slide count, retail-B-32 about zsh/DuckDB command mistakes, and taxi-B-26 about the reviewloop quirk. The supporting IDs are taxi-A-13, taxi-B-19, co2-A-03, co2-B-23, retail-A-10 and retail-B-18.
- **"About 7,000 words" is helpers.md alone, not the four files together.**
- **"Every packaging turn re-reads everything" is too broad.** It holds for the Codex runs, not for the Claude runs.

**Severity**
On Codex the reading load is substantial. On Claude it costs little wall time. The rework from late review rules is real but moderate (one or two scoped re-reviews per draft). Major is defensible for Codex hosts only.
verdicts.release_evidence:
Release word counts (wc -w): awb-package/SKILL.md 2,498; references/helpers.md 7,011; references/package-contract.md 2,879; references/review.md 2,339; templates and deck-rules about 6,000 more.

Timed logs (scratchpad/c01/timed.py over relay/*.jsonl and .ts):
- co2-A agent-006 reads SKILL.md, review.md (26,279 characters), helpers.md (42,969 characters) and the templates at 0.2-0.3 min. co2-A agent-005 and -007 open the same files again.
- taxi-A agent-007 re-reads SKILL.md and review.md at 4.4 and 4.5 min, right after compaction at 12:04:52 (4.3 min in).
- retail-A agent-006 re-reads at 2.9-3.5 min, after compaction at 12:02:43 (2.8 min in).

co2-A main rollout: an exec_command with max_output_tokens 12,000 returned "Warning: truncated output (original token count: 18235)". Codex agent-notes lines 28, 57, 71 and 89 record truncated combined reads and focused re-reads.

Claude runs: reading takes under 0.5 min per turn. review.md is read just before the review (co2-B agent-004 at 4.6 min, retail-B agent-005 at 5.2 min). retail-B's first review report has 15 narrative problems: number tracing, checks claimed without a cited result, imperatives outside Implications, glossary first use, and the record word "flagged".
verdicts.narrowed: The awb-package reference set is heavy: about 14.7k words in SKILL.md, package-contract.md, review.md and helpers.md, about 21k with the templates. On Codex this costs real time. Agents re-read the files at the start of each packaging turn. Their own per-command output caps (10-12k tokens) truncate combined reads, which forces focused re-reads. They re-read again after mid-turn auto-compaction. Together that is about 1-5 minutes per packaging turn (taxi-A agent-007, retail-A agent-006, co2-A agent-005 to -007). On Claude, reading costs under a minute of wall time. Separately, the number-tracing, check-citation, imperative and glossary rules live in review.md and take effect only at review. First reviews therefore flagged 9-21 narrative problems in the Claude runs and 1-3 in the Codex runs. The 35-69% packaging share is mostly drafting, exports, record updates, extra analysis inside packaging turns, and review subagents, not reading. The script's turn classification and the simulation's pacing inflate it. The first-review times quoted in the finding are when the review was recorded; the actual starts were 10.4, 7.3 and 5.4 min.

verdicts.reasoning:
The instructions really are long, and the release is the cause. awb-package/SKILL.md (2,498 words) says "Read the package contract first" (package-contract.md, 2,879 words). It then sends the writer to findings-template.md (1,772), methodology-template.md, methodology-note-template.md, manifest-template.md (1,278), deck-rules.md (1,882, needed for the chart roles) and review.md (2,339). That is about 13,500 words a writer must read before helpers.md, which adds 7,011 words and 43 KB on its own. The rules are packed into very long lines. One contract paragraph under Structural consistency runs about 1,900 characters and holds number tracing, check citations, tolerance and "exactly"/"every row". helpers.md has lines of 2,224, 2,792 and 3,843 characters.

Some of the rules the first full review enforces are not in the files a writer is pointed to before writing:
- Imperatives, the record words (ledger, flagged, disposition) and first use of a glossary term appear only in review.md Brief step 3. That is the reviewer's brief, and SKILL.md's sequence sends the writer there at step 5, after writing.
- Check citations and tolerance are in the contract but buried in that dense paragraph.

The Claude-agent runs show exactly this. taxi-B, co2-B and retail-B all read the contract and templates in the preview turn and review.md only just before launching the reviewer. retail-B's first full review had 15 narrative problems. Four came from rules found only in review.md (two imperatives, one first use of a glossary term, "flagged"). Four were about "exactly" or check citations, which the contract states. The rest were genuine overreach. retail-B's agent.md says "Reading long contract/template/review docs once was fine; the cost was in iterations driven by rules discovered late." That supports this narrower claim.

These parts of the finding do not hold:
1. "Most time goes to reading." The relay timelines show the package-doc reads finishing within about 1 minute of turn start in 5 of 6 full-draft turns: co2-A agent-006 by 0.3 min, retail-A agent-007 by 1.1, taxi-B agent-005 by 0.3, co2-B agent-004 by 0.9, retail-B agent-005 by 0.4. Most of the time before review went to writing the narratives, export and display.toml, check-draft repairs, and new analysis the user asked for in the same message. Examples are new producers in taxi-A agent-007 (board-airports, board-rankings), co2-A agent-006 (historical-combined) and co2-A agent-007 (territorial-change-tonnes). Only taxi-A spent about 4.5 minutes before its first write, mixed with a zone check.
2. Truncation and re-reading happen only in the Codex-agent runs (the A runs). The agent batched several large files into one cat under Codex's output cap, set its own max_output_tokens (1,400 on the manifest in retail-A), and re-read SKILL.md and the contract in every turn even though relay.py resumes the session. The Claude agents read each document once with no truncation. The skill does not tell the agent to re-read each turn, and the contract calls helpers.md a diagnostic reference. co2-A read helpers.md whole only in agent-006, not in agent-005 to -007 as the finding says.
3. The cited "first review started" times (12.1, 8.4, 7.1) are when the review was recorded. reviewloop's tail values put the actual starts at 10.4, 7.3 and 5.4 minutes.
4. In the Claude-agent runs, review was not a small share. Review started at about 48-55% of the turn, and the time after it was 5-6 minutes of 10-13.
5. The packaging-share percentages come from reviewloop's heuristic. It counts init turns that merely read awb-package as packaging (noted in retail-A-18) and a false review start in taxi-B agent-008 (taxi-B-26). A large share for the deliverable step is not a defect in itself.
6. Several cited IDs do not match their claims. taxi-A-20 is about the builder kit, retail-A-12 about slide count, retail-B-32 about the agent's zsh and DuckDB mistakes, and taxi-B-26 is a harness quirk. The relevant ones are taxi-A-13, retail-A-10 and taxi-B-19, plus retail-B agent.md lines 41 and 68.
verdicts.release_evidence:
- awb-package/SKILL.md line 8: "Read the [package contract](references/package-contract.md) first". Step 5 sends the writer to references/review.md only after the draft is written.
- references/package-contract.md, Structural consistency: a single paragraph of about 1,900 characters holds number tracing, check citations ("cites the check that establishes it"), tolerance and "exactly"/"every row".
- references/review.md Brief step 3: the readability rules ("the record words ledger, flagged, or disposition, a record ID ... or a sentence in the imperative ... outside Implications", first use of a glossary term). They appear nowhere in findings-template.md or SKILL.md.
- The headline checkpoint in SKILL.md is about 600 words over several paragraphs. The 15-word limit is repeated in SKILL.md, package-contract.md and findings-template.md.
- references/helpers.md: 59 lines, 42,974 bytes, longest lines 2,224, 2,792 and 3,843 characters. The contract scopes it ("To diagnose a helper's rows ... read helpers") and SKILL.md links only to its Missing evidence section and its number contexts.
- Word counts (wc -w): SKILL 2,498; contract 2,879; review 2,339; helpers 7,011; findings-template 1,772; deck-rules 1,882; manifest-template 1,278.
verdicts.narrowed: The awb-package writing rules are long (about 13,500 words required before helpers.md) and some are badly placed. Imperatives, record words and first use of a glossary term are stated only in review.md's reviewer brief, which SKILL.md's sequence has the writer read after drafting. Check citations, "exactly" and tolerance are buried in one very long contract paragraph. As a result, first full reviews raise avoidable problems: in retail-B 4 of the 15 problems came from review.md-only rules and 4 from the buried contract rules. The fix is a short writer-facing checklist in findings-template.md or SKILL.md step 3. Reading time is not the main cost: reads finished within about a minute in 5 of 6 full-draft turns, and most pre-review time was writing, export and check repairs. Truncated, repeated reads appear only with the Codex agent, which batched files into one cat and re-read the skill every turn; that is host and agent behaviour, not something the release requires.

consolidated.title: Thresholds and exclusions are still set or proposed after seeing which rows lead
consolidated.description: analysis.md now says a threshold, minimum or exclusion the brief leaves open is proposed before looking at the leaders, and disclosed when proposed after. Agents missed it in five runs. taxi-A's first zone ranking had no support floor, so Rikers Island led on 1 trip. taxi-B proposed a 65 mph rule after viewing the 2,182 rows it catches. It also recommended dropping the rate-code-99 group from the primary tip figures after seeing 0% medians. co2-A counted a -0.3% change as a cut, with no materiality threshold. retail-B offered to move the £2,000 product threshold if the list came out too long, and set a £20k flag from totals it had already queried. co2-B settled Antarctica, Kosovo, Libya and the matched 2023 year after seeing results. The opposite failure also appeared: taxi-A said it would wait for signoff on a floor the user had just delegated, then applied it in the same reply.
consolidated.caused_by_fix: no for the misses: #97 added the rule at analysis.md:13, and the same miss recurred. taxi-A-13's contradiction follows #97's wording, which does not separate a choice the user delegated in the current request from an unapproved change.
consolidated.evidence: taxi-A-01: reply 3 threshold table has no floor; reply 4 shows the unrestricted top 10; agent-notes lines 20 and 44. taxi-A-13: reply 5, paragraph 1 against paragraph 2. taxi-B-02: reply 3 decision section; msg 4 overrides it; ledger Q-011. taxi-B-12: reply 2 decision 1; ledger Q-006 is labelled 'settled before any analysis'. co2-A-10: r3, m4 (38 countries against 45 at a 5% threshold). retail-B-25: reply 1 definition 4; the agent-002 country y1/y2 query, then reply 2 decision 2. co2-B-18: A2 coverage section. Release: awb-init/assets/workbench/workbench-guides/analysis.md:13; README 'What you will be asked' item 4.

verdicts.reasoning:
I looked for a harness cause and didn't find one. But only taxi-A clearly shows the failure C-02 describes. Most of the other cited cases follow analysis.md:13 as it is written.

Harness explanations I checked and rejected:
- **Codex approval policy "never".** It only adds the line "Approval policy is currently never. Do not provide the sandbox_permissions". Nothing in it tells the agent not to ask the user questions.
- **Codex "Autonomy and persistence" text.** This is in the base instructions, so interactive Codex has it too.
- **Persona front-loading.** No persona brief mentions a threshold, minimum or floor.
- **"Go ahead and answer all five questions".** A real user could plausibly say this.
- **Interim messages.** The relay passes them on, and interactive Codex shows them too.
- **Study disclosure.** It has no bearing on this.

The rule did reach the taxi-A agent. agent-notes line 17 shows it read workbench-guides/analysis.md. Line 20 records that a "possible small-group qualification" must be proposed "before final comparisons or viewing zone leaders". At the reply 3 signoff it still proposed only validity screens. In reply 4 it ran Q5 without a floor, and the top 10 included zones with 1 trip (Rikers Island, Charleston/Tottenville, Great Kills). Line 44 explains the choice by misreading the user's "keep unknown zones" approval. The 300-trip floor came only after the user saw those leaders, and state.md/brief.md record that it was "chosen after seeing the unrestricted results". The same would happen on an interactive Codex host. The release's one sentence of guidance, with nothing in run.py or settings to enforce it, did not prevent it.

Cited cases that don't hold:
- **taxi-B, 65 mph.** The user asked for a speed limit "before analyzing". The agent proposed it after profiling only the speed distribution, before any answer was computed. That is not seeing "which rows lead".
- **taxi-B, rate-code-99.** The agent proposed this exclusion after seeing the 0% medians and did not apply it. It was open that the 0% medians prompted it, which line 13 allows. The real concern is narrower and different: the agent recommended a post-hoc exclusion for the main figures and called the remaining records "reliable". Q-006's label "settled before any analysis" is accurate.
- **retail-B.** The £2,000 threshold was proposed before any data was loaded. For the £20k flag, the y1/y2 query was piped through awk so that only the sorted Year 1 values were printed. The agent never saw growth leaders or country names, and the flag excludes nothing. The only problem is the offer to "adjust if the list ends up too long", which the user turned down.
- **co2-B.** Antarctica out and Kosovo in follow from the user's own "sovereign countries and territories" definition. Libya was dropped for missing data. The matched 2023 year was disclosed with "Tell me if you'd prefer it the other way". None of these changes which rows lead. The Claude agent also offered the 5% materiality alternative during scoping.
- **co2-A.** The agent took "reduced" literally (agent-notes: "No new threshold for emissions decline"). That is a missed materiality question during scoping, not a threshold set after seeing the leaders.
- **taxi-A "opposite failure".** The agent corrected itself within the same turn and then did what the user had asked, which is minor.

The finding IDs cited in C-02 don't match the findings files: taxi-A-13 is about package size, taxi-B-12 about incomplete tables, retail-B-25 about long replies. The transcript locations named alongside them are the evidence that counts.
verdicts.release_evidence: awb-init/assets/workbench/workbench-guides/analysis.md:13 is one sentence: propose an unsettled threshold, minimum or exclusion before looking at which rows lead, and disclose it when proposed after. No mechanism in run.py, settings.toml or the question ledger requires a recorded support floor before a ranking result runs. The README's "What you will be asked" item 4 repeats the promise. taxi-A agent-notes lines 17, 20, 40 and 44 show that the guide was read and the rule planned for, then skipped. The unrestricted top 10 is in taxi-A reply 4, and state.md row q5-zones says "No sample-size cutoff was authorized or imposed".
verdicts.narrowed: In one of five runs (taxi-A, Codex agent), the agent planned to propose a support floor for the top-10 zone ranking before seeing the leaders, recorded that plan in its notes, and then skipped it. It presented a top 10 with zones of 1 to 13 trips. A 300-trip floor was set only after the user saw those leaders and asked, and the agent disclosed that timing. This would also happen on an interactive Codex host, because the rule in analysis.md:13 is unenforced guidance. A smaller related gap: co2-A (Codex) never asked whether a tiny decline counts as "reduced", so the user had to ask for the 5% version (minor, scoping). The B runs (taxi-B, retail-B, co2-B) proposed their thresholds before computing answers, or disclosed proposals made after seeing results, which line 13 allows. taxi-B's rate-code-99 recommendation is a separate judgment issue: it recommended a disclosed post-hoc exclusion for the main figures rather than a sensitivity check. It is not a breach of the rule as written.

verdicts.reasoning:
The release does not cause this behaviour. It states the rule plainly in two places that agents read before analysis. analysis.md:13 says "propose it to the user before looking at which rows lead, and say so when you propose one after seeing results". awb-explore/SKILL.md:51 repeats it, and README item 4 tells the user to expect it. No helper, template or other instruction in the release pushes the other way. Checked run by run, most of the cited evidence either follows the rule or does not match the finding's description.

- **taxi-B-12 (Claude agent):** The user asked in msg 2 for a speed limit to be proposed before analysis. The agent proposed 65 mph from the speed distribution, said openly that the rule catches 2,182 trips with a median of 14 seconds, and waited for signoff. It ran no question results first. Q-006's note "settled before any analysis" is accurate.
- **taxi-B-02:** The rate-code-99 exclusion was put to the user as a recommendation, with an alternative, after the 0% medians appeared. It was plainly framed as a reaction to that result and was not applied. The user overrode it (Q-011). This is the rule's own allowance: propose after seeing results, and say so. Also, taxi-B proposed its 1,000-trip zone floor in reply 1, before any data, which is the rule working.
- **retail-B-25 (Claude):** £2,000 was proposed before any data was loaded. The agent did add "adjust if the list ends up too long or too short", a minor slip the user closed by fixing the threshold. The £20k flag came from a query whose awk step printed only the sorted Year 1 values: no country names and no Year 2 growth. The agent proposed the flag before computing growth and explained the basis (a natural gap between £14k and £21k). That follows the rule.
- **co2-B-18 (Claude):** In reply 1 the agent proposed the 5% materiality alternative up front. Its other choices were not thresholds picked from the leaders: Kosovo was included as the brief's "countries and territories" requires, Antarctica (near-zero CO2) was excluded as not a country, Libya was dropped for missing coal data, and the matched 2023 year was offered for override ("Tell me if you'd prefer it the other way"). None of these depended on which rows lead, and all were disclosed.
- **taxi-A-13:** A mid-turn progress line said the agent would wait for signoff, and the next line corrected it under the user's delegation. The wait cited the user's earlier instruction on cutoffs, not the release. The final answer was correct and disclosed that the 300 floor came after the unrestricted results. This is cosmetic.

Two cited cases hold, both in Codex-agent runs.

- **taxi-A-01:** Reply 4 showed an unrestricted Q5 top 10 led by Rikers Island on 1 trip, with no floor proposed first. The agent had read analysis.md, and agent-notes line 20 records its plan to propose "possible small-group qualification" before viewing zone leaders. At line 44 it then rationalised that the user had approved "no minimum support threshold", which the user never said; the user only approved keeping unknown/outside zones. This is non-compliance with a rule the agent had read, once.
- **co2-A-10:** Q2 counted any decline, including -0.3%, with no materiality threshold raised. The brief literally says "reduced", and the agent's notes treat baseline thresholds as already settled. This is a judgment miss, not a broken instruction. The same question in co2-B shows a Claude agent raising the 5% option on its own.

The rule is clear, present, and followed in most runs. The two real misses are agent execution failures, one per run, not repeated disregard of the rule.

A possible improvement, not a defect: awb-scope's interview names "method choices" but never prompts for a minimum-support floor on top-N ranking questions. Asking for one in the scoping round would catch the taxi-A case before the analysis turn.
verdicts.release_evidence:
Release text that prevents the behaviour:
- awb-init/assets/workbench/workbench-guides/analysis.md:13: "A threshold, minimum, or exclusion the brief does not settle is the user's decision: propose it to the user before looking at which rows lead, and say so when you propose one after seeing results."
- awb-explore/SKILL.md:51 repeats the same rule for exploration.
- README.md:67 ('What you will be asked' item 4) says such choices are "proposed before the agent sees which rows lead".
- No release instruction, helper or template conflicts with this rule.
- awb-scope/SKILL.md:25 and :44 cover "method choices" in the interview but never mention ranking support floors. This is the only gap.

Run evidence:
- taxi-A: feedback/agent-notes.md line 20 records the plan to propose a small-group qualification before viewing zone leaders; line 44 rationalises the unrestricted ranking. relay/agent-004.out.md shows that ranking.
- taxi-B: relay/agent-001.out.md decision 4 proposes the 1,000-trip floor before any data. relay/agent-002.out.md decision 1 proposes 65 mph with its count disclosed.
- retail-B: agent-002.jsonl, tool call toolu_01NYB31UKuVvL3u22BJ758D8, printed only the sorted Year 1 values.
- co2-B: relay/agent-001.out.md decision 2 offers the 5% alternative up front.
- co2-A: feedback/agent-notes.md:38 says "baseline thresholds remained local choices already authorized".
verdicts.narrowed:
Two Codex-agent runs missed a threshold before seeing results, despite a clear release rule.
- taxi-A showed an unrestricted Q5 top-10 zone ranking, led by Rikers Island on 1 trip, without first proposing a minimum-trip floor. The agent had read analysis.md:13 and noted a plan to propose one before viewing zone leaders.
- co2-A counted any CO2 decline, including -0.3%, as qualifying for Q2 without raising a materiality threshold. The brief's literal "reduced" arguably settles this.

The other cited instances follow the rule:
- taxi-B 65 mph and rate-code-99: proposed with disclosure and not applied.
- retail-B £2,000 and £20k: proposed before results, with the £20k flag based on Year 1 values only.
- co2-B Antarctica, Kosovo, Libya and 2023: settled by the brief or by missing data, and disclosed.

This is agent non-compliance, not release-caused. An optional hardening: awb-scope could ask for a support floor on top-N ranking questions during scoping.

consolidated.title: Review over-enforces citation form and tolerance wording, and repairs delete true context
consolidated.description: The review pass now ends, but it is strict about how evidence is cited rather than what it shows. taxi-B's first full review raised 21 problems, about 15 of them about citation form: 'every' or 'exactly' claims needing result IDs or scan paths, data-quality rows rejected for citing exploration queries, and the user's own word 'flagged' rejected as a record word. In co2-B, 9 of 16 problems across two reviews concerned 'matches/reconciles' wording. A tolerance counts only if the brief or settings recorded it before the result, never in a judgment detail. The agent cleared those problems by citing OWID's processing code and deleting context. co2-A spent one extra round on 'consistent within source rounding' in the donor note. retail-B's -4.4e-06 float gap failed 'equals exactly'. Repairs mostly deleted true statements: the JFK flat-fare context, the cash-tip context, and the empty fields on code-0 records. Package review did not loop.
consolidated.caused_by_fix: yes, partly: #101 (issue #85) caused most of these problems. It allows a tolerance only when a record held it before the result, and only in methodology.md or Notes. It limits citations to a result ID, an evidence path, or a quality ID with its scan. It also added 'flagged' to the record words. The refusal of exploration-query citations persists from Oct 16 (C-07).
consolidated.evidence: taxi-B-05: review-reports/agent-005-record01.txt (21 problems), agent-005-record02 (2), agent-006-record01 (1 error and 3 problems), agent-006-record02 (clean); the deletions are in reply 5. co2-B-02: in relay/agent-004.jsonl, 5 of the full review's 9 problems are match/reconcile wording, and so are 4 of the scoped review's 7, on the same sentences; A4 decision 3. co2-A-04: the agent-006 full review raised 1 problem at methodology-note.md:27; the scoped review 0.9 min later was clean. retail-B-12: agent-005 full review flags methodology.md:43, findings.md:140 and :146, and methodology-note.md:26; state.md line 12 still says 'reconciliation_gap 0'. Release: awb-package/references/review.md:26 (citation forms and tolerance rule) and :28 (record words). No loop: no request took more than two reviews (kit/reviewloop.py).

verdicts.reasoning:
I looked for a harness cause and found none. The reviewer enforced rules that the release states word for word.

1. The reviewer got no harness framing. In taxi-B turn 5, both reviewer launches were built-in `Plan` subagents. Their prompts contain only the project root, the investigation, the package and the path of the release's review.md, plus a line telling them to follow its Brief. There is no study disclosure and no persona text, and the relay, the simulated home and MCP auto-approval play no part in what a read-only reviewer reports. A real Claude Code user gets the same subagent type with the same brief.

2. It shows up with both models. The B runs (taxi-B, co2-B, retail-B) use Claude as the agent. co2-A uses Codex, and its review, apparently run without a separately detected reviewer subagent, flagged the same tolerance placement. So it is not one model's role quirk.

3. Each flagged item matches a release sentence:
   - review.md:26 requires every checked, matches, reconciles or adds-up sentence to cite a result ID, an evidence path, or a DQ ID with its `foundation/scans/` path. It allows a tolerance only in methodology.md or a slide's Notes, and only from brief.md or the result's settings. A tolerance found only in a judgment's detail is named as a problem.
   - review.md:27 says a sentence about how a source builds a series must rest on a sources.md `reference:`.
   - review.md:28 lists "flagged" as a banned record word.

4. The release contradicts itself. Its foundation/quality.md template tells DQ rows to cite "the scan or saved query that found it". taxi-B's DQ-002 and DQ-004 did exactly that, and review.md then rejected them for lacking a scan path. Scans are also gitignored and stay local to the checkout.

5. The user's word was banned. In taxi-B, the persona said "retain and flag it" (agent-003.in.md). The reviewer rejected "kept and flagged" in findings.md:105 and in the note, citing the release's record-word list.

6. The deletions are real, and each was a response to a release rule:
   - JFK flat fare: the median fare was exactly $70.00. The flat-fare sentence was cut after two rounds under the source-reference rule.
   - Cash tips: "cash trips show a tip on almost no records" was cut. DQ-001 records 0.036%, but only from an exploration query. The tipping caveat itself survives through the dictionary quote.
   - Code-0 records: "every one also has null passenger count, rate code, store-and-forward flag, congestion surcharge and airport fee" was cut down to the passenger count.
   - co2-B: the "match the world total" wording was replaced by a citation of OWID's processing code, in decision 3 of turn 4's reply.

None of this would change on an interactive host. The agent would still repair within the same turn, as review.md's After the review section directs.

7. Counts check out. In taxi-B's first review I count 10 citation or exactness problems, 2 record-word problems and 2 source-reference problems out of 21, so 14 rather than about 15. co2-B is 5 of 9, then 4 of 7. retail-B flagged methodology.md:43, findings.md:140 and :146, and methodology-note.md:26, and state.md line 12 still says "reconciliation_gap 0". kit/reviewloop.py shows no request took more than two reviews.

The finding overreaches in places, so I give a narrower version below.
verdicts.release_evidence:
Sentences in the release that cause each behaviour:
- awb-package/references/review.md:26: every sentence that asserts checked, verified, reconciles, sums or matches must cite a result ID, an evidence path, or a DQ ID with the path of the scan its row cites. A tolerance is stated only in methodology.md or a slide's Notes, and only one recorded before the result in brief.md or the result's settings. "A tolerance no such record holds, one only in a judgment's `detail` included, is a problem."
- review.md:27: a sentence about how a source builds a series must rest on a `reference:` in the source's sources.md row, or on a recorded check.
- review.md:28: bans the words ledger, flagged and disposition outside Implications.
- The release's foundation/quality.md template (as written in taxi-B/project/foundation/quality.md) tells a coverage-gap row to cite "the scan or saved query that found it", which review.md:26 then rejects.
- awb-init/assets/workbench/.gitignore and awb-clean/references/checks.md:33 keep foundation/scans local to the checkout. taxi-B and co2-B have no scans directory at all.

Reviewer launches and prompts: taxi-B/relay/agent-005.jsonl (Plan subagent, no disclosure). User's own word: taxi-B/relay/agent-003.in.md ("retain and flag it"). Deletions: taxi-B/relay/agent-005.out.md and co2-B/relay/agent-004.out.md (decision 3).
verdicts.narrowed:
Narrower version that holds: review.md:26-28 makes reviewers judge how evidence is cited, not only whether the claim is true. A data-quality row that cites a saved exploration query fails, even though the release's own quality.md template allows that citation. A tolerance recorded only in a judgment's detail cannot be stated, and neither can a user's own word such as "flagged". The agents' cheapest repair was to delete true context: taxi-B lost the JFK flat-fare sentence, the cash-tip rate and the empty fields on code-0 records, and co2-B replaced its match wording with a citation of OWID's code.

Points to drop or soften:
- Not every citation-form problem was pedantic. Some caught real defects. In taxi-B, methodology.md:36 claimed every result passes its values check when that check is not applicable for two results. In co2-B, the "year by year" match had no record behind it. In retail-B, "gap = 0" and "equals exactly" were literally false against the recorded -4.38e-06, and methodology.md:43 now states the gap honestly.
- The same full reviews also caught substantive errors: July's peak hour (a tie, not 6 pm), "fares near $90", and the untested "none of these limitations" claims.
- co2-A cost one round of 0.9 minutes and should count as minor, not major.
- In taxi-B the count is 14 of 21, not about 15.
- The cash-tip substance survives through the dictionary quote; only the empirical rate was deleted.

verdicts.reasoning:
The reviewer subagents are applying shipped text almost word for word, so the release is the cause. It is not reviewer drift and not the harness.

1. Citation forms. awb-package/references/review.md:26 says that in methodology.md a sentence asserting a check, a reconciliation or a match must cite one of three things: a result ID, an evidence path, or a DQ-NNN ID together with the foundation/scans/<name>.json path of the scan its row cites. Findings.md and the note must name that check in plain words.
2. Tolerances. The same line allows a tolerance only in methodology.md or a slide's Notes, and only when brief.md or the result's settings recorded it before the result. "A tolerance ... only in a judgment's `detail` ... is a problem." An exact check must say "exactly" or "every row". package-contract.md:49 repeats this.
3. Record words. review.md:28 bans the words ledger, flagged and disposition in findings.md and the note outside Implications.
4. Internal conflict. awb-clean/SKILL.md section 6 explicitly lets a `new` quality row cite a saved exploration query and says "its row has no scan link". Such a row can never meet the scan-path form in review.md:26. That conflict produced taxi-B's DQ-002 and DQ-004 problems. It also led to cutting "every code-0 record lacks rate code, store-and-forward, congestion and airport fee" back to "lacks a passenger count". DQ-002 records the fuller version as true, from payment-type-0-nulls.sql.

The cited evidence checks out:
- taxi-B agent-005-record01 has 21 problems. About 10 are pure citation form: exactly/every claims, DQ rows citing exploration queries rather than scans, an exploration query cited as a check. Two are "flagged", which is the word the user used in their instruction ("retain and flag it"). Three are source-reference demands. The reply-5 deletions are as described: the JFK flat-fare remark, the cash-tip remark (true per DQ-001, 0.036% of cash trips tipped), and "lack other fields".
- co2-B: 5 of the first review's 9 problems and 4 of the scoped review's 7 sit on the match, reconcile and world-total sentences. methodology.md:35 failed because its within-1-Mt tolerance lived only in a judgment detail. Decision 3 in agent-004.out.md dropped "matching totals". The final methodology.md no longer states the within-1-Mt world reconciliation or that the China/India sums equal OWID cumulative_co2; it cites OWID's processing code instead.
- co2-A: "consistent within source rounding" in the note was rejected only for where it appeared. The tolerance itself was pre-recorded as [parameters].eu27_rounding_tolerance_mt and stays in methodology.md. It cost one 0.9-minute scoped round.
- retail-B: the -4.38e-06 gap failed "= 0 ... exactly". The repair dropped the revenue reconciliation and cited only the line-count check. state.md line 12 still says "reconciliation_gap 0".
- No loop: reviewloop.py shows at most two reviews in any request.

Where the finding overstates:
- taxi-B's first review also caught real errors: July's 6 pm peak is actually a tie with 7 pm, the note's "fares near $90" ignores July's $82.52, and "none of these limitations changes the direction" was never tested. So "how evidence is cited rather than what it shows" is only partly true.
- retail-B's "= 0, exactly" really did contradict the recorded value, so that flag was correct. The defect is that the release gives no allowed wording for a near-exact match without a tolerance recorded beforehand.
- The JFK flat-fare context was not lost for good. In the next request, at the user's direction, the agent added a recorded check and restored it.
- Replacing "flagged" with "marked as a possible duplicate" lost no information.
- Some deletions were the agent's choice of the cheapest repair. Adding a methodology.md claim was possible for the cash-tip line, though its number would still need a represented result.

A real user on an interactive host gets the same reviewer brief, so they would hit the same rejections.
verdicts.release_evidence:
- awb-package/references/review.md:26: every checked, verified, reconciles, adds-up or matches sentence must cite a result ID, an evidence path, or a DQ-NNN plus "the path of the scan its row cites" (foundation/scans/<name>.json). A tolerance is allowed only in methodology.md or slide Notes, and only when brief.md or the result's settings recorded it before the result; "A tolerance no such record holds, one only in a judgment's `detail` included, is a problem; an exact check says 'exactly' or 'every row'."
- awb-package/references/review.md:28: bans the record words "ledger, flagged, or disposition" in findings.md and the note outside Implications.
- awb-package/references/package-contract.md:49: repeats the citation and tolerance rule, adding "a tolerance chosen after seeing the result is not one".
- Conflicting text, awb-clean/SKILL.md section 6: the example `new` row has evidence "investigations/churn/exploration/march-gap.sql", and the text says "A `new` issue's evidence is a saved query's path or a reference in words ... and its row has no scan link". Rows made this way can never satisfy the scan-path form review.md:26 requires.
- awb-package/references/review.md:43: two-review cap per request and "repair every ... narrative problem", with no guidance on adding support versus deleting.
verdicts.narrowed: The review's tolerance and citation rules (review.md:26, package-contract.md:49) leave no allowed wording for a true reconciliation that is near-exact or within a tolerance unless that tolerance was recorded before the result. The same rules leave no way to cite a quality row built from a saved query, which awb-clean explicitly creates with no scan link. The record-word rule (review.md:28) rejects plain words such as "flagged". So agents delete or shrink true, informative statements to clear the review. Examples: co2-B dropped the within-1-Mt world reconciliation and the OWID cumulative_co2 equality; retail-B dropped the revenue reconciliation (gap -4.38e-06); taxi-B dropped the cash-tip observation and cut code-0's missing fields to passenger count only; co2-A moved "within source rounding" out of the note. The review also caught genuine errors in the same passes: taxi-B's July 6 pm peak and the July Newark fare, and the untested "none of these limitations" claims in taxi-B and co2-B. retail-B's "= 0 exactly" really was false. The JFK flat-fare context was restored in the next request. Package review did not loop.

consolidated.title: Review stop rules hand trivial or self-inflicted problems to the user
consolidated.description: The review no longer loops, but two rules added in #96 now escalate problems to the user. First, a problem marked '(unchanged since the prior review)' must go to the user. Fresh reviewers still miss lines and catch them later, and the marker cannot tell a missed problem from one the agent's own repair created. One reviewer applied the marker to a problem the prior report had already listed. Second, when a second review in one request still finds problems, the agent must stop and ask. The results: taxi-B handed the user a two-word repair that only narrowed a claim. co2-B escalated the user's own approved word 'cut' as an overclaim, together with a problem its own repair had introduced. co2-B later broke the rule to fix three slide-4 lines marked unchanged that earlier reviews had missed, and the deck title with 'cut' passed every review. retail-B escalated a citation fix in the internal methodology.md, which held back the 'checks pass' confirmation the user had asked for. Users called these escalations disproportionate. Tag: four members are product and two are unclear (retail-B-38, retail-A-42); the stop rules are release text that would apply on any host.
consolidated.caused_by_fix: yes: #96 (issue #84) added the unchanged-line marker that sends a problem to the user, and the stop after a second review in one request. The reviewer variance behind them (C-17) persists.
consolidated.evidence: taxi-B-06: review-reports/agent-005-record02.txt marks both lines unchanged, though the repair to methodology.md:159 caused them; reply 5. co2-B-03: relay/agent-004.jsonl flags 'cut' at findings.md:7 and :37 (from the A3 preview, approved in U4); the scoped review flags them again, plus findings.md:12, which the repair created; A4 'Decisions for you' items 1-3; U5. co2-B-04: relay/agent-005.jsonl marks findings.md:42, :51 and :52 '(unchanged since the prior review...)'; release 001 findings.md line 1 still says 'cut'. retail-B-06: agent-006 marks methodology.md:64 unchanged; msg 7 says routine citation corrections need no separate decision. retail-B-38: the second scoped report marks a problem that the prior report listed. retail-B-08 and retail-A-42 confirm there was no loop: retail-B took 2, 2 and 1 reviews per request, retail-A 2, 1 and 1. Release: awb-package/references/review.md:35 (the marker) and :43 (take it to the user; stop after a second review).

verdicts.reasoning:
I looked for a harness cause and did not find one. Each escalation came from release text, and the agents quoted that text when they escalated.

taxi-B: review-reports/agent-005-record02.txt marks findings.md:163 and methodology-note.md:37 "(unchanged since the prior review)". In the same lines, the reviewer explains that the repair to methodology.md:159 caused both problems. That marking follows review.md:35 to the letter: the lines were unchanged and the prior report did not list the problem. So the marker cannot tell a problem the first pass missed from one the agent's own repair created. The agent's reply 5 then says "The review rules say I take this to you rather than repairing on a third pass", and hands the user the swap of "other fields" for "a passenger count". That swap only narrowed a claim.

retail-B: agent-006-record01 marks methodology.md:64 unchanged. Reply 6 says "The error predates this round. The review rules ask me to bring it to you rather than fix it myself." The item was one citation in the internal methodology.md, and it held back the "checks pass" confirmation the user had asked for. In msg 7 the user says routine citation corrections need no separate decision. In agent-006-record02, the reviewer marks the same problem unchanged even though it notes "The prior review reported it". That confirms retail-B-38.

co2-B: agent-004-record02 lists 'cut' at findings.md:7 and :37 again, plus findings.md:12, a problem the repair created. A4 says "The procedure stops my repairs after a second review" and asks three decisions. In agent-005, the agent repaired findings.md:42, :51 and :52, which were marked unchanged, against review.md:43. The released 001 findings.md line 1 still reads "Who has cut and who has grown CO2 emissions since 2000".

Harness angles I checked:
- **Agent system prompt:** says only "behave exactly as you normally would". It says nothing about reviews.
- **Reviewer briefs:** the agents launched Plan subagents pointed at the installed review.md Brief, as the release says to do.
- **Request boundaries:** one relay turn is one user request, the same as in an interactive session. So "second review in one request" fires the same way.
- **Personas and kit:** neither personas nor human-rules.md prime the users about reviews. The feedback prompt to the users is neutral ("where turns or time were wasted"); "disproportionately" in the kit appears only in the agent's prompt, about where time and tokens went. All three B-run users still independently called the escalations disproportionate or unnecessary.
- **README:** the users had read the README's warning about the stop rule. That would reduce complaints, not cause them.
- **Sandbox, simulated home, MCP auto-approval:** none of these touches the review procedure.

Caveats that narrow the finding:
- **co2-B 'cut':** the agent chose to bring the user's approved 'cut' to the user after the first review, citing that it was the user's wording. The stop rules did not force that choice. What the stop rule forced was bundling it with the problems the repair created (findings.md:12 and the world-total wording). The user's "disproportionate" complaint is partly about the reviewer's claim-strength rule, not only the stop rules.
- **retail-B-38:** this misapplied marker is a reviewer error. It did not change the outcome, because the second-review stop would have escalated the problem anyway.
- **The deck title:** the title that kept 'cut' shows reviewers are inconsistent, which happens on any host. It is not itself harm done by the stop rules.
- **retail-A:** it never escalated. It is only evidence that the review no longer loops.
- **Which runs escalated:** all three Claude-agent runs (B) escalated. None of the Codex-agent runs (A) did: their first reviews found 1-3 problems and their second passes were clean. So how often this happens depends on the host and how thorough its reviewer is. Claude Code is a supported host, so that is still the product.
verdicts.release_evidence: awb-package/references/review.md:35 says a scoped reviewer must end a line with "(unchanged since the prior review)" for a problem the prior report did not list, found on a line the diff left unchanged. Nothing in that text separates a missed problem from one created by a change elsewhere, such as a change to the supporting methodology line. review.md:43 says "Take a problem marked `(unchanged since the prior review)` ... to the user rather than repairing it. When a second review in one request still reports problems, stop repairing and start no third review in that request unless the user asks". Neither rule exempts trivial or self-inflicted repairs. README.md:70 and CHANGELOG.md:146 describe the same behavior for users. awb-package/SKILL.md:83 already lets a repair rewrite a user's sentence as long as the new wording is shown to them, so release text does not by itself require asking before such repairs.
verdicts.narrowed: The release's two stop rules (review.md:35 and :43) send the user minor problems, and problems the agent's own repairs created, with no way to tell those apart from a missed problem. This shows up as a decision for the user in taxi-B (the "lack a passenger count" wording), retail-B (one internal citation, which held back the "checks pass" confirmation) and co2-B (findings.md:12, created by the repair, bundled into the decision list). It shows up on hosts whose reviewer finds many problems; it happened in all three Claude Code runs and in none of the Codex-agent runs. In co2-B the agent's own judgment, not the stop rule, first sent the user's approved 'cut' to the user. retail-B-38 (the reviewer marking a problem the prior report had listed) is a reviewer error that did not change the outcome, and retail-A shows no escalation. Severity is closer to minor: two of the three users rated it minor, and the third, co2-B, rated it major only together with the other review stops.

verdicts.reasoning:
The release text requires these escalations, and nothing in it makes an exception for routine fixes. awb-package/references/review.md:35 tells a scoped reviewer to add "(unchanged since the prior review)" to any problem the prior report did not list, whenever it sits on a line the diff did not change. That test is only about the line, so it cannot tell a problem an earlier pass missed from one that a repair elsewhere created. review.md:43 says a marked problem goes to the user "rather than repairing it". It also says that when a second review in one request still reports problems, the agent stops repairing and shows the user each problem. README.md:70 and CHANGELOG.md:146 say the same thing. Because a marked problem cannot be repaired, the next review always finds it again, so the stop rule always fires as well. The two rules work together.

Evidence check:
- taxi-B: verified. review-reports/agent-005-record02.txt marks findings.md:163 and methodology-note.md:37 as unchanged. Its own reason is that the repair to methodology.md:159 cut back the support, so this was not a missed problem. Agent reply 5 (relay/agent-005.out.md) cites "The review rules say I take this to you rather than repairing on a third pass" and asks the user about a two-word change to "lack a passenger count". The user approved at once (human-006) and in feedback called it a "small approval loop", rated minor.
- retail-B: verified. agent-006-record01 marks methodology.md:64, a wrong result citation in the internal methodology, as unchanged and says earlier passes genuinely missed it. The agent did not repair it, the second review still found it, and the agent asked the user for a yes on the one-citation fix while saying the review was not yet cleared. The user replied that "routine citation corrections like this don't need a separate decision" (human-007) and in feedback called it "too broad". Item retail-B-38 is also verified: agent-006-record02 marks the same line unchanged even though the prior report listed it. That is the reviewer misapplying :35, but it did not change the outcome.
- co2-B: partly verified. The second scoped review (agent-004-record02) found findings.md:12, a problem the agent's own repair created, plus the sourcing of the world total. Under the stop rule the agent bundled these into "Decisions for you". In agent-005-record01, the three slide-4 "cut" lines (:42, :51, :52) are marked unchanged because earlier passes missed them. The agent went against :43 and repaired them, citing the user's earlier decision. That shows the rule is too broad, not that it is ignored. The deck title "Who has cut..." in release 001 findings.md:1 passed every review, which supports the point that fresh reviewers miss lines.

Where the finding overreaches:
- In co2-B, escalating the headline word "cut" was not caused by either stop rule. The agent itself chose to bring it to the user after the first review: "the other two concern the word 'cut' in headlines you approved ... so I'll bring those to you". The reviewer flagged it under step 3's rule against a "verb of change with an agent as its subject" (review.md:24). The user's "disproportionate" complaint in co2-B is mostly about that item.
- retail-A shows no escalation at all; it only confirms there was no loop. The one-word headline decision in retail-B came from the headline word-limit check, not from these rules.
- Users rated the escalations caused by the stop rules as minor (taxi-B, retail-B). co2-B's major rating covers the whole editorial process, including the "cut" item, so "major" overstates what these two rules caused.
verdicts.release_evidence: awb-package/references/review.md:35: "When the prior report does not list a problem you find on a line the diff leaves unchanged, end its line with `(unchanged since the prior review)` and why the earlier pass missed it." The test is only that the line is unchanged; it does not ask whether a repair elsewhere caused the problem. review.md:43: "Take a problem marked `(unchanged since the prior review)`, or a conflict between two rules, to the user rather than repairing it. When a second review in one request still reports problems, stop repairing and start no third review in that request unless the user asks: show the user each problem in plain words with a recommended repair." Neither rule exempts routine citation fixes, problems a repair caused, or narrowing rewordings that keep the evidence intact. README.md:70 and CHANGELOG.md:146 state the same behaviour.
verdicts.narrowed:
Two release rules make the agent ask the user about trivial or self-inflicted narrative problems: the unchanged-line marker in review.md:35 together with "take it to the user" in :43, and the stop after a second review in :43. The marker is based on whether the line changed, so it treats a problem that a repair created elsewhere the same as one an earlier pass missed. A marked problem cannot be repaired, so the next review finds it again and the stop rule fires too. Confirmed cases:
- taxi-B: a two-word narrowing change ("lack a passenger count") that the agent's own repair made necessary.
- retail-B: a citation fix in the internal methodology.md, which held back the "fully cleared" confirmation the user had asked for.
- co2-B: the problem its repair created at findings.md:12 was bundled into a user decision, and the three missed slide-4 "cut" lines would have had to go to the user (the agent broke the rule and repaired them).
Not caused by these rules: co2-B's question about the user-approved headline word "cut". The step-3 overclaim rule flagged it, and the agent itself chose to defer to the user's wording. retail-A is not affected. Severity is closer to minor or moderate than major: users rated the escalations these rules caused as minor.

consolidated.title: Untested explanations and overclaims still reach the user as fact
consolidated.description: #102 moved the untested-explanation rule into AGENTS.md's Conversation section and the headline checkpoint. Agents still stated untested causes and labels as fact, across several turns. taxi-B confirmed the user's cash-tip recollection from observed zeros and called speed outliers 'timing errors'. It also said code 0 'is a Flex Fare trip', then proposed a 'Flex Fare trips rose' headline right after calling the meaning unconfirmed. retail-B wrote 'not product demand', 'Christmas closure' and 'Lean the budget towards retention'. taxi-B's data-quality headline 'vendors differ in why, not how often' hid vendor 6's 35% invalid rate. retail-A's How we know slide turned the user's 'plausible' into 'as confirmed by the e-commerce lead'. retail-B's state.md keeps the causal 'product revenue drives the shape' on a descriptive finding. Nothing checks for these before the draft review. Tag: one member (retail-B-30) is unclear; the others are product, and the problem recurred across runs and turns.
consolidated.caused_by_fix: no
consolidated.evidence: taxi-B-01: replies 1-4, with the user correcting in msgs 2-5; feedback/human.md pain point 1, the main reason for the 7/10 score. retail-B-02: reply 2, reply 3 headline 3, reply 4; full review in agent-005 (15 problems). taxi-B-16: reply 4 headline 6; msg 5. retail-A-11: msg 4 ('plausible'); release 001 findings.md How we know, which passed the agent-008 scoped review. retail-B-30: state.md line 9; awb_provenance.py _finding_warnings has no causal-wording check. Release: awb-init/assets/workbench/AGENTS.md Conversation ('Offer an untested explanation as a question'; 'Record what the user recalls as their statement'); awb-package/SKILL.md headline checkpoint.

verdicts.reasoning:
I tried each harness explanation in turn and none of them accounts for the core instances.

1. **The agent had the rules in context.** In taxi-B the Claude agent printed the template AGENTS.md during turn 1 (agent-001 log), before it wrote reply 1. It read workbench-guides/analysis.md in turn 2. No CLAUDE.md exists in the project or any folder above it, and the host is Claude Code 2.1.301. The release README says Claude Code reads AGENTS.md from 2.1.277, so the rules would also load on each resumed turn. A real Claude Code user would get the same instructions.

2. **The overclaims were not prompted.** Each one appears in the agent's own summary or headline proposal, not in answer to a persona request:
   - taxi-B reply 2: 65 mph trips are "timing errors, not fast drivers", and Outside-NYC trips are "mostly heading to Long Island or Westchester".
   - taxi-B reply 3: "These aren't missing data: the dictionary defines code 0 as a Flex Fare trip".
   - taxi-B reply 4: the agent says the files cannot confirm what code 0 means, then in the same message proposes headline A3, "Flex Fare trips rose...". This breaks awb-package's headline checkpoint, which says an untested explanation must never be a headline's claim.
   - taxi-B reply 4, headline 6: "vendors differ in why, not how often", although the same reply had reported vendor 6 at 35% invalid.
   - retail-B reply 3: headline 3 says "...not product demand".
   - retail-B reply 4: "the Christmas closure", "December's low figures reflect trading patterns, not missing data", and early cohorts' existing customers "would push their repeat rates up".

3. **Neither the study disclosure nor the harness note pushes toward interpretation.** The note asks the agent to work as it normally would and to keep a friction log.

4. **Running headless does not change what a reply says.** The relay passes on the agent's text unchanged.

5. **The rigorous Codex persona affects detection, not occurrence.** A less rigorous real user would let these claims through to a board deck, so the harm is larger on a real host.

6. **The release partly works but leaks.** In retail-B reply 4 the agent did correctly turn one explanation into a question ("That's untested, so I'd keep it as a question"). In the same reply it stated the other explanations above as fact.

7. **The finding's "nothing checks" claim holds before the draft review.** The state finding write path (awb_provenance._finding_warnings) checks numbers and asserted-check wording only. check-draft has a causal-verb regex (_CAUSAL in awb_draft.py), but it exempts the How we know and Limitations slides. It also would not match labels, closures or "You're right". The draft review is a real backstop for package text: retail-B agent-005 removed three overclaims, including "most informative place to test". So the leak is in chat replies, the headline preview and state.md, before that review.

**Where the harness, or the persona, does explain or weaken a member:**
- **retail-A-11 is weak.** In msg 8 the simulated user (Claude) suggested the wording "other identical lines are genuine repeat items on orders and were kept". That moves from "plausible" to "genuine" on its own, and the user then approved the agent's "as confirmed by the e-commerce lead". So the scoped review passing it is defensible, and most of the drift came from the persona, not the release.
- **retail-B "Lean the budget towards retention" is weak.** The persona asked explicitly for a cautious commercial recommendation, and the agent attached a caveat saying the figures cannot show what extra spend would change.
- **retail-B-30 "product revenue drives the shape" is weak.** Product revenue is about 99% of net revenue, so the sentence describes how the total breaks down rather than making a causal claim. It breaks the letter of AGENTS.md but is not a real overclaim.
- **taxi-B's cash-tip "You're right" was partly shaped by the simulation.** The sim boundary let the agent read only URLs the user gave it, so it could not check the TLC dictionary in turn 1 and had only the data to go on. The wording ("You're right") still overclaims, and the rule to record a user's recollection as their statement, not as confirmed, applies either way.

**Spread:** the strong instances are in the two Claude-agent runs (taxi-B, retail-B), recurring across turns 1 to 4 of each.
verdicts.release_evidence:
- **awb-init/assets/workbench/AGENTS.md, Conversation:** "Offer an untested explanation as a question. Name every share's base and say when it changes."
- **AGENTS.md, Analytical invariants:** "Record what the user recalls as their statement, not as confirmed ... an association never drives, causes, or leads to anything."
- **awb-package/SKILL.md line 52 (headline checkpoint):** "Offer an untested explanation as a question, never as a headline's claim."
- **awb-init/assets/awb_provenance.py:1661, _finding_warnings:** checks numbers and asserted reconciliation or check wording only; it has no causal or explanation check when a finding is recorded in state.md.
- **awb-package/assets/awb_draft.py:1157, _CAUSAL:** catches only causal verbs (drive, cause, due to, ...) in drafts, and skips How we know and Limitations (_UNCHECKED). It does not cover labels like "Flex Fare", "Christmas closure", "timing errors" or "as confirmed by".
- **Agent turn logs:** taxi-B agent-001 printed AGENTS.md before reply 1, and agent-002 read workbench-guides/analysis.md. No CLAUDE.md exists in any folder above the project, and the host is Claude Code 2.1.301, so the rules were loaded.

verdicts.reasoning:
The release already has clear rules against this, and agents broke them repeatedly anyway. That puts it under the "ignored a clear instruction repeatedly" exception, so this is a product problem, not unsupported. The shipped awb-init/assets/workbench/AGENTS.md says, in Conversation: "Offer an untested explanation as a question." Under Analytical invariants it says: "Record what the user recalls as their statement, not as confirmed ... an association never drives, causes, or leads to anything." awb-package/SKILL.md's headline checkpoint repeats the first rule: "never as a headline's claim". Both Claude agents had AGENTS.md in context: they cat'd the template in turn 1, and the session was resumed by --resume on every turn. They still broke the rules across turns, and the Codex agent in retail-A did too.

I checked the evidence in the transcripts myself:
- **taxi-B reply 1:** "You're right about cash tips ... essentially not recorded", based only on 0.04% observed tips. The user pushed back in message 2.
- **taxi-B reply 2:** "these are timing errors, not fast drivers". The user pushed back in message 3.
- **taxi-B reply 3:** "These aren't missing data: the dictionary defines code 0 as a Flex Fare trip".
- **taxi-B reply 4:** says "the files can't confirm whether 0 really marks Flex Fare trips". In the same reply it proposes appendix headline A3, "Flex Fare trips rose from 4.0% to 8.8%", and headline 6, "vendors differ in why, not how often". Headline 6 drops vendor 6's 35% invalid rate, which reply 3 had reported. The user corrected both in message 5.
- **retail-B reply 3:** headline 3 says "not product demand". The user corrected it in message 4.
- **retail-B reply 4:** "the Christmas closure", "That would push their repeat rates up", and "Lean the budget towards retention". The user corrected these in message 5.
- **retail-A release 001** findings.md line 95 says "as confirmed by the e-commerce lead". The user had only called the repeated lines "plausible". The scoped review agent-008 passed that changed line.
- **retail-B state.md** line 9 says "product revenue drives the shape" on a descriptive finding. `_finding_warnings` in awb_provenance.py checks only numbers and wording that claims a reconciliation; it has no causal-wording check.
- **taxi-B human.md** lists this as pain point 1, severity major.

Where the release falls short:
- **The rule itself:** it is a six-word sentence with no examples. The CHANGELOG notes that AGENTS.md is held to a fixed word count by a test, which is why the rule is so short.
- **The headline preview:** `.preview/headlines.md` is described in the release as a file "which no check reads", so overclaimed headlines reach the user unchecked.
- **check-draft's `claims` check:** a regex over causal phrases, applied only to findings.md. It skips How we know, Limitations and similar slides, and it runs last.
- **The reviewer brief:** it has no item for a user's statement shown as a confirmation.

A real user on a normal interactive host would hit this, and would often lack Dana's rigour to catch it. Nothing about the harness caused it. In a real first session, init and analysis also happen in one session, so AGENTS.md is read the same way the sim read it.

Several parts of the finding are weaker than stated:
- **The fix it implies (a causal-wording check in `_finding_warnings`) would catch little.** Most cited overclaims are about meaning ("timing errors", "Christmas closure", "not product demand", "Flex Fare", "why, not how often"), and no phrase regex would catch them.
- **The draft review already catches some draft-level overclaims.** retail-B agent-005 flagged findings.md:70, :106 and :134. So the real gap is chat replies, the headline preview, and How-we-know attributions.
- **retail-B "drives the shape"** describes a part's share of a total, in a record. The user used "drives" themselves in message 2, and check-draft would flag it if it reached a finding slide.
- **"Lean the budget towards retention"** was a recommendation the user asked for in message 4, and it came with a caveat.
- **retail-A's "genuine repeat items"** wording came from the user's own example in message 8, and the user approved the result. Only the "confirmed by" attribution is the agent's.
- **Several cited member IDs point to unrelated findings.json entries.** taxi-B-16 is about sources.md, retail-B-30 about the scratchpad path, and retail-A-11 about truncated outputs. The e-commerce-lead issue is retail-A-09. The transcript evidence exists all the same.
verdicts.release_evidence:
- **awb-init/assets/workbench/AGENTS.md, Conversation:** "Offer an untested explanation as a question."
- **Same file, Analytical invariants:** "Record what the user recalls as their statement, not as confirmed ... an association never drives, causes, or leads to anything." These are the only explanation rules: terse, with no examples. CHANGELOG line 125 says the file is held to a fixed word count by a test.
- **awb-package/SKILL.md, headline checkpoint:** "Offer an untested explanation as a question, never as a headline's claim". The preview `.preview/headlines.md` is described as the file "which no check reads".
- **awb-package/assets/awb_draft.py `_CAUSAL` and `_UNCHECKED`:** the claims check only looks for causal phrases (drive, cause, due to, impact and the like), only in findings.md finding slides. It skips How we know, Limitations and open caveats, Open questions, and similar slides.
- **awb-init/assets/awb_provenance.py `_finding_warnings`:** checks numbers and reconciliation wording only, with no causal-wording check.
- **awb-package/references/review.md, Brief step 3:** checks claim strength and assertions that something was "checked or verified". It has no item for a user's recollection presented as a confirmation.
- **findings-template.md, Implications:** "Keep recommendations and next steps within the evidence."
verdicts.narrowed:
Agents of both lineages repeatedly ignored the clear AGENTS.md and headline-checkpoint rules. They stated untested causes and labels as fact in chat replies and in proposed slide headlines: taxi-B replies 1-4 (cash tips confirmed from zeros, "timing errors", code 0 "is" Flex Fare and then a "Flex Fare trips rose" headline, a vendor headline that hid vendor 6's 35%) and retail-B replies 3-4 ("not product demand", "Christmas closure", early cohorts "would push" repeat rates up). Once, in retail-A, a user's "plausible" reached a released How-we-know slide as "confirmed by the e-commerce lead" and passed a scoped review.

The release guards against this only with a short rule that has no examples, in a word-capped AGENTS.md. Nothing checks the headline preview. check-draft's causal-phrase regex covers only findings.md finding slides and runs last. The reviewer brief has no item for user statements presented as confirmations. Most of these overclaims are about meaning rather than causal phrases, so adding a causal-wording check to state-finding warnings would not fix them. The retail-B state.md "drives the shape" line and the solicited "lean towards retention" recommendation are weak examples.

consolidated.title: Review still misses definition and meaning errors the user catches in one read
consolidated.description: The review now reads the brief. It checks evidence form, traceability and a closed readability list. It does not check whether audience definitions match the agreed rules or what a metric means, and it does not check for omissions. In taxi-B the review missed: a trip-time rule that left out negative durations; base fare called the meter's time-and-distance fare beside a $70 JFK median, the same base-fare error as on Oct 16; and a count-check sentence that read as adding overlapping counts. In co2-B it missed: 'counting imports' without exports; a rising coal share presented as coal use growing; and 'energy mix' for coal's share of CO2, which passed both drafting reviews. In retail-B it missed an undisclosed narrower 'first observed purchase' (a goods line with positive quantity and price), which moves the January cohort from 368 to 383; Oct 16 had the same narrowing.
