The gate also accepts any recorded check as support. In taxi-B, 'at least half of JFK trips show exactly $70.00' backed a claim about rate type.
consolidated.caused_by_fix: no. #101 gave the reviewer the brief, but checks against it are limited to question coverage and claims about how a source is built.
consolidated.evidence: taxi-B-04: the draft text in relay/agent-005.jsonl ('trip time is zero or over three hours'; 'Base fare is the meter's time-and-distance fare'; the count-check sentence); review-reports/agent-005-record01.txt flagged the last two only for citation form; msg 6. taxi-B-07: review-reports/agent-006-record01.txt; reply 6; human/notes.md turn 7. co2-B-05: A1 decision 3; A3 slides 5 and 8; 'energy mix' in the A4 draft (relay/agent-004.jsonl) passed the full and scoped reviews; U4, U5. retail-B-27: queries/repeat-within-90-days.sql (is_product AND quantity > 0 AND price > 0) against brief.md line 62; release 001 methodology-note.md lines 19-20; referee q3b.py. Release: awb-package/references/review.md:26-28.

verdicts.reasoning:
I looked for harness causes and found none that explain the misses. In taxi-B, co2-B and retail-B the reviewer ran the way the release says it should. The drafting agent started a fresh Claude Code `Plan` subagent, the reviewer kind review.md names for Claude Code. The prompt (taxi-B relay/agent-005.jsonl, Agent tool input) only points the subagent at review.md's Brief and lists files to read. It has no study disclosure, nothing from the persona, and nothing that narrows the scope. Running under claude -p, auto-approving MCP tools, using the simulated home and relaying messages change nothing about what the reviewer reads or judges. The misses come from what the Brief asks for.

The Brief does read brief.md, but step 3 checks only these things:
- narrative-to-methodology traceability and matching caveats;
- claim strength;
- revalidation flags;
- that sentences claiming a check cite one;
- that every part of the business question is answered;
- that source-construction sentences rest on a reference or check;
- a closed readability list.

Step 4 says to report "exactly this, and nothing else." Nothing asks whether a draft's definitions match the agreed rules in brief.md (Population and Local terms), whether a metric's description fits its meaning or the figures shown next to it, or whether something was left out. A real user on any host gets this same reviewer.

Confirmed instances:
(1) In taxi-B, findings.md and the note said "trip time is zero or over three hours". At review time brief.md:16 said "duration of zero or less", and methodology.md said "≤ 0 seconds". The full review (agent-005-record01) did not flag it. Because methodology.md stated the rule correctly, this miss is also partly the reviewer failing to apply the traceability check it does have. Either way the cause is in the product.
(2) The same report flagged "Base fare is the meter's time-and-distance fare" only because it had no reference. It also flagged "JFK trips mostly show the flat fare" as unsupported, and the agent deleted that sentence. The definition then stood unchallenged beside the $70.00 JFK median.
(3) The count-check sentence ("records kept plus the records excluded by each rule equal the records going in") was flagged only for citation form, not for reading as if overlapping rule counts were added.
(4) In co2-B, "shows where the energy mix has moved toward coal" was in the agent-004 draft. The brief defines coal share as coal_co2/co2. The phrase passed both the full review and the scoped review (agent-004-record01/02).
(5) In retail-B, queries/repeat-within-90-days.sql filters on `is_product AND quantity > 0 AND price > 0`. That is narrower than brief.md:62, "earliest non-cancelled invoice". The released note's definition, "first purchase visible in the export", does not mention the narrowing. No review report raises it, and the orchestrator's referee check found January moves from 368 to 383 under the brief's definition.

Where the finding overreaches:
(a) In co2-B, "Counting imports" (headline 5) and "where emissions and coal use are growing" (slide 8) appeared only in the agent-003 headline preview. awb-package/SKILL.md:49 says the preview is a file "which no check reads", and the user corrected both at U4, before any draft existed. Neither phrase is in the agent-004 draft. So the review never saw them and could not have missed them. Only "energy mix" is a review miss.
(b) "The gate accepts any recorded check as support" rests on one case and overstates it. The $70.00 check supported "fare_amount includes flat fares such as JFK's", a definition the user set and brief.md:67 records. The check is reasonable evidence for that sentence. The user's own note (turn 7) says counts at exactly $70 "do not establish rate type" but calls the final definition "suitable".
(c) The retail-B narrowing does appear in the internal methodology.md:19, so it was not wholly undisclosed. It was missing from the note, it was never reconciled with brief.md, and the referee caught it, not the user. "Caught in one read" does not apply to it.
(d) Several evidence IDs do not match the runs' findings.json. retail-B-27 there is the front-loaded-persona finding; the cohort issue is retail-B-24. taxi-B-04 and taxi-B-07 are about other topics. The attached file paths are correct.

Partial harness factor: the Codex persona reads drafts more closely than a typical first-time analyst would, so the claim that a user catches these "in one read" is generous. That affects who catches the errors, not why the review misses them.
verdicts.release_evidence: awb-package/references/review.md, Brief steps 1, 3 and 4 (lines about 20-30, with 26-28 the brief.md and readability items). Step 1 reads brief.md and the glossary. Step 3 lists the only narrative checks, and none compares draft definitions with brief.md's Population or Local terms, checks a metric's meaning against its wording or the figures beside it, or looks for omissions. Its readability item says "only these". Step 4 says "Report exactly this, and nothing else". The source-construction item allows support by "a recorded check" and does not say the check has to establish the claim. Separately, awb-package/SKILL.md:49 says the preview-and-wait headlines file is one "which no check reads", which is why the co2-B preview errors were never in front of the review.
verdicts.narrowed:
The released draft review (review.md Brief, step 3) reads brief.md but has no check that draft definitions match the agreed rules in brief.md, that a metric's description fits its meaning, or that nothing was omitted. So definition and meaning errors that follow the right form pass both the full and the scoped review. Confirmed instances:
- In taxi-B, the trip-time rule was given as "zero or over three hours" against brief.md's "zero or less". Methodology.md stated it correctly, so this was also a missed traceability check.
- In taxi-B, base fare was defined as the meter's time-and-distance fare beside a $70.00 JFK median; the review flagged only the missing reference.
- In taxi-B, the per-rule count-check sentence read as if overlapping counts were added; the review flagged only citation form.
- In co2-B, a rising coal share of CO2 was called a shift in the "energy mix" and passed both drafting reviews.
- In retail-B, the cohort definition was narrowed to product lines with positive quantity and price. That differs from brief.md:62, is stated only in the internal methodology.md, and is missing from the note. No review flagged it; the referee found it.

Drop from the finding:
- the co2-B "counting imports" and "coal use growing" items, which appeared only in the headline preview the review never reads, and which the user corrected before the draft;
- the general claim that the gate accepts any recorded check, which rests on one weak case where the $70.00 check reasonably supported a definition the user had set.

verdicts.reasoning:
The mechanism is real and comes from the release. The reviewer's step 3 in review.md is a closed checklist, and step 4 says to report "exactly this, and nothing else". The list covers traceability between the narratives, claim strength, flag caveats, citations for checked or reconciled claims, brief coverage and source-build references, and a readability list that says "only these". Nothing in it compares the narratives' definitions and exclusion rules with the definitions agreed in the brief, asks whether a phrase correctly names what a metric measures, or looks for omitted cases. The source-build bullet (line 27) is satisfied by any `reference:` or "recorded check" that methodology.md cites. Unlike bullet 4, it does not require that the check establishes the claim or covers all of it.

taxi-B confirms the problem. After a full review (agent-005-record01) and a scoped one (record02), the human's msg 6 caught three issues in one read:
- **Trip-time rule.** The findings and note said "trip time is zero or over three hours". methodology.md said `bad_duration` (≤ 0 or > 3 hours), and brief.md line 16 says "zero or less".
- **Base fare.** It was called "the meter's time-and-distance fare" next to the $70.00 JFK median. The review flagged it only for lacking a reference. The agent then cited TLC's data dictionary and the sentence passed.
- **Count-check sentence.** It reads as adding overlapping rule counts, and the review flagged it only for citation form.

After the user's flat-fare correction, the agent added the statement that at least half of JFK trips show exactly $70.00 to the `metrics` judgment detail in settings.toml and reran. The scoped review agent-006-record02 then reported clean, so a self-authored judgment detail served as the "recorded check".

co2-B shows the same gap once. "A rising coal share ... shows where the energy mix has moved toward coal" was in the draft at findings.md:116. It passed the full review (agent-004-record01) and the scoped one (record02), and the user caught it in U5.

Parts of the finding do not hold:
1. **co2-B, two items.** "Counting imports" (slide 5) and the "emissions and coal use are growing" implication (slide 8) appeared only in the A3 headline preview (agent-003.out.md). The user corrected both in U4, before any draft existed and before any review ran. The review cannot have missed them.
2. **retail-B.** The user never caught the narrower purchase definition. The referee and orchestrator found it and rated it minor. methodology.md:19 does state the narrowing (a product line of positive quantity and price). Only the note (lines 19-20) and findings.md drop it, while brief.md line 62 still has the broader rule. The note dropping a qualification that methodology.md carries is something the existing bullet 1 already covers ("the same qualifications and caveats"; the note "states nothing methodology.md does not support"). That part is a reviewer miss within existing instructions. The missing comparison with the brief's definitions is the release's share.
3. **taxi-B trip-time rule.** Bullet 1 also covered the "zero" versus "≤ 0" mismatch, so this was partly the reviewer failing to apply an instruction it already had.

Nothing in the harness causes these misses. A real user on any host would get the same closed checklist. Note that the closed scope is deliberate (CHANGELOG lines 146 and 149, aimed at making the review converge), and the release relies on the user's read plus confirmed review rules (review.md:45) for meaning errors. That tradeoff argues for a severity below major.
verdicts.release_evidence:
- **awb-package/references/review.md:22-28**: step 3 is a closed list of checks, with no item comparing definitions or exclusion rules with brief.md, no item checking what a metric's wording means, and no omissions check.
- **review.md:28**: "readability, only these", a closed list.
- **review.md:29**: "Report exactly this, and nothing else".
- **review.md:27**: a source-build sentence passes if it "rests on a `reference:` ... or on a recorded check", with no requirement that the check establishes the claim. Compare line 26, which requires the cited check to establish everything a checked sentence asserts and excludes judgment-detail tolerances.
- **review.md:23**: the existing bullet 1 requirement for the same qualifications across narratives and nothing in the note beyond what methodology.md supports. This covers part of the retail-B and taxi-B trip-time items.
- **awb-package/assets/package-format/methodology-template.md:17**: asks only to explain departures from the shared glossary, not from the brief's agreed definitions.
- **CHANGELOG.md:149 and :146**: confirm the review's brief checks are limited to question coverage and source-build references, and that the scope was kept closed so the review converges.

Run evidence:
- taxi-B: review-reports/agent-005-record01.txt, agent-005-record02.txt, agent-006-record01.txt, agent-006-record02.txt; relay/human-006.out.md; brief.md line 16; agent-006.jsonl, which shows the settings.toml `metrics` detail edit followed by a rerun.
- co2-B: review-reports/agent-004-record01.txt and record02.txt; the "energy mix" passage at findings.md:116 in agent-004.jsonl; agent-003.out.md lines 89-95, where "counting imports" and "coal use are growing" appear in the preview only; human-004.out.md.
- retail-B: queries/repeat-within-90-days.sql line 9; brief.md line 62; released/001/methodology.md:19, which discloses the narrowing; methodology-note.md:19-20, which omits it; orchestrator-report.md:41 and :87, which rate it minor.

consolidated.title: No audience-appropriate defaults for displaying numbers: precision, clock format, rounding notes
consolidated.description: When the user records no precision, drafts default to full saved precision and 24-hour times. co2-A's donor deck showed 8,645.2 Mt, 23.57% shares and per-person figures to two decimals, and the user spent a whole correction round (6.7 min) on rounding. taxi-A's board deck used 18:00 until the user made 12-hour times a standing rule. co2-B's tables showed start, end and change values that do not subtract exactly after rounding (Ukraine 286 to 142 shown as -143), with no note. The user had to ask for the note and then made it a review rule.
consolidated.caused_by_fix: no. #101 added a precision line to the brief's Audience section and a review check against it. Both apply only when the user states a precision: nothing sets a default for an audience described as non-technical, and the headline checkpoint does not ask.
consolidated.evidence: co2-A-01: r6 draft, m7, r7 (6.7 min turn); feedback/human.md pain point 1; awb-package/SKILL.md line 30 and step 4.2; review.md:28 checks decimals only against a stated precision. taxi-A-08: reply 7 draft, msg 8 item 2; '00:00' in results/q1-volume.csv; awb-package/assets/package-format/ has no time-format guidance. co2-B-36: A3 Q1 and Q5 tables; U4; R-rounding-001 at methodology.md:123 in relay/agent-005.jsonl.

verdicts.reasoning:
I looked for a harness cause and found none. None of the listed mechanisms touches how numbers are formatted.
- Non-interactive exec, the sandbox, auto-approved MCP, the simulated home and the relay play no part in it.
- The study note appended to the agent prompt only asks for a friction log.
- The personas did not front-load precision or time format. co2-A's brief says only "semi-technical donors, no jargon" and taxi-A's says "board is not technical". Front-loading would have hidden the problem, not caused it.
- Codex is a host the release names (README line 5), so Codex agent behaviour is what a real Codex user gets.

The release is the enabling cause:
- awb-package/SKILL.md:30 and the brief.md template record a precision only "when the user states them". Nothing asks for one; the agent asks about Audience only when it is missing, and here it was given in the first message.
- review.md:28 flags decimals only against a precision the brief states.
- The export [round] stub says to use "the places the slide's number format shows", which leaves the choice to the agent.
- package-format has no guidance on clock format or on noting rounding mismatches.

Each symptom is real in its run:
- co2-A (Codex agent): the agent wrote display.toml with change_mt=1, per-person=2 and share=2 decimals. The r6 draft showed 8,645.2 Mt and 23.57%. In m7 the user asked for rounding, and r7 ran 11:49:04 to 11:55:47 (6.7 min). The numbers check also rejected the agent's own rounded "1,844.55 billion" and pushed it back to Mt.
- taxi-A (Codex agent): its producer wrote 24-hour labels ("00:00" in q1-volume.csv), which carried through to 18:00 in the draft. The user asked for 12-hour times and made it a standing rule.
- co2-B (Claude agent): the A3 chat table shows Ukraine 286 to 142 as −143 (also France, Czechia and Greece). The user asked for a "calculated before rounding" note, and the agent then offered R-rounding-001.

Overstatements to correct:
1. "Full saved precision" is wrong. export refuses more than 4 unrounded decimals, and the co2-A agent chose 1 to 2 places itself.
2. The symptoms depend on the model. In taxi-B, the Claude agent under the same release defaulted to "6 pm" / "5 am". In co2-B, Claude wrote whole Mt on the slides and its Codex human did not object to 2-decimal per-person figures.
3. Each sub-issue appeared once, in 3 of 6 runs. In taxi-A the time format was one of three items in a correction round. In co2-B the note was one sentence, and the mismatch was in a chat table, not an uncorrected draft.
4. "Major" fits only co2-A's precision round.
verdicts.release_evidence:
- awb-package/SKILL.md:30: precision is recorded only as something "the user states"; nothing prompts for it.
- awb-init/assets/workbench/investigation/brief.md, Audience: "Record also, when the user states them, the precision numbers need".
- awb-package/references/review.md:28: decimals are flagged only against a precision the brief's Audience states.
- awb-package/SKILL.md step 4.2 and helpers.md:51: the [round] stub is filled with "the places the slide's number format shows", the agent's choice, and is required only above 4 decimals.
- grep across awb-package/assets/package-format/ (findings-template.md, deck-rules.md) finds no clock-format or rounding-note guidance. deck-rules.md:61 says only to match the slide's decimals.
- co2-A foundation/display.toml [round]: change_mt=1, territorial/consumption_t_per_person=2, world_share_percent=2.
- co2-A relay/agent-006.jsonl draft: "8,645.2 Mt", "23.57%". check-draft rejected "1,844.55 billion".
- taxi-A results/q1-volume.csv label "00:00", and draft table cells "08:00 | 28.21% | 18:00".
- Counter-evidence: taxi-B (Claude agent) findings.md:42,126 uses "6 pm" / "5 am" by default.
verdicts.narrowed:
The release has no display-format defaults tied to the audience, and it never asks about display precision or clock format. A precision is recorded and reviewed only if the user volunteers it, and nothing covers noting that rounded start, end and change values may not subtract. So number formatting is left to the host model's taste.

With Codex as the agent, that produced:
- donor-deck figures at 1 to 2 decimals (8,645.2 Mt, 23.57%), which the agent chose itself; this is not "full saved precision";
- 24-hour times for a non-technical US board.

Each cost the user a correction: a full round in co2-A, and one item of three in taxi-A. In co2-B the user had to ask once for a "calculated before rounding" note. A Claude agent under the same release defaulted to 12-hour times (taxi-B), so the time-format symptom depends on the model. The release's gap is that it neither guides nor asks. Severity is moderate, not uniformly major.

verdicts.reasoning:
The release never asks for a display precision and gives no default. In the brief template (awb-init/assets/workbench/investigation/brief.md:19) and in awb-package/SKILL.md:30, precision is recorded only "when the user states" it. Step 1 asks who the audience is but never asks how precise the numbers should be. The headline checkpoint doesn't ask either.

The reviewer's readability check (review.md:28) flags extra decimals only against a precision stated in the brief's Audience section, so with none stated, nothing catches them.

When export finds a column with more than four decimals, its round_stub tells the agent to use "the places the slide's number format shows", and nothing says what that should be for a lay audience. The findings template (line 15) leaves each number "exactly as the slide should show it", which is the agent's call. No file in the release mentions clock format. Nothing says to note that rounded start and end values may not subtract exactly to the rounded change: methodology_lines state the rounding only in the internal methodology.md.

The runs confirm all three cited cases:
- **co2-A:** the turn-6 draft (read back at the start of turn 7) has "8,645.2 million tonnes", "US 23.57%" and "14.32 tonnes". chart-3 was rounded to 2 places. User message 7, item 1, is a rounding correction. Turn 7 took about 402 s.
- **taxi-A:** the turn-7 draft has "Both months peak at 18:00" and "25.63% at 08:00" for a non-technical board. The agent's own result file q1-volume.csv labels hours "00:00". User message 8, item 2, asks for 12-hour times and makes them a rule (R-time-format-001).
- **co2-B:** reply 3's Q1 table shows Ukraine 286 to 142 as −143. User message 4 asks for the note, and R-rounding-001 was later confirmed as a rule.

Where the finding overstates:
- "Full saved precision" is wrong. Export refuses any column showing more than four decimals unless it is rounded. The agents chose 1–2 decimals.
- Clock format is not caused by the release. The 24-hour labels came from the agent's own query. taxi-B (a Claude agent, same release and audience) wrote "5 am" and "6 pm" without being told. So that part is agent judgment the release could steer but doesn't drive.
- The rounding note cost co2-B one sentence inside a longer edit message.
- Only co2-A spent a real correction round. That turn also removed stray headline periods and edited the methods note. Part of its 6.7 minutes went to the agent recording a new result (territorial-change-tonnes) so the "billion tonnes" wording would trace, rather than to rounding as such.
- co2-B's draft also kept per-person figures at two decimals, and its user did not object.

Overall, the precision default is a genuine release gap a real user would hit, at least with the Codex agent. Treating the other two parts as major or as release-caused is weaker.
verdicts.release_evidence:
- awb-init/assets/workbench/investigation/brief.md:19: "Record also, when the user states them, the precision numbers need (such as whole percents)". Precision is never asked or defaulted.
- awb-package/SKILL.md:30: step 1 asks for the audience. It records a precision only as something "the user states", and never asks about display precision.
- awb-package/references/review.md:28: the readability check covers only "a number shown with more decimal places than a precision the brief's Audience states". With no stated precision there is no check.
- awb-package/SKILL.md:70 and references/helpers.md:51: round_stub asks for "the places the slide's number format shows", with no default for the audience.
- assets/package-format/findings-template.md:15: "number written exactly as the slide should show it", which leaves the precision choice to the agent.
- assets/package-format/ (findings-template, deck-rules, methodology templates): no clock-format guidance, and no guidance to say that changes are computed before rounding. methodology_lines (helpers.md:53) state the rounding only in the internal methodology.md.
- Nothing in the release pushes toward 24-hour times. The numbers check (awb_draft.py:1406-1408) skips both "18:00" and "6:00 pm" as non-quantities.
verdicts.narrowed: The release neither asks for nor defaults a display precision. The brief and SKILL.md record precision only when the user volunteers it, and the reviewer checks decimals only against a stated precision. So with no stated precision, lay-audience drafts can carry 1–2-decimal figures (co2-A: 8,645.2 Mt, 23.57%, 14.32 t per person) and need a user correction round. "Full saved precision" overstates it, because export forces rounding beyond four decimals. Clock format and notes on rounded values that don't subtract exactly also lack guidance, but those cases are agent-dependent and cheap: taxi-B's agent used 12-hour times unprompted, and co2-B's note took one sentence. They are missing defaults, not release-caused defects. Severity is closer to moderate than major.

consolidated.title: Rescaled, approximate or derived figures each cost a new recorded result
consolidated.description: The numbers check traces only recorded values, a per-column [scale], or configured rounding. co2-A recorded a display-only analytical result (territorial-change-tonnes, 7 validations) just to write 'about 8.6 billion tonnes' beside a chart kept in Mt. It deleted a '1,844.55 billion tonnes' denominator for the same reason, and recorded historical-combined to state the US plus EU-27 share (39.8%). co2-B recorded q1-full-ranking, filed under Q-001's wording, to ship full ranking datasets. retail-A wrote '22,523' where the user asked for 'about 22,500', and '£77,183.60' in a caveat, to avoid display configuration.
consolidated.caused_by_fix: no. #100 added display.toml [scale], but it applies per column, so a chart and a sentence cannot show the same column in different units.
consolidated.evidence: co2-A-02: agent-007 log (producer territorial-change-tonnes.py, awb/run, state finding); agent-006 methodology.md edit removing '1,844.55 billion tonnes'; awb-package/references/helpers.md line 50; SKILL.md step 6.2. co2-A-20: agent-006 producer historical-combined.py; SKILL.md step 6 rule 4. co2-B-17: U3, A3; questions.md (Q-001 has two results). retail-A-36: msg 8, reply 8; release 001 findings.md slide 5 caveat.

verdicts.reasoning:
I could not trace the core mechanism to the harness.

1. Personas did not script the requests. kit/personas/co2.md and retail.md never mention "about 8.6 billion tonnes", "39.8%/nearly 40%" or "about 22,500". The simulated humans asked for them on their own, as a donor-facing research lead or a commercial lead would. In co2-A msg 7 the user wanted chart 1 in whole million tonnes but the Answer bullet in "about 8.6 billion tonnes". In msg 6 the user asked for a "nearly 40%" headline because "their shares add to 39.8%". In retail-A msg 8 the user offered "about 22,500 lines" as an example.

2. The release itself blocks these figures:
   - **Unit change:** SKILL.md step 6 rule 2 allows a unit change only through a `[scale]` divisor. helpers.md line 50 makes `[scale]` global per column (`[results."<id>"]` tables hold only columns/values/percent), and it rescales the chart file too. So "billion tonnes" in text cannot sit beside a chart kept in Mt.
   - **Coarse rounding:** `[round]` takes only 0–20 places, and rule 2 says to rewrite from the recorded value. So "about 22,500" for 22,523 cannot trace.
   - **Sums:** rule 4 says a number computed from results that none records needs separately authorized analysis, or is left out. That covers the US+EU-27 combined share.
   - **allowed_numbers:** rule 3's escape is ambiguous for quantities, and rule 1 warns it never stands in for a result. The agent explicitly declined it as a bypass.

3. The agents' own logs name the checker as the reason:
   - co2-A agent-007 friction log: the checker "does not infer million-tonne-to-tonne dimensions". The agent recorded territorial-change-tonnes "so the billion-tonne Answer labels trace", calling it "substantial provenance overhead for a cosmetic unit change".
   - co2-A agent-006: check-draft flagged "1,844.55 billion" as untraced, and the agent deleted it.
   - co2-A agent-006 also recorded historical-combined, before any check ran, so the rule 4 sum would have provenance.
   - retail-A agent.md: "used exact 22,523 ... avoiding a new rounding allowance".

4. Harness factors don't change the outcome:
   - **Harness note:** it says "work exactly as you normally would" plus a private friction log. It could make the agent more literal at most; that is speculative.
   - **Non-interactive codex exec:** the agent could have ended its turn with a question through the relay, exactly as on an interactive host. And the user had asked for checks to pass before seeing slides.
   - **Auto-approved MCP:** on a real host this would add an approval prompt for awb/run. It would not remove the pressure to record a result.

Parts of the finding as written are overstated or misfiled:
   - **£77,183.60:** this does not show avoidance. The figure was already written as GBP 77,183.60 in the analysis-stage answers.md. "£77,184" would also trace, since the check accepts any half-up rounding of a recorded value at 0+ decimals. I found no log evidence tying it to display configuration.
   - **co2-B q1-full-ranking:** this is not a rescaled, approximate or derived figure. It is a new 215-row table. The agent's original Q1 result held only 20 rows, a design choice the agent made itself, so a new result was needed. The agent's complaint was about packaging authorization and reusing Q-001's wording, not number tracing. co2-B's actual instance of C-08 is a different one: agent-004 removed the "larger than the ten decreases combined" bullet because no result records that sum.
   - **"Each cost a new recorded result":** only co2-A recorded new results for this reason (two). retail-A rewrote the figure to recorded precision, and co2-B deleted the derived figure.
   - **Severity:** no user in these runs saw a failure. The cost was agent time, extra records, and a display-only "finding" added to state.md. That makes "major" debatable.
verdicts.release_evidence:
- awb-package/SKILL.md step 6 (lines 85-90): rule 1 says "allowed_numbers never stands in for representing a result". Rule 2 says to rewrite to the recorded value or precision, with a unit change tracing only "once that column has a [scale] divisor ... and export reruns". Rule 4 says "computed from results that none records: only separately authorized analysis records it; until then, leave it out."
- awb-package/references/helpers.md line 50: display.toml `[scale]` is per column. `[results."<result>"]` tables hold only `columns`, `values` and `percent`. Scaled cells are written into the chart file, so text and chart cannot use different units. `[round]` accepts 0–20 places only.
- helpers.md line 44 (Tracing): a number written to d places traces to a value that rounds half up to it, or to a value scaled by k/M/bn/million. So 8645.2 (Mt) cannot trace "8.6 billion", and 22,523 cannot trace "22,500".
- co2-A/relay/agent-007.jsonl: territorial-change-tonnes producer, awb/run, state finding "support donor wording of about 8.6 billion tonnes". Its friction log blames the checker.
- co2-A/relay/agent-006.jsonl: check-draft numbers rows for "1,844.55 billion", then the methodology.md edit deleting it. It also shows historical-combined recorded to support 39.8%.
- retail-A/feedback/agent.md line 27 and agent-notes.md line 125: 22,523 used instead of 22,500 to avoid a rounding allowance.
- kit/personas/co2.md and retail.md: no scripted rounding requests.

verdicts.reasoning:
The release causes the main mechanism, which I checked in both the code and the docs. In awb_draft.py, `_untraced` traces a number only to values inside its written decimal-place window. The window can also be scaled by %, k, thousand, million or billion. Nothing handles approximations ("about", "nearly"), and "22,500" traces only to the range [22,499.5, 22,500.5).

Unit conversion is allowed only through `[scale]`, and two things block using it beside an unchanged chart:
- It is global per column. `[results.<id>]` accepts only columns, values and percent.
- `export` also divides the chart file's cells by it, and check-draft requires each chart entry's scale to equal display.toml's (draft.py around line 2456).

So a sentence in billion tonnes cannot sit beside a chart the user wants kept in Mt. SKILL.md step 6 then leaves three options. Rule 2: change the column's unit, or rewrite the number from the recorded value. Rule 4: a computed number needs "separately authorized analysis"; until then, leave it out. Rule 1 adds that "allowed_numbers never stands in for representing a result". The co2-A agent read these rules correctly.

Run evidence, instance by instance:
- **co2-A, agent-007 (holds).** The user asked for "about 8.6 billion tonnes" with chart 1 kept in whole Mt. The agent wrote the producer territorial-change-tonnes.py, which only multiplies by 1,000,000. Its evidence has 7 checks, and the agent also recorded a state finding. Its notes say it did this to avoid using allowed_numbers on a computed value.
- **co2-A, agent-006, '1,844.55 billion' (holds).** check-draft flagged it in findings.md line 88 and methodology.md line 89 ("no represented result records this number at its written precision"), and the agent deleted the conversion. This is real, but the cost was small: the Mt figure stayed.
- **co2-A, historical-combined (holds, but as intended design).** It is real and caused by rule 4, but I would not call it a defect. The recorded sum is 39.8356 → 39.8%, while the rounded shares on the slide (23.6 + 16.3) add to 39.9. Recording the sum kept the stated total correct, and the agent itself called this step "defensible".
- **co2-B-17 (not an instance).** The Q1 result held only the top and bottom 20 rows, so the full ranking datasets needed rows that were never recorded. That is new data, not a rescaled, rounded or derived figure. The awkward reuse of Q-001's wording is a separate minor issue.
- **retail-A (weak).** The user offered "about 22,500" as example wording. The agent wrote 22,523 because of rule 2, and the user replied "The changes look right". "£77,183.60" is the exact recorded value 77183.6, and nobody asked for it to be rounded. The documented scale rule would have traced "about 22.5 thousand" and "£77.2k", so the release does offer an approximate form. It just never suggests one.

A real user on an interactive host who asks for a rescaled or rounded figure beside an unchanged chart would hit this. I'd rate it moderate rather than major: the users got their wording or accepted the exact one, and the cost was agent time plus a cluttered results ledger.
verdicts.release_evidence:
- **awb-package/SKILL.md step 6, numbers repair rules:**
  - Rule 1: "`allowed_numbers` never stands in for representing a result."
  - Rule 2: "A represented result records it at another value or precision: rewrite it from the recorded value. In another unit than its chart or dataset column, such as gigatonnes for megatonnes, it traces once that column has a `[scale]` divisor in `foundation/display.toml` and `export` reruns."
  - Rule 3 limits allowed_numbers to non-quantities, or to numbers the records support elsewhere.
  - Rule 4: "It is computed from results that none records: only separately authorized analysis records it; until then, leave it out."
- **awb-package/references/helpers.md:**
  - Line 42, Tracing: a number traces only within half a unit of its last written decimal place, optionally scaled by %, k, million or billion.
  - Line 50: display.toml holds `[scale]` as a global per-column divisor. `[results."<result>"]` tables hold only columns, values and percent, and any other key is an error. Export divides a `[scale]` column's cells, so the chart file shows the scaled unit.
- **awb-package/assets/awb_draft.py:**
  - `_untraced` (around line 1687): decimal-place windows plus `_SCALES`, with no handling of approximate wording. A grep finds "about" only in the methods-note length parser.
  - `recorded_scales` and `recorded_values` (lines 1589–1648): scaled values are added only for columns a chart or dataset entry records with a scale.
  - Around line 2456: a chart entry's scale must equal display.toml's global `[scale]`.
- **awb-package/assets/package-format/findings-template.md line 7:** shows "about 3% of volume", which works only because whole-percent rounding is a decimal-place window.
verdicts.narrowed: The numbers check cannot trace a unit-converted figure while its chart column stays in the recorded unit. `[scale]` is global per column, rescales the chart file itself, and check-draft requires the chart entry's scale to match it. The check also cannot trace a whole-number approximation such as "about 22,500" (it traces by decimal places only), or a sum of recorded values. SKILL.md step 6 rules 1, 2 and 4 then direct the agent to change the chart's unit, rewrite the number to the exact recorded value, or leave it out pending separately authorized analysis; allowed_numbers is ruled out. The clear instance is co2-A. It recorded a unit-only result (territorial-change-tonnes, 7 checks, plus a state finding) for the user-requested "about 8.6 billion tonnes" beside a chart kept in Mt, and it dropped a "1,844.55 billion tonnes" conversion that check-draft flagged. The historical-combined sum is the release's intended provenance design, and it kept the stated 39.8% consistent where the rounded shares (23.6 + 16.3) give 39.9. co2-B-17 is not an instance, because full rankings needed rows no result recorded. retail-A is minor: the user's example "about 22,500" became 22,523 and the user accepted it, and the documented scale-word form ("22.5 thousand", "£77.2k") would have traced. Suggested severity: moderate rather than major.

consolidated.title: First answers leave source codes undefined or misdescribed
consolidated.description: First-pass answers named source codes without defining them, and did not separate out the populations those codes dominate. taxi-A led its tipping answer with 0% medians for the Bronx and Brooklyn and blamed 'rate-code 99' without saying it means null or unknown. It did not offer the standard-rate population, though it had read the TLC dictionary in reply 1. taxi-B called an explicit payment_type 0 (419,151 records, none null) 'no payment type' and missing data, and later 'a Flex Fare trip'. Its ledger still says 'no recorded payment type'. Both agents' own profiling had already shown the codes.
consolidated.oct16_ref: new (related: Oct 16 taxi-B-04 rate-code-99 handling under C-14; C-90 rejected)
consolidated.caused_by_fix: no
consolidated.evidence: taxi-A-02: reply 4 Q3 table, msg 5, reply 5 (code 99 = Null/unknown; standard-rate medians); feedback/human.md section 2 item 2. taxi-B-03: reply 1 ('About 419,000 trips (7%) have no payment type'), replies 2-3, msg 4; the turn-1 peek in relay/agent-001.jsonl grouped by payment_type; the referee's spot-check found 0 nulls; questions.md Q-009.

verdicts.reasoning:
The finding is two cases joined together. The taxi-A case holds as a product issue. The taxi-B case is mostly a harness artifact.

taxi-A (Codex agent): no harness factor explains it.
- Turn 1: the agent opened the TLC dictionary PDF through Codex's web reader (agent-001.jsonl, web_search open of data_dictionary_trip_records_yellow.pdf). It wrote glossary entries for RatecodeID and "standard rate" from it.
- Codex ran with no rule limiting it to user-given URLs. In turn 5 it searched the web freely, with the query "RatecodeID 99 null unknown". The curl download failed with a 403 from nyc.gov, which a real user would also get.
- Turn 4: the agent's own result printout (agent-004.jsonl) already split tips by borough and rate code: Bronx code 1 median 15.06%, Brooklyn code 1 23.36%, code 99 all zero. Its friction log says "Rate-code 99 contributes thousands of all-zero recorded tips, whereas standard-rate strata differ greatly".
- It still led with 0% for Bronx and Brooklyn, named "rate-code 99" without defining it, and did not show the standard-rate figures.
- This is the agent's own presentation choice. Non-interactive exec, auto-approved MCP, the simulated home, the relay and the study note do not explain it. The persona listing a few codes up front does not either.

Release contribution (verified):
- awb-clean's scanner treats RatecodeID as an ID column. Its KEY_NAME regex `[a-z0-9]Id$` runs case-insensitive, so it matches "RatecodeID", and the scanner then skips the positive-sentinel and extreme checks for that column.
- Code 99 sits far above the other codes (max 6), so it meets the sentinel rule in checks.md, a "placeholder meaning missing".
- taxi-A's foundation/scans/yellow-trips.json has no RatecodeID sentinel issue. Code 99 therefore never reached the turn-3 cleaning signoff, where the user would have seen it before any tipping answer.
- AGENTS.md says "chat uses plain words", but the rule is about workbench terms. Nothing in the release tells the agent to define a source code the first time it cites one, or to offer the population without a dominant unknown code.

taxi-B (Claude agent): harness.
- The kit's claude-agent-system.md lets the agent read only "URLs the user gives you". The persona gave no dictionary URL.
- The agent's friction log says "sim boundary allows only user-given URLs, so I must ask the user to OK the TLC dictionary URL". In reply 2 it asked permission.
- So "no payment type" in replies 1–2 was a guess made without the dictionary, based on the co-occurring null fields.
- Once allowed in turn 3, it corrected itself straight away: "These aren't missing data: the dictionary defines code 0 as a Flex Fare trip".
- "Flex Fare" is the dictionary's actual definition, not a misdescription. In reply 4 the agent confirmed the values are explicit 0, never null, and noted that the dictionary postdates the data and does not explain the nulls. That is correct behaviour.
- Only the ledger question text for Q-009, written in turn 2 under the URL limit, keeps "no recorded payment type". That is minor, stale wording.
- Also, the release's checks.md already says 0 is not a placeholder candidate, so the release did not push the agent toward this reading.
verdicts.release_evidence:
- **Scanner:** release/analytics-workbench-skills/awb-clean/scripts/scan_dataset.py:65 has `KEY_NAME = re.compile(r"(^|_)(id|key|uuid|guid)$|[a-z0-9]Id$", re.I)`. It matches "RatecodeID", and the positive-sentinel check at line 477 skips key-like names. Line 492 does the same for extremes.
- **Rule the scanner misses:** awb-clean/references/checks.md:15 defines `sentinel` as numbers "that sit outside every other value", which code 99 is.
- **Scan output:** taxi-A/project/foundation/scans/yellow-trips.json lists RatecodeID (7 distinct values) but has no sentinel issue for it.
- **Chat guidance:** awb-init/assets/workbench/AGENTS.md "Conversation" covers plain words only for workbench terms. It has no rule to define source codes or separate populations dominated by an unknown code.
- **Agent had the data:** taxi-A relay/agent-004.jsonl result printout shows standard-rate (code 1) medians next to code-99 zeros, and reply 4 left them out.
- **Harness evidence for taxi-B:** kit/claude-agent-system.md says "URLs the user gives you". taxi-B feedback/agent-notes.md:16 records the URL limit. taxi-B quality.md DQ-002 records the correction.
verdicts.narrowed: taxi-A only: the Codex agent had read the TLC dictionary in turn 1 and had the rate-code breakdown in hand. It still led its first tipping answer with 0% Bronx/Brooklyn medians, blamed an undefined "rate-code 99", and held back the standard-rate medians it had already computed. The user needed an extra round to get them. Two release gaps contribute. First, awb-clean's scanner treats RatecodeID as an ID column (the case-insensitive `[a-z0-9]Id$` regex), so code 99 was never flagged as a placeholder at the cleaning signoff. Second, the release does not tell the agent to define a source code when it first cites one. The taxi-B payment_type-0 part comes from the harness: the sim boundary limited the agent to URLs the user gave, so it could not read the dictionary until turn 3, and it corrected itself as soon as it could. Severity is closer to moderate, since one follow-up fixed it.

verdicts.reasoning:
The taxi-A evidence holds up. Reply 4's Q3 table leads with 0% medians for Brooklyn and the Bronx and blames "rate-code 99" without defining it. It mentions that "standard-rate records show different patterns" but gives no figures and does not offer that subset as a decision. In turn 1 the agent had opened the TLC dictionary through the web reader (the curl download got a 403). The text "99 = Null/unknown" first appears in its logs in turn 5, after the user asked. Data check: RatecodeID holds 1-6 plus 99 (71,004 rows) plus 419,151 nulls.

The release contributes in two concrete ways.
(1) Helper code. awb-clean/scripts/scan_dataset.py tests column names with KEY_NAME = `(^|_)(id|key|uuid|guid)$|[a-z0-9]Id$` under re.I, so any name ending in "ID" counts as a key. The numeric-sentinel check (line 477, `not KEY_NAME.search(name)`) and the extreme check then skip that column. RatecodeID was in the scanned columns (foundation/scans/yellow-trips.json options), and 99 is more than twice the largest other value (6). Under any non-key name it would have been raised as `sentinel:RatecodeID:99`. The awb-clean skill and the README (line 67: "you decide ... when cleaning, what a placeholder means") would then have put the code's meaning to the user at the reply-3 cleaning signoff, before any answers. Because of the name test, the scan reported only S1-S6, none of them about RatecodeID.
(2) Missing rule. AGENTS.md **Conversation** tells chat to use plain words, but only for record terms (ledger, finding, flagged, disposition). Nothing says to name a coded value by its meaning in chat. That translation rule exists only for package drafts: findings-template.md ("a coded value by its display name"), methodology-note-template.md, and the readability rules in review.md. First-pass chat answers therefore have no guard.

Some release text pushes the other way, but none of it is a clear rule the agent kept ignoring. analysis.md requires metrics and values judgments ("column meanings", "distinct values that drive business interpretation"). awb-scope asks for population terms to be tested against the data. AGENTS.md says to ask for a plain decision with a recommendation and an alternative. Not offering the standard-rate subset in taxi-A is agent behaviour that the release's ask-for-a-decision rule would have covered.

The taxi-B half does not support the finding as written. The turn-1 peek grouped by payment_type and showed code 0 with 419,151 rows, and those were explicit zeros: my count found 0 nulls. Calling them "no payment type" in replies 1-2 was the agent's misreading. It came from a peek at the inbox files before landing, which the data guide's "inspect records only from landed copies" discourages, and before the agent could read the dictionary (it asked permission for the URL, which the run tagged as a harness issue in taxi-B-21). No release text causes it, and checks.md correctly treats 0 as not a placeholder. Reply 3, the first-answers reply, corrected it: "These aren't missing data: the dictionary defines code 0 as a Flex Fare trip". In that reply the agent also noted the dictionary postdates the data, called code 99 an "unknown" rate code, and separated the code-99 population. That last step goes further than the finding implies; taxi-B-02 is the opposite complaint, a post-hoc exclusion. Ledger Q-009's "no recorded payment type (payment_type 0)" names the code in brackets. Quality row DQ-002 describes it correctly.
verdicts.release_evidence:
awb-clean/scripts/scan_dataset.py line 51: NUMERIC_SENTINELS includes 99. Line 65: KEY_NAME = re.compile(r"(^|_)(id|key|uuid|guid)$|[a-z0-9]Id$", re.I), which matches RatecodeID, VendorID and PULocationID. Line 477: the sentinel check runs only when `not KEY_NAME.search(name)`.
awb-clean/references/checks.md line 15: the sentinel check covers numbers such as 999 outside every other value and says "0 is not a placeholder candidate"; line 23 says extreme is "not checked for key-like columns".
awb-clean/SKILL.md, Decide: the user decides "what a placeholder stands for (missing, zero, or real)".
README.md line 67: "when cleaning, what a placeholder means" is the user's decision.
awb-init/assets/workbench/AGENTS.md, Conversation section: plain-words rule limited to record terms; no rule to define a coded value in chat.
awb-package/assets/package-format/findings-template.md line 7 and methodology-note-template.md line 7: "a coded value by its display name", for drafts only. awb-package/references/review.md line 28: readability checks on glossary terms, drafts only.
Run evidence: taxi-A/foundation/scans/yellow-trips.json scanned RatecodeID and reported only S1-S6. A read-only count of the inbox parquet gives RatecodeID {1..6, 99: 71,004, null: 419,151} and payment_type 0: 419,151 with 0 nulls.
verdicts.narrowed: This holds for taxi-A only. Its first tipping answer (reply 4) led with 0% Bronx and Brooklyn medians and cited rate code 99 without defining it, though the agent had opened the TLC dictionary in turn 1. The release contributes in two ways. First, awb-clean's scan_dataset.py treats any column whose name ends in "ID" as a key and skips its placeholder (sentinel) check. RatecodeID 99, 71,004 rows against other values of 1-6, was therefore never raised for the user to define at the cleaning signoff the README promises. Second, AGENTS.md has no chat rule to name a coded value by its meaning; that rule exists only for package drafts. Not offering the standard-rate subset was the agent's own omission. The taxi-B part (explicit payment_type 0 called "no payment type") came from a pre-landing peek before the dictionary was read, was corrected in its first-answers reply, and is not release-caused.

consolidated.title: Missing early years described as zero, and a scenario called a ceiling
consolidated.description: co2-B's first answers said China's and India's missing early years 'count as zero' in the cumulative shares, and the agent wrote that wording into foundation/quality.md. Its fix then called an assumption-based sensitivity calculation a 'ceiling' ('at most 15.51%'). The agent did count each entity's years and caveat the short counts, as the guide now asks. Nothing tells it to describe missing periods as unreported, or forbids calling a scenario a bound. This is the third co2-B run in a row with this class of error.
consolidated.caused_by_fix: no
consolidated.evidence: co2-B-01: transcript A2 ('Earlier years count as zero in the cumulative totals'), U3, A3 ('I also calculated a ceiling ... at most 15.51%'), U4; the edit to foundation/quality.md in relay/agent-003.jsonl; first years counted as 1907 and 1858. Release: awb-init/assets/workbench/workbench-guides/analysis.md (the per-entity coverage count and caveat added by #97).

verdicts.release_evidence:
awb-init/assets/workbench/workbench-guides/analysis.md:15 says: "For a series summed over a period, also count the periods each entity in scope has data for, since a sum hides missing periods: a count below the period length is a caveat on the finding."

It sets no wording for that caveat. A grep of the whole release for "as zero|not zero|unreported|not reported|upper bound|lower bound|ceiling|bound|sensitivity|scenario" finds no guidance on describing missing periods or labelling assumption-based scenarios. The only hits are chart-axis, tolerance and datasets.toml range-check text.

The package review's claim-strength checks (awb-package/references/package-contract.md:50, helpers.md:41) cover causal phrasing in slides. They do not cover bound or scenario language, and they do not cover chat or foundation records, where these errors appeared.
verdicts.narrowed:
In co2-B the agent followed #97's per-entity coverage rule (118 and 156 of 175 years for China and India) and caveated the short counts. It produced two problems on its own; neither the harness nor the persona prompted them:
- **Turn 2.** It worded the caveat as "missing earlier years count as zero" in chat, the finding caveat, settings.toml, state issues and quality.md DQ-004. This accurately describes the SUM arithmetic and was paired with "a small understatement", but a lay audience can read it as zero emissions.
- **Turn 3.** It labelled a fill-at-first-reported-year scenario as an "upper bound" or "ceiling" ("at most 15.51%", "at most 1,134 Mt") in result columns, quality.md, history.md and chat. It did state the assumption alongside.

No computed value was wrong. The user caught both before packaging, and release 001 is clean. The release has no guidance on wording coverage gaps as unreported, or on labelling assumption-based scenarios as illustrative rather than bounds. This is the third co2 run with a gap-wording error, so the gap is real.

The severity should be moderate (a wording and interpretation risk caught by the user), not major. The citation should be corrected: the "zero" wording entered quality.md in agent-002, and agent-003's edit introduced the "ceiling" wording.

verdicts.reasoning:
Most of the cited evidence holds up. In co2-B transcript A2 (line 115) the agent wrote "Earlier years count as zero in the cumulative totals." In relay/agent-002.jsonl it wrote foundation/quality.md DQ-004 as "Cumulative sums since 1850 treat missing early years as zero, a small understatement for China and India." It put the same wording in the q4 finding caveat, the settings metrics detail and the Unresolved issues line. U3 challenged this. A3 (line 254) then said "I also calculated a ceiling ... at most 15.51%". In agent-003.jsonl the agent rewrote DQ-004 as "would add at most 1,134 Mt ... state the gap and the ceiling", and U4 challenged that. The first years, 1907 for China and 1858 for India, were counted. The oct16-ref report (C-20, README line 143) shows the same "count as zero" wording in the Oct 16 co2-B run and says Oct 15 had the same class of error, so "third in a row" is supported.

Release check:
- No shipped file causes this wording. A grep of the release for zero, unreported, as zero, ceiling, bound, scenario and illustrative finds nothing about how to describe missing periods or assumption-based scenarios.
- Nothing prevents it either. analysis.md "Add a result" (the #97 text) only says "count the periods each entity in scope has data for, since a sum hides missing periods: a count below the period length is a caveat on the finding". awb-explore SKILL.md "Coverage limitations" says to record each short entity under Unresolved issues. Neither says what the caveat should say.
- The agent followed both instructions exactly: it counted, caveated and recorded. Its default way of describing a SUM that skips NULLs became "count as zero" again, in the area #97 was meant to fix. So this is a gap in the guide's coverage-caveat instruction, not the agent ignoring a rule. Nothing about the harness shaped the wording, so a real user on any host would get the same text.

Why only a narrower version holds:
1. The "zero" wording is arithmetically accurate about the SQL. The original DQ-004 called it "a small understatement", so the agent was not claiming zero emissions. The flaw is ambiguous wording for a donor audience, not a false figure. The user caught it before any draft existed.
2. The "ceiling" half is not caused by the release. The agent stated its assumption both in chat and in the record. Its SQL comment gives the reason ("emissions were rising, so earlier years were very likely lower"). Calling the result a bound is the agent's wording choice, and the simulated user's standard is a stricter one. No guide encourages bound language, and expecting the release to police every bound-style word is a stretch.
3. "Major" severity is overstated. Both errors were in chat and in the records, both were fixed within one turn, and neither reached a package.

Citation correction: the edit that wrote the zero wording into quality.md is in agent-002.jsonl. agent-003.jsonl contains the replacement that introduced the "ceiling"/"at most" wording.
verdicts.release_evidence: SIMS/release/analytics-workbench-skills/awb-init/assets/workbench/workbench-guides/analysis.md line 15: "For a series summed over a period, also count the periods each entity in scope has data for, since a sum hides missing periods: a count below the period length is a caveat on the finding." It gives no wording for that caveat. SIMS/release/analytics-workbench-skills/awb-explore/SKILL.md line 52 (Coverage limitations) says to record each short entity under Unresolved issues, also with no wording. foundation/quality.md template: "A confirmed coverage gap ... is an open row", with no wording guidance. Nowhere in the release (guides, skills, templates, package-contract.md, review.md) is there anything about describing missing periods as unreported, or forbidding "ceiling", "bound" or "at most" for an assumption-based scenario. The nearest rule is review.md line 27 ("a sentence about how a source builds a series ... rests on a reference:"), which applies only at package-review time, after both errors here had already happened and been fixed.
verdicts.narrowed: The per-entity coverage instruction (analysis.md "Add a result", added by #97; awb-explore SKILL.md "Coverage limitations") makes the agent count and caveat an entity's short years but says nothing about how to word the caveat. So co2-B again described unreported early years with zero wording: "count as zero" in chat A2, and "treat missing early years as zero" in quality.md DQ-004 (relay/agent-002.jsonl), with the same wording in the finding caveat and Unresolved issues. This repeats Oct 16's C-20. It is ambiguous wording rather than a wrong figure: the sum matches OWID's own cumulative_co2, and DQ-004 called it an understatement. Severity is moderate, not major. The "ceiling ... at most 15.51%" wording (agent-003) was stated with its assumption and a reason, so it is the agent's own wording choice that the user corrected, not something the release causes.

consolidated.title: Agent removed cross-sheet copies on its own inference that they were re-extracts
consolidated.description: The lineage-aware scan now finds the UCI workbook's overlap on 1-9 December 2010. retail-B then removed the 22,523 identical rows itself and told the user afterwards. Neither the user nor the source documentation had said the rows were re-extracts. The agent read awb-clean's example 'such as overlapping periods' as enough. The scan also reports the cross-sheet copies and the within-sheet repeats as one duplicate-rows issue (S1). That issue was left 'open', with a correction recorded for only one part.
consolidated.caused_by_fix: yes: #98 (issue #92) wrote the re-extract rule with the trailing example 'such as overlapping periods or a repeated export', which reads as a sufficient test. Its lineage-free match also puts both kinds of repeat into one issue.
consolidated.evidence: retail-B-01: reply 2; msg 3 ('I'd expect to be asked before removing transaction rows'); the agent-002 clean-record S1 correction; agent-notes turn 3; awb-clean/SKILL.md:33 (the example is absent from the 1db6084 text). retail-B-17: agent-002 clean-record S1, status open with the correction filled; foundation/quality.md DQ-001.

verdicts.reasoning:
I checked each harness explanation against the logs. None of them caused this.

What happened. In turn 2 (relay/agent-002.jsonl) the agent counted the overlap between the two sheets: 22,523 rows shared, all dated 1-9 Dec 2010. It then invoked awb-clean with the args "known exact overlap". It rewrote foundation/views/01_online_retail.sql to drop the second sheet's copy, and recorded S1 with the rationale "The sheets' periods overlap ... every row in that window matches exactly in both, so they are re-extracts". The user found out from reply 2 ("Fixed: December 2010 appeared twice ... I kept one copy"). Message 3 approved the removal after the fact and added "I'd expect to be asked before removing transaction rows where their meaning is uncertain."

Neither the user nor the source said the rows were re-extracts:
- The user's messages 1-2 never mention the overlap.
- The saved UCI page (foundation/references/uci-online-retail-ii/uci-dataset-page.html) only says the data covers 01/12/2009-09/12/2011. It never mentions the sheets or an overlap. Its "# Instances 1067371" counts the overlap rows twice.

The agent says itself that it acted on the skill text:
- agent-notes turn 3: "the awb-clean rule let me remove cross-sheet overlaps myself when periods overlap ... Possibly the skill's self-decide rule for cross-sheet duplicates is too permissive."
- feedback/agent.md item 9 says the same.

Harness explanations ruled out:
1. Persona front-loading: human/BRIEF.md says nothing about the overlap. The user's complaint quotes the release README, not the persona.
2. Non-interactive session (AskUserQuestion is in --disallowedTools; the system prompt says the agent cannot ask mid-turn): the agent never tried to ask about the overlap. In the same reply it put two other decisions to the user, in one message as the skill prescribes. So it had a working way to ask and chose to decide this one itself.
3. Auto-approved Bash, Write and MCP tools: on an interactive host, the view rewrite would raise a Bash permission prompt the user could deny. That prompt is a raw SQL file write, not the plain-words data-meaning question the README promises. It does not change what the agent decided.
4. The study disclosure and relay behaviour are unrelated.
5. The only real confound is model prior knowledge. Agent-notes turn 1 says it already knew about the Dec 2010 overlap in the UCI data, which may have raised its confidence. But its recorded rationale rests only on the data, and it credits the skill rule. On a private workbook with overlapping periods, the same reading of the skill text applies.

The release text makes the misreading easy:
- awb-clean/SKILL.md:33 lets the agent remove cross-part copies "that the user or the source's documentation says are re-extracts of the same rows, such as overlapping periods or a repeated export". "Overlapping periods" reads naturally as a qualifying condition on its own.
- awb-init/references/landing.md:39 adds "Sheets or extracts covering overlapping periods can hold the same rows twice."
- This contradicts README.md:67 ("You decide whether identical rows shared by files or sheets are copies ... unless the source says they are re-extracts").
- It also contradicts SKILL.md:33's own warning that a part's name can be data ("one file per month"). Here the sheets are named by period.

Git check: the "such as overlapping periods" text arrived with 6fe8699 ("#92: agent removes cross-part copies only for known re-extracts"), which is in the trial-merged release under test. At 1db6084 the 'Decide yourself' paragraph (line 31) has no cross-part self-decide clause at all.

Severity caveat: the removal was substantively correct (the rows are true copies, and the user agreed), so the harm is to process and trust. "Major" reflects the broken README promise, not wrong numbers.

The second half of the finding holds only in part:
- The scan did merge cross-sheet copies and within-sheet repeats into one duplicate-rows issue (S1, count 34,335, with single-sheet and cross-sheet examples).
- In the agent-002 record, S1 was 'open' with only the cross-sheet correction filled.
- But "left open" was temporary. In agent-003, after the user decided the within-sheet repeats, the agent re-recorded S1 as 'corrected'. Final foundation/quality.md DQ-001 says 'corrected', even though the within-sheet part was kept rather than corrected.
verdicts.release_evidence:
Release copy, all under release/analytics-workbench-skills:
- awb-clean/SKILL.md:33: the self-decide clause "`duplicate-rows` across sheets, files or extracts that the user or the source's documentation says are re-extracts of the same rows, such as overlapping periods or a repeated export, removed keeping one part's copy".
- awb-clean/SKILL.md:35: "Rows shared by parts known to be re-extracts, as above, are yours to remove."
- awb-init/references/landing.md:39: "Sheets or extracts covering overlapping periods can hold the same rows twice ... awb-clean step 2 says who decides".
- README.md:67: the user decides whether shared identical rows are copies "unless the source says they are re-extracts".

Git, read-only: commit 6fe8699 (#92) introduced the clause and is in the integration-ux-sim-fixes trial merge 8917223. At 1db6084, the awb-clean 'Decide yourself' paragraph (line 31) has no cross-part clause.

Run evidence:
- retail-B relay/agent-002.jsonl: the INTERSECT ALL count of 22,523; the Skill call with args "known exact overlap"; the view rewrite; clean-record S1 with status open and the correction "so they are re-extracts".
- transcript reply 2 and message 3.
- feedback/agent-notes.md, turns 1 and 3.
- feedback/agent.md item 9.
- human/feedback.md item 2.
- human/BRIEF.md: no overlap fact.
- relay/agent-002.err: AskUserQuestion disallowed.
- relay/agent-003.jsonl: S1 re-recorded as corrected.
- project/foundation/quality.md line 13: DQ-001 corrected.
verdicts.narrowed:
The main claim holds as stated. retail-B's agent removed 22,523 identical cross-sheet rows (1-9 Dec 2010) without asking. It inferred they were re-extracts only because the sheet periods overlapped and the rows matched. Neither the user nor the UCI documentation said so. The cause is that awb-clean/SKILL.md:33's example "such as overlapping periods" (new in #92), together with landing.md:39, reads as permission to decide alone, which contradicts README.md:67.

The secondary claim is narrower. The scan does merge cross-part copies and within-part repeats into one duplicate-rows issue (S1). That forced a mixed 'open' record with only the cross-sheet correction in turn 2. It was not left open: once the user decided the within-sheet repeats in turn 3, the agent set DQ-001 to 'corrected', which in turn mislabels the kept within-sheet repeats.

The removal itself was substantively correct and approved afterwards. The harm is a broken README promise and lost user trust, not wrong numbers.

verdicts.reasoning:
The core claim holds. In retail-B, agent-002 counted the cross-sheet overlap at step 51, and the result was 22,523 rows. It removed them with `QUALIFY sheet = min(sheet)` in foundation/views/01_online_retail.sql at step 72, recorded S1 as `open` with the correction filled (step 80), and only afterwards told the user ("Fixed: December 2010 appeared twice", reply 2). The user had not called the rows re-extracts. The UCI page the agent saved to foundation/references says only that the data covers 01/12/2009 to 09/12/2011; it says nothing about the sheets overlapping. The agent's own rationale was: "The sheets' periods overlap by 1-9 Dec 2010 and every row in that window matches exactly in both, so they are re-extracts". Its turn-3 notes say the rule "let me remove cross-sheet overlaps myself when periods overlap". Message 3 contains "I'd expect to be asked before removing transaction rows where their meaning is uncertain".

The release text the agent loaded is identical to release/awb-clean/SKILL.md. Line 33 does state the right condition ("that the user or the source's documentation says are re-extracts"), and README:67 repeats it. Two wordings weaken it, though:
- Line 33 follows that condition with "such as overlapping periods or a repeated export", which reads as if an overlap the agent observes is itself a re-extract.
- Line 35 says "Rows shared by parts known to be re-extracts ... are yours to remove", and "known" can be met by the agent's own knowledge. In turn 1 the agent noted it already knew about the UCI December 2010 overlap.

awb-init/references/landing.md:39 adds to this: it says "Sheets or extracts covering overlapping periods can hold the same rows twice" and defers to awb-clean. Before 1db6084 the whole cross-part clause did not exist: duplicates were the agent's call only under a recorded grain, and whether repeated rows were errors was the user's call. So the self-decide path is new wording, and its example invites the misreading.

This is not a clear instruction ignored repeatedly. It happened once, and retail-A's Codex agent asked the user before removing the overlap, so the text can be followed correctly. That makes this a narrower wording defect, not an unconditional cause.

The second claim also holds. scan_dataset.py produces a single `duplicate-rows` issue (one self.add at line ~551) covering both cross-part copies and within-part repeats. SKILL.md decides those under different rules, and record_cleaning takes one status per issue. DQ-001 was `open` with a partial correction after turn 2. After turn 3 it became `corrected`, even though the within-sheet repeats were kept by the user's decision.

Severity is arguably below major. The removed rows really were identical copies, including invoice number and minute. The removal was disclosed in the same reply, and the user then approved it. The harm is to process: the user was not asked first.
verdicts.release_evidence:
The release's own wording:
- **awb-clean/SKILL.md:33:** "`duplicate-rows` across sheets, files or extracts that the user or the source's documentation says are re-extracts of the same rows, such as overlapping periods or a repeated export, removed keeping one part's copy".
- **awb-clean/SKILL.md:35:** "Rows shared by parts known to be re-extracts, as above, are yours to remove. For any other parts, ask in plain words".
- **awb-init/references/landing.md:39:** "Sheets or extracts covering overlapping periods can hold the same rows twice ... `awb-clean` step 2 says who decides whether it is removed".
- **README.md:67:** "You decide whether identical rows shared by files or sheets are copies or separate records, unless the source says they are re-extracts". This is the correct rule, but the skill's examples blur it.
- **awb-clean/scripts/scan_dataset.py ~536-554:** a single `duplicate-rows` issue covers all repeats on the non-lineage columns, both cross-part and within-part.
- **1db6084 .agents/skills/awb-clean/SKILL.md:** had no cross-part self-decide clause at all ("`duplicate-rows` under a recorded grain"; "whether repeated rows or keys are errors" was the user's decision).

Run evidence:
- **retail-B/relay/agent-002.jsonl:** steps 51, 54, 72, 75 and 80. The step-80 S1 correction reads "The sheets' periods overlap ... so they are re-extracts of the same rows".
- **retail-B transcript:** reply 2 and message 3.
- **feedback/agent-notes.md:** turn 3.
- **project/foundation/quality.md:** DQ-001, now `corrected` despite the kept within-sheet repeats.
- **project/foundation/references/uci-online-retail-ii/uci-dataset-page.html:** no mention of the overlap.
- **Counterexample:** retail-A transcript lines 98-161, where that run's agent asked before removing the overlap.

Citation errors: the second evidence cite "retail-B-17" in findings.json is about commit/rerun sequencing; the split-issue finding is retail-B-14.
verdicts.narrowed:
awb-clean step 2 states the right condition: cross-part copies are the agent's to remove only when the user or the source's documentation says they are re-extracts. Two wordings weaken it, and together with landing.md they let an agent count its own observation of overlapping periods, or its prior knowledge of the dataset, as meeting the condition:
- the example "such as overlapping periods" on line 33;
- "parts known to be re-extracts" on line 35.

In retail-B, the Claude agent did exactly that. It removed 22,523 cross-sheet rows (1-9 Dec 2010) before asking and disclosed the removal afterwards. That happened in one of two retail runs: retail-A's agent asked first. The rows were genuine copies, and the user approved the removal afterwards, so the harm is process rather than data.

Separately, the scan reports cross-part copies and within-part repeats as one `duplicate-rows` issue, while the skill decides them under different rules. As a result DQ-001 carries a partial correction under a single status: `open` after turn 2, then `corrected` after turn 3 even though the within-sheet repeats were kept.

consolidated.title: Brief-coverage check forces internal verification questions onto visible slides
consolidated.description: review.md now requires every question that methodology.md repeats for a represented result to be answered in a slide's headline, bullets or chart, not only in Notes. It does not tell audience questions apart from internal verification questions. taxi-A's first reviewer therefore made the agent put a verification bullet on the tipping slide. The user had it removed, which cost a correction, a recorded user-override exception and another scoped review.
consolidated.oct16_ref: new; side effect of the C-11 fix (#85)
consolidated.caused_by_fix: yes: #101 (issue #85) added the brief-coverage item at review.md:27.
consolidated.evidence: taxi-A-03: the first reviewer's report in SIMS/taxi-A/agent-home/.codex/sessions/2026/10/17/rollout-2026-10-17T08-11-07-*.jsonl ('This represented question is answered only in findings.md:72 speaker notes'); reply 7, msg 8 item 1, reply 8; feedback/agent.md section 1 item 1. Release: awb-package/references/review.md:27.

verdicts.reasoning:
I looked for a harness cause and found none.

Every step from the user's check to the forced bullet follows release text:
1. In message 6 the persona asked the agent to "Confirm it's not a mix-up". It improvised this under the general human-rules instruction to ask follow-ups. The persona file does not script it, and a real analyst could ask the same thing.
2. The agent saved the check as result q3-verification under ledger question Q-016. The shipped analysis guide (awb-init/assets/workbench/workbench-guides/analysis.md:11) requires a result's `question` to be "in the user's own words, never paraphrased", so the result's question became the user's check text.
3. review.md step 3 and package-contract.md:49 require any narrative sentence saying something was verified to cite the recorded result in methodology.md. So the agent had to represent q3-verification in order to mention the check, even in speaker notes.
4. The contract's `questions` rule then requires methodology.md to repeat that question word for word (methodology.md:87).
5. review.md:27 requires every part of each such repeated question to be answered in a slide's headline, bullets or chart, "not only in a slide's Notes".

Harness factors ruled out:
- **Reviewer:** a native Codex subagent spawned with spawn_agent (rollout session_meta shows thread_source=subagent, agent_path /root/board_draft_review), as review.md's Codex branch prescribes. Its narrative problem, "This represented question is answered only in findings.md:72 speaker notes", is a faithful reading of "every part … not only in Notes". A Claude Plan reviewer given the same brief would most likely make the same call.
- **Non-interactive run:** review.md tells awb-package to repair every narrative problem without asking the user, so an interactive host behaves the same.
- **Study disclosure:** the harness note only says "Work exactly as you normally would" and asks for a friction log.
- **Sandbox, MCP auto-approval, relay:** none of them touch this path.
- **The user's correction:** genuine. The persona reasoned that the board never sees the Manhattan figure. The release itself provides no audience flag: the ledger's Audience and Show columns govern only the Open questions slide (provenance.py:2443), not this coverage check.

The finding overstates some details:
- **Avoidability:** the agent could have left the internal check out of the deck entirely, since q3-standard already holds the hourly grain. The conflict appears only when a check is mentioned in notes or methodology. But the user later explicitly asked for exactly that ("Speaker notes are fine"), and the release makes notes-only placement impossible without an exception.
- **Extra scoped review:** not attributable to C-12. The same correction message's 12-hour-time rule and headline edit made the review stale anyway, and one scoped review covered all three.
- **Override written into brief.md and methodology:** this was the agent's own workaround. The release's route is `--accept` with the user's reason after a reviewer flags the problem again. That route is still a ceremony, so the cost exists, but its form was the agent's choice.
- **Severity:** the user-visible cost is one bullet in a correction message that also carried two unrelated corrections. That reads as minor, not major.
verdicts.release_evidence:
- awb-package/references/review.md:27: "every part of its Business question and of each question methodology.md repeats for a represented result ... is answered in a slide's headline, bullets, or chart, or listed as unanswered ..., not only in a slide's Notes: or nowhere". There is no audience-versus-internal distinction.
- awb-package/references/review.md:26 (step 3, fourth bullet) and package-contract.md:49: a sentence saying something was checked or verified must cite the result in methodology.md. package-contract.md:49 also says "methodology repeats verbatim ... the question each represented result answers (`questions`)".
- awb-init/assets/workbench/workbench-guides/analysis.md:11: a result's question is "in the user's own words, never paraphrased".
- src/provenance.py:2443: the ledger's only show/audience flag applies to the Open questions slide.
- taxi-A evidence:
  - review-reports/agent-007-record01.txt, the third narrative problem (methodology.md:83).
  - settings.toml [results.q3-verification], which carries the user's check text as its question.
  - The draft's methodology.md:87 and findings.md:72.
  - brief.md:25 and methodology.md:79, where the agent recorded the override.
  - transcript message 8, item 1.
  - agent-notes.md:85 and :93.
verdicts.narrowed: When a check the user asks for in chat is saved as its own result (whose question must be the user's words) and that result is cited so the deck can mention the check in speaker notes or methodology, review.md:27 requires the check's answer to appear in visible slide content. The only alternatives are listing it as unanswered or a user-accepted exception. Nothing in the release lets a reviewer treat an internal verification question as exempt from audience coverage. In taxi-A this cost one user correction (the bullet removal) and an exception the agent wrote into brief.md and methodology. The extra scoped review is not attributable, because the same message's other corrections triggered it anyway, so severity is closer to minor than major.

verdicts.reasoning:
The release causes this through a chain of its own instructions, and the agent followed each one correctly.

1. awb-init/references/provenance.md:17 says a result's `question` is "one line in the user's words". In taxi-A, message 6 the user asked in chat: "Confirm it's not a mix-up" and "Give me the hour-of-day range". The agent recorded result q3-verification with the question "Confirm the standard-rate medians are not a mix-up with Manhattan all-card medians, and give the standard-rate hour-of-day range."
2. awb-package/SKILL.md:71 (step 4.3) and package-contract.md:49 (`questions` check) require methodology.md to repeat every represented result's question verbatim. The result had to be represented for two reasons: its hourly-range part appears on the slide, and review.md:26 requires any "verified/matches" sentence to cite a recorded result.
3. review.md:27 requires "every part of ... each question methodology.md repeats for a represented result" to be answered in a slide's headline, bullets or chart, "not only in a slide's Notes:".
