It makes no distinction between questions the audience asks and internal sanity checks. Nothing in review.md, SKILL.md, package-contract.md, helpers.md or the findings template offers such a carve-out. helpers.md:31 even hands audience suitability to the draft review.
4. review.md:43 tells awb-package to "repair ... every narrative problem" after the first review. Asking the user is reserved for the second review, so the agent had no sanctioned way to ask first.

The run evidence confirms each step:
- The recorded first report (review-reports/agent-007-record01.txt, the same report as the 08-11-07 rollout) holds: narrative methodology.md:83 "Confirm the standard-rate medians are not a mix-up..." "This represented question is answered only in findings.md:72 speaker notes; its confirmation must appear in a slide headline, bullet or chart, or be listed as unanswered." That is a correct literal application of review.md:27.
- In reply 7 the agent says the tipping slide "visibly confirms that the matching medians came from different populations."
- In message 8, item 1, the user asks to drop exactly that bullet as noise for the board, with "Speaker notes are fine."
- In reply 8 the agent removed it and wrote an override into brief.md:25 and methodology.md:79 ("At the user's explicit direction, the no-mix-up verification is retained in speaker notes...").
- feedback/agent.md section 1 item 1 describes the same chain.

A real user on any host would hit this. Asking in chat for a sanity check is ordinary, and the reviewer subagent applies the same text everywhere. Nothing here depends on the harness.

Some of the stated cost is overstated:
- "Another scoped review" is not attributable to this issue. Message 8 also carried the 12-hour-time rule and an answer-headline rewrite, and those edits would have forced a fresh scoped review anyway (agent-008-record01 checks R-time-format-001).
- The prose override in brief.md and methodology.md was the agent's choice. The release's own route would be to record the user's acceptance with `--accept` when a review flags the problem. That is still a ceremony, so the friction stands, but the exact form is the agent's.
- "Major" is generous. The cost was one bullet, one correction item in a three-item message, resolved in one turn.
verdicts.release_evidence:
Release under test (scratchpad/sims/release/analytics-workbench-skills):
- awb-package/references/review.md:27: "every part of its Business question and of each question methodology.md repeats for a represented result ... is answered in a slide's headline, bullets, or chart, or listed as unanswered ... not only in a slide's Notes: or nowhere". There is no audience-versus-verification distinction.
- review.md:43: "In awb-package, repair every error violation, every narrative problem". Asking the user comes only after a second failing review.
- review.md:26: a "checked or verified ... matches" sentence must cite a recorded result, which forces the verification result to be represented.
- awb-package/SKILL.md:71: "repeat each of its questions verbatim in the methodology section".
- package-contract.md:49: the `questions` check.
- awb-init/references/provenance.md:17: a result's question is "one line in the user's words".

taxi-A run evidence:
- review-reports/agent-007-record01.txt: the narrative problem on methodology.md:83.
- transcript.md: message 6 (the user's mix-up request), reply 7 (bullet added), message 8 item 1 (bullet removed), reply 8.
- Override text at project/investigations/trip-pattern-comparison/brief.md:25 and draft/methodology.md:79.
verdicts.narrowed: review.md:27, combined with the rule that a result's question is recorded in the user's words and repeated verbatim (SKILL.md:71, provenance.md:17), turns a sanity-check question the user asked in chat into a visible slide bullet once that result is represented. review.md:43 then makes the agent add the bullet without asking first. In taxi-A the user had to remove it as noise, and the agent wrote a prose override into brief.md and methodology.md. The extra scoped review is not attributable to this issue, because the same user message's 12-hour-time rule and headline edit required one anyway. The impact was one correction item resolved in a single turn, which is closer to moderate than major.

consolidated.title: Workbench vocabulary and process narration still reach chat and files the user reviews
consolidated.description: Chat, and files the user is asked to read, still carry record terms and internals. Examples: 'provisional', 'eligible view', 'publication', 'cohort checks', 'shared dataset owid_co2', '.venv/bin/python', commit hashes, '91 validation checks', 'upstream-change checks'. quality-proposal.md uses column names and question IDs, and the headline preview lists result IDs. Claude agents' interim narration also reaches the user ('Now state.md', 'Ledger done', 'That producer came out convoluted', review mechanics). Report rules no longer demand IDs. The plain-words rule still loses to habit and to lines the release itself requires, such as the upstream-check notice and the recorded interpreter.
consolidated.caused_by_fix: partly: retail-A's 'UCI sent no version headers ... upstream-change checks' line is the once-at-landing notice that #98 (issue #92) added for C-74. The rest predates the fixes.
consolidated.evidence: taxi-A-09: quality-proposal.md. taxi-A-10: replies 1, 3, 4, 6 and 8; feedback/human.md section 4. taxi-B-19: the opening lines of replies 2-6, after msg 3 asked for updates focused on results. co2-A-07: r2, r5; the 'Primary result' and 'Results' lines in draft/.preview/headlines.md. co2-B-07: interim lines of A2, A4, A5 and A6 (confounded by C-77). retail-A-07: replies 1, 3, 4 and 5; awb-init/references/landing.md. retail-B-28: replies 4-6. Release: awb-init/assets/workbench/AGENTS.md Conversation ('chat uses plain words').

verdicts.reasoning:
I looked for a harness cause and found two that change how much of the interim narration showed up. Neither one explains the main finding.

Harness factors I checked:
(1) The relay delivers every assistant text block of a turn, joined with blank lines. Claude agents are read through `_claude_reply` and Codex agents through `_codex_reply`, both in kit/relay.py. The real hosts show these messages too: Claude Code prints interim text between tool calls, and Codex shows its preamble messages. The difference is presentation. In the sim the interim lines arrive as one block at the top of the reply. On a real host they are spread out between tool calls. That makes them more prominent here, but it does not create them.
(2) kit/claude-agent-system.md tells Claude agents "The user sees only your final reply each turn". The relay contradicts this. In taxi-B, agent-notes.md line 33 shows the agent read msg 3's "keep updates focused on results" as being about its closing message only, so it kept narrating. The persistence of narration after that request, which the finding cites as taxi-B evidence, is therefore confounded by the harness.
(3) human-rules.md asks the persona to log anything "jargon-heavy". That makes jargon more likely to be noticed. It does not cause the jargon.
(4) No other harness factor applies: not front-loading, the sandbox, MCP auto-approval, the simulated home, or the study disclosure.

Most of the finding stands without the narration part:
- The Codex-agent runs show the same leaks in their final summaries. Codex agents do not get the misleading prompt line. Examples:
  - taxi-A reply 1: ".venv/bin/python", twice.
  - taxi-A reply 4: "eligible-trip view", "All 35 validation checks passed".
  - taxi-A reply 8: "two provisional reference calculations", "fully published".
  - co2-A reply 2: "shared dataset is available as `owid_co2`", "cohort checks".
  - retail-A reply 4: "Committed through `7f1ccf0`", "91 validation checks".
  - retail-A reply 3: "upstream-change checks won't be available".
- Several of these lines are required by the release itself:
  - awb-init/SKILL.md:40 says "Report in one line the interpreter its `interpreter` entry records".
  - awb-init/references/landing.md:11 says "tell the user once, at landing, that upstream changes to it cannot be detected".
  - The footer rule in workbench AGENTS.md counts `provisional` answers, and its own example reads "1 provisional".
  - awb-package/SKILL.md:96 requires "Report the review's outcome" and headlines "marked provisional".
- The plain-words rule covers chat only. AGENTS.md says "Records keep precise terms and IDs", and no rule covers a file handed to the user for review. awb-package/SKILL.md:49 says only headlines and figures for `.preview/headlines.md`. Both files cited in the finding contain record vocabulary:
  - taxi-A quality-proposal.md: column names, "Q-011", "publication.json", "canonical view", notes addressed to the agent.
  - co2-A .preview/headlines.md: "Primary result: territorial-change", "Results: ...". Its reply 5 links the user to this file.
- The interim lines from Claude agents use the release's own terms: "promote", "mechanical checks", "scoped re-review", "ledger" (co2-B A2/A4/A6, retail-B R5/R6). A real interactive Claude Code user would see these lines.

One problem in the finding's citations: several run IDs do not match their run findings.json entries. taxi-A-09 is about README data states, while taxi-A-08 is the quality-proposal finding. taxi-B-19 is about instruction gaps. retail-A-07 is about the timing of the review-rule question. retail-B-28 is a harness finding about session files. I checked the underlying replies and files directly, and the cited excerpts do exist.
verdicts.release_evidence:
- awb-init/assets/workbench/AGENTS.md:28 says "Records keep precise terms and IDs; chat uses plain words". The rule covers only chat, not files the user is asked to read.
- AGENTS.md:34 says the closing line counts "any `provisional` answer as provisional", with the example "2 answered, 1 provisional, 2 open".
- awb-init/SKILL.md:40 says "Report in one line the interpreter its `interpreter` entry records", which produces ".venv/bin/python" in chat.
- awb-init/references/landing.md:11 says "tell the user once, at landing, that upstream changes to it cannot be detected".
- awb-package/SKILL.md:96 says "Report the review's outcome ...", with headlines "marked provisional".
- awb-package/SKILL.md:49 defines `.preview/headlines.md` content only loosely, and the Codex agent added result IDs to it.
- awb-clean/SKILL.md:79 says "their quality IDs kept in the files".
- The harness confound is in kit/claude-agent-system.md: "The user sees only your final reply each turn". kit/relay.py `_claude_reply` and `_codex_reply` join all of a turn's texts.
verdicts.narrowed: On both hosts, the release's own required lines put workbench terms into chat: the provisional count in the closing line, the one-line report of the recorded interpreter (".venv/bin/python"), the notice that upstream changes cannot be detected, and the review outcome. Agents also use record vocabulary in their final summaries ("eligible view", "publication", "shared dataset owid_co2", commit hashes, check counts). Files handed to the user for review (taxi-A quality-proposal.md, co2-A .preview/headlines.md with "Primary result:" IDs) carry record terms, because the plain-words rule covers only chat and treats files as records. Claude agents' interim process lines also reach real interactive users, and their vocabulary comes from the skills ("promote", "mechanical checks", "scoped review"). The evidence that narration continued after the user asked for results-only updates (taxi-B msg 3) is harness-confounded, and so is how prominent the narration looks. The sim prompt tells Claude agents the user sees only their final reply, and the relay puts the interim lines at the top of the reply. Several evidence IDs in the finding point to unrelated run findings (taxi-A-09, taxi-B-19, retail-A-07, retail-B-28) and need relabelling.

verdicts.reasoning:
Only a narrower version of the finding holds. Three parts of it fail.

What I checked in the runs:
- Chat leaks are real in all three Codex-agent runs:
  - taxi-A: '.venv/bin/python' in r1, 'published as validated datasets' in r3, 'eligible-trip view' and 'All 35 validation checks passed' in r4, 'provisional reference calculations' in r8.
  - retail-A: '.venv/bin/python' in r1, 'UCI sent no version headers ... upstream-change checks' in r3, '91 validation checks', 'no stale results' and 'Committed through 7f1ccf0' in r4. The commit was one the user had asked for.
  - co2-A: 'cohort checks' and 'shared dataset `owid_co2`' in r2.
  - Each user flagged these as jargon: taxi-A human.md §4, retail-A §2.4, co2-A §2.4.
- Files the user is pointed to carry IDs:
  - taxi-A quality-proposal.md has column names, Q-011, publication.json and 'canonical view'.
  - The headline previews in taxi-A, taxi-B ('Finding (Q-002; airport-share, ...)') and co2-A ('Primary result: territorial-change', 'Results: ...') list question and result IDs.

What the release causes:
1. AGENTS.md Conversation applies plain words to chat only, and says 'Records keep precise terms and IDs'. Its word list covers only ledger, finding, flagged, limitation and disposition. It says nothing about data-layer terms (publication, view, shared dataset, checks), which the guides use throughout. It also says nothing about files written for the user to read. awb-package/SKILL.md:49 has the agent write `.preview/headlines.md` with no format and no plain-words requirement. Agents treat that file as a record.
2. Some lines the release requires surface internals:
   - awb-init/SKILL.md:40 says 'Report in one line the interpreter its `interpreter` entry records', and README:65 promises it. All three Codex runs printed `.venv/bin/python`. Claude in taxi-B phrased the same line plainly, so the line can be written plainly.
   - awb-init/references/landing.md:11 says to 'tell the user once, at landing, that upstream changes to it cannot be detected'. That produced the retail-A r3 line and the retail-B r4 line.
3. The awb-status Findings item asks for counts by status per result ('2 findings, 1 supported'). That produced 'seven supported and seven provisional findings' (retail-A r5; the user spent msg 6 asking 'What are the 14?'). It also produced taxi-A's 'nine supported findings and two provisional reference calculations', which the user could not map onto five questions. The problem is the per-calculation counting more than the words.

What does not hold:
- 'provisional' is not a leak. AGENTS.md requires it in the closing line, and the README's 'Words you will meet' defines it.
- The Claude agents' interim narration is harness-caused. kit/claude-agent-system.md, appended to the Claude agent's system prompt, says 'The user sees only your final reply each turn, not your tool calls'. relay.py:7 forwards 'the agent's interim messages within a turn' verbatim. So 'Now state.md', 'Ledger done' (taxi-B), 'That producer came out convoluted' (co2-B) and 'Promoting...' / 'Mechanical checks...' (retail-B) were written as if unseen. On a real host the agent knows interim text is visible. This is likely the C-77 confound.
- quality-proposal.md appears in one run only, and it is a file the agent invented, not a release artifact.

Also relevant: Codex repeatedly linked and quoted SKILL.md files to the user (taxi-A r1 and r8; retail-A r1, r3, r6 and r8; co2-A r1). That breaks an explicit AGENTS.md rule ('never send them to a skill or instruction file'). It is a clear instruction ignored repeatedly, and belongs in a separate finding.

Several cited run IDs are wrong:
- taxi-A-09 and taxi-A-10 are about data states and the reference-only role. The quality-proposal finding is taxi-A-08.
- taxi-B-19 should be taxi-B-13.
- co2-A-07 and co2-B-07 are cited correctly.
- retail-A-07 should be retail-A-06.
- retail-B-28 is an unrelated harness finding, and retail-B's user never complained about narration.
verdicts.release_evidence:
These are the release lines that cause the leaks:
- awb-init/assets/workbench/AGENTS.md, Conversation section: 'Records keep precise terms and IDs; chat uses plain words: ledger rows are questions, findings are what we found, flagged findings await recheck, limitations are caveats, and a disposition is the decision on <finding>.' Plain words apply to chat only, and the word list has no data-layer terms.
- awb-init/SKILL.md:40: 'Report in one line the interpreter its `interpreter` entry records'. README.md:65 promises setup 'says which Python it recorded'.
- awb-init/references/landing.md:11: 'tell the user once, at landing, that upstream changes to it cannot be detected'. awb-status/SKILL.md (Sources item) repeats this as a known limitation.
- awb-status/SKILL.md, Findings item: '`active.counts`, then each `questions.by_question` entry ... with its findings by status, as "Which zones grew fastest: 2 findings, 1 supported"'. This yields counts per calculation.
- awb-package/SKILL.md:49: the preview-and-wait headlines go to `.preview/headlines.md`, 'which no check reads'. No format and no plain-words requirement is given.

These release lines already address parts of the finding:
- AGENTS.md: 'never send them to a skill or instruction file'. Codex broke this repeatedly.
- AGENTS.md's closing line requires counting 'provisional' answers, and README 'Words you will meet' defines Provisional and supported. That word is intended vocabulary.
- awb-clean/SKILL.md Report: 'the recorded issues in plain words, their quality IDs kept in the files'.

Harness confound:
- kit/claude-agent-system.md: 'The user sees only your final reply each turn, not your tool calls or files'.
- kit/relay.py:7 passes the agent's 'interim messages within a turn' to the user verbatim.
verdicts.narrowed:
Users still see the workbench's data-layer terms and its IDs, mostly from the Codex agent:
- **Chat:** 'published', 'eligible view', 'shared dataset owid_co2', ingestion and validation check counts, and the `.venv/bin/python` path.
- **Files the user is pointed to:** the headline previews in taxi-A, taxi-B and co2-A list question and result IDs, and one ad-hoc quality proposal lists column names and IDs.
- **Status reports:** awb-status counts findings per calculation ('seven supported and seven provisional'), which users cannot map onto their own questions.

The release contributes in two ways:
- AGENTS.md applies 'plain words' to chat only. Its word list covers only ledger and finding terms. Files written for the user, such as `.preview/headlines.md`, fall under 'records keep precise terms and IDs'.
- It requires the interpreter line (awb-init SKILL.md:40), the upstream notice (landing.md:11) and status counts by finding status.

Excluded from the narrowed finding:
- The Claude agents' internal interim narration is caused by the harness prompt.
- 'provisional' is README-defined vocabulary the release intends users to see.

consolidated.title: README still long for analysts; data stages and some mechanics unclear
consolidated.caused_by_fix: partly: #105 (issue #94) added the 'bring no data in' sentence at README line 54, which taxi-A's setup contradicted and co2-A found ambiguous.
consolidated.evidence: taxi-A-11: reply 1 (originals preserved under storage/landed at setup), msg 3; README line 54. taxi-A-12: feedback/human.md section 3; human/notes.md turns 1, 2 and 8. taxi-B-27: README is 4,718 words (wc -w). co2-A-23: README lines 54, 70 and 85. co2-B-27: README line 70. retail-A-27: README items 6-7. retail-A-28: 'Words you will meet' and 'Good to know'. retail-B-24. For comparison, the Oct 16 README was about 5,345 words.

verdicts.reasoning:
The finding is about the README, and the README is the release, so I checked how far the harness could explain it.

The harness does inflate the itemized list:
- relay.py's closing prompt asks every user for "(3) the README: what was missing, unclear, or wrong".
- human-rules.md tells the persona to read the whole README before message 1, admin half included, and to log jargon and confusion every turn.
So the long list of small "unclear" points is partly produced by the prompts, and a real analyst might skim.

The core claim survives that lens:
1. All 6 runs flag length in their own turn-1 notes, written before the feedback prompt. That holds for both model families as the user: Claude in taxi-A, co2-A and retail-A, Codex in taxi-B, co2-B and retail-B. A single model's habit does not explain it.
2. The length is a fact of the release. wc -w gives 4,718 words, and lines 1-107 (everything before Included skills and Install and administer) are about 3,000 words.
3. Personas front-loading answers does not create the complaint. The README's own example first message tells users to front-load.

Sub-points checked one by one:
- **"Setup and the scoping round bring no data in" (line 54): confirmed, and it is skill behavior, not harness.**
  - taxi-A: the Codex agent called awb/data land for both sources in reply 1, during setup. That copied the originals to storage/landed, and in message 3 the user asked whether the data was "in".
  - taxi-B: the Claude agent ran DuckDB over the inbox Parquet at setup and reported counts, though it copied nothing.
  - Auto-approved MCP tools could have made the landing easier, but the decision to land was the agent's own. awb-init/SKILL.md never says setup must not touch data, so the README's promise has no backing in the skills. A real user who names the landed folder, as the README's example does, would hit the same contradiction.
- **Project vs investigation: confirmed.** "Words you will meet" (lines 94-100) has no entry for investigation.
- **Item 7 and the two checkpoint modes explained by mechanism (lines 69-70): confirmed** as a judgment by the taxi-A, co2-A and retail-A users.
- **What the finished slides look like / findings.md is long: confirmed** in taxi-A only. It is minor.
- **Review-stop granularity, and a new rule triggering another review: confirmed** in co2-B, with similar reports in taxi-B and retail-B. The README does document the stop, so this is more about review-gate behavior than missing documentation.

Weak or inaccurate parts:
- "landed / published / screened" never appear in the analyst sections. They are the agent's words, so this is mainly an agent-vocabulary problem; the README's real gap is that it never says what state the data is in.
- "Unassessed join check" is helper jargon the agent surfaced in co2-B. The fix belongs in the agent's explanation, not the README.
- On the jargon bullet:
  - **"check-draft"** appears only in How it works (line 195), not in an analyst section.
  - **"MCP server"** is not named in the quick-start; line 106 says "`awb` tool server".
  - **Commits** (line 105) and **R-periods-001** (line 99) are accurate.
- The finding's evidence IDs are mislabeled. taxi-A-11, taxi-A-12, co2-A-23 and retail-B-24 in findings.json are unrelated items: chart export, chart grammar, a reviewloop parser gap, and the cohort definition. The matching entries are taxi-A-09, taxi-A-28, taxi-B-08, co2-A-21, co2-B-27 and retail-B-21. retail-A has no README-length entry; its evidence is in feedback/human.md section 3 and human/notes.md turn 1.

Severity: minor.
verdicts.release_evidence:
- release README.md: 4,718 words (wc -w); lines 1-107 come to about 3,000 words before Included skills and Install and administer.
- README line 54: "Setup and the scoping round bring no data in".
- README lines 69-70: items 6 and 7, the checkpoint modes and review problems.
- README lines 94-100: the glossary has no 'investigation' entry.
- README line 99: R-periods-001. Line 105: commits. Line 106: "`awb` tool server". Line 195: check-draft, in How it works only.
- awb-init/SKILL.md: steps 3-5 never forbid landing or inspecting data during setup.
- taxi-A/relay/agent-001.jsonl: "MCP awb/data land" for tlc-yellow and tlc-zones in reply 1. taxi-A/transcript.md, message 3: "is the data now fully 'in'".
- taxi-B/transcript.md, reply 1: "A first look at the files", with DuckDB reading inbox Parquet at setup.
- human/notes.md turn 1 in all six runs flags README length.
- kit/relay.py around line 361: the feedback prompt explicitly asks for README critique. kit/human-rules.md line 10: the user must read the README before the first message.

verdicts.reasoning:
The shipped README causes the core complaint, but several of the listed sub-points either come from the agent or are overstated.

What holds up:
- Length. The release README.md is 4,718 words (wc -w), and all six runs got a byte-identical copy (cmp). By line range: the intro and What you get (lines 1-34) are about 706 words and the Quick-start (35-108) about 2,294. Included skills is 182, Install and administer (122-188) is 1,304, and How it works plus Versioning is 232. So the analyst path comes first but runs about 3,000 words, and roughly 1,700 words of admin material sit in the same file. Four users said the README was long and wanted a short analyst entry point (taxi-B, co2-A, co2-B, retail-B). Two more called items 6-8 or item 7 dense (taxi-A, retail-A).
- Items 6 and 7 (README:69-70) are each a single dense paragraph that describes the mechanism: scoped versus full reviews, unchanged lines, second-review stop, rule conflicts. taxi-A, co2-A and retail-A all reread them. Nothing in them says how small a problem can cause the stop. Nor does the README say that adding a review rule makes the last review stale. review.md:39 lists a change to foundation/review-rules.md as making the review stale, but README:70 only says "nothing changed since" (co2-B).
- "Investigation" is used at README:3, 33, 80 and 85, but "Words you will meet" (94-100) never defines it or says how it differs from the project (taxi-A).
- README:13 describes findings.md as the slide-by-slide outline. It does not warn that the file is long and written for the deck builder, or show what a finished slide looks like (taxi-A only).

What does not hold up, or is narrower:
- **Landing at setup.** The contradiction of "Setup and the scoping round bring no data in" (README:54) came from the agent. awb-init/SKILL.md:10 says data preparation follows on request, and project AGENTS.md:38 says broader preparation needs an explicit request. Only taxi-A's agent ran land in the setup turn (relay agent-001: awb/data land for tlc-yellow and tlc-zones). None of the other five runs landed at setup. retail-A's notes confirm that setup "didn't download yet. As expected."
- **co2-A's ambiguity.** The user found the line unclear, but also said "It was fine; I just asked 'download the data' later."
- **Data states.** The README's plain-words Bring the data in step (README:81) covers landing and conversion, and the clean/explore question (README:82) covers screening. taxi-A's "is the data in?" question was triggered by the agent's early landing. The narrow true part is that the analyst section never names the landed, queryable and cleaned states the agent later uses in chat.
- **'Unassessed join check'.** This is helper or agent vocabulary, not README text. co2-B's agent did explain it in chat ("the queries join on the dataset's verified unique key, which I'll note as a caveat", transcript.md:100). It belongs to agent communication, not to the README.
- **Jargon.** MCP, check-draft, Parquet and DuckDB appear only in Install and administer and How it works (README:122-195), which retail-A itself said are for installers. In the analyst sections there are only commits (README:105, explained in plain words), the awb "tool server" (README:106) and the example ID R-periods-001 (README:99).

Harness note: the persona rules (kit/human-rules.md:10) tell users to read the whole README before their first message, and the feedback template has a README section. That invites README comments, but it does not create the length or the missing definitions.
verdicts.release_evidence:
Release analytics-workbench-skills/README.md:
- 4,718 words in total. The Install and administer, How it works and Versioning sections (lines 122-203) are about 1,540 words and share the file with the analyst Quick-start (lines 35-108, about 2,294 words).
- Items 6 and 7 of What you will be asked (README:69-70) are dense paragraphs that describe the mechanism.
- README:70 does not say that a new review rule makes the last review stale. awb-package/references/review.md:39 lists a change to foundation/review-rules.md as a staleness trigger.
- The Words you will meet glossary (README:94-100) never defines "investigation".
- README:13 does not say findings.md is long or written for the builder.

Counter-evidence for the landing point:
- awb-init/SKILL.md:10 says "data preparation, analysis, and packages follow on request".
- awb-init/assets/workbench/AGENTS.md:38 says "broader preparation needs an explicit request".
- Only taxi-A/relay/agent-001.jsonl shows land calls in the setup turn; the other five runs have none.

Counter-evidence for the jargon point: MCP and check-draft appear only at README:147-195. Counter-evidence for the join-check point: "unassessed" comes from helper output (awb_provenance.py:1006-1012), not from the README.

consolidated.title: Agents' own command and coding slips
consolidated.caused_by_fix: no
consolidated.evidence: taxi-A-30: agent-004 and agent-007 logs; agent-notes lines 35, 46, 79, 80 and 86; relay/agent-007.err. taxi-B-34: exits 1 and 127 in relay/agent-002.jsonl. co2-A-26: a failed agent-007 awb/package export, then a successful one. co2-B-33: 'git add -A && git status --short', then 'git reset -q' in relay/agent-002.jsonl. retail-A-40: agent-notes turns 2-4. retail-B-37: agent-004 state next calls. retail-B-39: agent-002 exit 127; agent-003 sql binder and parser errors; agent-001 'head -0'.

verdicts.reasoning:
I checked each cited slip in the logs. The agents made all of them through their own habits or their own tools. None comes from the release.

Codex tool slips:
- taxi-A: the text() shadowing broke Codex's own functions.exec JavaScript runtime ("TypeError: text is not a function at exec_main.mjs").
- taxi-A: the apply_patch failure is Codex's patch tool rejecting a paragraph prefix (codex_core::tools::router in agent-007.err).
- retail-A: the JS syntax error was an extra "})();" in a functions.exec script.
- retail-A: the duplicate TOML key came from an apply_patch insertion placed at the wrong line.
- co2-A: the agent assumed the manifest's results were plain IDs and passed whole objects as MCP args. The release's MCP server refused cleanly ("args must be an array of strings") and wrote nothing.

zsh slips (Claude agents in the B runs, Bash tool under zsh):
- 'echo =====' gave "(eval):1: ==== not found".
- 'Q="python3 src/awb.py questions add"; $Q' gave exit 127, because zsh does not split words in $Q.
- A real macOS host would also run zsh. That does not make these release problems: nothing in the release suggests these patterns (I grepped for them).

SQL and shell slips:
- DuckDB rejected 'share' and 'value' as aliases, and QUALIFY combined with GROUP BY ALL. The release's sql wrapper reported the binder error helpfully.
- BSD head rejects 'head -0'.
- In retail-A, the grep for 'signed' matched 'assigned', and an audit query listed codes by hand and missed POST.

Agent habit: in co2-B the agent ran 'git add -A' and its own note says "nothing in skills caused it".

Part of the finding is inaccurate. The retail-B call 'S next --drop 1 --drop 1 2>/dev/null' was not refused. The code removes the duplicate, because drop numbers are resolved against the list before anything changes, and the help text says so. Exit status was 0 behind '| tail -1', and the call dropped one item. A later agent note (agent-008) corrects this: "second effectively ignored ... Expected behaviour per help, but surprising."

Two harness factors explain why the finding exists at all:
- Every slip comes from the private friction log that the study note in each agent prompt asked for ("append ... a private friction log"). On a normal host these self-corrected, harmless slips would go unrecorded and would not count as release usability findings.
- Several slips occur only with Codex-specific tools (functions.exec, apply_patch) or in auto-approved, unattended command chains.

The finding itself says the slips had no effect on results. The release did not cause them, so this is not a product finding. Agent behaviour, recorded only because the study asked for it, is the most precise attribution, which here falls under harness.
verdicts.release_evidence:
These checks found the release behaving correctly. Paths are under SIMS.

- release/analytics-workbench-skills/awb-init/assets/awb_provenance.py, lines 1845-1870: a drop is "resolved against the list before anything changes", and 'if matches[0] not in chosen' silently removes a repeated '--drop 1'. The 'state next' help (lines 2628, 2665) says "resolved before any change", so the retail-B '--drop 1 --drop 1' behaviour is documented and was not a refusal.
- co2-A/relay/agent-007.jsonl: the MCP package export returned "args must be an array of strings" and the agent's retry succeeded. The release's error was clear and nothing was written (agent-notes line 101).
- retail-B/relay: 'awb.py sql --read-only' reported "refused a statement DuckDB cannot plan (Binder Error: Combining QUALIFY with GROUP BY ALL is not supported yet)". The QUALIFY examples in awb-clean/references/correction-views.md do not use GROUP BY ALL.
- No release file contains 'echo =', 'git add -A', 'head -0', or a word-split shell-variable pattern.
- co2-B/feedback/agent-notes.md line 33: "nothing in skills caused it".

These are the agents' own tools or the host shell, not the release:
- taxi-A/relay/agent-007.err: Codex apply_patch "Failed to find expected lines".
- taxi-A agent-notes line 46: Codex functions.exec text() shadowing.
- retail-A agent-notes line 73: functions.exec SyntaxError.
- taxi-B/relay/agent-002.jsonl: zsh "(eval):1: ==== not found" and exit 127 "(eval):2: no such file or directory: python3 src/awb.py questions add".
- taxi-A/relay/agent-001.in.md line 16: the study note telling the agent to keep the private friction log that records all of these slips.

The only release-adjacent nudge is weak. co2-B notes that batching many records adds through MCP (one call each) is clunky, which pushes agents toward shell chains where these zsh mistakes happen.
verdicts.narrowed: Narrower version: in every run the agent made self-corrected command, coding, SQL and editing slips with no effect on results, and none originates in the release. The causes were Codex's functions.exec and apply_patch tools, zsh rules under Claude Code's Bash, DuckDB reserved words and its QUALIFY limitation, BSD head, and git habit. The release's error messages were clear each time. Correction: 'state next --drop 1 --drop 1' was not refused. Repeated drop numbers resolve against the original list and are silently de-duplicated, as the help documents, so the call dropped one item with exit 0. At most a minor ergonomics note follows: the CLI could warn when the same drop target appears twice.

verdicts.reasoning:
The slips all happened as described, give or take one detail below, but nothing in the release causes any of them. Several were stopped or caught by the release's own guards.

Each slip checked:
- **taxi-A agent-007:** the pandas query really used chr(), which raised 'ValueError: "chr" is not a supported function'. That was the agent's own quoting choice.
- **taxi-A agent-007.err:** an apply_patch call failed with 'Failed to find expected lines'. apply_patch is a Codex tool.
- **taxi-A text() shadowing:** the 'text is not a function' error came from the exec_main.mjs helper inside Codex's functions.exec. That belongs to Codex, not the release.
- **taxi-A manifest read:** the agent's ad hoc one-liner in agent-003 read json.loads(publication.json).get("rows") and printed None. No release file documents a 'rows' key in publication.json, so the agent guessed the key.
- **taxi-B and retail-B zsh errors:** "(eval):1: ==== not found" came from 'echo =====' used as a separator, in taxi-B agent-002/005/006 and retail-B agent-005. "no such file or directory: python3 src/awb.py questions add" came from a Q="..." variable that zsh did not word-split (exit 127), in taxi-B agent-002 and retail-B agent-002. No release file contains 'echo =' or such a variable idiom. AGENTS.md line 20 actually tells agents to use the awb MCP tools when the host offers them. Using them would have avoided these shell chains, and these agents had those tools.
- **retail-B agent-003:** the DuckDB errors are its own SQL. One was 'Combining QUALIFY with GROUP BY ALL is not supported yet'. The other was 'share' written as an alias without AS. The QUALIFY examples in correction-views.md are a different, valid pattern. The read-only refusal message was clear.
- **retail-B agent-001:** 'head -0' failed on macOS, which is harmless and has nothing to do with the release.
- **co2-A agent-007:** the agent passed objects such as {result_id, evidence, question} as --result values. The MCP schema in awb_mcp.py declares args as {"type":"array","items":{"type":"string"}}, and awb-package/SKILL.md line 69 documents '--result <id>'. The server refused with 'args must be an array of strings' and the next call succeeded. The release prevented this mistake rather than caused it.
- **co2-B agent-002:** the agent ran 'git add -A && git status --short' and then 'git reset -q'. AGENTS.md line 50 says 'Commit when asked'. The agent's own notes say "nothing in skills caused it", and it obeyed the rule by unstaging.
- **retail-A:** the missed POST code, the misplaced TOML line from apply_patch, and the JS SyntaxError in a Codex functions.exec script are all self-reported agent slips. The 'signed'/'assigned' grep is self-reported at agent-notes line 130, which falls after the cited turns 2-4. None of them trace to release text.

One detail in the finding is wrong. retail-B's 'state next --drop 1 --drop 1' was not refused. awb_provenance.py resolves each drop target against the original list and skips a repeated match ('if matches[0] not in chosen'), so the command dropped one item and exited 0. The tool output shows 'Show the slide headlines...' still under Next steps, and a separate call removed it. The --help epilog states that drops are 'resolved before any change'. The agent expected the drops to apply one after another, which is its own slip, and the release documents the real behaviour.

Overall these are Codex/Claude command habits and tool-specific errors. A real user's agent on a macOS zsh host might make the same ones, but the release is not the cause. Where the release touches them at all, it prevents or catches them.
verdicts.release_evidence:
- **Prevents the co2-A error:** awb-init/assets/awb_mcp.py defines ARGS as {"type":"array","items":{"type":"string"}} ('one array item per argument, exactly as on its command line'). awb-package/SKILL.md line 69 documents '--result <id>'.
- **Prevents co2-B committing:** awb-init/assets/workbench/AGENTS.md line 50 says 'Commit when asked; ...'.
- **Steers away from the shell chains:** AGENTS.md line 20 says 'When the host offers the awb MCP server, use its tools for awb.py commands, and the CLI otherwise'. B-variant agents used shell chains anyway.
- **Documents the --drop behaviour:** in awb-init/assets/awb_provenance.py, the cli_state epilog for issues/next says '--drop takes the item's number in the list or text only one item contains (case-sensitive), resolved before any change'. The state_list code skips a repeated target instead of refusing it ('if matches[0] not in chosen').
- **No cause found in shipped files:** no release file contains 'echo =', a command stored in a shell variable, 'head -0', 'git add', pandas .query/chr usage, or a 'rows' key for publication.json. The QUALIFY examples in awb-clean/references/correction-views.md lines 36-37 are a different, valid pattern from the failing query.
verdicts.narrowed: The release causes none of these slips. They are one-off command and coding mistakes by Codex and Claude, made with the agents' own tools: Codex functions.exec and apply_patch, zsh '=word' expansion and unsplit command variables, DuckDB SQL syntax, ad hoc key guesses, and a habitual git add. Each was recovered from and none affected any result. The release's MCP args schema, its AGENTS.md MCP-preference and commit-when-asked rules, and its documented --drop behaviour prevented or caught several of them. One detail is wrong: retail-B's 'state next --drop 1 --drop 1' was not refused. The helper skips the repeated target, dropped one item and exited 0.

consolidated.title: Helper and MCP outputs are large and repetitive; long status and state results get cut off
consolidated.description: Status, state, check-draft and export repeat full finding texts, ledger_order and whole blocks on every call; in retail-B each export printed about 5k tokens. The draft manifest reached about 80 KB. The awb MCP server cuts results at 16,000 characters and saves the rest to a private temp file. taxi-B lost the questions section of awb-status (5,233 characters) and rebuilt it from questions list. retail-A's saved overflow ended in an 'exit status 0' trailer that broke json.loads. Tool results carry no structured content.
consolidated.caused_by_fix: no for the cap and the trailer, which awb_mcp.py had before the fixes. #104 (issue #93) added questions.by_question and active.caveats to the status payload, which likely helps push it over the cap.
consolidated.evidence: taxi-B-10: awb-init/assets/awb_mcp.py (MAX_CHARS 16000, _clip); relay/agent-004.jsonl; status payload about 16.5 KB per orchestrator-report.md (the referee tagged it unclear). retail-A-13: agent-notes Turn 5 (JSONDecodeError: Extra data, char 16410); structured_content null in relay/agent-009.jsonl; awb_mcp.py line 500. retail-A-14: release 001 manifest.json is 80,562 bytes. retail-B-21: agent.md section 5; agent-005 ran 3 exports and 5 check-drafts. co2-B-24: status and check-draft results in relay/agent-002.jsonl to agent-006.jsonl. taxi-A-23: long state and status reads truncated.

verdicts.reasoning:
I looked for a harness cause and found none for the core problem. The 16,000-character cut comes from the release's own MCP server. awb_mcp.py sets MAX_CHARS from AWB_MCP_MAX_CHARS with a default of 16000 (line 72). _clip (lines 464-472) keeps the head and a 2,000-character tail and saves the full text to a mkdtemp directory. The harness never sets AWB_MCP_MAX_CHARS: claude-mcp.json passes only HOME, and the Codex config.toml passes no env. Neither host would have cut these results on its own. A status of about 21 KB is well under Claude Code's own MCP output limit, so a real user on an interactive host gets exactly the same clipping.

I measured every awb MCP result in all six runs. read state and read status were clipped 9 times in taxi-A, once in taxi-B (status, 21,230 characters total, 5,233 cut) and 6 times in retail-A. Saved overflow files for state run 16-20 KB. A taxi-A state output is the brief plus the current state. With 16,000 kept, the cut falls in the middle of 'Current findings' and 'Unresolved issues'. A clipped status JSON is not valid JSON inline either. The read tool has no section or compact mode for state or status (only eda-show takes a section), so the agent cannot narrow the request.

retail-A's json.loads failure also comes from the release. execute() joins stdout, stderr and 'exit status N' (lines 497-501), and _clip writes that whole text to the file. The status JSON (16,408 characters) is therefore followed by a blank line and 'exit status 0', which matches 'Extra data: line 3 column 1 (char 16410)'. Every result is built by _text() with content only, so structured_content: None in the Codex log is how the server always behaves. This much is documented ('Results are plain text').

Parts the harness caused or the finding overstates:
- **taxi-B's lost questions section.** This comes from the harness. The overflow file landed in /tmp/awb-mcp-…, and the sim system prompt forbids reads outside the sim folders. The agent says it could not read the file for that reason. On a real host, the agent would read the named file, perhaps after a permission prompt.
- **Export size.** retail-B's exports are about 9-10K characters each (roughly 2.5-3k tokens, not 5k). They do repeat all of methodology_lines on every call.
- **check-draft size.** check-draft results are only 1.9-4.3K characters, which is not large.
- **Manifest size.** Manifests are 50-80 KB in every run. However, the only manifest truncation came from Codex's own output cap on the agent's `cat` of the whole file. The agent called that read its own poor choice.
verdicts.release_evidence:
- **Server code:** release/analytics-workbench-skills/awb-init/assets/awb_mcp.py line 72 sets `MAX_CHARS = max(1000, int(os.environ.get("AWB_MCP_MAX_CHARS") or 16000))`. Lines 464-472 (_clip) save the full text to `_private_dir()` (mkdtemp). Lines 497-501 add 'exit status N' to the text before _clip saves it, so the trailer lands in the file. `_text()` returns `{"content":[text], "isError"}` and never sets structuredContent. The read tool's state and status commands take no section or compact arguments (lines 362-397).
- **Harness configs:** taxi-B/agent-home/claude-mcp.json and retail-A/agent-home/.codex/config.toml do not override AWB_MCP_MAX_CHARS.
- **Measured clips:** read state/status results came back clipped (LEN about 15,997) in taxi-A agent-005 to agent-009 (9 times), taxi-B agent-004 (1), and retail-A agent-005 to agent-009 (6).
- **Saved overflow files:** under {taxi-A,retail-A}/agent-home/.cache/tmp/awb-mcp-*, 16-20 KB each.
- **json.loads failure:** retail-A relay/agent-005.jsonl shows `json.loads` failing on read-status-e9270bbe.txt, which `raw_decode` then recovered.
- **taxi-B status:** relay/agent-004.jsonl shows '[... 5233 characters cut; the full output is in /tmp/awb-mcp-9t4d6u08/…]'. feedback/agent.md item 2 says the file was 'outside my allowed paths', which is the boundary set in kit/claude-agent-system.md.
- **retail-B exports:** relay/agent-005.jsonl export results are 9,061, 10,000, 10,156 and 2,577 characters, each carrying the full methodology_lines.
- **check-draft (co2-B):** results are about 1.9-2.6K characters.
- **Manifests:** released/001/manifest.json sizes are 50-80 KB in every run (retail-A 80,562 bytes).
verdicts.narrowed:
The awb MCP server cuts every result at its own 16,000-character default. On projects of the size simulated here (5 root questions, about 11 findings), read state (brief plus state, 16-20 KB) and read status (16-21 KB of JSON) regularly go over that limit. The cut removes part of the findings and issues sections, and a clipped status is no longer valid JSON. Neither command has a section or compact option, so the agent cannot ask for less. The saved overflow file holds the raw text with the 'exit status N' line (and any stderr) appended, so json.loads fails on it. Tool results carry no structuredContent. Export results are about 10K characters and repeat all of methodology_lines on every call.

Not supported as a release defect:
- taxi-B losing the questions section: the harness's path boundary blocked reading the overflow file, which is readable on a real host.
- check-draft being 'large': its results are 2-4K characters.
- The 5k-tokens-per-export figure: the real size is about 2.5-3k tokens.
- Manifest size as a cut-off problem: the only truncation came from the Codex host's cap when the agent ran cat on the whole file.

verdicts.reasoning:
The release causes the core of this finding. The cited run evidence holds up, though a few details are overstated.

1. The status helper duplicates its own content. collect_status.py builds active.findings at line 262, then at lines 269-270 builds active.caveats as {finding, status, caveat: reason} for every finding that has a reason. That repeats each full finding text and its reason a second time. In taxi-B's saved status output, all 11 caveats repeat their finding text (about 8.2k + 7.9k characters).

2. The release's own MCP server clips the release's own status output. awb_mcp.py sets MAX_CHARS = 16000 (line 72). _clip (lines 464-472) keeps the head and tail and saves the full text to a private mkdtemp directory. At normal investigation sizes (11-14 findings, about 19 questions), status ran 16.4k-21.1k characters and state about 17.8k, so they were cut. The relay logs show the server's own "[... N characters cut; the full output is in .../awb-mcp-*/...]" note:
   - taxi-B agent-004: status cut by 5,233 characters out of a 21,111-character total.
   - taxi-A agent-005 to 009: every state and status read was cut.
   - retail-A agent-005 to 009: state and status were cut.

3. The saved overflow file is not valid JSON, and the release causes this. execute() appends "exit status N" at line 500 before clipping, so the saved file is the JSON followed by "\n\nexit status 0". I confirmed json.loads fails on retail-A's saved file with "Extra data: line 3 column 1 (char 16410)", which matches the agent's note. The retail-A referee blamed the Codex host for the truncation and the trailer. That is wrong: the file sits in the awb-mcp-* directory that _private_dir creates.

4. Tool results carry no structured content: _text returns only content plus isError, and Codex logs show structured_content None. This is true, but it is a missing feature rather than a failure.

5. Export repeats a large block on every call. export reprints methodology_lines (about 6.3k characters) every time, and awb-package SKILL.md step 4 says to run export "on every revision". check-draft reprints ledger_order (about 1.3k characters) on every call.

6. No release document mentions AWB_MCP_MAX_CHARS or how to handle cut output, so nothing in the release prevents this.

Overstatements and harness factors:
- retail-B exports were 9-10k characters each, about 2.5-3k tokens, not about 5k tokens.
- check-draft results are modest at 2-5k characters.
- taxi-B could not recover the cut middle only because the sim's path boundary blocked /tmp. That part is harness. On a normal host the agent could read the file, at the cost of an extra step or a permission prompt.
- The 50-80 KB manifests are real (retail-A release 001 is 80,562 bytes; analytical_settings alone is 28.8k). But they only hurt when an agent reads the whole file with cat. The release does not tell it to, and the retail-A agent called its own whole-manifest read a poor choice.
- Sessions are resumed across turns, so repeated state reads are not caused by harness context resets.
- The evidence IDs cited in the finding (taxi-B-10, retail-A-13/14, retail-B-21, taxi-A-23) do not match the runs' findings.json. The matching entries are taxi-B-07, retail-A-11, retail-B-18, taxi-A-13 and co2-B-24.

Severity minor is right: agents recovered each time, at extra tool calls and context.
verdicts.release_evidence:
- awb-init/assets/awb_mcp.py:
  - line 72: MAX_CHARS = max(1000, int(os.environ.get("AWB_MCP_MAX_CHARS") or 16000))
  - lines 464-472: _clip saves the full text to _private_dir() and keeps head + 2000-character tail.
  - line 500: parts.append(f"exit status {process.returncode}") runs before _clip, so the saved overflow file ends in "exit status 0".
  - line 504: _text returns only content and isError, with no structuredContent.
- awb-status/scripts/collect_status.py:
  - line 262: visible_findings includes the full finding text and reason.
  - lines 269-270: active.caveats = [{"finding": f["finding"], "status": ..., "caveat": f["reason"]} ...], which duplicates every finding.
  - lines 1063-1065: no compact or summary option.
- awb-status/SKILL.md says to run status through the awb MCP tools when the host offers them.
- awb-package/SKILL.md step 4: "Export ... with `export` on every revision". helpers.md line 53: export prints methodology_lines.
- awb-package/assets/awb_draft.py lines 2653-2663 build ledger_order, which check-draft prints on every call. Only review-receipt show budgets its output to _READ_LIMIT 16000 (line 4836).
- No .md file in the release mentions AWB_MCP_MAX_CHARS or how to read cut output.

Run evidence I verified:
- taxi-B/relay/agent-004.jsonl: status result 15,997 characters with "[... 5233 characters cut ...]". The saved /tmp/awb-mcp-9t4d6u08/...read-status file is 21,111 characters, fails json.loads at char 21098, and its trailer is '\n\nexit status 0'.
- retail-A/agent-home/.cache/tmp/awb-mcp-wvwye0kf/...read-status-e9270bbe.txt fails json.loads with "Extra data: line 3 column 1 (char 16410)".
- retail-A relay agent-005: results have structured_content None.
- taxi-A agent-005 to 009: state and status reads cut.
- retail-B agent-005: exports of 9,061, 10,000, 10,156 and 2,577 characters; check-drafts of about 2.5k characters, about 1.3k of it ledger_order.
- Manifests: retail-A release 001 is 80,562 bytes; others are 50-77 KB.
verdicts.narrowed:
In a normal-sized investigation (about 11-14 findings, about 19 questions), the release's status helper returns 16-21k characters. About half of that is repetition: every finding's text and reason appears again under active.caveats. The release's own awb MCP server cuts results at 16,000 characters, so status (and, by turn 5, state) arrives with its middle missing; in taxi-B the cut middle held the questions section. The full text is saved to a temp file that ends with an "exit status N" trailer, so json.loads fails on it. export reprints about 6k characters of methodology_lines on every revision, and check-draft reprints ledger_order each time. Overstated or harness parts:
- retail-B exports were about 2.5-3k tokens each, not 5k.
- check-draft output is modest.
- taxi-B could not read the overflow file only because of the sim's path boundary; on a normal host the agent could read it with an extra step.
- The 80 KB manifest only costs context when an agent reads the whole file, which the release does not instruct.
- The missing structuredContent is a feature gap, not a defect.

consolidated.title: Headline preview is saved in a hidden .preview folder that export has not created yet
consolidated.description: #103 gave the preview a defined location, but it is a dot-folder that Finder hides. The users never opened the file they were asked to review and relied on the chat copy (taxi-A, co2-A, retail-A). The checkpoint also writes .preview/headlines.md 'in the draft folder' before export, and export is the step that creates that folder, so the Claude agents created it by hand (co2-B, retail-B).
consolidated.caused_by_fix: yes: #103 (issue #90) put the preview at draft/.preview/headlines.md (awb-package/SKILL.md:49; awb_draft.py PREVIEW = '.preview'), while export, a later step, creates the draft folder.
consolidated.evidence: taxi-A-07: replies 6 and 8; human/notes.md turns 7 and 9. co2-A-09: r5; feedback/human.md pain point 6. retail-A-29: reply 6; notes.md turn 7. co2-B-11: 'mkdir -p .../draft/.preview' in relay/agent-003.jsonl. retail-B-16: an agent-003 Write before any export. Release: awb-package/SKILL.md:49 and step 4.

verdicts.reasoning:
The finding has two halves, and neither shows harm to a user.

1) "Users never opened the hidden file they were asked to review" (taxi-A, co2-A, retail-A).
- The evidence contradicts this for co2-A. The co2-A human notes (turn 6) say "I opened the preview file it linked; it's readable". Pain point 6 in co2-A/feedback/human.md says "I could open it from the link, but I'd never have found it browsing the folder."
- In taxi-A and retail-A the simulated users chose not to open the file because the headlines were already in chat ("luckily headlines were in chat"; "I didn't open it, the chat list was enough").
- Chat is where the release puts them. awb-package/SKILL.md:49 writes the headlines to the file and also says to "show them" in chat with their figures. taxi-A agent-006 did exactly that: a link, then the full list of headlines inline. The user was never asked to open the file to review it.
- The "Finder hides it" complaint is the persona's guess. The simulated humans are models reading through tools; none tried Finder or failed to find the file. kit/human-rules.md also steers them to open files "only when a real user would", which pushes them toward relying on chat. That is a harness influence on "never opened".
- The README names the target hosts as VS Code Copilot, Claude Code and Codex. Links in their chats open the file directly, and VS Code's file explorer shows dot-folders by default. Finder visibility is not the surface these users would use.
- The dot-folder is deliberate: CHANGELOG line 173 says the inventory, check-draft and release all skip `.preview`.

2) "export has not created the draft folder yet, so the agents created it by hand" (co2-B, retail-B).
- The text inconsistency is real. Step 4 says export "creates the draft folder", yet step 3 writes into that folder first.
- That is true in every mode, not only for the preview. Step 3 writes findings.md and methodology.md at the contract's draft/ paths before export, and awb_draft.py's `_NO_DRAFT` message itself says "write findings.md and methodology.md there, then run export". Export only runs `draft.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)`.
- It cost nothing. co2-B chained `mkdir -p .../draft/.preview && cat > ...` in one Bash call with no error. retail-B used a single Write call, which creates parent folders itself, with no error. Neither run spent an extra turn or showed the user anything.
- It surfaced only because the agent prompt asks agents to log friction in agent-notes.md and agent.md.

So the claimed user-facing impact is not supported. What survives is a cosmetic wording inconsistency in the agent instructions. The release causes it, but it is agent-only, costs nothing, and no real user would encounter it.
verdicts.release_evidence: awb-package/SKILL.md:49: preview-and-wait writes `.preview/headlines.md` "in the draft folder" and says to "show them" in chat. SKILL.md:17 (step 4): "export on every revision, which creates the draft folder". SKILL.md:58 and references/package-contract.md lines 7-20: findings.md and methodology.md are also written at draft/ paths before export. assets/awb_draft.py line 50: `_NO_DRAFT = "no draft at {}; write findings.md and methodology.md there, then run export"`. Line 3857: `draft.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)`. CHANGELOG.md:173: `.preview` is intentionally skipped by the inventory, check-draft and release. Run evidence: co2-A/human/notes.md turn 6 and co2-A/feedback/human.md item 6 (the user opened the file via the link). taxi-A/relay/agent-006.last.md (link plus all headlines in chat). taxi-A/human/notes.md lines 42 and 54, and retail-A/human/notes.md line 54 (users relied on chat; no failed attempt to open the file). co2-B relay agent-003 (`mkdir -p ... && cat >`, no error). retail-B relay agent-003 (one Write call to draft/.preview/headlines.md, no error).
verdicts.narrowed: The awb-package SKILL.md step 4 says export "creates the draft folder", but step 3 already writes into it: the preview's `.preview/headlines.md` and, in every mode, findings.md and methodology.md. So agents always create the folder themselves before export. Two Claude agents (co2-B, retail-B) noted the ordering and absorbed it with one mkdir or Write call, with no error and no effect on the user. This is a cosmetic, agent-only wording fix (say the agent's first write creates the folder), not a problem a user would hit. The hidden `.preview` location caused no observed failure. The headlines are shown in chat by design, and the one user who clicked the link (co2-A) opened the file without trouble.

verdicts.reasoning:
Neither half of C-19 holds up as a problem a user would hit.

1. Hidden dot-folder. awb-package/SKILL.md:49 has the agent write `.preview/headlines.md` and "show them with the figures behind each headline" in chat. The release never asks the user to open or browse to the file. The folder is a dot-folder on purpose, so check-draft and release skip it (awb_draft.py:46-48, :1802, :5185). The runs show the design working.
- taxi-A reply 6 lists all eight headlines in chat and asks for approval there. The human's notes say the chat list was enough.
- taxi-A reply 8 links `.preview/revisions-before-release.md`. The agent made that file up; nothing in the release asks for it. The changed slides were shown in chat anyway.
- retail-A reply 6 lists the headlines in chat. Notes turn 7 say "I didn't open it, the chat list was enough", and the human's feedback does not list it as a pain point.
- co2-A contradicts "users never opened the file". Notes turn 6 say "I opened the preview file it linked; it's readable", and feedback pain point 6 says "I could open it from the link, but I'd never have found it browsing the folder." What remains is a cosmetic remark that the file is hidden in Finder for someone who browses instead of clicking the link. That user only went to the file because the agent put chart plans and caveats there, beyond the chat copy the skill specifies.

2. The draft folder does not exist before export. SKILL.md:17 says export "creates the draft folder", yet step 3 writes into that folder before step 4. That is true of the first-pass findings.md and methodology.md as well as the preview (CHANGELOG:172). So the agent writes into a folder that does not exist yet on every first draft, preview or not. export uses `mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)` (awb_draft.py:3857), so creating the folder early is harmless.
- co2-B agent-003 created it with one `mkdir -p ... && cat >` command.
- retail-B agent-003 used the Write tool, which creates parent folders itself.
- No errors in either run, and nothing reached the user. The Claude agents in co2-B, retail-B and taxi-B logged it only as an ordering ambiguity in their agent notes.

Overall, the cited evidence shows the chat-first preview working as designed. One cited user did open the file without trouble. The folder-ordering point is a small wording mismatch that costs the agent one mkdir.

verdicts.reasoning:
I could not find a harness cause. Every flagged item comes from deterministic code in the release's awb_draft.py, and that code reacts only to the text of the draft or rule. Sandbox, relay, auto-approval, simulated home, persona and study disclosure play no part in that path.

All five runs used the release helper unchanged: the sha256 of each project's src/packaging/draft.py matches the release's awb_draft.py (b47e81a9...). I copied the module to scratchpad/verify-C20 and ran check_numbers and _quantities on the finding's examples. Each result matched what the sims reported:
- '21:00/22:00/23:00' is reported as joined digits. The 24-hour-time skip uses _ALONE, which refuses a time followed by '/digit'.
- In '5.6439%/6.6888%' the first % is dropped. The _NUMBER lookahead fails on '%/6', so 5.6439 is read as a bare number and does not trace. '5.64/6.69%' also reads 5.64 bare.
- 'divided by 1000000000' is reported as untraced. Export's _sources (line 3716) writes this text into methodology_lines, and helpers.md says those lines are meant for methodology.md. So two released helpers contradict each other.
- 'uci-20261017' gives 20261017. _identifier treats an all-lowercase first part as a word, so the ID is not blanked.
- 'after these 2024 files' is read as a count.
- review-rules add uses _RULE_NUMBER (line 4069), a bare digit-run regex, on both the rule and the draft. That is why 'CO2' gives '2' at findings.md:1 (co2-B agent-006), years appear for the retail-A source rule (agent-009), and 'payment code 0' triggers at findings.md:43 (taxi-B agent-006/008).
- co2-A agent-006 check-draft returned a name row for 'coal-share' at findings.md:94. That is a result ID that also appeared in prose ('largest coal-share drop'). The plain-word exemption covers only [A-Za-z]+, so hyphenated words are still names.

The draft text that triggers these flags is ordinary notation a real agent on an interactive host would write: compact time lists, percent pairs, pasted methodology_lines, dated acquisition IDs, slug-style result IDs reused as prose. Relaying the warning to the user in co2-B was model behaviour, but the warning itself is the release's.

Some parts are known trade-offs rather than surprises:
- helpers.md documents the year-as-count rule, the slash-pair unit rule and the "fails safe" stance.
- A code comment says the review-rules number warning over-warns on purpose, and it is only advisory.
- In retail-A the rule really did repeat the draft's years, which is the case the warning targets.
- Some taxi-A rewrites only lowered precision, for example 3.6337% to 3.6%. They were not all false positives.
- In taxi-A the % sign was on both values, not only the second.

None of this makes it a harness effect.

verdicts.narrowed:
This is a product issue, with a few details corrected.

The numbers check misreads compact notation:
- Slash-joined 24-hour times are reported as joined digits.
- In a slash-joined percent pair, the first value is read without its % even when the % is written. In taxi-A the % was on both values.
- A year after a word such as 'these' is read as a count.
- A date inside an all-lowercase hyphenated ID (uci-20261017) is read as a number.

The check also rejects the 'divided by <n>' text that export writes into methodology_lines for methodology.md. That is a real contradiction between two helpers.

The name check flags a hyphenated result ID ('coal-share') when the same phrase appears in prose.

review-rules add warns on any shared digit run, including the 2 in 'CO2' and 'code 0'. The release does this on purpose and documents it, and the warning is only advisory. The retail-A years were the case it is meant for, not a pure false positive.

Some of the taxi-A rewrites lowered real precision rather than fixing false positives.

verdicts.reasoning:
Every sub-claim traces to shipped code in awb-package/assets/awb_draft.py. I ran the shipped functions on the cited strings, read-only, from a script in the scratchpad.

1. Percent pairs. check_numbers reads 'JFK 5.6439%/6.6888%' as an unitless 5.6439 followed by 6.6888%. The _NUMBER regex's trailing lookahead `(?![...]|[.,/:][0-9])` sees '/6' after the first '%', so it backtracks and drops the unit. When the record holds fractions, the first value then fails to trace (_untraced returns 'value'); written with its % it traces. helpers.md:44 documents only the '368/53.5%' form, where the first value carries no unit. The taxi-A text had a % on both values, so this is an undocumented parsing bug. The finding's wording ('% only on the second value') understates it.

2. Slash-joined times. '21:00/22:00/23:00' is reported as a 'joined' number. The 24-hour-time skip in _NOT_QUANTITY carries a lookbehind that excludes times after a slash. This matches the documented fail-safe ('any other join ... is reported').

3. Years. 'after these 2024 files' and 'historical 2024 rule text' are read as counts. This is documented (helpers.md:45-47); the remedy is to reword or use allowed_numbers.

4. Export's scale text. _sources() (awb_draft.py:3704-3720) writes ', divided by 1000000000' into methodology_lines. SKILL.md step 4/line 71 and methodology-template.md tell the agent to paste those lines into methodology.md. recorded_values adds the scaled values but never the divisor itself, so the helper's own output fails check-draft. co2-B agent-004 shows numbers rows at methodology.md:86-87 for '1000000000', and the agent had to add allowed_numbers 'divided by 1000000000'.

5. Acquisition ID. 'online-retail-ii/uci-20261017' is not blanked: it is not a path, and the hyphenated-identifier rule skips a lowercase word prefix ('uci'). So 20261017 is read. retail-A agent-007 shows the row at methodology.md:28; the agent fixed it with allowed_numbers 'uci-20261017'.

6. Name check. project_names keeps result IDs and excludes only letters-only names (helpers.md:27, awb_draft.py:59). The hyphenated ID 'coal-share' therefore matches the prose 'ten largest coal-share declines' (co2-A agent-006, findings.md:94). findings rows fail check-draft (_structure_passed requires findings == []).

7. review-rules add. _RULE_NUMBER `(?<![0-9])[0-9]+...` (awb_draft.py:4069) has no letter lookbehind, so it extracts '2' from 'CO2'. It also extracts '0' from 'payment code 0' and 2009/2011 from a source label. A code comment admits the over-warning is deliberate. The cited warnings appear in co2-B agent-006 (findings.md:1), taxi-B agent-006 (findings.md:43) and retail-A agent-009. co2-B relayed the warning to the user ('Its warning about the number 2 is spurious').

Nothing in the release prevents these cases. No agent ignored an instruction; each used the documented remedies. All of this is deterministic helper behavior, so any interactive user would hit it. Minor severity is right: the warnings never block, the draft rows are cleared by rewording or allowed_numbers, and the cost is friction.

Run evidence: taxi-A relay/agent-007.jsonl check-draft numbers rows (methodology.md:21 '2024' x2, :45 '21:00/22:00/23:00', :51 '5.6439'/'4.0830'/'0.2374', :59 '08:00/09:00'/'18:00/19:00', :61/:71 first members of slash-joined percent pairs); project/.workbench-tmp/repair_board_wording.py shows the rewrites; co2-B relay/agent-004.jsonl numbers rows for '1000000000' and allowed_numbers 'divided by 1000000000'; co2-A relay/agent-006.jsonl findings row line 94 'coal-share'; retail-A relay/agent-007.jsonl row methodology.md:28 '20261017' and manifest allowed_numbers 'uci-20261017'; co2-B agent-006 warning 'the rule names 2' plus its out.md relaying it; taxi-B agent-006 'the rule names 0'; retail-A agent-009 'the rule names 2009/2011'.
verdicts.narrowed: The finding holds as stated, with one correction to its first bullet. The real percent defect is in 'X%/Y%' with a % on both values: the shipped helper drops the first value's own %, so it fails to trace against a fraction. That is an undocumented parsing bug, not the documented 'unit after the second belongs to it alone' rule. The clear defects are: (a) that X%/Y% bug; (b) export's own methodology_lines text ('divided by 1000000000'), which SKILL.md says to paste into methodology.md, fails check-draft's numbers check; (c) review-rules add pulls digits out of words such as 'CO2'; (d) the name check fails a draft over a hyphenated, word-like result ID used as ordinary prose ('coal-share'). The other cases are documented fail-safe design with a documented remedy (reword or allowed_numbers), but they are still friction the release causes: slash-joined 24-hour times, a year used as an adjective ('these 2024 files'), the date inside 'uci-20261017', and rule warnings for 'payment code 0' and source-label years.

consolidated.title: Agent-facing instructions conflict or leave gaps the agent must resolve alone
consolidated.description:
Agents met several small conflicts and gaps:
- taxi-A: awb-clean says a cleaning pass reads neither workbench guide, while AGENTS.md requires data.md before first publication.
- taxi-B: no answerer value for documentation lookups; no rule for the 'user's words' of sub-questions the user never phrased; unclear whether the preview may be written before the first export; unclear whether to offer a review rule before a draft exists.
- retail-A: awb-package asks which datasets to include and whether a methods note is needed even after the user has said.
- retail-A: the rule to treat helpers as black boxes seemed to forbid reading run.py (arguably a misreading).
- retail-B: no record for standing working preferences, so it invented a 'Project conventions' section in AGENTS.md.
- co2-B: unclear whether to go on from analysis into awb-package when the user had asked for headlines first.

Each was resolved without harm. Tag: retail-A-34 and co2-B-40 are unclear; the other members are product, and the gaps are in shipped text.
consolidated.caused_by_fix: no
consolidated.evidence: taxi-A-26: reply 3; agent-notes line 27. taxi-B-26: feedback/agent.md section 2; questions.md Q-008 recorded with answerer stakeholder; awb_provenance.py _ANSWERERS. retail-A-31: msg 1, msg 6, reply 6; awb-package/SKILL.md step 1 (Establish). retail-A-34: agent.md section 2. retail-B-22: reply 7; 'Project conventions' in the project's AGENTS.md. co2-B-40: A2 'Decision for you'; agent-notes turn 2.

verdicts.reasoning:
I looked for a harness cause and did not find one. Each gap traces to wording in the shipped release, and an agent on a normal interactive host would read the same text.

Harness causes I checked:
- **Non-interactive turns.** Running each turn through codex exec or claude -p does not create any of these gaps. An interactive agent would also have to settle them while it works.
- **Sandbox, auto-approved MCP tools, relay.** The Codex sandbox, the auto-approved MCP tools and the relay play no part in any member.
- **Personas front-loading answers.** This triggered retail-A-31: the user said "no tables, I want the methods note" before being asked. Real users do the same, and the skill tells the agent to ask anyway.
- **Simulated home in retail-B.** The run used `--setting-sources project,local`, so user-level memory was missing. That could change where the preference got written. It does not change that the workbench names no place to record a standing preference.
- **Study disclosure.** This is the strongest harness factor. The prompt asked agents to log anything "confusing, contradictory, missing", and most of the evidence comes from those logs. That makes small gaps easier to spot. It does not create them, and it means the user-visible effect is close to zero.

Members confirmed in shipped text:
- **taxi-A.** awb-clean line 10 says "a cleaning pass reads neither guide". It also lists a landed acquisition as a target, and its correction-views publish branch publishes data. AGENTS.md says to read data.md before "publishing data". The agent read data.md for first publication (agent-notes line 27).
- **taxi-B, answerer value.** `_ANSWERERS = ("user", "stakeholder", "data")`. Only a result can answer a data question, and the other two need a text answer with `--by` naming who gave it. Q-008 ended up answered by the "NYC TLC data dictionary" under the answerer `stakeholder`.
- **taxi-B, user's words.** analysis.md and the settings.toml comments require each result's question "in the user's own words, never paraphrased". There is no rule for sub-questions the user never phrased. settings.toml shows fragments used as questions, e.g. "keep the possible Newark rate-code trips as a caveat or sensitivity check".
- **taxi-B, preview before export.** awb-package puts the preview at `.preview/headlines.md` inside the draft folder, but step 4 says `export` creates that folder. The agent created the folder by hand.
- **taxi-B, review rule before a draft.** The offer to save a review rule is triggered only by correcting a draft. Corrections made before a draft exists are not covered; retail-B's notes hit the same gap.
- **retail-A-31.** awb-package step 1 tells the agent to ask which datasets to include, and to ask about the methods note when the request mentions one. Both read as unconditional, even after the user has answered.
- **retail-B-22.** No skill or template names a home for standing working preferences, so the agent added "Project conventions" to AGENTS.md. It justified this with "Existing project conventions win".

Weaker members, matching the finding's "unclear" tag:
- **retail-A-34.** AGENTS.md routes run.py through `run` next to the helpers, then says to treat helpers as black boxes and "open one's source only to adapt or debug it". awb-package's gather step says to read run.py. That is a plausible ambiguity but an arguable misreading.
- **co2-B-40.** awb-init line 44 says to invoke awb-package after initialization if the user explicitly asks for a package. Elsewhere packages follow on request after scoping and analysis. This is partly a judgment about the conversation itself, and the agent's choice to stop and ask was correct.

Severity minor stands. Every member was resolved correctly and none cost the user anything beyond at most one extra round trip.

All paths are under the release folder:
