verdicts.narrowed:
The finding holds as minor, and the release text is the cause. Seven small gaps are confirmed in the shipped text:
1. awb-clean says a cleaning pass reads neither guide, while AGENTS.md requires data.md before any pass that publishes, whether a first publication or the correction-views publish branch.
2. The answerer list has no value for a lookup the agent does in documentation.
3. Each result's question must be in "the user's own words, never paraphrased", with no rule for sub-questions the user never phrased.
4. The headline preview path sits inside a draft folder that only `export` creates.
5. The offer to save a review rule covers only corrections to a draft.
6. awb-package step 1 asks about datasets and the methods note unconditionally.
7. No record is named for standing working preferences.

retail-A-34 (whether run.py counts as a black-box helper) and co2-B-40 (whether to go on into awb-package) are weaker. They are plausible ambiguities but partly the agents' own judgment calls. Most members were surfaced only because the study prompt asked for a friction log. Every one was resolved correctly, so the user-visible effect is near zero.

verdicts.reasoning:
I read the shipped files and the cited evidence. Most members trace to real gaps or wording conflicts in the shipped text. Three members do not hold up.

Members that hold:
- taxi-A. awb-clean/SKILL.md line 10 says "a cleaning pass reads neither guide". The project AGENTS.md tells the agent to read data.md before publishing data or editing foundation/views/, and gives no exception for awb-clean. A cleaning pass edits foundation/views/ in step 3 and can publish through the publish branch in correction-views.md, so the two texts conflict. In taxi-A the agent saw the tension and read data.md for the first publication (agent-notes line 27), which was correct. The user had asked to "bring in" the files and clean them.
- taxi-B, answerer. awb_provenance.py has `_ANSWERERS = ("user", "stakeholder", "data")`, and `questions answer --by` expects a person. Nothing fits a fact the agent looks up in documentation. Q-008 was recorded as answerer stakeholder, answered by "NYC TLC data dictionary". awb-scope says to answer quick lookups yourself, but it does not say how to record one that later analysis relies on.
- taxi-B, user's words. The settings.toml comments and analysis.md require each result's question "in the user's own words, never paraphrased". Nothing covers derived checks the user never phrased. The newark-rate-sensitivity result ended up with a fragment that is not a question ("keep the possible Newark rate-code trips as a caveat or sensitivity check"), and check-draft requires methodology.md to repeat it word for word.
- taxi-B, review rule before a draft. awb-package step 1 and AGENTS.md only describe offering a review rule for a correction to an existing draft. They say nothing about a correction the user gives before any draft exists.
- taxi-B, preview before export (co2-B notes line 56 report the same). awb-package/SKILL.md says export "creates the draft folder". Step 3 writes the preview and findings.md into that folder before export runs. The step order resolves it, so this is a phrasing tension only.
- retail-A, repeated questions. awb-package step 1 asks for the dataset selection on every new package without exception. It also says "When it or the request mentions a methods note, ask whether the audience needs" one, which by its own wording fires exactly when the user has already asked for the note. The user asked for the note in msg 1 and said "no tables" plus a one-page note in msg 6. The agent sensibly did not ask again (reply 6; agent.md line 25).

Members that fail:
- retail-A-34. The README defines helpers as the code under src/. The investigation's run.py is the investigation's own code, adapted from a template, and awb-package Gather tells the agent to read run.py and producers/. The black-box rule does not cover it, so this is a misreading. The finding itself calls it arguably a misreading.
- co2-B-40. awb-init and awb-scope say packages follow on request. The user's latest message asked to "proceed with the five questions". Offering the headline preview, as the agent did, matches the shipped text. The doubt was about what the user meant, not a gap in the text.
- retail-B-22. The release names no record for standing working preferences. But the AGENTS.md text ("Existing project conventions win") already expects project conventions, and adding them to AGENTS.md is what any host would normally do. This is at most a nominal gap with no cost.

None of these caused harm, and severity is minor.

- taxi-A feedback/agent-notes.md line 27.
- co2-B feedback/agent-notes.md line 56: the same preview-ordering ambiguity.
- retail-B project AGENTS.md lines 54-57: the agent-added "Project conventions" section.
verdicts.narrowed:
Shipped agent-facing text has a handful of small conflicts and gaps that agents resolved unaided, without harm:
1. AGENTS.md tells the agent to read the data guide before publishing data or editing foundation/views/. awb-clean says a cleaning pass reads neither guide, and AGENTS.md has no exception for it.
2. The question ledger has no answerer value for facts looked up in documentation (_ANSWERERS is user, stakeholder, data).
3. A result's `question` must be the user's own words, with no rule for derived sensitivity or check results the user never phrased.
4. awb-package step 1 always asks for the dataset selection, and asks whether a methods note is needed precisely when the request already mentions one.
5. The review-rule offer covers only corrections to an existing draft.
6. awb-package says export "creates the draft folder", while step 3 writes the headline preview and narratives there first.

Excluded: the run.py black-box reading (retail-A-34) is a misreading; the co2-B question of whether to go on into packaging comes from user intent, not the text; and the retail-B "Project conventions" section is a nominal gap, since AGENTS.md is the normal home for standing preferences. consolidated.title: End-of-turn status line: undefined before a ledger exists, ignores open decisions, next step names no actor
consolidated.description: The AGENTS.md footer rule does not cover the init turn, before any ledger exists, so co2-B and retail-B improvised 'none recorded yet' and 'not yet recorded'. The trigger, 'changed workbench records', is ambiguous: co2-B's release turn changed records and ended without the line. taxi-B's footer said '5 answered (provisional), 0 open' while the user's decision on the tip population was still pending. co2-A's 'next: build the PowerPoint from the package' left it unclear who would build it. Tag: co2-A-22 is unclear; the other members are product.
consolidated.caused_by_fix: partly: #102 (issue #86) made the footer count answered (provisional), but it still counts only ledger roots and leaves out open decision sub-questions.
consolidated.evidence: taxi-B-17: reply 3 closing line; feedback/human.md section 3. co2-A-22: r6 footer; human/notes.md turn 7. co2-B-21: A1 last line; A6 has no line after review-rules add and state next --drop. retail-B-31: reply 1 final line; agent-notes turn 1. Release: awb-init/assets/workbench/AGENTS.md Conversation (footer rule).

verdicts.reasoning:
I looked for a harness cause and found none that explains the behavior. The footer comes from the agent's own reply text. Nothing about how the turns were run touches it: not non-interactive execution, the sandbox, auto-approved MCP, the simulated home, or the relay. In every Claude-agent run the rule was in context, because each turn of co2-B, taxi-B and retail-B ends with the line (co2-B's release turn being the one exception).

1. Init turn, before any ledger exists. All six runs wrote a turn-1 line, and each worded it differently: "not yet recorded" (taxi-B, retail-B), "none recorded yet" (co2-B), "captured, none answered" (taxi-A), "5 open" (co2-A), "remain open" (retail-A). The agent notes in co2-B and retail-B say they guessed. Init writes README and sources.md, so the rule does apply to that turn, but it gives no wording for the case with no ledger. The friction-log disclosure only made the agents write the doubt down; the inconsistent wording would appear either way. User impact is close to nil, because every version was plain and correct.

2. Ambiguous trigger. This part is weak. co2-B A6 did change records (review-rules add, state next --drop, release) and ended without the line. But taxi-A, taxi-B, co2-A, retail-A and retail-B all ended their release turns with it. One omission in six release turns is a lapse, not proof the trigger is unclear. A likely contributor is that awb-release's own Report section, which lists what to report, never mentions the line. That is still the release, not the harness.

3. Open decisions ignored. This part holds and is the strongest. In taxi-B A3 the agent recorded a must-answer decision as a child question of Q-003 (questions add --kind decision --priority must --parent Q-003). It then reported "5 answered (provisional), 0 open". That follows the rule exactly, because the rule counts only "the ledger's roots". The simulated user said in feedback/human.md section 3 that the agent "reported no open questions while asking me to decide the tipping population." Any real user would see the same line. The line's "next:" does name the decision, which softens it.

4. No actor in the next step. In co2-A A6, "next: build the PowerPoint from the package" left the user unsure whose job it was (human/notes.md turn 7: "is that my job or its job?"); they settled it from the README. The rule's own example ("next: explore the March extract") names no actor either. It happened once and is mild, which matches the finding's "unclear" tag.

Nothing in the harness (front-loaded personas, the study disclosure, relay behavior) produces these outputs; it only makes them easier to notice.
verdicts.release_evidence: awb-init/assets/workbench/AGENTS.md, Conversation section, line 34: "A turn that changed workbench records ends with one plain line: any change to the user's questions, the ledger's roots, counting any `provisional` answer as provisional, and the next step; other turns have none. For example: Your five questions: 2 answered, 1 provisional, 2 open · next: explore the March extract." It counts roots only, says nothing about a turn with no ledger yet, and its example next step names no actor. awb-release/SKILL.md "Report" lists what a release turn reports and does not mention the line. README.md line 104 repeats the rule in user-facing words. Run evidence: last-line survey of every agent-NNN.out.md in all six runs. taxi-B relay/agent-003.jsonl: questions add of a must-priority decision under Q-003, followed by the "0 open" footer. co2-B relay/agent-006.jsonl: review-rules add, state next --drop and release, then the reply ends with no line. co2-B and retail-B feedback/agent-notes.md turn 1: footer improvised. co2-A human/notes.md line 42.
verdicts.narrowed: Narrower and minor. Because AGENTS.md's footer counts only the ledger's roots, taxi-B reported "5 answered (provisional), 0 open" while a must-answer child decision it had just recorded was still pending, and the simulated user found that confusing. The rule also gives no wording for the init turn, when no ledger exists, so all six runs improvised (harmless but inconsistent). The "ambiguous trigger" claim does not hold: co2-B's release turn is the only one of six that dropped the line, a one-off lapse that awb-release's Report section likely encouraged. co2-A's next step with no named actor happened once and is mild.

verdicts.reasoning:
I checked each of the four members against the shipped footer rule (awb-init/assets/workbench/AGENTS.md line 34). Only the taxi-B member is caused by the release.

taxi-B-17 holds and the release causes it. At reply 3 (commit 412d7d9) all five root questions were 'answered (provisional)'. Q-011, a must-priority user decision under Q-003 about the tip population, was still open. The rule says to report 'the user's questions, the ledger's roots', and CHANGELOG line 124 says the footer counts roots and 'never ledger rows'. So '5 answered (provisional), 0 open' is exactly what the rule produces. The rule's example has no place for an open must sub-question or a pending decision, although awb-status reports must_subquestions right after roots. The footer did name the decision in its 'next:' part, but the user still objected in feedback/human.md section 3: the agent 'reported no open questions while asking me to decide the tipping population'. The orchestrator report records the same problem.

co2-B-21 (A1) and retail-B-31 (init turn) do not show a user-facing defect. All six runs' init turns printed a footer even though no ledger existed yet, and each worded it differently: 'not yet recorded', 'none recorded yet', 'captured, none answered', '5 open', 'remain open'. Two agents noted in their own logs that the rule was unclear here. Every line was accurate and sensible, though, and no human complained; the retail-B human only noted neutrally that the questions were not yet recorded. This is a gap in the spec with no harm observed.

co2-B A6 is an agent lapse, not an ambiguous trigger. That turn ran review-rules add, state next --drop and release, all clear record changes under 'A turn that changed workbench records'. Release turns in the other five runs (taxi-A A9, taxi-B A7, co2-A A8, retail-A A9, retail-B A7) all kept the footer. The co2-B agent's notes raise no ambiguity. The turn still ended with a clear prose next step, so the user lost nothing.

co2-A-22 is mostly an agent error. The A6 draft turn said 'next: build the PowerPoint from the package', which skipped the user's review and the release that actually came next. The human was briefly unsure who builds it and settled that from the README (notes.md turn 7). The rule's example, 'next: explore the March extract', names no actor. But other footers in the same runs say 'your …' without trouble, so the release is at most a weak contributor here.
verdicts.release_evidence: awb-init/assets/workbench/AGENTS.md line 34: "A turn that changed workbench records ends with one plain line: any change to the user's questions, the ledger's roots, counting any `provisional` answer as provisional, and the next step; other turns have none. For example: Your five questions: 2 answered, 1 provisional, 2 open · next: explore the March extract." CHANGELOG.md line 124: the footer counts "the ledger's roots ... never ledger rows". By contrast, awb-status/SKILL.md line 30 reports `must_subquestions` after roots. taxi-B evidence: in questions.md at commit 412d7d9, Q-011 (decision, user, must, parent Q-003) is `open` while all roots are `answered (provisional)`, and reply 3 ends "5 answered (provisional), 0 open · next: your decision on the "unknown" rate-code trips". The trigger wording is not what caused the missing co2-B A6 footer: five of six release turns kept it. Init-turn footers appear in all six runs, each worded differently, and none drew a user complaint.
verdicts.narrowed: The footer rule counts only the root questions and has no slot for an open must sub-question or a pending user decision. So when every root is provisionally answered but a must decision is still waiting on the user, the line reads '0 open' even though the agent is asking for a decision in the same message (taxi-B reply 3, Q-011). The 'next:' part named the decision, so this is minor confusion, but a real user flagged it. The other parts do not hold as release-caused. The init-turn wording was improvised but accurate and harmed no one. co2-B's missing release-turn footer was a one-off agent lapse against a clear rule. co2-A's 'next: build the PowerPoint' was the agent stating the wrong next step.

consolidated.title: Required slides take up the requested slide count
consolidated.description: The title, Answer, How we know and Limitations slides take four places. With 'about 8 slides' requested, that left four finding slides for five questions. taxi-B moved two questions to the appendix, retail-A merged Q2 and Q3, co2-A ended with 10 assembled slides, and retail-B with 9 plus 2 in the appendix. Users are not told up front whether the title slide counts. The contract allows moving How we know and Limitations to the appendix, which agents rarely offered.
consolidated.caused_by_fix: no
consolidated.evidence: taxi-B-15: reply 4; package-contract.md:46. co2-A-19: r5 preview; deck-rules.md. retail-A-17: reply 6, msg 7; README line 22. retail-B-23: reply 3 decision 2, reply 5; human.md section 3.

verdicts.reasoning:
The core of the finding comes from the release, not the harness. package-contract.md:46 and findings-template require a title slide, Answer, at least one finding, How we know, and Limitations and open caveats. SKILL.md:54 counts main slides "title included". So in an "about 8" deck, four places go to non-finding slides. Every brief asked for about 8 slides and five questions, which made the clash certain. That setup is not artificial: the README's own example asks for "about 8 slides", and a real user on an interactive host would hit the same arithmetic. Running non-interactively, the sandbox, the relay and auto-approved MCP tools play no part. The study disclosure does produce the agents' self-reports in agent.md. But two human personas raised the friction on their own: taxi-B notes ("Eight slides becomes eleven with appendices, requiring a length choice") and retail-B human.md section 3 ("Clearer upfront counting ... would help"). co2-A's human called it "Odd ... explained, and fine".

Several details in the finding are wrong. (1) "Agents rarely offered" to move How we know or Limitations to the appendix. In fact 3 of 4 runs did. The taxi-B reply 4 offered it as the alternative but recommended against it. co2-A reply 5 moved Limitations to the appendix unasked. retail-B reply 3 moved How we know to the appendix unasked and offered moving another finding. Only retail-A (reply 6) merged Q2 and Q3 to fit 8 without offering the appendix route. (2) "Users are not told whether the title counts." The agent said so at the headline checkpoint in every run: taxi-B "Eight main slides need the four required slides"; retail-B "9 main slides including the title"; co2-A and retail-A listed the title as slide 1 of 8. The gap is narrower: the README (lines 22 and 68-69) lists the required slides and the appendix option but never says before the checkpoint that the title counts toward a requested length. (3) co2-A's main sequence was exactly 8. Its "10 assembled" adds one appendix slide and the builder's divider, so the request was not overrun. In all four runs the user accepted the layout.
verdicts.release_evidence: package-contract.md:46 (required slides: title, Answer, at least one finding, How we know, Limitations; an appendix may hold findings, How we know, Limitations, Supporting datasets). awb-package/SKILL.md:54 ("Report the main slides, title included, and appendix slides against any recorded length, proposing which move to the appendix when the main slides exceed it"). README.md:22 (required slides and the appendix option) and README.md:68-69 (length asked; slide count reported only at the headline checkpoint). Neither README passage says the title counts toward the requested length. deck-rules.md:91 (the builder adds an appendix divider). Run evidence: taxi-B/relay/agent-004.out.md, co2-A/relay/agent-005.out.md, retail-A/relay/agent-006.out.md, retail-B/relay/agent-003.out.md, taxi-B/human/notes.md:35, retail-B/feedback/human.md:28, co2-A/human/notes.md:37.
verdicts.narrowed: The required title, Answer, How we know and Limitations slides take four places in a requested ~8-slide main sequence. With five questions, the agent must move findings or required slides to the appendix, or merge findings, so "about 8" ends as 8 main slides plus 1 to 3 appendix slides, or 9 main slides. The README lists the required slides but does not say before the headline checkpoint that the title counts toward the requested length. At the checkpoint the agents did disclose the count, title included, and 3 of 4 runs used or offered appendix placement for How we know or Limitations. Only retail-A merged two questions instead of offering the appendix route. Severity minor, a design trade-off the users accepted, not a defect that blocks work.

verdicts.reasoning:
Most of the finding is either intended design that the release already handles, or wrong. Only a small gap in the README holds up.

1. **The required slides do take up the length, but by design, and the release covers it.** findings-template.md (Slide rules, line 12) requires the title, Answer, at least one finding, How we know, and Limitations. It lets How we know and Limitations move to the appendix. Its Appendix section (line 104) says the appendix holds slides "that would take the deck past the length" in the brief. awb-package/SKILL.md line 54 tells the agent to "Report the main slides, title included, and appendix slides against any recorded length, proposing which move to the appendix when the main slides exceed it." So there is real pressure on the slide count, but the release makes it a choice the user approves at the headline checkpoint.

2. **"Users are not told whether the title slide counts" is false for the checkpoint, where all four runs told them:**
   - taxi-B reply 4: "Eight main slides need the four required slides, which leaves room for four finding slides."
   - retail-B reply 3: "9 main slides including the title."
   - co2-A reply 5 and retail-A reply 6 both list the title as slide 1 of the eight.

   The claim holds only for the README, which the user reads before starting. README line 22 lists the required slides and the appendix option, and line 53 asks for "about how many slides". Neither says the title, or the Appendix divider the builder adds, counts toward that number.

3. **"Agents rarely offered moving How we know or Limitations to the appendix" is contradicted.** Three of the four cited runs offered or used that move:
   - taxi-B reply 4 offered it as the alternative and recommended against it.
   - co2-A reply 5 put Limitations in the appendix, keeping all five findings in the main deck.
   - retail-B reply 3 put How we know in the appendix.

   Only retail-A merged Q2 and Q3 instead. Merging is allowed: the template only requires that every part of each question stays in a headline, bullet or chart.

4. **No user hit a real problem.**
   - The taxi-B user called moving volumes and zones to the appendix "an acceptable tradeoff".
   - The co2-A user praised "a sensible appendix".
   - The retail-A user said "The order is fine".
   - The retail-B user accepted nine main plus two appendix slides. Only in feedback section 3 did they ask for clearer counting up front of main slides, required slides and the appendix.

5. **Smaller points.**
   - Several cited evidence IDs don't match the current findings.json. taxi-B-15, retail-A-17 and retail-B-23 are about other topics. The matching findings are taxi-B-10, retail-A-12 and retail-B-20. co2-A-19 is correct.
   - The README promises the agent "proposes what could move to the appendix" with no condition. The skill asks for that only when the main slides exceed the length, which is why retail-A merged instead of offering an appendix. The effect is minor.

What is left is a small documentation gap caused by the release: the README is the only place it shows.
verdicts.release_evidence:
- **awb-package/SKILL.md:54** already covers the main complaint: "Report the main slides, title included, and appendix slides against any recorded length, proposing which move to the appendix when the main slides exceed it." It also has the agent say up front that the deck opens with a title slide, then the Answer slide.
- **awb-package/assets/package-format/findings-template.md:12** sets the required slides, and lets How we know and Limitations move to the appendix. Line 104 says the appendix is for slides past the brief's length.
- **awb-package/references/package-contract.md:46** gives the required slide set, and says a required slide moved to the appendix still counts.
- **README.md:22** lists the required slides and the appendix option.
- **README.md:53 and :69** ask for "about how many slides" and promise a count against that length at the checkpoint. Neither says whether the title slide or the builder's Appendix divider (deck-rules.md:27) counts toward the requested length.

**Run evidence:**
- **taxi-B reply 4:** the four required slides were stated, and How we know/Limitations to the appendix was offered as the alternative.
- **co2-A reply 5:** Limitations moved to the appendix, with "ten slides in the assembled deck" (divider included) disclosed.
- **retail-A reply 6:** Q2 and Q3 merged to make eight slides, title included.
- **retail-B reply 3:** "9 main slides including the title", with How we know in the appendix. Its human.md section 3 asks for clearer upfront counting.

All four users accepted.
verdicts.narrowed: The README never says whether the title slide (or the Appendix divider the builder adds) counts toward the "about N slides" the user requests, so users first learn the counting rule at the headline checkpoint. With five questions and about 8 slides, the four required slides force a choice there: move slides to the appendix or merge findings. The skill makes the agent report the count, title included, and propose appendix moves, and three of the four agents offered or used the How we know/Limitations move. Every user accepted the result, and one asked for the counting rule to be stated up front. Severity: minor or trivial; it is a README gap only.

consolidated.title: Review-rule workflow costs extra rounds: ask before repairing, staleness on add, limited scopes
consolidated.description:
Review rules now belong to the user, but the workflow adds friction:
- review.md says to ask, before repairing, whether a correction should become a rule, and to record the rule before the repair. That is a blocking round, so agents repaired first and asked afterwards (co2-B twice, retail-A), and the rules arrived a turn later.
- Adding a rule makes the passed review stale, because foundation/review-rules.md is part of what the receipt covers. That forced another scoped review at release (co2-B, retail-A), while the README says a stable draft needs no new review to release.
- Rules apply to one package or to all packages, not to an investigation, so retail-B applied investigation-level rules to every package.
- The question to the user came as three bare options with no plain explanation (retail-A).
- A rule the user asked for fired on the methodology sentence that describes it (taxi-B).
- Guidance on writing rule patterns is thin (co2-B's 'at least .* if').
consolidated.oct16_ref: C-06 (#85); new side effects of its fix
consolidated.caused_by_fix: yes: #101 (issue #85) added ask-before-repair, --confirmed, and the package-or-all scope. #96 (issue #84) included foundation/review-rules.md in what the receipt covers, so adding a rule makes the review stale. #105 wrote README line 70, which says a release then needs no new review.
consolidated.evidence: co2-B-06: U6, A6 ('Adding it meant one more quick review'); reviewloop shows 1 scoped review in agent-006. co2-B-22: A4 and A5 offer rules ('Optional...') after the repairs. co2-B-38: --pattern in relay/agent-005.jsonl. retail-A-08: reply 8; notes.md turn 9. retail-A-09: reply 8, msg 9, reply 9 (review-rules add, then a scoped review at release of about 1.2 min). retail-B-13: msg 6 ('for future packages in this investigation'); reply 6. taxi-B-09: review-reports/agent-006-record01.txt, R-payment-codes-001 at methodology.md:22. Release: review.md:45; README line 70.

verdicts.reasoning:
I read the transcripts, the relay logs (through logview and reviewloop), the review reports, the rules files and the human notes. Only part of the finding holds.

What holds, and comes from the release:
- **Ask-before-repair conflicts with how corrections arrive.** In all four runs the user's correction came in the same message as "go ahead / prepare the full draft / finish the corrections": co2-B msgs 4 and 5, retail-A msg 8, retail-B msg 5, taxi-B msg 5. review.md:45 and awb-package SKILL.md:24 say to ask first and record the rule before repairing. On any host where asking means ending the turn, that rule forces the user to wait a round before the edits they asked for are made.
- **Both model families repaired first and asked afterwards.** The Claude agents in co2-B, retail-B and taxi-B did it. So did the Codex agent in retail-A, which posted the question mid-turn and said "I'll complete the requested edits either way". The co2-B agent's own notes name this as a knowing deviation ("User had asked to finish; I repaired and offered the rule afterwards").
- **A rule added late made the passed review stale.** In co2-B and retail-A the user answered the rule question in the same message as the release request. The rule-add then made the passed review stale, because review.md:39 counts foundation/review-rules.md among the files that make a review stale. That forced one extra automated scoped review at release. reviewloop shows co2-B agent-006 took 1.4 minutes in total and found nothing. retail-A reply 9 took about 1.7 minutes, including the release.
- **Rule scope is only one package or all packages.** README:99 and the `--package <investigation>/<package>` flag offer nothing else. retail-B asked for "this investigation", and the agent fell back to all packages. There was no effect here, since it was the only investigation.

What does not hold:
- **"Costs extra rounds."** No extra user round happened in any run. The rule question rode along with a stop that was happening anyway: the headline or draft review, or the release request. The observed cost was rules arriving a turn later, plus about a minute of automated review in two runs.
- **README contradiction.** README:70 defines "stable" as "nothing changed since", and README:70 and :99 say the reviewer checks your rules. So the extra review is consistent with the README, though the README doesn't say outright that adding a rule triggers a new review.
- **taxi-B's rule "firing on its own description."** The reviewer was right going by the rule's wording. The rule says any mention of Flex Fare must credit the label to the dictionary and say its meaning is uncertain, and methodology.md:22 did neither. The agent fixed it in the same turn.
- **Thin guidance on rule patterns.** This rests only on the co2-B agent's friction notes, which it kept because the study asked it to. The rough 'at least .* if' pattern caused no wrong verdict.
- **retail-A's "bare options".** The question did say in plain words what would be checked. The terse bulleted options and the link to SKILL.md were the Codex model's own formatting. The human's "what does all packages mean" complaint is mostly model phrasing, nudged by review.md's own "every package or this one alone".

Harness factors:
- relay.py:39 blocks AskUserQuestion, and claude-agent-system.md tells the agent it cannot ask mid-turn. In interactive Claude Code, the three Claude-agent runs could have asked mid-turn and avoided the blocking round. So the harness made the conflict worse on that host.
- It did not cause it. The Codex run behaved the same way, Codex has no general mid-turn wait, and review.md does not tell the agent to use a question tool on any host.
- The staleness-on-add mechanism is plain release logic and does not depend on the harness.

So a narrow, minor product version holds.
verdicts.release_evidence:
- review.md:45: when a correction could recur, "ask the user before repairing"; "Only on their yes, record the rule before repairing"; the only scope is `--package <investigation>/<package>`, otherwise every package.
- awb-package/SKILL.md:24: "first ask the user whether later drafts should be checked for it".
- review.md:39: a review goes `stale` once foundation/review-rules.md changes.
- review.md:35: a scoped review judges each newly added rule against every narrative in full.
- awb-release/SKILL.md:20: a stale receipt requires a scoped review before release.
- README:70: "stable once ... the last review passed with nothing changed since; a release then needs no new review".
- README:99: a rule covers every package's drafts or one package's.
- Harness: relay.py:39 adds AskUserQuestion to the agent's disallowed tools; claude-agent-system.md says "You cannot ask anything mid-turn".
verdicts.narrowed: review.md:45 and awb-package SKILL.md:24 say to ask whether a correction should become a rule, and to record it, before repairing. In practice corrections arrive with "go ahead / finish", so on hosts where asking ends the turn the agent can't comply without holding back the requested edits for a round. Agents in all four rule-adding runs (Claude: co2-B, retail-B, taxi-B; Codex: retail-A) repaired first and offered the rule afterwards, so rules were recorded a turn late. When the user's yes came with the release request (co2-B, retail-A), adding the rule made the passed review stale (review-rules.md is covered by the receipt) and forced one extra automated scoped review at release, about 1 to 1.7 minutes, with no new problems. No extra user rounds occurred. Separately, rules can only cover one package or all packages, so a request for an investigation-level rule (retail-B) falls back to all packages; that had no effect here. Not supported: the extra-rounds claim, a README contradiction, taxi-B's Flex Fare violation (correct under the rule's wording), thin pattern guidance (no harm observed), and retail-A's terse options (model formatting). The harness made the first point worse for the Claude-agent runs by blocking AskUserQuestion.

verdicts.reasoning:
I checked each bullet against the shipped files and the run logs. Only two parts hold, and both cost very little.

1. **The ask-before-repair ordering is in the release, and agents in four runs didn't follow it.** Two shipped files tell the agent to ask whether a correction should become a rule before repairing it, and to record the rule before the repair: awb-package/SKILL.md:24 and awb-package/references/review.md:45. Followed literally, an edit the user just asked for waits a full round for an answer about the rule. The Claude agents in co2-B (replies 4 and 5), retail-B (reply 5) and taxi-B (reply 5) all repaired first and asked afterwards, marked "Optional". The Codex agent in retail-A (reply 8) asked mid-turn and said "I'll complete the requested edits either way". co2-B's own notes call this a deviation. Both model families broke the instruction the same way, which points to a real conflict with a user who asked for the edit now.
   - **What it cost:** the rule arrives a turn later. review.md:39 counts foundation/review-rules.md as part of what the review covers, so adding the rule marks the passed review stale. That forced one extra automatic scoped review before release in co2-B (reply 6: "Adding it meant one more quick review") and in retail-A (reply 9; its notes confirm). Each of those whole replies, review and release included, took about 80 to 100 seconds. No user exchange was added, because the rule question rode along with other questions. So "extra rounds" is overstated: the extra cost was one short automated review.

2. **No per-investigation scope.** `review-rules add` keeps a rule for one package (`--package`) or for every package (awb_draft.py help text; README line 99). In retail-B the user asked for checks "for future packages in this investigation". The agent made them apply to all packages and said so (reply 6). The project had only one investigation, so nothing changed. In a project with several, rules meant for one investigation would also check the others.

**What does not hold:**
- **README contradiction:** README line 70 says a release needs no new review only when the last review passed "with nothing changed since". A rules change is a change, and the re-check is documented behaviour that verifies the new rule before release.
- **"Three bare options" (retail-A):** the agent's own wording. A question sentence came before the options, and review.md:45 already says to ask in plain words.
- **Rule firing on its own methodology sentence (taxi-B):** the rule the agent wrote says "any mention of Flex Fare must attribute the label". methodology.md:22 mentioned Flex Fare without attribution, so the reviewer applied the rule as written. The rule's wording is the agent's, and it was repaired within the same turn.
- **Thin pattern guidance:** the help text exists ("a Python regular expression matching a likely violation on one line"). A match is only a candidate, since review.md step 2 has every rule judged by reading anyway. A rough pattern like co2-B's 'at least .* if' changes no verdict, and users never write patterns.
verdicts.release_evidence: awb-package/SKILL.md:24 ("first ask the user whether later drafts should be checked for it ... record it as a review rule only on their yes"); awb-package/references/review.md:45 ("ask the user before repairing ... Only on their yes, record the rule before repairing"); review.md:39 (review goes `stale` once foundation/review-rules.md changes); awb-release/SKILL.md:20 (a stale review needs a scoped review before release); awb-package/assets/awb_draft.py cli_review_rules: `--package INVESTIGATION/PACKAGE` "keep the rule for this package alone (default: every package)", with no investigation scope; README.md:99 (rules apply to every package or to one); README.md:70 ("last review passed with nothing changed since; a release then needs no new review", which is consistent with re-reviewing after a rules change); `--pattern` help: "a Python regular expression matching a likely violation on one line (default: none, judged by reading)".
verdicts.narrowed: The instruction in awb-package SKILL.md:24 and review.md:45 to ask about a rule, and record it, before repairing conflicts with a user who has asked for the edit now. Agents in co2-B, retail-A, retail-B and taxi-B repaired first and asked afterwards, so the rule arrived a turn later. Because review-rules.md is part of what the review covers (review.md:39), a rule added along with the release request made the passed review stale and forced one extra automatic scoped review before release (co2-B and retail-A, about a minute each, no extra user exchange). Separately, rules can only cover one package or every package, so a user who asks for an investigation-wide rule gets a project-wide one (retail-B, harmless with one investigation). The README-contradiction, bare-options, self-firing-rule and pattern-guidance bullets do not hold.

consolidated.title: Scoping proposals are incomplete, mis-scoped or mis-paced
consolidated.description:
First scoping rounds missed or misjudged things the user then had to raise:
- taxi-B's invalid-record rules left out negative distances and any speed rule, and counted Unknown and Outside-NYC pickups as invalid.
- retail-B recommended a products-only 'net revenue' for a company-total question, and planned to ask who would read the deck after msg 1 had already said.
- co2-A defined 'largest by emissions' itself, and numbered two choices under one item.
- co2-B announced a second round for simple choices (ranking year, consumption scope) instead of offering them with recommendations in the first.

Tag: co2-A-24 and co2-A-25 are unclear; the other members are product.
consolidated.caused_by_fix: partly: #102 (issue #86) sends decisions beyond four to a second round, which co2-B followed even for simple choices.
consolidated.evidence: taxi-B-13: reply 1 decision 3, msg 2; feedback/human.md section 4. retail-B-11: reply 1 definition 1, msg 2. retail-B-26: reply 1 closing paragraph; msg 1. co2-A-24: r3 table header. co2-A-25: r1 item 1 (transcript line 28); awb-scope/SKILL.md says 'never number unrelated choices under one item'. co2-B-28: A1 'Next round, I'll ask'; U2.

verdicts.reasoning:
I looked for a harness cause and found none for the main members. Some members do not hold, so the finding needs narrowing.

Harness checks:
- The agent prompt does say "You cannot ask anything mid-turn," but this does not explain the deferrals. awb-scope caps each round at four decisions on any host, so an interactive host would also need a second round.
- The study note appended to the agent prompt only asks for a friction log, so it does not touch scoping.
- Personas front-loading answers made the problem cheaper, not worse. The co2-B and retail-B humans answered the deferred items before being asked.

Members that hold:
- **co2-B-28 holds, and the release is the direct cause.** awb-scope says "ask decisions at the same level together, at most four ... ask any beyond four in a second round." Reply 1 had four decisions and listed three more for "Next round" with no recommendations: ranking year, consumption check, expectations. None of the three depends on the round-1 answers. The co2-B agent notes say: "Scope 'at most four decisions per round' forced me to defer some ... to round 2." The human's feedback section 4 flags this.
- **retail-B-26 holds.** Reply 1 deferred "who exactly will read the deck" to round 2 under the same cap (agent notes line 17). Message 1 had already named the leadership team and the budget decision. The human wrote "as outlined earlier" and flagged it in feedback.
- **taxi-B-13 holds in part.** The persona did drop "implausible durations or speeds" from its own question 4. But the user explicitly asked the agent to "propose sensible definitions and exclusion rules." The agent proposed duration and distance limits but no speed rule, and counted Unknown and Outside-NYC pickups as invalid rather than as missing geography. The user corrected both.

Members that do not hold:
- **"Negative distances" is unsupported.** I queried the inbox files: there are 0 negative trip_distance values against 108,416 zeros. The agent's turn-1 query already used trip_distance<=0, so leaving negatives out of its wording changed nothing.
- **co2-A-24 is not a usability problem.** The agent ranked by 2022 emissions and labelled that in the table header. The user never raised it, co2-B's user picked the same end-year rule, and co2-A's human called scoping "excellent."
- **co2-A-25 is real but trivial, and not caused by the release.** Item 1 adds a context question to a decision, but the release explicitly forbids that, so this is the model (Codex) ignoring a rule. No user noticed it.
- **retail-B-11 is contestable rather than wrong.** The persona brief says it was "unsure whether [non-product lines] belong in revenue; you would like the agent's recommendation." The agent gave a reasoned products-only recommendation, offered all lines as the alternative, and planned to show non-product totals separately. The persona simply chose differently.
verdicts.release_evidence:
These files tie the members that hold to the release, not the harness:
- awb-scope/SKILL.md, "Pace by dependency", contains the four-per-round cap.
- co2-B/feedback/agent-notes.md line 17 and retail-B/feedback/agent-notes.md line 17 both name that cap as the reason for deferring.
- taxi-B/feedback/agent-notes.md line 8 also calls the four-decision cap slow.
- co2-B reply 1 lists three independent items under "Next round, I'll ask"; retail-B reply 1 includes "who exactly will read the deck" after message 1 had said leadership team.
- taxi-B reply 1, decision 3, lists the invalid-record rules with no speed rule and with "Unknown"/"Outside NYC" as invalid.
- A DuckDB count on taxi-B/inbox returns (0 negative, 108,416 zero, min 0.0) for trip_distance.
verdicts.narrowed: awb-scope's cap of four decisions per round makes agents defer simple, independent choices to an announced second round, often without recommendations. co2-B deferred the ranking year, consumption scope and expectations; retail-B's deferred set included the audience, which message 1 had already given. Separately, taxi-B's first invalid-record proposal had no speed rule and counted Unknown and Outside-NYC pickups as invalid, and the user had to correct both. Drop "negative distances": the data has none, and the agent's check used <=0. Drop co2-A-24: the default was disclosed and no user raised it. co2-A-25 is a trivial model breach of a rule the release already has. retail-B-11 is a contestable recommendation the persona asked for, not a clear misjudgment.

verdicts.reasoning:
The cited behaviour does happen in each run, but the release causes only one part of it, and that part is a documented design choice rather than a defect.

taxi-B-13 (reply 1, decision 3): the agent proposed 'distance is zero', no speed rule, and 'Unknown or Outside NYC' as invalid. The user corrected all three in msg 2. Nothing in the release produced this. awb-scope tells the agent to test each measure and population term "against source data". awb-clean already treats a placeholder that means missing as a user decision, separate from an invalid value. Which domain rules a first proposal includes is the model's judgement. The negative-distance omission also has no effect: counting both monthly Parquet files in taxi-B/inbox gives 0 rows with trip_distance < 0 and 108,416 with zero, so 'distance is zero' already covered every bad distance.

retail-B-11: the agent recommended products-only net revenue and offered 'every line' as the alternative, and the user picked the alternative. This is the recommended-answer-plus-alternative pattern awb-scope asks for. The release does not push toward products-only. The human feedback does call the recommendation wrong for a company-total question, but that is a judgement call, not something the release caused.

retail-B-26: the agent planned to ask "who exactly will read the deck" after msg 1 had named the leadership team, the decision and "plain commercial language". awb-scope says "Record any reader the user describes in the brief's Audience section; awb-package asks for it when a package needs it." awb-package asks only when the Audience section is missing or blank. So the release says not to ask; this was the agent's lapse.

co2-A-25: r1 item 1 asks the shortlist-driver choice and also "Please add any countries or activities the Initiative cannot support" under one number. Two shipped instructions forbid that: awb-scope's "never number unrelated choices under one item", and awb-init's "one choice per numbered decision". The CHANGELOG also has an entry for this rule. The agent broke a clear instruction once, so the release did not cause it.

co2-A-24: the agent picked "ranked by their 2022 emissions" and stated it in the table header. awb-scope already tells the agent to push on measure definitions, and the user accepted the choice without objecting. This was an agent choice, not a release cause. The co2-A human rated the scoping "excellent".

co2-B-28: this one is release-caused. awb-scope's Pace by dependency says to ask "at most four" decisions at the same level and to "ask any beyond four in a second round". README line 64 tells users decisions "come up to four at a time", and CHANGELOG line 157 records the cap as deliberate. co2-B had 7 decisions (4 asked, 3 previewed for the next round), and retail-B had the same 4 + 3 split. Because of the cap, the deferred items were listed without recommendations. In both runs the user answered them in their next message anyway, so no exchange was lost. The co2-B human said only that it "risked slowing setup".

Overall: the finding's main claim, that first scoping rounds miss or misjudge things the user then has to raise, comes from agent judgement or from ignoring instructions the release already gives. It is not caused by the release.
verdicts.release_evidence:
awb-scope/SKILL.md section 2 (Pace by dependency): "ask decisions at the same level together, at most four, each with a recommended answer and its reason. A decision is one choice: never number unrelated choices under one item; make each its own decision, and ask any beyond four in a second round." This prevents co2-A-25 and causes co2-B-28.

awb-scope/SKILL.md section 2: "Record any reader the user describes in the brief's Audience section; awb-package asks for it when a package needs it." This prevents retail-B-26.

awb-scope/SKILL.md section 2 (Dig into what makes an answer usable): "the definition of the measure and of each population term, tested with a concrete example and against source data". This covers co2-A-24 and taxi-B.

awb-init/SKILL.md step 4: "one choice per numbered decision". This also covers co2-A-25.

awb-clean/SKILL.md: the user decides "what a placeholder stands for (missing, zero, or real)". The release separates missing values from invalid ones.

awb-package/SKILL.md: asks for the audience only "When it is missing or blank".

README.md line 64: decisions "come up to four at a time".

CHANGELOG.md line 157: the four-per-round cap and the one-choice-per-item rule are deliberate.

Data check: the taxi-B inbox Parquet files hold 0 rows with trip_distance < 0 and 108,416 with zero.
verdicts.narrowed: The release causes one part of this. awb-scope caps a round at four same-level decisions and sends the rest to a second round; the cap is deliberate and documented (README line 64, CHANGELOG line 157). With more than four decisions, the agent listed the extras for a later round without recommendations: co2-B asked 4 and deferred 3 (the ranking year, the consumption scope, prior expectations), and retail-B did the same, 4 then 3. Both users answered the deferred items in their next message, so no exchange was lost. A user who waited would spend one extra scoping exchange, which is a minor design tradeoff, not a defect. The other members are not caused by the release. taxi-B's rule gaps (no speed rule; missing geography counted as invalid) and retail-B's products-only recommendation are agent judgement calls the user corrected. taxi-B's negative-distance gap has no effect, since the data has no negative distances. retail-B-26 and co2-A-25 go against explicit shipped instructions. co2-A-24 was a disclosed choice the user accepted.

consolidated.title: The handoff from init to scope has no place for a full first brief and no investigation scaffold
consolidated.description: awb-init and awb-scope require the first interview before any investigation record exists. A fully specified first message is therefore parked in a README section the agent invents (co2-A, taxi-A), or its records wait a turn (retail-A). awb-scope has no helper to create an investigation, so agents copy templates and write records by hand, and template placeholder prose stays in them (taxi-A, taxi-B).
consolidated.caused_by_fix: no
consolidated.evidence: taxi-A-24: replies 1-2; agent-notes lines 6 and 23. taxi-B-25: item 1. co2-A-16: r1; agent-002 later moved the section into brief.md; awb-init/SKILL.md step 4. retail-A-32: reply 1; agent-notes Turn 1.

verdicts.reasoning:
I looked for a harness cause and did not find one. The release itself causes the issue, but only a narrower version of the finding holds.

Harness explanations I checked and rejected:
(1) Personas front-loading facts. The personas did volunteer facts their briefs reserved for "if it asks" (taxi-A-25, co2-A-25 and similar). But the first messages in co2-A, taxi-A and retail-A follow the release README's own recommended opener almost word for word. The README says "The more you put in the first message, the fewer questions follow" and reports that "Most of those users gave their questions, audience, length, and storage folders in the first message." A real user following the docs sends the same fully specified first message.
(2) Non-interactive runs. relay.py resumes each agent session by a fixed id or thread id, so conversation context carried over between turns as it would on an interactive host. In taxi-A and co2-A the agents said they parked the brief in the README for durability, so the user's context would not be missing from project records before the investigation existed. That reason applies just as much on a real host.
(3) The Codex sandbox, MCP auto-approval, the simulated home and the study disclosure play no part in this sequencing.

The sequencing comes straight from the skill text. awb-init step 2 says "Do not interview here". Step 4 says to run awb-scope's "first interview round before it creates the investigation". awb-scope says "Before writing the records, ask the user every open decision". The README template has no place to hold a brief in the meantime. awb-scope's New branch tells the agent to "Adapt" the brief, state and history templates and copy run.py, with no create command. Both taxi-A (Codex) and taxi-B (Claude) logged the hand copying as friction.

What does not hold:
(a) The README parking is not forced. Only 2 of the 3 Codex agents did it (taxi-A, co2-A). retail-A's Codex agent and all three Claude agents (taxi-B, co2-B, retail-B) kept the brief in the conversation and created the investigation the next turn without visible harm. Both parked sections were moved into brief.md the next turn.
(b) retail-A's "records wait a turn" is the designed flow. Four genuine decisions were open, and its own agent called it "workable".
(c) The placeholder-prose clause is wrong about the cause. The only leftover template text in taxi-A and taxi-B is the two standing guidance lines under "Unresolved issues" and "Next steps" in state.md. The shipped `state issues` / `state next` helper (`edit_list` in provenance.py, "Only list-item lines change") appends beneath those lines by design. The same lines remain in co2-A and co2-B, so a scaffold helper would not have removed them.
(d) The finding cites the wrong evidence IDs. taxi-A-24 is about sandbox limits and taxi-B-25 is about the path leak; both are tagged harness and unrelated. retail-A-32 does not exist (retail-A has 19 findings). The matching findings are taxi-A-18, taxi-B-18 and co2-A-16, plus retail-A's agent-notes for Turn 1.
verdicts.release_evidence:
- awb-init/SKILL.md, line 26 (step 2): "Do not interview here: step 4 hands the question to awb-scope". Line 48 (step 4): "run awb-scope's first interview round before it creates the investigation, asking it in this report".
- awb-scope/SKILL.md, line 44: "Before writing the records, ask the user every open decision they can answer". Line 57 (New branch): "Adapt the brief, state, and history, and copy run.py with its settings.toml". There is no create or scaffold command.
- README.md, line 46: "The more you put in the first message, the fewer questions follow". Line 48 gives the full example opener. Line 92: "Most of those users gave their questions, audience, length, and storage folders in the first message".
- awb-init/assets/workbench/README.md has only an "Active investigation: none" line and no section for holding a brief.
- In the installed helpers (project src/provenance.py), `edit_list` says "Only list-item lines change" and appends after the existing body lines, so the state.md guidance lines stay by design.
- Run evidence: the README "Scoping handoff" section appears in taxi-A (agent-002's `cat README.md` output) and in co2-A (agent-notes line 9, later moved per line 24). The Claude-agent runs taxi-B, co2-B and retail-B ask their decisions first and keep the brief in the conversation.
verdicts.narrowed: By design, the release creates no investigation records until the first scoping round is answered. It gives no interim place for the fully specified first brief that its own README recommends, and awb-scope has no create helper, so agents hand-copy the brief, state and history templates (taxi-A, taxi-B). Faced with that gap, 2 of 3 Codex agents (taxi-A, co2-A) improvised a temporary "Scoping handoff" section in the project README and moved it into brief.md the next turn. Claude agents and retail-A's Codex agent kept the brief in the conversation with no harm. Severity is minor. retail-A's one-turn wait is intended behavior, and the claim that placeholder prose is left behind because there is no scaffold does not hold: the leftover state.md guidance lines are kept by the shipped helper regardless.

verdicts.reasoning:
The release causes the core mechanism. The finding overstates two of its parts.

What the release does:
- awb-init/SKILL.md step 4 says: "When the hand-off shares a turn with setup, run awb-scope's first interview round before it creates the investigation, asking it in this report."
- awb-scope/SKILL.md step 2 says: "Before writing the records, ask the user every open decision they can answer."
- Settled content therefore has nowhere to go until the round is answered. No shipped file gives the first message a home before the investigation exists. The README template only has an "Active investigation: none" line and no intake section, and AGENTS.md says nothing about it.
- A fresh session after setup would run `awb.py state`, see "No active investigation", and find no record of the question unless the agent improvised one.
- There is no create helper. `awb_cli.py` COMMANDS has no investigation-create command, and `state switch` refuses unless `investigations/<slug>/state.md` already exists. awb-scope's New branch tells the agent to adapt the brief, state and history templates and copy run.py and settings.toml by hand.

What the runs show:
- **taxi-A** (Codex agent): in turn 1 the agent added an invented "Scoping handoff:" block to README holding the five questions, audience and deliverables. Agent-notes line 6 calls it "an adaptation: no dedicated intake template exists". In turn 2 it moved the block into brief.md and removed it from README. Line 23 notes "no short built-in create command".
- **co2-A** (Codex agent): it invented a "## Scoping handoff" section, and agent.md item 6 attributes this to the sequencing. In turn 2 it replaced the section with an invented "## Active investigation brief" pointer section that is still in the final README, so the drift persisted.
- **retail-A** (Codex agent): it did not park anything. Its records waited one turn, and its notes call this "workable but delays durable investigation records".
- **taxi-B** (Claude agent): it copied templates by hand and noted that a scaffold helper would reduce guesswork.

Overstatements:
1. **"Fully specified."** In all three cited Codex runs the first message still left real decisions open: usefulness criteria (taxi-A), four method choices (co2-A) and four definitions (retail-A). The interview round was warranted, so the one-turn wait is intended design. The defect is only that the parts already settled have no durable home while the round is pending.
2. **"Template placeholder prose stays."** The true placeholders were replaced in every run, for example the brief's "State the question..." and state.md's "<!-- use an ISO date -->". What remains is state.md's standing guidance: the Status and Claim legend and the "List relevant data problems..." lines. The helpers tolerate it ("Only list-item lines change"), awb-scope itself keeps some template pointer lines on purpose, and taxi-A deliberately "kept shipped template guidance". retail-A stripped those lines and taxi-A dropped history's Entry format block, so the result is inconsistency, not leftover placeholders. That part of the finding is not supported.

Harness factors: sessions are resumed (relay.py `--resume` / `codex exec resume`), so the conversation persisted across turns as it would on a real host. Parking in README was the agent choosing durability, not a context loss. Persona front-loading made the first messages unusually rich (the referee marked taxi-A-25 and retail-A-17 as harness), but real users also paste rich briefs.

Real-user impact is minor: one turn before records exist, a possible ad hoc README section, and manual template work that costs agent time without a visible defect.
verdicts.release_evidence:
- awb-init/SKILL.md step 4: "When the hand-off shares a turn with setup, run `awb-scope`'s first interview round before it creates the investigation, asking it in this report". Step 2: "Do not interview here".
- awb-scope/SKILL.md step 2: "Before writing the records, ask the user every open decision they can answer ... Write the records without a separate confirmation round."
- awb-scope/SKILL.md step 3, New: "Create `investigations/<slug>/` ... Adapt the brief, state, and history, and copy run.py with its settings.toml". This is manual and has no helper.
- awb-init/assets/awb_cli.py COMMANDS has no investigation-create command. awb_mcp.py AWB_COMMANDS state subcommands are finding, render, flag, issues, next, switch.
- awb_provenance.py switch_active raises "investigations/{investigation}/state.md does not exist" unless the folder was already created by hand.
- The README template (assets/workbench/README.md) has only "Active investigation: none" and no intake section. Nothing in the release mentions "intake" or "Scoping handoff", so the agents invented it.
- The state.md template carries standing guidance paragraphs. awb_provenance.py cli_state says "Only list-item lines change", so helpers tolerate that prose.
verdicts.narrowed: Before the first scope round, the release has no durable place for the settled parts of a rich first message. awb-init step 4 requires awb-scope's first interview round before any investigation exists, and awb-scope writes records only after that round, so those parts wait a turn. Some agents park them in a README section they invent: taxi-A removed its section later, while co2-A left an invented pointer section in README. A fresh session before scope finishes would find no record of the question. Separately, awb-scope has no create-investigation helper, so a new investigation is always a manual copy of templates. The claim that template placeholder prose stays is not supported: the true placeholders were replaced in every run, and what remains is standing state.md guidance, kept by some runs and stripped by others. The wait itself is intended, since every cited first message still left decisions open for the user.

consolidated.title: check-draft's pass and fail signals do not match where the draft is in its lifecycle
consolidated.description: check-draft prints passed: true while its review row is stale or missing, though Done and release both require a current review (taxi-A, retail-B). The read-only form (MCP read, --verify-only) returns an error before the first writing run ('manifest.json records no inventory list'), and again when the inventory or receipt is stale after edits. Expected steps therefore look like tool failures (co2-A, co2-B).
consolidated.caused_by_fix: partly: #96 (issue #84) added the review status as an informational row that does not affect passed. The verify-only error predates the fixes (awb_draft.py:2746 at 1db6084).
consolidated.evidence: taxi-A-23: replies 7-8; feedback/agent.md section 1 item 8. retail-B-19: agent-006 check-draft shows 'review': {'status': 'stale'} with 'passed': true; awb-package/SKILL.md step 6. co2-A-14: 2 failed read check-draft calls in agent-006, 1 in agent-007. co2-B-09: relay/agent-004.jsonl and agent-005.jsonl; awb_draft.py:3113.

verdicts.reasoning:
Nothing in how the simulation was run explains this finding. Every behavior described comes from deterministic release code, and it showed up the same way for a Codex agent (co2-A, taxi-A) and a Claude agent (co2-B, retail-B).

How the release produces it:
1. In awb_draft.py check_draft, verify-only mode raises "manifest.json records no inventory list; run check-draft without --verify-only" whenever no writing run has recorded an inventory yet. After edits, verify-only correctly reports size and checksum mismatches against the recorded inventory.
2. awb_mcp.py exposes check-draft on the read tool only as --verify-only. Its execute() sets isError for any nonzero exit, and check-draft exits 1 whenever passed is false. So every failing check, including a writing check-draft through the package tool (retail-B's first call), shows up as a failed tool call.
3. The final line of check_draft sets passed from the structure checks and flags only. The review row is informational by design: helpers.md calls it "informational in check-draft", awb-package SKILL.md line 92 makes Done require both passed:true and review current, and release gates on review.

Harness explanations I tried and rejected:
- **Auto-approved MCP tools.** These don't explain it. On a real host the write tool (package) is more likely to need per-call approval than the readOnlyHint read tool, so agents would lean on the read check even more.
- **Codex sandbox.** The package tool worked fine in co2-A.
- **Persona front-loading and relay behavior.** These play no part.
- **Study disclosure.** It explains why agents wrote this friction up. It does not explain the friction.
- **Sim hiding tool calls from the user.** If anything this understates the effect. On a real host the user would see the red failed-tool markers.

What I verified in the logs:
- **co2-A:** two failed read check-draft calls in agent-006 (inventory error) and one in agent-007 (verify mismatches after edits).
- **co2-B:** five isError read check-draft calls across agent-004 and agent-005, all with the inventory error.
- **taxi-A agent-007:** writing check-draft returned passed:true with review "none", then "stale", before the review ran.
- **retail-B agent-006:** passed:true with review "stale".

Why the finding needs narrowing:
1. **The passed/review half is documented, intended behavior, and no agent misread it.** taxi-A ran check-draft before its review (the skill orders the review first), then reported only after review was current. retail-B told the user one review item still needed their yes. Both agents' own feedback says the skill explains this. The harm is hypothetical: "a caller reading passed alone could mistake" it.
2. **The verify-only errors are not "expected steps" in the documented workflow.** awb-package runs the writing check-draft last. awb-release runs verify-only only on a release candidate. The agents used verify-only as a preflight while iterating. co2-B admits this broke the skill's order: "I ran read check-draft repeatedly before the review... The skill orders check last." The error text itself tells the agent what to do, both agents called the result "expected", and both finished correctly.

What still holds is an ergonomics problem a real user's agent could hit on any host. The read tool, the only non-writing way to run the checks and the natural pick under the release's MCP-first rule, offers only release-candidate verification. Mid-draft that gives noisy failures marked isError.
verdicts.release_evidence:

verdicts.reasoning:
Both behaviors in C-27 happen as described. Both are documented, intended semantics in the release. The shipped instructions already stop the misreading the finding warns about, and every cited agent read the signals correctly.

(1) passed: true while the review is stale, missing or failed. In awb_draft.py check_draft (around lines 3149-3152) the review row is marked "Informational" and is left out of `passed`. The CLI epilog says the review row "is informational, and release refuses unless it is current". helpers.md line 36 and package-contract.md line 72 say the same. awb-package/SKILL.md step 6 defines Done as "check-draft prints passed: true ... and its review row is current". The release gate (awb_draft.py around line 5169) refuses unless the review is current. The cited runs show agents applying that rule:
- taxi-A: its agent.md item 8 says "The skill explains the extra review-current condition". The final reports were given only with review:current.
- retail-B turn 6 (agent-006): check-draft did return passed true with review stale, and later passed true with review failed. The agent told the user the automated checks pass, but that one review item still needs a yes "before the draft is fully cleared". That is correct.
No user was misled and no release went out early.

(2) The read-only form errors before the first writing run and after edits. awb_mcp.py maps read check-draft to `check-draft --verify-only`. Its tool description calls it "verify a release candidate, writing nothing". The package tool's description says the writing form rewrites the inventory, and that "the read tool's check-draft verifies without writing". The awb-package sequence never calls the read form: step 6 runs the writing `check-draft`, and only awb-release uses --verify-only. Refusing a draft with no recorded inventory, or one whose files no longer match it, is correct release-gate behavior. The error names its own fix: "run check-draft without --verify-only" (awb_draft.py:3113). The agents used the release gate as a mid-draft preflight anyway:
- co2-A: 2 failed read calls in agent-006 (missing inventory) and 1 in agent-007 (chart checksum and size mismatches after re-export).
- co2-B: repeated read calls in agent-004 and agent-005.
The co2-B agent admits it deviated: "I ran read check-draft repeatedly before the review... The skill orders check last." Even so, every agent understood the error. co2-A's harness log says "as expected before finalization". co2-B said "The read tool only verifies, so the inventory gets written once the review is done". Both then ran the writing form and finished correctly.

Citation problem: C-27 cites "retail-B-19", but retail-B findings.json id 19 is about project conventions. The matching finding is retail-B-16.

What remains is a matter of taste: a `passed` key that leaves out a gate that is documented separately, and isError marking whenever a check fails. That is not a defect the release causes, and it led to no wrong claim or blocked step.
