consolidated.title: awb-status counts findings users cannot map to their questions, and skips the per-question layout
consolidated.description: Status still opens with calculation-level counts. retail-A reported 'seven supported and seven provisional findings' for five questions. It counted intake and sensitivity checks as findings, and used 'provisional' to mean 'headline not yet approved'. taxi-A's 'nine supported findings and two provisional reference calculations' could not be mapped onto the questions. The finding model also has no reference-only role, so replacing still-valid reference calculations left Q3 and Q5 'awaiting recheck'. taxi-A and co2-A gave status as prose paragraphs inside packaging turns, without the per-question list or the 'You can ask for' requests. retail-A did the user's other request first, against the skill's 'after the report' order, so the report would include it. Tag: co2-A-05 is unclear; the other members are product.
consolidated.caused_by_fix: partly, through three fixes. #102 (issue #86) added 'answered (provisional, awaiting recheck)', which taxi-A's superseded reference results triggered. #104 (issue #93) put active.counts before the per-question entries, and set the order 'other requests after the report'. #104's state template and #105's glossary define promotion as following headline approval, so supporting checks never leave provisional.
consolidated.evidence: taxi-A-05: msg 8, reply 8; awb-status/SKILL.md Report. taxi-A-06: replies 5, 6 and 8; agent-notes line 67. co2-A-05: r5; agent-005 had read the awb-status SKILL.md. retail-A-01: status in reply 5, msg 6 ('What are the 14?'), reply 6; README 'Provisional' (line 97). retail-A-30: msg 5, reply 5; awb-status/SKILL.md line 10. Release: awb-status/SKILL.md:29.

verdicts.reasoning:
I looked for harness causes and found one real influence, but it does not explain the defect.

The harness influence: each persona BRIEF lists "ask where things stand at least once (awb-status)" as a checklist step. So in every run, status was asked in a message that also asked for other work: taxi-A msg 8 (status, three corrections, release), co2-A msg 5 (status, then awb-package), retail-A msg 5 (Q4 rework, then status). The runs never show a status request on its own.

Why that does not make this a harness artifact:
- The release says this case is supported. README line 84 promises "One screen: each of your questions with its findings, every open caveat, anything at risk, and up to five requests you can type next", and says other requests in the same message, such as "where are we? Then reword question 3.", are carried out after the report. awb-status/SKILL.md line 10 says the same. A real user who follows the README would send exactly this kind of mixed message.
- In taxi-A (agent-008) and co2-A (agent-005), the agent ran `cat` on awb-status/SKILL.md and called `read status`. It still gave the status as prose, with no list of questions and no "You can ask for" section.
- co2-A's status output was not truncated. taxi-A's was cut by the release's own awb_mcp.py (16000-character default; the harness does not set AWB_MCP_MAX_CHARS), so the cut is release behaviour.
- The Claude-agent run taxi-B (claude -p) shows the same pattern: "All 11 findings are provisional" and a bullet list with neither part. So it is not specific to Codex.
- None of the following explain it: codex exec versus interactive use (interim messages appear the same way), the sandbox, auto-approved MCP tools, the simulated home, or the study note.

The counting complaint is caused by the release whatever the output format. The collector's active.counts, which SKILL.md line 29 says to report first, counts every recorded calculation as a finding. In retail-A that was 7 supported and 7 provisional: intake, revenue reconciliation and sensitivity checks stay provisional for good, because under the README's definition (line 97) only an approved headline promotes a finding. Even the per-question breakdown would have read Q-001 as "2 supported, 4 provisional". The user had to spend msg 6 asking "What are the 14?". In taxi-A, the "two provisional reference calculations" come from the finding model having no reference-only role (agent.md item 3, agent-notes turn 6).

Two members do not hold:
1. retail-A ordering. The user wrote "Then use awb-status — where are we?" at the end of msg 5. The agent followed that order on purpose (agent-notes line 85). That is correct behaviour toward the user, not a defect, so I would drop this member.
2. taxi-A 'awaiting recheck'. Q3 and Q5 showed it only inside the agent's own records, and the agent fixed it before the user saw anything ("recheck" never appears in the transcript). The user only ever saw the leftover "two provisional reference calculations" in the count.
verdicts.release_evidence:
- awb-status/SKILL.md:29 (Findings: report `active.counts` first, then `by_question`), :10 (do other requests after the report), :38-40 ("You can ask for" list).
- README line 84 promises the one-screen per-question layout with up to five suggested requests, including when other requests share the message.
- README line 97: "Provisional" means a finding whose headline or wording is not yet approved, so supporting calculations stay provisional.
- awb-init/assets/awb_mcp.py:72 truncates at 16000 characters by default, which cut taxi-A's status output.
- Collector output: retail-A cached status shows active.counts {supported 7, provisional 7}, with Q-001 at {supported 2, provisional 4}. taxi-A shows counts {supported 9, provisional 2}, with Q-003 and Q-005 each at {provisional 1, supported 2}.
- Runs: taxi-A agent-008 and co2-A agent-005 both `cat` awb-status/SKILL.md and then write the status as prose. The Claude agent in taxi-B does the same ("All 11 findings are provisional", no per-question list, no suggested requests).
verdicts.narrowed: awb-status reports counts of calculations rather than counts per question. The collector's active.counts, which SKILL.md:29 says to report first, and even its per-question counts include intake, reconciliation, sensitivity and reference calculations. Those stay 'provisional' for good, because only an approved headline promotes a finding. So users cannot map the counts to their questions: retail-A's '7 supported and 7 provisional' for five questions cost the user a turn, and taxi-A's '9 supported, 2 provisional reference calculations' could not be mapped. When status shared a message with other requests, which the README says is supported, both Codex and Claude agents read the skill and still left out the per-question list and the 'You can ask for' requests: taxi-A and co2-A gave prose, retail-A and taxi-B gave bullets. Drop the retail-A ordering member: the user explicitly asked for status after the Q4 work. The taxi-A 'awaiting recheck' was agent-internal and fixed before the user saw it. Its only user-visible effect was the two provisional reference calculations in the count.

verdicts.reasoning:
Most of the finding holds, and the release causes it. One part does not hold: the retail-A ordering point.

1) Counts that cannot be mapped to questions. awb-status/SKILL.md:29 tells the agent to open the Findings item with `active.counts`. The collector builds that by counting every row in state.md's findings table (collect_status.py, active block), so supporting checks, alternate rankings and reference calculations are all counted. Under the finding model, a finding stays provisional until the user approves its headline (README.md:97; investigation/state.md:10). Intake, sensitivity and reconciliation checks never get a headline, so they stay "provisional" indefinitely. retail-A reply 5 reported "seven supported and seven provisional findings" for five questions. The user's next message asked "What are the 14?" (msg 6), and reply 6 explained them as supporting calculations. Even a fully compliant report would not have fixed this. retail-A's cached status shows by_question folds child questions into their root: Q-001 would read {supported 2, provisional 4}, with the intake, reconciliation and sensitivity checks included, even though the user had already accepted Q1.

2) No reference-only role. This is confirmed in code. awb_provenance.py's answer function can only add results to a question (`entry["results"] += linked`); it can never remove one. Per provenance.md:23 and the collector's recheck rule, any superseded answering finding makes the question show "awaiting recheck". taxi-A's agent notes (verify-Q3 entry) record that Q3 and Q5 went to awaiting recheck for this reason. The agent's workaround, setting the findings back to provisional, then appeared in status as "two provisional reference calculations" (reply 8), which the user could not map (human.md item 4).

3) Prose instead of the per-question layout. The skill is clear: "one screen, in this order" (line 26), each by_question entry (line 29), and a "You can ask for" list (lines 38-40). The agents read the SKILL.md (taxi-A agent-008, co2-A agent-005, retail-A agent-005) and skipped the layout anyway. That is the agent ignoring a clear instruction. But it happened in all 6 runs: the B runs, driven by Claude (co2-B reply 3, retail-B reply 4), also returned a short summary with no per-question list and no requests. Each time, status came bundled with other work. Both the taxi-A and co2-A users said this broke the README's "one screen" promise (README.md:85). Because it happens every time, the instruction is not working in practice. For taxi-A specifically, its by_question output would have mapped the 11 findings onto the questions (Q3 and Q5 each 2 supported + 1 provisional), so the unmappable count there partly comes from skipping the layout.

4) The retail-A ordering point is not a defect. User msg 5 explicitly put status last ("Then use awb-status — where are we?"), and the agent followed the user's order. SKILL.md:10 does not mention deferring to the user's own ordering, but nobody was harmed.

Also, co2-A's status did not misstate counts ("all nine saved results are current"); its problem is only the layout.
verdicts.release_evidence:
- awb-status/SKILL.md:29: "**Findings.** `active.counts`, then each `questions.by_question` entry…" (the per-calculation total comes first).
- awb-status/SKILL.md:26 and 38-40: one-screen order and the "You can ask for" list.
- awb-status/SKILL.md:10: other requests "after the report".
- awb-status/scripts/collect_status.py: the active block counts every findings row; ledger() builds by_question with results_under(), which folds child-question results into the root; the recheck rule treats any superseded answering finding as needing recheck.
- awb-init/references/provenance.md:23: a superseded answering finding means awaiting recheck.
- awb-init/assets/workbench/investigation/state.md:10, plus README.md:97 (a finding stays provisional until the user approves its headline) and README.md:85 (the "One screen… each of your questions… up to five requests" promise).
- awb-init/assets/awb_provenance.py, answer function around lines 2200-2245: results can only be appended to a question, never removed.

Run evidence:
- taxi-A reply 8 (prose; "nine supported findings and two provisional reference calculations").
- taxi-A cached status 20261017-081556: counts {supported 9, provisional 2}; by_question gives Q3/Q5 {provisional 1, supported 2}.
- taxi-A agent-notes, verify-Q3 entry: superseded findings put Q3/Q5 into awaiting recheck; the agent restored them to provisional.
- co2-A reply 5 (prose; agent-005 had read the SKILL.md).
- retail-A reply 5 / msg 6 / reply 6; cached status 20261017-075719: counts {supported 7, provisional 7}; by_question Q-001 {supported 2, provisional 4}.
- co2-B reply 3 and retail-B reply 4: the same compressed summary from the Claude-driven runs.
verdicts.narrowed: awb-status leads its Findings item with `active.counts` (SKILL.md:29). That counts every findings row, including supporting checks, alternate rankings and reference calculations. A finding stays provisional until the user approves its headline, a result can never be unlinked from a question, and superseding one forces the question into awaiting recheck. So supporting and reference calculations stay "provisional" indefinitely, and status reports totals like "7 supported, 7 provisional" for five questions. by_question also folds sub-question checks into the user's question, so a fully compliant report is still confusing. Separately, in all six runs, with both agents, a status request bundled with other work came back as a short summary without the per-question list or the "You can ask for" requests the skill and README promise. Remove the retail-A ordering claim: the user explicitly asked for status last, and following that order was correct.

consolidated.title: check-draft's linkage between slides and methodology sections is brittle
consolidated.description: The first citation in a methodology section sets the slide's primary result, and the weakest cited result sets its claim strength. In taxi-A, a descriptive verification citation downgraded the tipping slide's claim, and inserting a paragraph changed its primary result until the citations were reordered. Rewording a headline requires the identical methodology heading; one forgotten heading came back as four check rows (retail-B). A reworded slide keeps its old slug: co2-B's stayed '45-countries-cut-co2-as-gdp' after 'cut' became 'fell'.
consolidated.caused_by_fix: partly: #103 (issue #90) made the first cited result the primary result, and keeps slide slugs when headings are reworded.
consolidated.evidence: taxi-A-22: reply 7; agent-notes lines 83 and 86. co2-B-37: agent-notes turn 5; slide_slugs in package-contract.md. retail-B-15: agent-006 check-draft rows headings, claims, storyline and unlinked_findings.

verdicts.reasoning:
I could not tie this finding to the harness. Each mechanism comes from the released check-draft code and the package contract, and none of it depends on codex exec, claude -p, the sandbox, MCP auto-approval, the relay or the simulated home.

1. **taxi-A, primary result changed (holds).** In turn 7 the agent added methodology text after the review. Check-draft call 3 in agent-007.jsonl then showed two slides with new primary results: q2-airports became board-airports, and q5-supported became board-rankings, which moved that slide's ranking question from Q-013 to Q-005. The check still returned passed:true with no warning. The agent noticed only by reading ledger_order, put the original citation first again, and call 4 showed the original primaries. This is documented design: helpers.md says "a slide's primary result is the first represented result its matching methodology section cites", and methodology-template.md says to put the primary first. A paragraph that cites another result earlier changes the slide's linkage without any signal. The paragraph was inserted after a failed apply_patch, but the patch mistake was the agent's own, and any editor on any host can insert a paragraph like this.

2. **taxi-A, claim downgrade (holds, narrower than stated).** Check-draft call 1 returned a claims row for the tipping section: it stated association, "its results support descriptive". The cause is the descriptive q3-verification result cited in the same section, through _weakest() in awb_draft.py. The verification was on that slide because the reviewer required it there. The effect is limited to the methodology Claim strength label. awb_draft.py says "Only causal wording is checked: it exceeds descriptive and association", so the slide's wording limits did not change.

3. **retail-B, four rows for one cause (holds).** In agent-006, one missing methodology heading after a headline edit produced rows under headings, claims, storyline and unlinked_findings, and passed:false. The storyline row gave wrong advice: "finding slide is out of place; move it to finding position 6". That happened because the unlinked slide sorts last. Adding the heading cleared all four rows.

4. **co2-B, stale slug (does not hold as a defect).** Keeping the old slug after a reword is intended and documented in manifest-template.md and package-contract.md ("A slide keeps its slug when its heading is reworded while its primary result stays"). Its purpose is to make the order robust, not fragile. co2-B had no presentation_order, so the slug had no effect, and it appears only in manifest.json. The agent itself wrote "fine per contract". It was logged only because the harness asked the agent to keep a private friction log. That makes it an artifact of the study disclosure, not a release problem.
verdicts.release_evidence:
The release's own files define the cited behaviour.

- awb-package/references/helpers.md, storyline paragraph: a slide's primary result is the first one its methodology section cites.
- methodology-template.md: "the primary result first, since it alone places the slide in the deck".
- package-contract.md line 50: a finding slide takes the weakest claim among the results its section cites.
- awb_draft.py, _weakest() and the _CLAIMS comment: only causal wording is checked.
- awb_draft.py, slide_slugs(): the slug is kept on a reword, by design.
- manifest-template.md lines 48-50: the same slug rule.

Run evidence:

- taxi-A/relay/agent-007.jsonl, check-draft call 1: claims row "states association... its results support descriptive".
- The same file, call 3: primaries board-airports and board-rankings (Q-005) with passed:true. Call 4: q2-airports and q5-supported (Q-013) restored.
- retail-B/relay/agent-006.jsonl, first check-draft: headings, claims, storyline ("move it to finding position 6") and unlinked_findings rows all for the same heading, passed:false.
- co2-B/storage/.../001/manifest.json: slide_slugs keeps '45-countries-cut-co2-as-gdp', presentation_order is absent.
- co2-B agent-notes line 88: "fine per contract".
verdicts.narrowed:
check-draft decides each slide's linkage from citations in its methodology section, implicitly, and reports problems with that linkage poorly.

- **(a) Silent primary-result change.** Citing another result earlier in a section changes the slide's primary result, and with it the slide's ranking question, with passed:true and no warning. In taxi-A this happened on two slides; the agent caught it only by comparing ledger_order output.
- **(b) Verification result lowers the label.** A descriptive verification result cited in the same section forces that section's Claim strength label down to descriptive. This affects the label only: wording checks treat descriptive and association the same.
- **(c) One cause, four rows.** One missing methodology heading after a headline edit comes back as four rows (headings, claims, storyline, unlinked_findings). One of them is a failing storyline row that wrongly says to move the slide.

The co2-B slug claim should be dropped. Keeping a slug when the heading is reworded is documented, intended behavior with no effect for the user.

Severity: minor.

verdicts.reasoning:
The release produces every behaviour the finding describes. All of it is written down as design, though, and only part of it does real harm.

1) The claim downgrade is confirmed and comes from the release. In taxi-A reply 7 (agent-007.jsonl), the first check-draft failed with a claims row on the tipping slide: "methodology.md states association on its **Claim strength:** line; its results support descriptive". The slide's methodology section cites `q3-standard` (recorded as association) and `q3-verification` (recorded as descriptive). The release's methodology.md now labels that finding "descriptive". This follows from package-contract.md line 50 ("takes the weakest claim among the results its methodology section cites") and methodology-template.md line 35, implemented in `_weakest`/`_claim_review` in awb_draft.py. The cost is small. awb_draft.py line 1148 says "Only causal wording is checked", so moving from association to descriptive changes no wording the deck may use. It only understates the claim in the internal methodology reference, and it took one check row to fix.

2) The primary result does move when citations are reordered, but the finding names the wrong slide and overstates the effect. In the third check-draft of reply 7, the primary result moved on the airports slide (q2-airports to board-airports) and the rankings slide (q5-supported to board-rankings, question Q-013 to Q-005). It did not move on the tipping slide. storyline stayed [] and the check passed. The agent saw the change in the informational ledger_order and put the citations back in their original order. This is the rule the contract documents (line 34, first cited result), implemented in `_citations`/`finding_primaries`. It is fragile in principle, because a supporting citation placed first can silently change ordering and slug matching. In this run nothing failed.

3) The four-row report from one forgotten heading is confirmed and is the clearest product defect. In retail-B agent-006, the first check-draft returned four rows for one missing methodology heading: a headings row, a claims row ("no ### section with this heading"), unlinked_findings, and a storyline row reading "finding slide is out of place; move it to finding position 6". The storyline row tells the user to make the wrong fix. check-draft (awb_draft.py lines 3089-3103) still runs the claims and storyline checks when headings fails. It only holds back slide_slugs. The rule that headings must match is itself documented (contract line 49, methodology template "Use the same heading text"). The agent forgot it once, not repeatedly, so this is not a case of ignoring a clear instruction.

4) The slug that keeps an old word is intended behaviour, not a defect. Contract line 36, manifest-template line 50 and the `slide_slugs` docstring all keep a slide's slug when its heading is reworded, so that presentation_order stays valid. co2-B's released manifest does keep "45-countries-cut-co2-as-gdp" for the "fell" heading. The slug is an internal manifest key, and the agent itself wrote "fine per contract".
verdicts.release_evidence:
Release files under `SIMS/release/analytics-workbench-skills/awb-package/`:
- `references/package-contract.md`: line 34 (the primary result is the first represented result the section cites); line 49 (headings must be identical); line 50 (a `###` slide takes the weakest cited claim); line 36 (a slide keeps its slug when its heading is reworded).
- `assets/package-format/methodology-template.md` line 35 (claim strength is "the weakest Claim in state.md among its results").
- `assets/package-format/manifest-template.md` line 50 (slug persistence).
- `assets/awb_draft.py`: `_weakest` (line 1224) and `_claim_review` (lines 1308-1355); the comment at line 1148 says only causal wording is gated; `_citations`/`finding_primaries` (lines 2530-2553); `slide_slugs` (lines 2565-2611); check-draft lines 3089-3103 run the claims and storyline checks even when headings fails, suppressing only the slug update.

Run evidence:
- taxi-A `relay/agent-007.jsonl`: check-draft #1 claims row on the tipping slide; check-draft #3 ledger_order shows the primary moving to board-airports and board-rankings, with storyline=[] and passed=true.
- taxi-A released `methodology.md` line 57: "Claim strength: descriptive" for the tipping finding.
