- co2-B `released/001/manifest.json` slide_slugs; co2-B agent-notes line 88.
verdicts.narrowed: check-draft does not hold back its dependent checks when a methodology heading is missing. One headline reworded without the matching methodology `###` heading comes back as four rows: headings, claims, unlinked_findings, and a storyline row that gives the wrong fix ("move it to finding position N"). This happened in retail-B. Separately, the documented rules that the first citation sets a slide's primary result and the weakest citation sets its claim strength make methodology edits fragile in a small way. In taxi-A, citing a descriptive verification result forced the tipping finding's Claim strength line from association down to descriptive; that understates the claim in the internal reference but changes no permitted deck wording. Inserting a paragraph silently moved the primary result of the airports and rankings slides, not the tipping slide; the check still passed and the order did not change. The slug claim (co2-B) should be dropped: keeping a slide's slug across a rewording is intended, documented behaviour for an internal key.

consolidated.title: Chat figures, counts and bases misstated, or changed without notice
consolidated.description: retail-B's Answer headline gave 55% without the identified-customer base. It used a 90% share of Year 2 revenue to support a growth claim, and its methodology mixed two bases. co2-A charted a different ten countries from the ten the user asked for, and told the user in chat it had used 'the same ten countries'. taxi-A gave 91.844997% as 91.85% in chat; the release correctly shows 91.8%. Tag: taxi-A-17 and co2-A-11 are unclear. retail-B-03 is product: it broke a clear AGENTS.md rule three times, and the problem recurs across runs.
consolidated.caused_by_fix: no
consolidated.evidence: retail-B-03: reply 3, msg 4; the agent-005 full review notes 'methodology.md:28 ... mixes two bases'; AGENTS.md 'Name every share's base and say when it changes' (added by #102). co2-A-11: m6, r6; release 001 charts/chart-2.csv; findings.md line 39. taxi-A-17: reply 5 table; Q3 row of the orchestrator-report spot-check.

verdicts.reasoning:
I found no harness cause for the retail-B part. Only a narrow version of the finding holds. The co2-A part is not supported, and the taxi-A part is a trivial model slip with a different cause.

retail-B (Claude agent, Codex persona as the user):
- In reply 3, the headline preview's Answer line read "top 10% of customers brought 55%". It left out the identified-customer population, although the user had asked in msg 2 for both bases to be named.
- The same preview backed "Australia grew most... but through one account" with "One customer holds 90% of Australia's Year 2 revenue". That is a share of revenue level, not of growth. The share of growth was 97%, which the agent found only after the user challenged it in msg 4.
- The rule is in the project's AGENTS.md, line 30: "Name every share's base and say when it changes."
- AGENTS.md was very likely loaded. The agent ran Claude Code 2.1.301 with the builtin cc-plugin-agents-md plugin, `--setting-sources` included `project`, and every turn after the first was a fresh `--resume` process. The replies also end with the AGENTS.md turn-end line in turns that did not use awb-status.
- Each harness factor fails to explain the slip:
  - The persona's careful msg 2 made the slip more likely to be caught, not to happen.
  - Running non-interactively changes nothing at the headline preview step.
  - Neither the study disclosure nor the simulated home bears on how bases are worded.
  - On a real interactive host, AGENTS.md is created partway through the awb-init session, so it would be loaded no better than here.
- The release's part in this:
  - The awb-package headline checkpoint repeats the explanation rule but not the base rule.
  - The independent review runs only at draft time, so the chat preview goes unchecked. The orchestrator's retail-B issue #2 notes the same gap.
  - human.md line 45 confirms the risk: "The initial summary omitted the identified-customer qualifier, which could mislead leadership."
- The methodology "two bases" item (methodology.md:28, 22.5% of lines across the whole export next to 13.4% of window revenue) was a draft error. The release's own review flagged it in agent-005-record01.txt and it was fixed. The released methodology.md:28 gives "227,423 of 1,019,322 lines... 13.4%". That is the release working as intended, not a defect the user saw.
- So the claim that the rule was broken "three times" overcounts. There are two chat slips plus one draft slip that review caught.
- The released deck names its bases correctly. The Answer bullet reads "55.1% of total net revenue" and the Australia slide reads "97% of it from one account".
- The C-32 label is also wrong: retail-B-03 in findings.json and in the orchestrator's list is the imperative-headline issue, not this one.

co2-A-11 is not supported:
- human-006.jsonl shows the persona read the original .preview/headlines.md before writing msg 6.
- Line 47 of that preview already listed the ten later charted: US, Japan, Germany, Italy, UK, France, Spain, Netherlands, Czechia and Belgium. Line 48 planned a chart of their 2022 levels.
- The user's "For those ten countries, chart the % change" refers to that list. chart-2.csv in release 001 holds exactly those ten.
- So the agent's "same ten countries" was accurate. The referee compared against the reply-3 table of the 45 countries with any decline, which the user was not referring to.

taxi-A:
- The chat in reply 5 said 91.85%. The exact value in results/q3-standard.csv is 0.91844997, which rounds to 91.84%.
- The agent's tool output showed pandas' 6-decimal display "0.918450", and the agent rounded that rounded value again.
- This is a 0.01-point model slip in chat. The agent's own refinements.md has 91.84% and the release shows 91.8%.
- The harness did not cause it, but neither did the release in any meaningful way, and it is not a base problem.
- findings.json's taxi-A-17 is also a different issue (the threshold sign-off).

The finding's claim that this recurs across runs is therefore not supported. Only retail-B shows base misstatements.
verdicts.release_evidence:
- awb-init/assets/workbench/AGENTS.md line 30: "Offer an untested explanation as a question. Name every share's base and say when it changes." This one line is the only place the base rule appears.
- awb-package/SKILL.md, headline checkpoint (lines 45-54): the preview-and-wait mode shows headlines with their figures in chat and repeats only "Offer an untested explanation as a question, never as a headline's claim". There is no check of share bases.
- The independent review runs only once a draft exists, so a headline preview shown in chat goes unreviewed.
- CHANGELOG.md line 154 confirms the checkpoint repeats only the explanation rule.
- retail-B/transcript.md reply 3, Answer row: "top 10% of customers brought 55%". Slide 6: "One customer holds 90% of Australia's Year 2 revenue" offered for a growth claim.
- The user corrects both in msg 4. Reply 4 gives 97% of the growth.
- retail-B/feedback/human.md line 45 confirms the identified-customer qualifier was missing.
verdicts.narrowed:
Only retail-B shows the problem, and only in chat. The user caught both slips, and the release names its bases correctly.

In retail-B's reply-3 headline preview, the Claude agent misstated share bases in chat twice, against the AGENTS.md "Name every share's base" rule:
- The Answer line said "top 10% of customers brought 55%" without naming identified customers.
- It offered a 90% share of Australia's Year 2 revenue as support for a growth claim; the share of growth was 97%.

The release has no check on share bases before the draft. The headline checkpoint repeats the explanation rule but not the base rule, and the review runs only at draft time.

The methodology two-base slip was caught and fixed by the release's own review. The co2-A "same ten countries" claim is not supported: the ten charted are exactly the ten in the preview the user referred to. taxi-A's 91.85% (exact value 91.84%) is a 0.01-point double-rounding slip in chat, not caused by the release and unrelated to share bases. The finding's claims of recurrence across runs and of three rule breaks do not hold.

verdicts.reasoning:
I checked the three runs one at a time against the shipped files.

co2-A (charted a different ten countries): the evidence contradicts this. In reply 5 the headline preview (.preview/headlines.md, as written during agent-005) already listed the ten largest emitters among the 38 qualifying countries. Those were US, Japan, Germany, Italy, UK, France, Spain, Netherlands, Czechia and Belgium, and the plan was to chart their 2022 levels. The user's message 6 says "For those ten countries, chart the % change", which refers to that preview chart. Release 001 charts/chart-2.csv and findings.md (Q2 slide) show exactly those ten. So when reply 6 said "the same ten countries", that was accurate. The referee compared the chart against the reply-3 table, which listed the top ten of the 45 countries before the user picked the 5% threshold. The swap of Canada, Mexico, Australia and Poland follows from the user's own choice of 38, and the preview the user approved names the new ten.

taxi-A (91.85%): the slip is real but tiny and comes from the agent, not the release. The result is 0.91844997, which rounds to 91.84%. The agent wrote its own pandas command (to_string), which printed 0.918450, and then rounded a second time to get 91.85%. No release helper produced that output. The release's numbers check traces package text, and the release itself correctly shows 91.8%.

retail-B: the slips are real, but the release has a clear rule against them and caught them. The shipped awb-init/assets/workbench/AGENTS.md line 30 says "Name every share's base and say when it changes". The project had no CLAUDE.md in the folder or above it, and the host was Claude Code 2.1.301 with the AGENTS.md plugin, so the rule was in context.
- In reply 3, the Answer headline "top 10% of customers brought 55%" left out both "identified" and the base of the 55%. The same message's slide 4 did state both bases ("64% of identified revenue, 55% of total"). Adding "identified" would have kept the headline within the 15-word cap, so the cap did not force the omission.
- Australia's "90% of Australia's Year 2 revenue" did name its base. The real problem is that a share of revenue was used to support a growth claim, which is an analysis error rather than an unnamed base.
- The user caught both at the release's headline checkpoint (preview-and-wait), and reply 4 fixed them: 97% of the growth came from one account, and the headline now says "identified customers".
- The methodology.md:28 mix (22.5% of all lines next to 13.4% of revenue in the window) was caught by the release's own package review (agent-005 record01). It was fixed before release, and release 001's methodology.md:28 now gives 227,423 of 1,019,322 lines in the window.

Counting this as "broke the rule three times" overstates it. One of the three instances named its base, and one was caught by the product's own review. All the slips fall in one drafting pass, and none reached the release. The claim that the problem recurs across runs does not hold either: no other run's findings record a misstated share base, and the two cross-run examples cited are the co2-A non-issue and the taxi-A arithmetic slip. Nothing in the release causes these misstatements, its rule and checkpoints already address them, and the agent did not keep ignoring the rule after it was corrected.
verdicts.release_evidence:
- awb-init/assets/workbench/AGENTS.md:30 says "Offer an untested explanation as a question. Name every share's base and say when it changes." CHANGELOG.md:154 records this rule being added.
- awb-package/SKILL.md:45-54 defines the headline checkpoint (preview-and-wait), where the user caught the retail-B headline slips.
- awb-package/references/review.md is the independent package review that flagged "methodology.md:28 ... mixes two bases" (retail-B/review-reports/agent-005-record01.txt:10). It was fixed in release 001 (methodology.md:28).
- awb-package/assets/package-format/findings-template.md:14 sets the 15-word headline cap, with an exception if the user agrees to a longer one. The cap did not force the base to be dropped: "identified" fits within 15 words.
- No shipped helper produced taxi-A's 0.918450: it came from an ad hoc `.venv/bin/python -c ... to_string` command in taxi-A/relay/agent-005.jsonl.
- co2-A: draft/.preview/headlines.md (reply 5 version in co2-A/relay/agent-006.jsonl item_4) lists US, Japan, Germany, Italy, UK, France, Spain, Netherlands, Czechia and Belgium. These match release 001 charts/chart-2.csv exactly.
verdicts.narrowed: In retail-B, the first headline preview (reply 3) left "identified" and the 55% share's base out of the Answer headline. It also used Australia's 90% share of Year 2 revenue to back a growth claim. The internal methodology draft mixed two bases in one sentence. All three are agent slips against the shipped AGENTS.md rule, all within one drafting pass. The release's headline checkpoint (the user) and its package review caught them, and they were fixed before release 001. Separately, taxi-A's chat said 91.85% instead of 91.84% because the agent rounded twice from its own pandas printout. That is a one-off agent arithmetic slip, and the released figure (91.8%) is correct. Neither of these is caused by the release. The co2-A part of the finding does not hold.

consolidated.title: First results reports give highlights, not the full answers the questions ask for
consolidated.description: The Claude agents' first answers gave partial rankings and ranges instead of the tables the questions ask for. taxi-B's top ten named only four zones, and its borough, hour and weekday breakdowns were partial. co2-B gave values for only a few countries, left the coal eligibility count ambiguous, and proposed a slide plan with no room for the required slides. retail-B gave ranges instead of the 24 monthly figures and 12 cohort rates, and still called the questions answered. Each cost a follow-up request.
consolidated.caused_by_fix: no
consolidated.evidence: taxi-B-18: reply 3, msg 4, reply 4 tables. co2-B-08: A2 answers 1, 2 and 5; U3; A3 tables. retail-B-09: reply 3 (ranges only), msg 4 ('Ranges alone don't fully answer those questions'), reply 4. The 'answered (provisional)' footer added by #102 did appear (taxi-B-17).

verdicts.reasoning:
I looked for a harness cause and found none that explains the partial first reports.

What the transcripts show:
- **taxi-B, reply 3.** Question 5 asks which 10 zones lead. The reply named only four (Flushing Meadows, South Ozone Park, JFK, LaGuardia). Borough tips covered only Manhattan and Queens, plus the Bronx/Brooklyn 0% case. Hours and weekdays were summarised in prose. The footer still read "5 answered (provisional)". Message 4 asked for the full tables, and reply 4 supplied them.
- **retail-B, reply 3.** The answers came only as figures behind each headline in the headline preview: ranges such as "30% to 52%", peak and low months, annual totals. Message 4 said "Ranges alone don't fully answer those questions", and reply 4 gave the 24-month and 12-cohort tables.
- **co2-B, reply 2.** It named all 10 countries for Q1, Q2 and Q5 but gave values for only the top one to five. The coal count read "59 countries ... Libya also qualifies", which is ambiguous. The proposed plan (title, overview, five question slides, implications) left no room for How we know or Limitations. Message 3 asked for the tables.

Harness factors I checked and ruled out:
- **Relay truncation.** The relay joins every top-level assistant text block from claude -p and cuts nothing. The partial replies are what the agent actually wrote.
- **Agent prompt and study note.** Neither says anything about reply length. Both say to work as normal.
- **Long first messages.** The personas put everything in the first message, as the README tells users to.
- **Strict simulated user.** The Codex user's brief demands specific, quantitative answers, so a follow-up was certain. But a real user who asks "which 10 zones" and gets four names would also notice.
- **Which model played the agent.** The A runs (Codex agent) gave fuller first tables. But there the Claude user asked for "the numbers in chat" up front, which confounds the comparison. The Oct 16 reference run found the same partial-answer pattern from Codex agents in co2-A and retail-A, so this is not specific to Claude.

The cause lies in the release's reporting rules:
- AGENTS.md says only "Answer in chat, giving file paths" and "Summarize helper output". Nothing requires showing every item a question asks for (all N of a top-N, every period of a series) or naming the result file that holds them.
- The #102 change made preview-and-wait show "the figures behind each headline that chat has not shown". retail-B followed that to the letter and still sent ranges.
- The #102 'answered (provisional)' footer labels the state; it does not make the answer complete.
- In taxi-B and retail-B the full tables already existed as result CSVs, but the agent never pointed to them. The taxi-B agent's own notes say there is "no package path for 'readable results table' outside a draft".

A real user on an interactive host would get the same first reply.

The finding overstates two things:
- **"Each cost a follow-up request."** In all three runs the request for full tables went into a message the user had to send anyway: a tipping decision and headline request in taxi-B, December checks and wording changes in retail-B, a status and headline preview in co2-B. It cost an extra request line and a longer later reply, not an extra exchange.
- **co2-B is the weakest case.** All ranked names were present. The reply pointed to the results folder. The coal count was stated, only ambiguously. The slide plan was an offhand proposal made before the agent loaded awb-package, and it was corrected once the agent did.
verdicts.release_evidence:
- **awb-init/assets/workbench/AGENTS.md, Conversation section.** It says "Summarize helper output, quoting it only on failure or request. Answer in chat, giving file paths". It sets no completeness requirement for an answer: no rule to list every item of a top-N, every period of a series, or every group's base, and no rule to point to the result CSV.
- **awb-package/SKILL.md, headline checkpoint, preview-and-wait.** It says "show them with the figures behind each headline that chat has not shown". The headline-level figures it asks for are what retail-B reply 3 gave: ranges and peaks, not the 24 monthly figures or 12 cohort rates.
- **CHANGELOG.md line 153 (#102).** It adds the 'answered (provisional)' display and footer count, plus the headline-checkpoint figures rule. It labels the state but does not require the full answer to be shown.
- **README.md.** "Along the way, answers come in chat" is the only statement of what the user sees.
- **The full tables existed but were not linked.** taxi-B's investigations/airport-trips-and-tipping/results/ and retail-B's investigations/marketing-budget-evidence/results/ held the complete tables, but neither reply 3 pointed to them. The taxi-B agent's notes (feedback/agent-notes.md, turn 4) say: "no package path for 'readable results table' outside a draft; produced it in chat from result CSVs."
- **Ruled out: relay truncation.** relay.py `_claude_reply` joins all top-level assistant texts without cutting any.
verdicts.narrowed: Under the released reporting rules, the Claude agent's first results report in taxi-B and retail-B gave highlights rather than the complete answer the question asks for. taxi-B named 4 of the top 10 zones, and its borough and hour breakdowns were partial. retail-B gave only ranges and headline figures at the preview-and-wait checkpoint in place of the 24 monthly figures and 12 cohort rates. Neither reply pointed to the result CSVs that held the full tables, and both footers counted the questions as answered (provisional). co2-B shows a weaker form: all ranked names but few values, a coal count that was stated but ambiguous, and a slide plan made before the agent loaded the package skill. The cost was an extra request bundled into a message the user would have sent anyway, not an extra exchange.

verdicts.reasoning:
The core pattern holds in all three Claude runs, and nothing in the harness explains it. The agent system prompt (taxi-B/prompts/claude-agent-system.md, identical to kit/claude-agent-system.md apart from paths) has no length or brevity constraint. So a real Claude Code user would plausibly hit this too.

No shipped file causes it directly, and no shipped file prevents it. Several workbench steps have an explicit Report section: awb-explore step 6, awb-package step 7, and awb-status's one-screen order. The analysis step has none. README line 83 says only that the agent "computes each answer", and line 33 says "answers come in chat". workbench-guides/analysis.md covers results, validation and promotion but says nothing about what the user sees. Nothing anywhere requires the first results report to give the whole answer the question asks for: every ranked item with its value, every month or cohort, every group with its base.

The only nearby text leans the other way.
- AGENTS.md line 28: "Summarize helper output, quoting it only on failure or request."
- The awb-package preview-and-wait checkpoint asks only for "the figures behind each headline that chat has not shown". In retail-B the user asked for answers and headlines in one message. The agent then used the headline table as its only answer, with a "Figures behind it" column of ranges and highlights.
- The "N answered (provisional)" footer comes from ledger status, which run.py sets when a result declares `answers`. It says nothing about whether chat showed the full answer.

The same release is not enough to cause the problem on its own. All three Codex runs (taxi-A, co2-A, retail-A) gave complete tables in their first results reply. retail-A shows all 24 months and all 12 cohorts. taxi-A shows all 10 zones and every borough, though its user had asked only for "key numbers in chat". co2-A shows values for all 10 in each ranking, with baseline and end-year values for coal and an explicit 60-eligible, 59-analyzed count. So the release leaves a gap that Claude's tendency to summarize falls into; it does not dictate the behaviour.

Checking the evidence:
- taxi-B is confirmed. Reply 3 names four of the top ten zones ("All ten are in Queens"), gives selected weekdays, an hour range, and Manhattan and Queens tip medians (Bronx and Brooklyn only in the decision block). Airport medians appear as ranges such as "$55–58". Message 4 asks for the full tables and reply 4 supplies them. The reply 3 footer reads "5 answered (provisional)". The finding cites the footer as taxi-B-17, but taxi-B-17 is actually the joins-check finding.
- co2-B is partly overstated. A2 names all ten countries in every ranking, so the rankings were complete; only the values were partial (Q1 gives values for 3 of 20 countries, Q2 for 1 of 10, Q5 for 5 of 10). The coal count is ambiguous as claimed: "the 59 countries... Libya also qualifies". The slide-plan point is a different issue. It was a plan proposed before awb-package was loaded, and the user settled it with "methods and limitations in an appendix".
- retail-B is confirmed. Reply 3 gives "30% to 52%" and a few months only. Message 4 says "Ranges alone don't fully answer those questions", and reply 4 gives both full tables. The footer reads "5 answered (all provisional...)".
- "Cost a follow-up request" overstates the cost. In each run the follow-up message was needed anyway: the tipping decision in taxi-B, the status and headline requests in co2-B, the status, December check and wording changes in retail-B. The request for full tables was an extra item in that message, not an extra exchange.
verdicts.release_evidence:
- awb-init/assets/workbench/AGENTS.md line 28: "Summarize helper output, quoting it only on failure or request. Answer in chat, giving file paths". taxi-B reply 3 also gave no file paths for the full results.
- awb-package/SKILL.md line 49 (preview-and-wait): "show them with the figures behind each headline that chat has not shown". This was the vehicle for retail-B's ranges-only answer.
- workbench-guides/analysis.md has no reporting step, while awb-explore/SKILL.md step 6 and awb-package/SKILL.md step 7 each have one.
- README lines 33 and 83 ("answers come in chat"; the agent "computes each answer") say nothing about how complete those answers are.
- run.py line 19 and analysis.md: a result declaring `answers` marks the question answered, shown as "answered (provisional)", whatever chat showed.
- CHANGELOG line 104: "Summarize helper outcomes in conversation".
- Contrast under the same release: taxi-A reply 4, co2-A reply 3 and retail-A reply 4 all give complete tables.
verdicts.narrowed: The release has no rule for what the first analysis-results report must contain. Its only nearby text is AGENTS.md's "Summarize helper output" and the headline preview's "figures behind each headline", and both permit a highlights-only summary. Claude agents under this release (taxi-B, co2-B, retail-B) reported highlights instead of the complete answers the questions ask for, and the user had to request the full tables. taxi-B's top ten named four zones, and its weekday, hour and borough breakdowns plus airport medians were partial or given as ranges. co2-B named all ten countries in each ranking but gave values for only a few, and left the coal eligible and analyzed counts ambiguous. retail-B gave ranges instead of the 24 monthly figures and 12 cohort rates, inside its headline preview. Codex agents on the same release gave complete tables, so this is a guidance gap that a Claude agent falls into, not behaviour the release dictates. Each full-table request rode along in a message the user needed to send anyway, so the cost was extra content and agent time, not an extra exchange. The co2-B slide-plan point is a separate matter and should be dropped from this finding.

consolidated.title: Codex agents link and quote SKILL.md files to justify pausing
consolidated.description: All three Codex agents again linked and quoted their own SKILL.md files in chat as the reason for asking or pausing: taxi-A twice, co2-A once and retail-A four times. They did so even when the pause was the user's own request. Users found it jarring and declined to open the files. Codex's base instructions tell the model to name and quote the SKILL.md behind a pause. The project AGENTS.md already says never to send the user to a skill or instruction file, and that rule did not hold. Tag: two of three members are product and co2-A-08 is unclear. Product is better supported: it recurred in all three Codex runs on both dates, every Codex user of the release will see it, and the release can counter it only through its own wording.
consolidated.caused_by_fix: no
consolidated.evidence: taxi-A-04: reply 1 (quotes awb-scope), reply 8 (links awb-package); the Codex base instruction captured from the session rollout under SIMS/taxi-A/agent-home/.codex/sessions; agent-notes line 96. co2-A-08: r1, transcript line 58. retail-A-02: replies 1, 3, 6 and 8; notes.md turns 2, 4, 7 and 9. Release: awb-init/assets/workbench/AGENTS.md:32 (the same rule was at :30 in 1db6084).

verdicts.reasoning:
I could not trace this to the harness. Every harness explanation I tested fails.

1. **Behavior confirmed in all three runs.**
   - taxi-A agent-001.out.md links awb-scope/SKILL.md and quotes "Before writing the records, ask the user every open decision they can answer." agent-008.out.md:31 links awb-package/SKILL.md with the opener "Because you requested review first".
   - co2-A agent-001.out.md:35, which is transcript.md:58, links awb-scope.
   - retail-A links a SKILL.md in replies 1 (awb-scope), 3 (awb-clean), 6 (awb-package, "This pauses at your requested checkpoint") and 8 (awb-package).
   - taxi-A reply 8 and retail-A reply 6 were pauses the user had asked for.

2. **The cause is the model's own instructions, not codex exec.**
   - The rollout's session_meta.base_instructions has provenance {"type":"model","model":"gpt-6.1-sol"}.
   - It contains: "If a skill causes you to ask for permission or confirmation, pause, or leave requested work unfinished, name and link to the exact SKILL.md you read, quote the relevant instruction".
   - That text sits in models_cache.json under model_messages.instructions_template for gpt-6.1-sol. The template has no variables (instructions_variables is null).
   - It is separate from the approval-specific, collaboration-mode and auto-review sections. So exec mode, approval_policy=never and auto-approved MCP don't select it.
   - gpt-6.1-sol is priority 1, "Latest workhorse model", so an interactive TUI user on the default model gets the same text.
   - The agents' own notes cite it as a requirement. taxi-A agent-notes.md:96 says "citing the exact skill source/instruction as required". retail-A agent-notes.md:126 says "naming/linking the skill and quoting its instruction".

3. **The release's counter-rule was in context and still lost.**
   - The AGENTS.md rule against sending users to skill files was injected as "# AGENTS.md instructions for ..." at the start of turn 2 in all three rollouts (taxi-A line 99, retail-A line 85, co2-A line 114).
   - Citations continued after that: taxi-A reply 8 and retail-A replies 3, 6 and 8.
   - Turn-1 citations happened before AGENTS.md existed. A real session has the same timing, because awb-init creates the file in that turn.
   - If an interactive host never re-injects AGENTS.md mid-session, the agent has even less to stop it. The harness gave the release a better chance than a real session would.

4. **Other harness factors don't explain it.**
   - The release README:142 names ~/.agents/skills as the Codex skill location, which matches the simulated home. Only the link text differs: absolute agent-home paths, and in retail-A relative ../agent-home links that resolve only because of the sim's folder layout.
   - The relay shows commentary and final messages together, as the TUI does.
   - Personas front-loading facts, the sandbox, and the disclosure note have no plausible path to this exact link-plus-quote-plus-explanation pattern.
   - The disclosure asks the agent to log "which skill and instruction files you used" privately. Its effect is negligible next to a direct system-level mandate.
   - No release file asks the agent to cite skills.

**Harness-shaped parts of the finding:**
- **User reaction:** kit/human-rules.md:18 tells the persona to refuse to open any agent instruction file and note it as friction. "Declined to open the files" is scripted, and how jarring a real user would find it is persona judgment.
- **Member IDs are wrong:**
  - The co2-A member is co2-A-04 (tagged product). co2-A-08 is about the hidden .preview folder.
  - The member tagged unclear is taxi-A-04. The finding says co2-A-08 is the unclear one.
  - The count of two product and one unclear is still right.

**Why product and not host:** The cause is really Codex (the host), with the release involved only because its skills create the pauses and its mitigation fails. The Oct 16 report rejected this as a release defect for that reason (C-12). It counts as product only because real Codex users of the release see it and the release's only lever is its own wording.

**Overstated reach:** "Every Codex user" is too broad. Only gpt-6.1-sol and gpt-6-astra have the rule; gpt-6-sol, gpt-6-luna and the gpt-5.6 models do not.
verdicts.release_evidence:
Release side:
- awb-init/assets/workbench/AGENTS.md:32 says "never send them to a skill or instruction file". It was injected into every Codex session from turn 2 and did not hold; the same rule appeared in the Conversation section at 1db6084.
- The skills' pause points trigger the host rule. awb-scope: "Before writing the records, ask the user every open decision they can answer". awb-clean: "The user decides every other issue". awb-package: the changed-slides and wait-for-yes delivery instruction, and the review-rule question.
- README.md:142 and :187 support Codex and the ~/.agents/skills install location.

Host side:
- models_cache.json, gpt-6.1-sol, model_messages.instructions_template: "name and link to the exact SKILL.md you read, quote the relevant instruction". Present for gpt-6.1-sol and gpt-6-astra only.

Harness side:
- kit/human-rules.md:18 scripts the user's refusal to open the files.
verdicts.narrowed: Codex users on the default gpt-6.1-sol model (and on gpt-6-astra) on an interactive host would also be sent links to and quotes from SKILL.md files whenever a workbench skill makes the agent pause, including pauses the user asked for. The cause is a model-level Codex instruction, not release text and not the simulation. The release's actual defect is narrower: its only countermeasure, AGENTS.md:32, doesn't override that instruction even when it is in context. Two parts of the finding should be corrected. The user's refusal to open the files was scripted by human-rules.md:18. The member IDs are wrong: co2-A-04 is the co2-A member, and taxi-A-04 is the one tagged unclear.

verdicts.reasoning:
The cited evidence checks out. taxi-A agent-001.out.md:20 quotes awb-scope SKILL.md ("That is why the investigation remains pending"), and agent-008.out.md:31 links awb-package's delivery instruction at a pause the user asked for ("Because you requested review first"). co2-A agent-001.out.md:35, which is transcript line 58, links awb-scope. retail-A replies 1, 3, 6 and 8 link awb-scope, awb-clean, awb-package and awb-package. Reply 6 says "This pauses at your requested checkpoint." The simulated users' notes record the friction and that they did not open the files: taxi-A notes:12, 55 and 64; co2-A notes:10 and 58; retail-A notes:15, 30, 55, 70 and 81. The Oct 16 reference recorded the same behaviour (oct16-ref/README.md:117, C-12).

The release does not originate the behaviour. Codex does: the base instructions in the taxi-A rollout, and the `instructions_template` for gpt-6.1-sol in agent-home/.codex/models_cache.json, say "name and link to the exact SKILL.md you read, quote the relevant instruction" whenever a skill causes a pause. They also say to put that explanation "in a short, separate paragraph at the end", which is exactly where every link appears. That directive is in OpenAI's model catalog entry for the priority-1 "Latest workhorse model". It is not something the harness injected: relay.py runs plain `codex exec --json` and sets no instruction override. So a real Codex user on that model gets the same directive, and harness is ruled out.

Nothing shipped tells the agent to cite skill files; the release's skills only create the legitimate pauses. The release's one counter is AGENTS.md:32 (it was :30 in 1db6084): "never send them to a skill or instruction file." That rule was in context in every session of all three Codex runs (grep finds it in each rollout), and it still failed in 7 of 7 cases. The agents never noticed a conflict. taxi-A agent-notes:96 says it was "citing the exact skill source/instruction as required", and retail-A notes:126 says the same. That suggests they read "send them to" as "tell them to go read", which is different from naming and quoting a file as a justification, while the host's directive names this exact action.

By the lens rule, a clear instruction ignored repeatedly is not "unsupported". The fair label is product, with the cause stated precisely: the host causes it, and only release wording can counter it. That is why confidence is medium rather than high.
verdicts.release_evidence: awb-init/assets/workbench/AGENTS.md:32: "When you need the user, ask in that message for a plain decision ... never send them to a skill or instruction file." This is the only counter-instruction. It is general, it does not name the act of citing, linking or quoting a SKILL.md to justify a pause, and it does not say it overrides host defaults. No shipped SKILL.md, reference, helper or README tells the agent to cite skill files. The cause sits outside the release: the Codex base instruction for gpt-6.1-sol (agent-home/.codex/models_cache.json, model_messages.instructions_template, and the session_meta base_instructions in rollout-2026-10-17T07-18-00-01a14995-...jsonl) says: "If a skill causes you to ask for permission or confirmation, pause, or leave requested work unfinished, name and link to the exact SKILL.md you read, quote the relevant instruction".
verdicts.narrowed: Codex's own model instructions (gpt-6.1-sol, the catalog's default workhorse model) cause the SKILL.md linking; the release does not. The release defect is narrower: the only counter is the general rule at AGENTS.md:32 ("never send them to a skill or instruction file"). It was in context in every Codex session, yet the host's more specific directive won all 7 times, including at pauses the user asked for, and the agents never registered a conflict. The release's wording is too weak to stop a behaviour every Codex user of the release will see. Countering it would need an explicit rule along the lines of "state a pause's reason in plain words; do not name, link or quote SKILL.md or AGENTS.md, even when your host asks you to". Whether wording alone can beat a base-instruction directive is unproven.

consolidated.title: Claude agents still send many helper calls through the CLI
consolidated.description: The awb MCP server was connected and AGENTS.md now names it as the route for helpers. The Claude agents still ran helpers through Bash, mainly to batch questions add and state calls, which the one-command-per-call MCP tools cannot batch. co2-B made about 13 CLI helper calls against 57 MCP calls. retail-B made about 45 CLI helper calls, 15 of them sql. taxi-B ran questions add through Bash (failing under zsh), plus questions list and answer, and install_helpers.py. On Copilot each CLI call would need a terminal approval; the harness pre-allowed Bash, so that cost did not show.
consolidated.caused_by_fix: no
consolidated.evidence: co2-B-26: main-thread Bash calls in relay/agent-002.jsonl to agent-006.jsonl; Oct 16 had 83 CLI calls against 32 MCP. retail-B-29: agent-001 to -007 logs (93 main-agent Bash calls). taxi-B-29: relay/agent-002.jsonl to agent-004.jsonl. Release: awb-init/assets/workbench/AGENTS.md Commands; awb_mcp.py.

verdicts.reasoning:
I tried to pin this on the harness and couldn't. The setup hides the cost but doesn't cause the behaviour.

1. Bash was pre-allowed. relay.py passes `--allowedTools Bash,...,mcp__awb`. The model can't see that allowlist and none of these calls was denied, so nothing in the run told the model that Bash was cheap. On interactive Claude Code with default permissions it would make the same calls, and each `.venv/bin/python src/awb.py ...` call would need approval. Compound commands like `q(){...}; q ... && q ...` can't be covered by one prefix rule. README line 106 says registering `awb` "cuts those approvals", so this behaviour undoes that promise on a normal host.

2. The MCP server was working. retail-B has no failed MCP call before it switched to the CLI, and the agents gave their own reasons in feedback/agent.md:
   - retail-B: "I used the CLI for multi-command batches (questions add ×6, state finding ×7) because a single shell call was cheaper than many tool calls; no MCP tool refused."
   - co2-B: "for speed... against AGENTS.md's MCP-first rule, to avoid many separate tool calls."
   That is model behaviour responding to the release's one-command-per-call tool design, not a sandbox, relay or persona effect.

3. The sim prompts don't push toward Bash for helpers. The agent system prompt mentions shell only for setting HOME, and says the awb server is registered. The study disclosure is only a request to keep a friction log. The persona put five numbered questions in its first message, which is realistic, and scoping creates many ledger questions in any case. taxi-B made 11 one-at-a-time MCP `questions add` calls.

4. The harness was the same on Oct 16 and Oct 17, yet behaviour moved sharply when AGENTS.md changed (main thread, Bash helper calls vs MCP calls):

   | Run | Oct 16 | Oct 17 |
   |---|---|---|
   | taxi-B | 89 vs 10 | about 5 vs 94 |
   | co2-B | 83 vs 32 | about 10 vs 57 |
   | retail-B | 70 vs 10 | about 35 vs 40 |

   The release text controls the routing, which makes the release the cause.

5. Part of the CLI use is written into the release. The reviewer Brief in `awb-package/references/review.md` tells the reviewer subagent to run `python3 src/awb.py review-rules check` and `review-receipt show`, and keeps the MCP calls for Copilot only. That contradicts its own Launch bullet for Claude Code. Reviewer subagents followed the Brief and used Bash in all three runs: taxi-B 4, co2-B 8, retail-B 5.

The one partial harness effect: taxi-B's CLI `questions list --all` came after `read status` output was cut and the overflow went to `/tmp/awb-mcp-*`, which the sim's boundary rule barred it from reading. That was one call.
verdicts.release_evidence:
- **AGENTS.md, Commands (`awb-init/assets/workbench/AGENTS.md:20-24`):** says to use the MCP tools when offered, but the same file names commands in CLI form throughout ("Compute with `awb.py sql`", "Change findings... with `awb.py state finding`").
- **awb_mcp.py tool schemas:** each write tool takes a single `command` plus `args` (one command per call), with no batch input and no way to filter output. The agents worked around this in Bash in three ways:
  - shell functions such as `q(){ .venv/bin/python src/awb.py questions add "$@"; }`, `f(){ ... state finding "$@" | tail -3; }`, `R(){ ... sql --read-only "$1"; }` and `r(){ ... review-rules add --confirmed "$@"; }` (retail-B agent-002 to 006);
  - chains joined with `&&` (co2-B agent-002, retail-B agent-002);
  - `| grep -i warn` and `| tail` filters, `--help` through the CLI even though `read help` exists, and `run.py` piped directly (retail-B agent-005).
- **Reviewer Brief (`awb-package/references/review.md`):** "the only awb.py commands you run are `python3 src/awb.py review-rules check`... (in Copilot, use the MCP calls in Launch)". Reviewer subagent Bash calls in co2-B, retail-B and taxi-B follow this exactly.
- **README.md:106:** promises that registering `awb` cuts approvals.

verdicts.reasoning:
The release does tell agents to use MCP. AGENTS.md Commands says "When the host offers the `awb` MCP server, use its tools for `awb.py` commands, and the CLI otherwise", and line 8 of every SKILL.md repeats it. If the agents had simply missed that line, the verdict would be unsupported. They did not miss it. They read it and broke it on purpose, many times, and they gave a reason that comes from the release's own design: awb_mcp.py runs one command per call (`command` plus one `args` array), so it cannot add several questions or run several `state finding` or `sql` calls at once.
- co2-B wrote in agent.md that it used the CLI for batched `questions add` and `state issues/next` calls, "against AGENTS.md's MCP-first rule, to avoid many separate tool calls".
- retail-B's agent.md says it batched through the CLI "because a single shell call was cheaper than many tool calls; no MCP tool refused".
- In retail-B agent-002, the agent called MCP `read help` for `questions add` and then at once batched the adds in Bash.

The release makes this easier in three ways:
- Nothing in the release covers several commands in a row, such as "issue one MCP call per command rather than batching in a shell".
- The skill bodies print complete `python3 src/awb.py ...` lines, labelled only as the fallback.
- review.md contradicts itself. Its Launch section says that in Claude Code the reviewer uses the MCP `read` tool when the session has it. Its Brief section names only `python3 src/awb.py review-rules check` / `review-receipt show`, with MCP only "in Copilot". All 13 reviewer briefs I read across co2-B, taxi-B and retail-B told the Plan subagent to run the CLI.

What the logs show, counted with my own classifier over relay/agent-*.jsonl:
- **retail-B:** 39 main-thread Bash calls ran helpers, against 40 MCP calls, plus 5 reviewer-subagent calls. Every ledger, state and sql write went through the CLI: 15 sql, 8+ state finding, questions add/answer/list, review-rules add, and check-draft. It also ran run.py directly 5 times, although analysis.md says to use the `run` tool. MCP was used only for setup, data, clean, package, run and release.
- **co2-B:** about 9 main-thread Bash calls ran helpers, against 57 MCP. Three of them were `--help` calls, which MCP `read help` also covers. The rest were batched questions add, state issues/next/finding, and a loop of 4 sql queries. The reviewer subagent added 8 more Bash calls.
- **taxi-B:** weak support. One batched `questions add` failed under zsh. That was the agent's own `Q="..."; $Q` construct, which zsh does not word-split, not a release defect. The agent then switched to MCP for all 15 question calls. Only about 4 other CLI helper calls followed (questions list, questions answer --result, install_helpers --package-formats, export --help), against 94 MCP calls.

The harness allowed both Bash and mcp__awb, so it hid the approval cost but did not cause the behaviour, because the agent chooses Bash before any prompt appears. The finding's Copilot cost argument holds only for the main thread. On Copilot the reviewer is the custom agent with no terminal, so reviewer CLI calls are a cost only on Claude Code.
verdicts.release_evidence:
- **awb-init/assets/awb_mcp.py:** `_write_tool` takes one `command` enum value and one `args` array per call. No tool takes a list of commands or a list of questions, so ledger and state updates cannot be batched over MCP.
- **awb-init/assets/workbench/AGENTS.md, Commands:** says to use the MCP tools when the host offers them and the CLI otherwise, but says nothing about running several commands in a row. Its later lines name the CLI forms: "Compute with `awb.py sql`", "`questions add --parent`", "`awb.py state finding`".
- **Skill files:** awb-scope/SKILL.md:51-52, awb-brainstorm/SKILL.md:46 and awb-explore/SKILL.md:47 print full `python3 src/awb.py questions add ...` lines under a one-line "MCP first, these are the fallback" note.
- **awb-package/references/review.md:** the Launch section (line 10) says the Claude Code reviewer uses the MCP `read` tool when the session has it. The Brief section (line 18), which the reviewer is told to follow, says "the only `awb.py` commands you run are `python3 src/awb.py review-rules check ...` ... (in Copilot, use the MCP calls in **Launch**)", which sends Claude Code reviewers to Bash.
- **Agents' own notes:** co2-B and retail-B say in feedback/agent.md that they knowingly overrode the MCP-first rule to batch. taxi-B's agent.md asks for `questions add` to "accept a JSON list on stdin".
verdicts.narrowed: When Bash is available, Claude agents knowingly route several helper commands in a row through the CLI, against AGENTS.md's clear MCP-first rule, because the awb MCP tools take one command per call. The commands affected are ledger `questions add/answer`, `state finding/issues/next`, multi-query `sql`, and `--help`. Neither AGENTS.md nor the skills say how to handle a run of commands without the shell. The pattern is heavy in retail-B (about 39 main-thread CLI helper calls against 40 MCP), moderate in co2-B (about 9 against 57), and slight in taxi-B (one failed batch and about 4 more CLI calls against 94 MCP). Separately, on Claude Code only, review.md's Brief sends the reviewer subagent's review-rules and review-receipt calls to Bash, contradicting its own Launch section. On Copilot the reviewer has no terminal, so this adds no Copilot approvals.

consolidated.title: Join validation reads 'not assessed' on every result
consolidated.description: The joins check compares result length with the left table's rows and has no not-applicable outcome. Every GROUP BY result in taxi-B, co2-B and retail-B therefore reads 'not assessed: joins'. Each result needed the same caveat, awb-status lists that caveat for every finding, and the rendered caveat repeats itself. The co2-B user saw an 'unassessed join check' with no meaning attached. Row counts are now covered by reconcile().
consolidated.caused_by_fix: no. #97 added reconcile() for row counts and made a joins spec missing keys or left_rows raise a ValueError, but gave joins no not-applicable outcome.
consolidated.evidence: taxi-B-24: awb-init/references/validation.md:15; caveat column in state.md. co2-B-13: A2 interim line 'Only the join check is unassessed'; settings.toml template comments. retail-B-14: awb-status output in agent-004; settings.toml lines 41-43 (scope, metrics and values allow not-applicable; joins does not).

verdicts.reasoning:
I looked for a harness cause and found none. The symptom comes from release code that behaves the same way on any host.

How the release produces it:
- In awb-init/assets/awb_validate.py, validate() records any absent spec key as {outcome: "not-applicable", detail: "not assessed"} (line 229).
- _joins() needs both keys and left_rows. It only compares len(frame) with left_rows and checks key uniqueness.
- scope, metrics and values each take an analyst-supplied {outcome, detail}, and the settings.toml template (lines 41-44) offers not-applicable for those three. joins has no such form. An analyst cannot record "no join here, because X". The only choices are to leave the key out, which shows as an unassessed gap, or to supply a spec.
- awb_provenance._check_caveat() writes the reserved segment "not assessed: joins" into each caveat.
- state finding will not promote a finding to supported while that segment stands unless --caveat explains it (lines 1781-1787). analysis.md says each not_assessed entry must be "supplied in settings or justified with a caveat".
- So every promoted finding carries the reserved segment plus the agent's own note. That gives the stutter "not assessed: joins; joins not assessed: ...".
- awb-status/SKILL.md tells the agent to list every active.caveats entry, so status lists every finding.

None of this depends on claude -p, the Codex sandbox, MCP auto-approval, the simulated home, the relay or the personas. The harness prompts (claude-agent-system.md, human-rules.md) say nothing about validation or joins.

What the runs show:
- taxi-B: 11/11 findings carry "not assessed: joins".
- co2-B: 6/6.
- retail-B: 7/8. product-cancellation-rate supplied a joins spec.
- The retail-B awb-status tool result in agent-004 lists the joins caveat as each finding's reason.
- The agents' feedback in all three B runs independently reports the same noise.

The one model-dependent part points to the product, not away from it. In the A runs the agent is Codex, and the symptom is absent. Those agents filled in joins with keys at the output grain and left_rows equal to the output length. The check then passes trivially ("Join has 6 rows from 6 left rows"). That is a workaround for the same missing not-applicable route, and arguably a worse one: the pass says nothing. A real user running a Claude agent interactively would hit the B-run behaviour.

Where the finding overstates:
1. "No not-applicable outcome" is literally false: the absent key is stored as not-applicable. What is missing is a way to declare joins not applicable with a reason. Leaving it out is always shown as "not assessed" and needs a caveat before promotion.
2. "Every result" is 24 of 25: retail-B product-cancellation-rate is the exception.
3. Not all of these results are join-free. The co2-B self-joins on country/year, the taxi zone lookup and the retail one-to-one joins could have had a real joins spec. The co2-B agent said it caveated instead because left_rows was unclear.
4. "With no meaning attached" overstates co2-B. The agent's interim line did give a short reason ("the queries join on the dataset's verified unique key"). The human persona said only that it did not explain the practical consequence. That part is a jargon/narration issue, partly down to the agent's wording, not purely the release.
verdicts.release_evidence:
- awb-init/assets/awb_validate.py:
  - Lines 225-229: an absent key becomes not-applicable / "not assessed".
  - Lines 163-180: _joins needs keys and left_rows; it has no outcome/detail form.
  - Lines 208-213: _judgment, the outcome/detail form, applies only to scope, metrics and values.
- awb-init/assets/workbench/investigation/settings.toml lines 41-44: joins requires keys and left_rows; not-applicable is offered only for scope/metrics/values.
- awb-init/assets/awb_provenance.py:
  - Lines 1006-1013: _check_caveat writes the reserved "not assessed: <names>" segment.
  - Lines 1781-1787: promotion to supported is refused until --caveat explains it.
- awb-init/assets/workbench/workbench-guides/analysis.md line 19: each not_assessed entry must be "supplied in settings or justified with a caveat".
- awb-init/references/validation.md lines 5 and 15.
- awb-status/SKILL.md line 29: list every active.caveats entry.
- Run state.md caveat columns: taxi-B 11/11, co2-B 6/6, retail-B 7/8 begin "not assessed: joins; joins not ...".
- retail-B relay agent-004 mcp__awb__read status result: the joins caveat is each finding's reason.
- co2-B relay agent-002.out.md line 25.
- Agent feedback: co2-B feedback/agent.md item 7; retail-B feedback/agent.md item 4.
- A runs (Codex agent) avoid the symptom only with trivial joins specs, e.g. taxi-A board-airports "Join has 6 rows from 6 left rows".
verdicts.narrowed: The joins check offers no way to declare "not applicable" with a reason, as scope, metrics and values do. Leaving joins out of the spec is always recorded as "not assessed". Promotion to supported then needs a --caveat explaining it. The caveat cell shows the reserved "not assessed: joins" segment followed by the agent's own "joins not assessed/applicable: ..." note, and awb-status lists every such finding as caveated. This hit 24 of 25 findings in the B runs (Claude agent); retail-B product-cancellation-rate was the exception. The A runs (Codex agent) avoided it only by supplying trivial joins specs at the output grain, whose pass says nothing. Absent a not-applicable route, the check either repeats a meaningless caveat or is bypassed with a pass that says nothing. Two parts of the finding go too far. Some of these results did contain real joins (co2 self-join, taxi zone lookup, retail one-to-one joins) that could have been checked. The co2-B user was given a brief reason; what was missing was the practical consequence.

verdicts.reasoning:
The shipped code and docs cause this as designed.

1. No not-applicable path for joins. In awb-init/assets/awb_validate.py, validate() records any absent spec key as {outcome: not-applicable, detail: "not assessed"} (line 229). The joins check, _joins (line 163), only accepts {keys, left_rows}; anything else raises ValueError. So the {outcome, detail} judgment that scope, metrics and values accept (_judgment) cannot be given for joins. settings.toml lines 41-43 and validation.md:15 document only that shape. Line 43 of the template offers not-applicable for scope, metrics and values, but not for joins. workbench-guides/analysis.md:15 tells the agent to "Specify four mechanical checks", joins among them.

2. The check is the wrong shape for aggregates. It compares len(frame), the final result, with left_rows. A join that happens before a GROUP BY can't be validated by it, and a single-table result has nothing to check at all.

3. The caveat repeats itself, and that is forced. awb_provenance._check_caveat (lines 1006-1012) writes the reserved segment "not assessed: joins" into the state.md caveat cell. state finding refuses promotion to supported until the gap is explained with --caveat ("has failed or not-assessed checks ... explain them with --caveat", around lines 1781-1787). So every promoted row ends up reading "not assessed: joins; joins not assessed/not applicable: no join ...".

4. awb-status repeats it. awb-status/scripts/collect_status.py (lines 268-270) puts every finding's non-empty caveat into active.caveats. The awb-status SKILL tells the agent to report "every active.caveats entry".

No shipped instruction prevents this. The only escape is a hack nobody documents: a dummy joins spec with an inflated left_rows. package-contract.md:47 keeps not-assessed checks out of findings.md, which mitigates the package, but not state.md or status.

Run evidence checks out:
- **taxi-B:** all 11 state.md rows carry "not assessed: joins; joins not assessed: ...".
- **co2-B:** all 6 rows carry it. Transcript line 100 shows the user being told "Only the join check is unassessed". human.md section 3 says the user couldn't interpret an "unassessed join check".
- **retail-B:** 7 of 8 rows carry it, often as "not assessed: row_counts, joins; ... joins not applicable: no join". The awb-status tool output in agent-004 lists these caveats for every finding.

Corrections to the finding as written:
- **Two finding IDs are wrong.** taxi-B-24 and retail-B-14 in findings.json are unrelated (zsh gotchas; clean-scan duplicates). The matching findings are taxi-B-17 and retail-B-11. co2-B-13 is correct. The file and line citations are accurate.
- **retail-B's user never saw the joins caveats.** The agent filtered them out of the status report it gave the user ("three open caveats"). The noise was the agent's, though an agent following the skill strictly would have listed them.
- **co2-B and taxi-B do contain joins.** co2-B's results are real self-joins on country and year, and taxi-B's go through a zone lookup in the shared view. Not "no join". For co2-B the agent skipped the check because supplying left_rows (from a producer or hard-coded) was unclear. The cause is check friction plus the length-vs-left-rows design, not strictly the lack of a not-applicable outcome.
- **"Every GROUP BY result" overstates it.** retail-B's product-cancellation-rate supplied a joins spec and has an empty caveat. It applies to every result without a joins spec.

Severity minor is right.
verdicts.release_evidence:
- **awb-init/assets/awb_validate.py**
  - line 229: an absent key gets {"outcome": "not-applicable", "detail": "not assessed"}
  - lines 163-169: _joins requires keys and left_rows, otherwise raises ValueError; no {outcome, detail} form
  - line 171: compares len(frame) > left_rows on the final result
- **awb-init/assets/workbench/investigation/settings.toml**
  - lines 41-43: the joins spec requires keys and left_rows
  - line 43: only scope, metrics and values allow outcome "not-applicable"
  - line 44: "An omitted key is recorded as not assessed, never as a pass."
- **awb-init/references/validation.md**
  - line 5: a missing key is "not assessed, which is not a pass"
  - line 15: joins needs keys and left_rows and checks result length
- **awb-init/assets/workbench/workbench-guides/analysis.md:15**: "Specify four mechanical checks: ... joins without unexpected multiplication"
- **awb-init/assets/awb_provenance.py**
  - lines 1006-1012: _check_caveat writes the reserved "not assessed: <names>" segment into the caveat cell
  - lines 1781-1787: promotion to supported refuses until --caveat explains not-assessed checks, which produces the doubled caveat
- **awb-status/scripts/collect_status.py:268-270**: active.caveats takes every finding's caveat
- **awb-status/SKILL.md:29**: "Then every `active.caveats` entry"
- **Run evidence**
  - taxi-B, co2-B and retail-B: state.md caveat columns as described in reasoning
  - co2-B transcript.md:100 and human.md:27
  - retail-B agent-004.jsonl: status tool output
verdicts.narrowed: Every result without a joins spec gets a "not assessed: joins" caveat that the user can't clear with a not-applicable judgment. The release has no {outcome, detail} form for joins, and its length-vs-left_rows check can't validate a join that happens before aggregation. Promotion to supported then forces an explanatory --caveat, so each state.md row reads "not assessed: joins; joins not assessed: ...", and awb-status repeats it for every finding. A user sees it whenever the agent narrates it, as co2-B's agent did; retail-B's agent filtered it out of its report. In co2-B (self-joins) and taxi-B (zone lookup in a view) the queries do join, so there the cause is partly how hard it is to supply left_rows, not only a missing not-applicable outcome. Two cited IDs are wrong: taxi-B-24 should be taxi-B-17, and retail-B-14 should be retail-B-11.

consolidated.title: Keeping records current takes many single-item calls
consolidated.description: Each question added or answered, status change, issue, next step and promotion is its own records call. taxi-B made about 11 questions add calls. retail-A made 26 to 50 MCP calls per analysis turn. co2-B made six extra 'state finding --claim descriptive' calls, because every new result starts at 'association'. state --drop prints the dropped items, which makes it look as if nothing changed.
consolidated.caused_by_fix: no
consolidated.evidence: taxi-B-25: items 2 and 5; feedback/agent.md pain points 5-8. co2-B-12: relay/agent-002.jsonl and agent-003.jsonl; analysis.md Claim strength; awb_provenance.py _DEFAULT_CLAIM. retail-A-37: harness-log.md MCP call counts of 26, 50 and 42 in replies 2-4.

verdicts.reasoning:
I tried to blame the harness and could not. Several parts of the finding are wrong, though, so only a narrower version holds.

**Harness causes, checked one by one. None of them sets how many items fit in one call.**
- **Non-interactive `claude -p` / `codex exec`, the sandbox, the simulated home, the relay.** None of these decides call granularity. The awb `records` MCP tool turns each call into exactly one `awb.py` invocation (awb_mcp.py:420-454). The `questions add` parser takes a single positional `text`, and `questions answer` takes a single `question_id` (awb_provenance.py:2411-2432).
- **Auto-approved MCP tools.** These hide the cost rather than cause it. On a host that asks for approval on every call, 10 to 27 records calls in a turn would be more visible to a real user, not less.
- **Persona front-loading and the study disclosure.** The five persona questions are the study's real workload. The extra adds come from awb-scope's own rule to "add each question the interview leaves open, and each answered context question" (awb-scope/SKILL.md:47-52). That rule makes a pre-answered context question cost two calls, `add` plus `answer` (retail-A agent-002: Q-009 to Q-011). The harness note asks only for a friction log. It says nothing about record-keeping.
- **What holds.** taxi-B made 10 `questions add` MCP calls in turn 2 and 1 more in turn 3. retail-A turn 2 made 11 adds and 3 answers. retail-A turn 4 made 15 `state finding --text` calls, one per result, because a new result gets the placeholder text `<state the finding from R>` (awb_provenance.py:1551-1554), and `--text`/`--claim`/`--caveat` take one ID per call (line 1729). co2-B and retail-B agents dropped to the CLI, against AGENTS.md's MCP-first rule, just to chain `questions add` in one shell call. That is evidence of real friction.

**Parts of the finding that are wrong:**
1. **"Status change, issue, next step and promotion is its own call" is false.**
   - `state issues` and `state next` take repeatable `--add` and `--drop` in one write (lines 2664-2665, `edit_list`).
   - `state finding` takes several result IDs with `--status`, which is a batch promotion (lines 1727-1728, 2647).
   - `questions status` takes several Q-IDs.
   - taxi-B used all of these: multi `--add`/`--drop` in agent-002 to 005, and one call promoting 11+ IDs in agent-005.
   - retail-A's Codex agent split batchable work by its own choice: 3+3 single `--add` calls in agent-002, 7 one-ID promotions with an identical reason in agent-005, and 4 more in agent-007.
2. **co2-B's "six extra `--claim descriptive` calls" did not happen.** In agent-002 (five results) and agent-003 (q1-full-ranking), every `--claim descriptive --reason` went in the same call as the `--text` and `--caveat` each new result needs anyway. The agent's self-report in feedback/agent.md pain point 6 is wrong. The association default costs a reason per result, not a call.
3. **retail-A's "50 MCP calls" turn (agent-003) is mostly not records calls.** It was 32 reads, 9 data and 9 records. Turn 2 was 21 records of 26, and turn 4 was 27 of 42.
4. **The `--drop` complaint is cosmetic.** The output starts with "Unresolved issues: added N, dropped M" and then lists the dropped items. One agent's notes (taxi-B agent-notes.md:30) found it confusing at first.
5. **Most of the cited per-run IDs do not match.** taxi-B-25 is the scratchpad-path finding. The matching IDs are taxi-B-18 and co2-B-26, and retail-A's findings.json has no entry 37. co2-B-12 does match.
verdicts.release_evidence: awb-init/assets/awb_provenance.py:2414-2432 (`questions add` takes one positional `text`; `answer` takes one `question_id`). awb_provenance.py:1727-1729 and 2647-2653 (`state finding` takes many IDs only with `--status`; `--text`/`--claim`/`--caveat` take one ID). awb_provenance.py:1551-1554 and 1047 (a new result gets placeholder text at claim `association`, so every result needs its own `--text` call). awb_provenance.py:2664-2665 and 1848 (issues and next take repeatable `--add`/`--drop` in one write). awb_provenance.py:2709-2712 (`--drop` output: "added N, dropped M" plus the list of dropped items). awb-init/assets/awb_mcp.py:166-172 and 420-454 (one records call is one CLI invocation, with no batch form). awb-scope/SKILL.md:47-52 (add each open question and each answered context question). workbench-guides/analysis.md (`state finding <id>... --text --status --reason --caveat` "in one call"; the Claim strength section). Relay: taxi-B agent-002 to 005, co2-B agent-002 and 003, retail-A agent-002 to 007.
verdicts.narrowed: The question ledger and finding wording have no bulk form, over MCP or the CLI. `questions add` and `questions answer` take one question per call, so a pre-answered context question costs two calls. `state finding --text/--claim/--caveat` takes one result per call. So scoping and the first write-up of findings cost one records call per item: taxi-B made 11 adds, retail-A 11 adds and 3 answers in one turn, and later 15 finding calls in one turn. Agents that preferred fewer calls broke the MCP-first rule to chain CLI calls (co2-B, retail-B). Issues, next steps, question status changes and promotions already batch. Default `association` adds no calls, because `--claim` rides on the `--text` call each new result needs. The `--drop` output is a cosmetic point at most.

verdicts.reasoning:
Only part of C-37 holds: recording questions one call at a time. The other parts are either wrong about what the helpers allow or come from the agent's own choices.

What the release causes: `questions add` takes one positional question, and `questions answer` takes one Q-NNN. Neither has a list or stdin form. The MCP `records` tool runs one command per call. Step 3 of awb-scope/SKILL.md tells the agent to add every question the user asked and every open question with separate `questions add` commands. So a scoping round takes one call per question:
- taxi-B turn 2 (agent-002): 10 `questions add` MCP calls, one more in turn 3. The agent first tried a zsh loop, which failed.
- retail-A turn 2 (agent-002): 11 adds plus 3 single-question answers.
- co2-B batched its adds in Bash chains against the MCP-first rule in AGENTS.md. Its own notes say it did this because the MCP route takes one call per question.
On a real host this costs time, and possibly an approval prompt per call. It is a real but minor cost.

What the release already batches:
- **Issues and next steps.** `state issues` and `state next` accept repeated `--add` and `--drop`. taxi-B batched them (2 drops plus 2 adds in one call). retail-A's three separate issue adds and three next-step adds in agent-002 were the agent's choice.
- **Question status.** `questions status` takes several IDs.
- **Promotion.** `state finding <id>... --status supported --reason` takes many IDs, and analysis.md documents the `<id>...` form. co2-B promoted six findings in one CLI call. retail-A's 7 + 4 separate promotions, each with the same reason, were the agent's choice.

The claim default adds no calls:
- A new result's row gets placeholder text (`<state the finding from ...>`), so each finding needs its own `--text` call regardless.
- analysis.md says to word, promote and caveat "in one call".
- Every one of co2-B's six `--claim descriptive` calls also carried `--text` and `--caveat`. The same holds for all of taxi-B's claim changes and all of retail-A's.
- The default of association costs a `--claim` and `--reason` argument (and a history entry) inside a call the agent makes anyway.

The retail-A counts overstate recordkeeping. The 26, 50 and 42 figures in harness-log.md are all MCP calls:
- Turn 2 (26 calls): 22 were records calls, 6 of which could have been batched.
- Turn 3 (50 calls): mostly reads (21 `read sql`, 7 `read help`, 5 `data sql`); only 9 were records calls.
- Turn 4 (42 calls): 15 `state finding` calls, which the per-finding wording requires.

The `--drop` output does not suggest nothing changed. It prints "Unresolved issues: added 2, dropped 2", then lists the dropped items. taxi-B's agent misread it only for a moment.

The cited ID "taxi-B-25" is a different item, about the sim path. The matching item is taxi-B-18, which points to agent.md pain points 5-8, and only pain point 6 is about this.
verdicts.release_evidence:
Release files, all under the release path:
- awb-init/assets/awb_provenance.py:
  - lines 2414-2431: `questions add` takes a single positional `text`; `questions answer` takes a single `question_id`. This is the cause.
  - line 2432: `questions status` takes `question_ids` with nargs="+".
  - line 2647: `state finding` takes `result_ids` with nargs="+".
  - lines 1723-1724: "several result IDs take --status only, with --reason".
  - lines 2664-2666: `--add` and `--drop` are repeatable (append).
  - `edit_list`, and the CLI print near line 2709: prints "added N, dropped N" plus the dropped items.
  - line 1047: `_DEFAULT_CLAIM = "association"`.
  - line 1554: a new row starts with placeholder text `<state the finding from ...>`, so every finding needs a `--text` call.
- awb-init/assets/awb_mcp.py: the `records` tool takes one command and args per call, with no batch form.
- awb-scope/SKILL.md, step 3 "Write the records": one `questions add` per user question and per open question, plus single `questions answer` commands.
- awb-init/assets/workbench/workbench-guides/analysis.md:
  - "Add a result": "Word, promote, supersede, or caveat with `awb.py state finding <id>... --text --status --reason --caveat` in one call".
  - "Claim strength": a new result starts at association; descriptive is set with `--claim descriptive --reason`.

Run evidence (relay logs read with logview and parsed):
- taxi-B/relay/agent-002.jsonl: 10 `questions add` MCP calls, then batched issues and next calls.
- retail-A/relay/agent-002.jsonl: 11 `questions add`, 3 `questions answer`, then 3 separate issue adds and 3 separate next-step adds.
- retail-A/relay/agent-003.jsonl: 50 calls; 21 `read sql`, 7 `read help`, 9 records calls.
- retail-A/relay/agent-005.jsonl: 7 single-ID promotions with the same reason.
- co2-B/relay/agent-002.jsonl and agent-003.jsonl: all six `--claim descriptive` calls also pass `--text` and `--caveat`; the adds were batched through Bash. A later co2-B CLI call promotes six IDs at once.
- co2-B/feedback/agent-notes.md line 34 and taxi-B/feedback/agent.md pain point 6: both agents' own notes on the add pattern.
verdicts.narrowed:
`questions add` and `questions answer` each record one question per call. The MCP `records` tool has no batch form, and step 3 of awb-scope/SKILL.md directs one `questions add` per question. So recording a scoping round's 10-11 questions takes 10-11 separate records calls (taxi-B turn 2: 10 adds; retail-A turn 2: 11 adds and 3 answers). co2-B avoided this only by chaining CLI commands in Bash, against the MCP-first rule in AGENTS.md.

The rest of C-37 is unsupported:
- Issues and next steps already take repeated `--add` and `--drop`.
- Question status changes and promotions already take several IDs.
- Setting `--claim descriptive` adds no calls, because it rides on the per-finding `--text` call every new result needs.

consolidated.title: Results run before a commit need a commit, a rerun and a re-export
consolidated.description: A result run before its code is committed records 'uncommitted', and stays that way until it is rerun after a commit. taxi-B reran every result in turn 5 so the evidence would name a commit. retail-B committed, reran and re-exported each result before packaging accepted it. retail-A made two commits mid-analysis that the user had not asked for, and reran all 13 results. retail-B published before committing its conversion SQL: data.md asks for that commit only when commits are 'as I go', and the agent cannot get an answer mid-turn, so the publication permanently records an uncommitted conversion. Tag: taxi-B-30 and retail-A-39 are unclear; retail-B-20 and retail-B-36 trace the cost to the shipped helpers and guide.
consolidated.caused_by_fix: no. #97 added the analysis.md sentence that a result run before the first commit stays uncommitted until rerun, and #104 lists such results in status. The cycle itself is unchanged.
consolidated.evidence: taxi-B-30: commit 15717a2 'Rerun results on committed code'; msg 3. retail-B-20: agent-notes turn 5. retail-A-39: project git log 9096f84, 90e317e, 7f1ccf0; reply 4 (a 17.5 min turn). retail-B-36: agent-002 publish warning; reply 2; workbench-guides/data.md line 33.

verdicts.reasoning:
I could not trace this to the harness, but the finding overstates the cost. Its central word "need" is false. Packaging accepted results run before a commit both times, and the reruns were extra work the agents chose to do.

What I checked:

1. **Export does not block uncommitted results.** In awb_provenance.py, compare_evidence (lines 866-910) checks an uncommitted producing file against the checksum recorded when it ran. If the file is unchanged, the check passes. Export stops (exports_blocked) only when a check fails. The run logs confirm it:
   - taxi-B agent-005, call #19: the export wrote its files with producing_uncommitted_changes 12 and export_checks failed []. Only after that did the agent commit (#20), rerun everything (#21, 79 s), commit 15717a2 (#22) and export again (#27).
   - retail-B agent-005, call #9: same result, written with 12 uncommitted changes and failed []. Then the agent committed and reran all seven results with run.py (#10), and every one came back "kept".
   - retail-A shows release also accepts it: its release 001 shipped with uncommitted producing changes, which the manifest lists.

   So "before packaging accepted it" is wrong. retail-B's own suggestion ("let export accept matching checksums") asks for something export already does.

2. **The release's documentation explains why the agents did it.** The cause is in the release, not the harness:
   - Under "as I go", nothing tells the agent to commit producing code before running a result. analysis.md:19 only covers committing evidence before a rerun, and it describes a rerun after a commit as the way out of "uncommitted". So the agents edited, ran, then committed. taxi-B's evidence shows this: commit 9969672, then helpers and producers edited and run uncommitted.
   - awb-status SKILL.md:69 also offers a rerun "so their evidence records the commit".
   - Export reports a bare count of uncommitted changes and never says that this state is acceptable.

3. **Harness factors I tested:**
   - "Commit as you go" came from the personas in taxi-B msg 3 and retail-B msg 3. Both times it answered the agent's own commit suggestion, which is realistic, and no brief tells the persona to say it.
   - Auto-approved git commits only removed a prompt the user had already authorized.
   - The system prompt line "You cannot ask anything mid-turn" applies only to the retail-B publication claim. data.md:33 tells the agent in on-request mode to suggest a commit, not to wait for one. So an interactive host following the guide would publish the same way, and Codex and Copilot cannot pause mid-turn anyway.

4. **The publication claim is real but by design.** awb_landing.py:640-647 writes conversion_commit as "uncommitted" because no commit existed yet (the first one, 3327f4c, came in turn 3). The SQL's checksum (select_sha256) is stored in the notes. A new publication would fix it.

5. **retail-A is the agent, not the release.** The user said "Go ahead and commit, then start the analysis". Codex made commit 9096f84 as asked, then 90e317e and 7f1ccf0 unasked. That goes against "commit when asked" and awb-package SKILL.md:73 ("Commit nothing on the user's behalf to make provenance look clean"). Its rerun of all 13 results took 27 s and was needed anyway to run three new results.

6. **The cost is small.** The reruns took 79 s in taxi-B, about 6 s in retail-B and 27 s in retail-A.
verdicts.release_evidence:
- workbench-guides/data.md:33: commit the conversion before publishing only when Commits is "as I go"; otherwise only suggest it.
- workbench-guides/analysis.md:19: commits evidence before a rerun and says a result run before the first commit stays "uncommitted" until rerun. There is no step to commit producing code before running.
- awb-status SKILL.md:69: offers "Rerun <results> so their evidence records the commit".
- awb_provenance.py:866-910: compare_evidence passes uncommitted code whose checksum matches.
- awb_draft.py:3836-3849: export blocks only on a failed comparison; lines 3925-3931 report the uncommitted count with no explanation.
- awb-package SKILL.md:73: "Commit nothing on the user's behalf to make provenance look clean."
- awb_landing.py:640-647 and 1220-1226: conversion_commit is "uncommitted" when no HEAD exists; the SQL's checksum (select_sha256) goes in the notes.
- Runs: taxi-B agent-005 #19 export written with 12 uncommitted changes and no failed checks, then #20-#22 commit, rerun (79 s) and 15717a2.
- retail-B agent-005 #9 export written with 12 uncommitted changes, then #10 commit and run.py (all results kept).
- retail-B publication.json conversion_commit is "uncommitted", with select_sha256 recorded.
- retail-A agent-004: commits 9096f84 (asked), 90e317e and 7f1ccf0 (not asked); full rerun took 27 s.
verdicts.narrowed: Under "commit as you go", the guides never say to commit producing code before running a result. Agents therefore run first and commit after. The evidence then names the previous commit plus checksummed uncommitted changes. Export and release accept that state, but nothing tells the agent so, and analysis.md and awb-status both present a rerun as the fix. As a result, taxi-B and retail-B committed, reran and re-exported (79 s and about 6 s) only so the evidence would name a commit, without packaging requiring it. Separately, in the default on-request mode, a dataset published before the user's first commit permanently records conversion_commit "uncommitted", with the SQL's checksum kept in its notes.
