That follows from data.md:33, which tells the agent to suggest a commit, not to commit first. The retail-A extra commits come from the Codex agent's own choice and go against the release's rules.

verdicts.reasoning:
The finding says results run before a commit "need" a commit, a rerun and a re-export before packaging accepts them. Neither the shipped helpers nor the run evidence bear that out.

1. Export accepts evidence with uncommitted code. compare_evidence() compares checksums under "uncommitted-code", and when the producing commit is "uncommitted" it passes with "no producing commit; producing files compared under uncommitted-code". The manifest template allows `uncommitted` plus checksums, and allows a SHA with `producing_uncommitted_changes`.
   - taxi-B turn 5: the first successful export wrote all six charts (`written: true`, `export_checks failed: []`) while reporting `producing_commit: "differs by result"` with 12 uncommitted changes. The agent then committed (15717a2) and reran everything, and every result came back "kept".
   - retail-B turn 5: the same pattern. The export succeeded with "differs by result" and 12 changes, then came commit 7c155f6, run.py (all 7 "kept"), and a re-export. "Before packaging accepted it" is false: packaging had already accepted it.
   - retail-A: release 001 shipped with `products` and `products-three-customers` evidence still carrying 2 and 4 uncommitted paths, disclosed in the manifest. The full commit-and-rerun was never needed to release.

2. "Records 'uncommitted'" is wrong for these runs. In taxi-B and retail-B every result ran after the project's first commit, so the evidence named a SHA (9969672 or 3327f4c) plus 2–4 checksummed dirty paths. The literal "uncommitted" value only applies before the first commit, which none of these results were run before.

3. The release tells agents not to do this for appearance's sake. awb-package/SKILL.md step 5 says "Commit nothing on the user's behalf to make provenance look clean." In retail-A (`Commits: on request`) the user asked for one commit ("Go ahead and commit, then start the analysis"). The agent then made two more (90e317e, 7f1ccf0) against AGENTS.md's "Commit when asked". Its notes say the 13-result rerun was partly for 3 newly added results and a changed requirements file. The rerun took about 25 s (`recorded_at` runs from 07:45:46 to 07:46:11), so the cost is small.

4. What the release does contribute is a nudge, not a requirement.
   - analysis.md line 19 gives "rerun after that commit" as the way to clear pre-first-commit `uncommitted`.
   - awb-status suggests "Rerun <results> so their evidence records the commit", but only for evidence with no SHA, which was not the case here.
   - In "as I go" mode no guide says to commit before running. The export report also never says that "differs by result" or N uncommitted changes is acceptable.
   That fully explains agents choosing to tidy up, which they did in all three runs, but it is not "need".

5. The publication sub-claim (retail-B-36) is real but cosmetic.
   - awb-init creates a repo with no commit, and data.md line 33 only suggests a commit under "on request" ("...otherwise suggest committing them... Then publish").
   - publish() sets conversion_commit to "uncommitted" when there is no HEAD. All three runs' publication.json files say "uncommitted" (retail-B, taxi-B ×2, retail-A).
   - The SQL's sha256 is stored in the notes, the publish warning says so, and nothing downstream (export, release, status) treats it as a gap.
   - An interactive host would behave the same, so the "cannot get an answer mid-turn" framing is not harness-specific. The outcome is the designed one.
verdicts.release_evidence:
Shipped release files:
- awb-init/assets/awb_provenance.py compare_evidence() (about lines 867–985): the uncommitted-code comparison checks bytes/sha256. When the evidence has "uncommitted", committed-code passes with "no producing commit; producing files compared under uncommitted-code".
- awb-package/assets/awb_draft.py lines 3905–3931: export writes producing_commit / producing_uncommitted_changes into the manifest and reports them. It does not refuse.
- awb-package/assets/package-format/manifest-template.md lines 17–18: allow `uncommitted` with checksums, or a SHA plus `producing_uncommitted_changes`.
- awb-package/SKILL.md line 73: "Commit nothing on the user's behalf to make provenance look clean."
- awb-init/assets/workbench/AGENTS.md line 50: "Commit when asked".
- workbench-guides/analysis.md line 19: says rerunning after the first commit clears `uncommitted`. It gives no commit-before-run ordering for "as I go".
- awb-status/SKILL.md line 69 and collect_status.py uncommitted_evidence(): suggest a rerun only for evidence whose producing_commit is not a SHA.
- workbench-guides/data.md line 33: under "on request", suggest a commit and then publish.
- awb_landing.py lines 642–647 and 1225: conversion_commit is "uncommitted" without HEAD; the publish warning notes the sha256 is in publication.json notes.

Runs:
- taxi-B agent-005: the export before the rerun returned written:true with "differs by result" and 12 changes. Commit 15717a2 followed, then a full rerun (all "kept").
- Evidence at commit bb7e82b names SHA 9969672 with 2 dirty paths each.
- retail-B agent-005: the export returned written:true with "differs by result" and 12 changes. Commit 7c155f6 followed, then run.py (all "kept"), then a re-export.
- retail-B evidence at 24077a2 names SHA 3327f4c with 2–4 dirty paths.
- retail-A: the user asked "Go ahead and commit" (msg 4). Commits 90e317e and 7f1ccf0 were not asked for. The rerun took about 25 s. Release 001 shipped with uncommitted products evidence.
- All three runs' publication.json files have conversion_commit "uncommitted" plus select_sha256.
verdicts.narrowed: Narrower version that holds (minor, partly cosmetic): nothing requires a commit, rerun and re-export. Export and release accept results whose evidence records uncommitted, checksummed code. Still, in all three runs agents chose to commit, rerun every result and re-export just so the evidence names a clean commit. The release gives three nudges and nothing to stop it: analysis.md line 19 offers the rerun as the remedy, awb-status suggests rerunning so evidence records the commit, and no guide says to commit before running in "as I go" mode or that "differs by result" / N uncommitted changes is acceptable at export. The reruns came back unchanged and were cheap (about 25 s in retail-A). Separately, the default flow has awb-init create a repo with no commit and keeps "Commits: on request". The first publish therefore always happens before any commit, so publication.json permanently records conversion_commit "uncommitted". The conversion SQL's sha256 is kept in its notes and nothing downstream flags it. That is a designed provenance label, not a gap in provenance.

consolidated.title: awb-scope's 'look facts up in source systems' conflicts with data.md's 'inspect records only from landed copies'
consolidated.description: taxi-B queried the inbox Parquet files with DuckDB before landing them. co2-B ran curl and grep on the codebook while unsure whether that was allowed. retail-B relied on its prior knowledge of the dataset instead of looking at the documentation.
consolidated.caused_by_fix: no
consolidated.evidence: taxi-B-11: DuckDB peek at inbox/yellow_tripdata_2024-*.parquet in relay/agent-001.jsonl; awb-scope/SKILL.md; workbench-guides/data.md:9. co2-B-19: relay/agent-001.jsonl; awb-scope/SKILL.md 'Scoping writes investigation records only'. retail-B-34: reply 1; agent-notes turn 1; awb-scope/SKILL.md lines 10 and 38.

verdicts.reasoning:
Only taxi-B supports the finding as written. The other two runs don't show the data.md conflict.

taxi-B (product): In turn 1 the agent loaded awb-init, then awb-scope, and before landing anything it ran raw DuckDB from the project venv against inbox/yellow_tripdata_2024-*.parquet and inbox/taxi_zone_lookup.csv. It pulled the schema, row counts, payment-type tips, vendor counts and validity counts, then showed the user the numbers as "a first look at the files". Its friction log names awb-scope's "look facts up yourself ... in source systems" as the reason. It also says it could not tell whether a peek before landing was allowed, and guessed that it counted as a "quick lookup". It had not read workbench-guides/data.md, the guide that says to inspect records only from landed copies. AGENTS.md says to read it "before assessing a source", but awb-scope never links it.

The release sets this up. awb-init:48 runs scope's first interview round in the same turn as setup, before any landing. awb-scope:33 asks for definitions "tested ... against source data", and :38 says to look facts up in source systems. Neither mentions landing first.

I checked each harness explanation and none holds:
- The persona's front-loaded request ("verify cash tips before drawing tipping conclusions") is a realistic opening. It also asked for the check before conclusions, not during scoping.
- Bash auto-approval doesn't matter. An interactive user would most likely approve a read-only Python call, and the instruction conflict would still be there.
- Running non-interactively played no part, because the skill itself says to look facts up rather than ask.
- The study note only made the agent write its doubt down. It did not cause the peek.

co2-B (does not support the data.md claim): The agent ran curl|grep on the OWID codebook, a URL the user gave it. A codebook is documentation, and data.md:9 explicitly allows assessing a candidate "from its documentation or schema". The doubt in its log was about wording inside awb-scope ("look facts up" vs "Scoping writes investigation records only"), not about data.md. The study note's friction-log request is what brought that doubt to the surface. The only data.md gap is that it didn't keep the codebook under foundation/references at that point, and it did keep its references later.

retail-B (mostly harness): The agent described the export's contents from memory of the public UCI Online Retail II dataset (postage, bank charges, Amazon fees, the Dec 2010 overlap between sheets). It downloaded nothing and read no documentation. Relying on memory only works because the simulation uses a well-known public dataset. With a real company's private export, that memory wouldn't exist. Its log, like co2-B's, cites the tension inside awb-scope, not data.md, and it hadn't read data.md in turn 1. All this run shows is that the same release gap can also lead to not looking at all.

So: product, but narrower. The release causes it in taxi-B, and the other two runs give no independent support for the data.md conflict as stated.
verdicts.release_evidence: awb-scope/SKILL.md:33 says to test definitions "against source data and analytical logic when they exist". awb-scope/SKILL.md:38 says "Look facts up yourself in the repository, catalog, and source systems, and answer a question a quick lookup settles". awb-scope/SKILL.md:10 says "Scoping writes investigation records only; data work, analysis, and packages follow on request". None of these link workbench-guides/data.md or say anything about landing. awb-init/assets/workbench/workbench-guides/data.md:9 says "inspect records only from landed copies, landing only what the assessment needs". awb-init/assets/workbench/AGENTS.md:13 says to read data.md "before assessing a source", but awb-scope never points to it. awb-init/SKILL.md:48 runs scope's first interview round in the same turn as setup, which is always before any landing. Run evidence: taxi-B/relay/agent-001.jsonl, the raw DuckDB query on inbox/*.parquet, and the turn 1 entry in taxi-B/feedback/agent-notes.md that cites awb-scope:38. co2-B/relay/agent-001.jsonl is a curl of the codebook URL, which is documentation that data.md:9 permits. retail-B/relay/agent-001.out.md describes the dataset from the model's memory of a public dataset.
verdicts.narrowed: During the first interview round, which awb-init runs before any landing, awb-scope tells the agent to test definitions against source data and to look facts up in source systems. It doesn't link workbench-guides/data.md or say that records may be inspected only from landed copies. Following that, the taxi-B agent queried the user's unlanded inbox Parquet files with raw DuckDB and gave the user the counts, without the provenance a landed copy would have. co2-B and retail-B don't show this conflict. co2-B read documentation, which data.md allows. retail-B leaned on the model's memory of a famous public dataset, which is a harness artifact. Both show only that awb-scope's own wording is unclear about whether looking at sources before landing is allowed.

verdicts.reasoning:
The conflict exists in the shipped text, but only one of the three runs actually shows it.

Shipped text:
- awb-scope/SKILL.md:38 says to "Look facts up yourself in the repository, catalog, and source systems, and answer a question a quick lookup settles."
- awb-scope/SKILL.md:33 says to test definitions "against source data and analytical logic when they exist".
- The release README.md:64 says the scoping round has the agent look up "facts the data or files can settle".
- README.md:54 says "Setup and the scoping round bring no data in".
- awb-init hands the question to awb-scope before any data is landed (SKILL.md:10, :48).
- workbench-guides/data.md:9 says "inspect records only from landed copies".
- AGENTS.md:13 sends the agent to data.md before it assesses a source. awb-scope never points to that rule or makes an exception to it.

Put together: in a new project, the scoping round may not land data, but it is told to check facts against the data or files. data.md forbids looking at records that have not been landed. A record-level lookup during scoping cannot satisfy both instructions. This does not depend on the host.

taxi-B confirms it. relay/agent-001.jsonl shows a read-only DuckDB query over inbox/yellow_tripdata_2024-*.parquet and taxi_zone_lookup.csv during the awb-scope round, before anything was landed. The agent's notes for turn 1 quote the "source systems" line as its reason, and feedback/agent.md:24 names the data.md conflict. The simulated user also noticed: human.md:33 says the agent "looked at the data during setup, despite the stated separation". No harness rule pushed the agent into this.

co2-B does not show the data.md conflict. It ran curl and grep on the OWID codebook, which is documentation. data.md:9 explicitly allows assessing a candidate "from its documentation or schema". The agent's doubt was about awb-scope:10 ("Scoping writes investigation records only") against :38. That is a separate, milder ambiguity. A loosely related point: data.md:11 asks for a codebook to be kept under foundation/references/, and the one-off curl kept nothing.

retail-B does not show it either. The agent had not read data.md. It relied on what it already knew about the UCI dataset because it read awb-scope:10 and "data work follows on request" as forbidding a download. Nothing in the release stopped it from reading the UCI documentation page, which data.md permits. So the claim that it ignored the documentation is a choice the agent made under the scope ambiguity, not something data.md caused.

Evidence IDs: the cited taxi-B-11 and retail-B-34 do not match these issues in the runs' findings.json. The matching entries are taxi-B-08 (pre-landing peek, tagged as the scope/data.md conflict) and retail-B-35 (prior knowledge). co2-B-19 matches. Severity minor holds: the peek was read-only and gave the user useful checks, such as that cash tips are missing. The cost is muddled guidance on what may be inspected before landing, and how choices that inspection shaped get recorded.
verdicts.release_evidence:
- awb-scope/SKILL.md:38: "Look facts up yourself in the repository, catalog, and source systems".
- awb-scope/SKILL.md:33: "tested ... against source data and analytical logic when they exist".
- awb-scope/SKILL.md:10: "Scoping writes investigation records only; data work, analysis, and packages follow on request".
- README.md:54: "Setup and the scoping round bring no data in".
- README.md:64: "The agent looks up facts the data or files can settle".
- awb-init/SKILL.md:48 hands the question to awb-scope before any landing.
- awb-init/assets/workbench/workbench-guides/data.md:9: "Assess a candidate from its documentation or schema ...; inspect records only from landed copies".
- AGENTS.md:13 says to read data.md "before assessing a source", and awb-scope does not point to it.
- Run evidence:
  - taxi-B relay/agent-001.jsonl: DuckDB describe and aggregates over inbox/yellow_tripdata_2024-*.parquet during the scope round.
  - taxi-B feedback/agent-notes.md turn 1 and agent.md:24.
  - taxi-B feedback/human.md:33.
  - co2-B relay/agent-001.jsonl: a curl and grep of owid-co2-codebook.csv, which is documentation.
  - retail-B agent-notes.md turn 1: relied on prior knowledge.
verdicts.narrowed: For a record-level lookup in a new project, the shipped instructions conflict. awb-scope (lines 33 and 38) and README:64 tell the agent to check facts against the source data and files during the scoping round. README:54 says that round brings no data in, and data.md:9 allows inspecting records only from landed copies. As a result the agent queries user-supplied files before landing them (taxi-B, relay/agent-001.jsonl, findings.json taxi-B-08), and the simulated user found that inconsistent. co2-B and retail-B do not show this conflict. Reading a codebook is documentation assessment, which data.md allows. retail-B's reliance on prior knowledge came from the separate ambiguity of awb-scope:10 ("Scoping writes investigation records only") against :38, not from data.md.

consolidated.title: Landing and record reference grammar is dense and strict
consolidated.description: landing.md now mixes the land() signature with the archive and spreadsheet forms and the full source-reference grammar, so finding the one signature needed is slow (co2-B). The clean-record evidence field packs several references into one string with a suffix rule, and it refused a string listing several references (taxi-A). For a fetched source that is also an archive, retail-B had to infer that the fetch callable should extract the members, since data.md and landing.md each cover only one half.
consolidated.caused_by_fix: partly: #98 (issue #92) moved the source-reference grammar out of the sources.md template into awb-init/references/landing.md, which co2-B found dense.
consolidated.evidence: co2-B-16: landing.md output in relay/agent-002.jsonl. taxi-A-27: agent-003 awb/records failure ('RecordError: N1 evidence names no saved query'); agent-notes line 34. retail-B-35: agent-002 fetch_online_retail_ii.py; data.md lines 19-21; landing.md lines 21-29.

verdicts.reasoning:
None of the three observations comes from how the simulation was run. The harness did shape one of them, though, and none of them caused a problem the user could see.

taxi-A: this one is real and caused by the release. Codex sent an N1 evidence string to the clean-record helper over MCP: "src/preparation/yellow_trips-check.sql; both publication.json files; investigations/.../intake-integrity.sql". record_cleaning.py (lines 300-310) refused it with exit 2: "RecordError: N1 evidence names no saved query". The rule only looks at how the string ends. Evidence that ends in .sql must be one existing path with no spaces. Anything else is stored as free text and not checked. So the same three references in a different order, ending in "...files", would have passed, and none of the paths in it would have been checked. Nothing about the harness affects how the evidence is written: not codex exec, not the sandbox, not the auto-approved MCP call, not the simulated home. An agent on a normal interactive host would send the same payload and get the same refusal. The cost was small. The error message was clear, the retry worked on the first try, and nothing was written. The agent did drop two citations to fit the rule. The agent also admitted the helper's documentation describes the grammar and its first payload simply did not follow it.

retail-B: this is a real gap in the release's docs. data.md line 19 covers archives only for supplied files, using the `land` CLI. Line 21 covers fetched sources, using `land()` with a fetch callable. landing.md's archive section (lines 21-29) shows only the CLI form. Neither file says what to do with a fetched archive. The agent inferred that the fetch callable should download the zip and extract the .xlsx into extracted/ inside the partial directory. That worked the first time (fetch_online_retail_ii.py). Any user whose source is a zip at a URL would face the same missing instruction. Nothing failed.

co2-B: this one is the weakest, and the harness partly produced it. The relay's agent note (relay.py around line 279) tells the agent to log anything "confusing, contradictory, missing, or too long" in the instruction files. The remark "landing.md is very long ... I only needed the land() signature. The section is findable" is a direct answer to that prompt. The log shows no slowness. The agent read the whole file in one `cat`, which exited 1 only because of a zsh quirk with `echo ======`. It then wrote a working fetch script with no further lookups. The file itself does mix several concerns. land() is one dense paragraph full of rules about refusing credentialed URLs, and it sits next to the archive, Excel, read-only SQL and source-reference sections (12.8 KB). That is a fact about the release, but the claim that finding the signature was slow has no evidence behind it.

Summary: the release is the cause wherever there is a cause, so this is not a harness artifact. Severity is minor at most. The user never saw any of it, and the only real cost was one failed helper call that recovered on the first retry.
verdicts.release_evidence: awb-clean/scripts/record_cleaning.py lines 30-37 and 300-310: the .sql suffix rule. A string ending in .sql must be one existing project path with no spaces, or it is refused. Any other string is stored as text without checking the paths in it. awb-clean/SKILL.md line 73 says "A `new` issue's evidence is a saved query's path or a reference in words". The relay log taxi-A/relay/agent-003.jsonl has the failed records/clean-record call ("N1 evidence names no saved query: src/preparation/yellow_trips-check.sql; both publication.json files; ...") and the successful retry right after it, which used the single intake-integrity.sql path. awb-init/assets/workbench/workbench-guides/data.md line 19 covers archives for supplied files via the `land` CLI, and line 21 covers fetched sources via `land()`. Neither covers a fetched archive. awb-init/references/landing.md lines 21-29: the archive section shows only the CLI command. Lines 5-13 cover land() and do not mention archives. landing.md line 9 is a single paragraph holding the land() signature and the full credential-URL refusal rules. The file is 12,832 bytes and also covers publish, Excel, read-only SQL and the source-reference grammar (lines 53-61). co2-B/relay/agent-002.jsonl: landing.md was read in one cat and a working fetch script was written straight after. kit/relay.py around line 279: the harness asks for a friction log that names anything "too long".
verdicts.narrowed: Two release behaviours hold up, both minor and with no impact the user sees. (1) The awb-clean clean-record evidence field decides by the string's suffix. A string that ends in .sql is refused unless it is exactly one existing saved-query path. Listing several references therefore fails, while the same references ordered to end in words pass with no path checking (taxi-A: one refusal, recovered in one retry, two citations dropped). (2) Neither data.md nor landing.md says how to land an archive that is fetched rather than supplied. The agent has to infer that the fetch callable should write both the archive and its extracted members into the partial directory (retail-B: inferred correctly, no failure). The co2-B claim that landing.md's density made the land() signature slow to find is a harness-prompted remark with no behavioural evidence and should be dropped or reduced to "landing.md mixes many concerns".

verdicts.reasoning:
I checked the three parts of the finding separately. The skill copies used in co2-B, retail-B and taxi-A are identical to the release files.

1. landing.md is dense and mixes concerns (co2-B). This part is real and comes from the release. awb-init/references/landing.md is 61 lines and about 1,970 words. Its land() paragraph (line 9) is one block that starts with the signature and then runs through the rules for refusing credentials in URLs, parameter-name matching, port and host checks, and what happens to the .partial directory. The same file also holds publish(), archives and spreadsheets (lines 21-39), read-only SQL refusals (41-47) and the awb-status source-reference grammar (53-61). That grammar is unrelated to landing. The "slow to find" part is overstated. The land() section comes first, its signature opens the section, and data.md line 5 sends the reader there. The co2-B agent read the file once and wrote a working fetch script on the next step. Its note, agent-notes line 35, says "The section is findable but the doc mixes many concerns."

2. Fetched source that is also an archive (retail-B). This gap is real and comes from the release. data.md line 19 handles archives through the `land` command. Line 21 handles fetched sources through land() with a fetch callable. landing.md's archive section (lines 21-29) shows only the `land` command form. Nothing says that a fetch callable for an archive should write both the archive and its extracted members into the partial directory. Line 9 only says the callback "writes every original file". retail-B guessed right on the first try (agent-notes lines 29 and 38; fetch_online_retail_ii.py writes the zip plus extracted/), so the gap cost nothing in this run.

3. Clean-record evidence field (taxi-A). This part does not hold up as a defect. The release documents the rule. record_cleaning.py lines 30-37 say evidence is one line, that evidence ending in .sql must be a single saved-query path, and that "Evidence citing a saved query that is ... inside a sentence is refused". awb-clean/SKILL.md line 73 says "A `new` issue's evidence is a saved query's path or a reference in words." The relay log shows taxi-A read `help clean-record` (call 42), failed once (call 45), and succeeded on the retry (call 46). The error message names the exact fix. In agent-notes line 34 the agent writes: "The help documented this strict grammar; my first payload failed to follow it." It was one slip against a clear instruction, not a repeated failure. The description "packs several references into one string" is also wrong: the field takes one saved query or plain words, by design.

The suffix rule does have a quirk: only evidence that ends in .sql gets validated. That quirk caused nothing in these runs.

The harness did not cause either of the parts that hold. Both are written into the shipped docs. Neither one led to an error, a retry or a wrong result, so minor severity fits.
verdicts.release_evidence:
- awb-init/references/landing.md line 3: the intro lists every concern the file covers, including "the source reference grammar `awb-status` reads".
- landing.md line 9: one very long paragraph holding the land() signature plus all the URL credential, port and parameter refusal rules.
- landing.md lines 21-29: the archive section gives only `python3 src/awb.py land <source> <acquisition-id> <archive>.zip <extracted-folder> --notes ...`, with no land()/fetch variant.
- landing.md lines 53-61: the source-reference grammar, in the same file.
- workbench-guides/data.md line 19 (archive through the `land` command) and line 21 (fetched source through land()): each covers one half and neither joins them.
- awb-clean/scripts/record_cleaning.py lines 30-37 (docstring) and lines 299-309 (check that refuses .sql-ending evidence that is not a single path); awb-clean/SKILL.md line 73. Both document the single-reference evidence rule.
- Run evidence: co2-B agent-notes line 35 ("findable"); retail-B agent-notes lines 29 and 38 (worked first time, inference not spelled out); taxi-A agent-003 relay calls 42/45/46 (read help, one failure, success on retry) and agent-notes line 34 (agent says the help documented the rule).
verdicts.narrowed: landing.md puts too much in one place. The land() signature sits inside one long paragraph of URL credential and port refusal rules, and the same file also carries publish(), spreadsheets, read-only SQL refusals and the unrelated awb-status source-reference grammar. Separately, neither landing.md nor data.md says how to land a fetched archive: the archive section shows only the `land` command form, so an agent has to work out that the fetch callable should write both the archive and its extracted members into the partial directory. Neither problem caused a failure: co2-B found the signature right away, and retail-B's fetch worked on the first try. The clean-record evidence part does not hold. The single-reference rule is documented in the script help and SKILL.md, the error message names the fix, and taxi-A recovered in one retry, saying its first payload ignored documented grammar.

consolidated.title: Init templates leave instruction text and hand-filled fields in project records
consolidated.description: The state.md and source-register templates carry instruction paragraphs, and fields such as an assessment basis before any data exists and a Restrictions column the helper says to fill by hand. Agents had to strip, hedge or complete them. awb-init says to 'adapt' the README, .gitignore and AGENTS templates, which is unclear in an empty project. co2-B copied them verbatim, so its README still carries the template's 'why overtime rose in Q3' examples.
consolidated.caused_by_fix: no
consolidated.evidence: co2-A-17: agent-002; foundation/sources.md template line 28; awb_landing.py line 705. co2-B-39: project/README.md lines 46-47; awb-init/SKILL.md step 3.1. retail-A-33: agent-notes Turns 1-2; awb-init/assets/workbench/foundation/sources.md and investigation/state.md.

verdicts.reasoning:
I looked for a harness cause and found none. The things the finding describes come from release files, which are the same on any host: the template text, the word "adapt" in awb-init step 3.1 and awb-scope, the helper's "fill Restrictions yourself", and awb-status's basis check. None of them depend on how the simulation was run (codex exec or claude -p, the sandbox, the simulated home, auto-approved MCP tools, or the relay). The study disclosure explains why agents wrote this friction down, not why it exists.

Persona front-loading does trigger the retail-A case: the user named the source in the first message, so the register was created at setup. But a real user naming their source up front is ordinary, and awb-init step 3.4 tells the agent to create the register "when a source becomes a real candidate", which naming it does.

Not every part of the finding holds up.

(1) Assessment basis is a real gap. The sources.md template (line 16) and the copy awb_landing.py writes (line 726) say Relevance and fitness must open with "from documentation" or "from landed records". collect_status.py lines 305-310 flag any non-empty cell without that opening as uncertain. A candidate registered before any documentation is read cannot honestly meet this. retail-A turn 1 says so and used "Not yet assessed" wording, which awb-status would flag.

(2) The instruction paragraphs cause inconsistency, not harm. co2-A dropped the sources.md paragraphs but kept the state.md ones, and its notes call that copy a slip. retail-A stripped the state.md paragraphs but kept the sources.md ones. co2-B, taxi-A and taxi-B kept both. The product seems to mean them as a lasting legend: awb_landing.py writes the full sources.md template, paragraphs included, when the file is missing, and the state helpers edit sections in place. The ambiguity is real and comes from the release. The harm is cosmetic.

(3) Hand-filling Restrictions is deliberate design. awb_landing.py lines 704-705 say columns needing human judgment stay as they are, and the land/retain help at line 992 says to fill Restrictions yourself. co2-A filled it and moved on. That is the intended workflow, not a template defect.

(4) The "overtime" examples are not specific to co2-B. All six project READMEs match the template exactly from "Where work belongs" onward, so every one carries the Q3 overtime examples. repair.md step 3 reconciles the "Asking for things" requests back to the template, so verbatim examples look intended. co2-B's agent was unsure what "adapt" meant (its agent-notes line 13 says so), but leaving the examples in only matters if they are confusing in a user's README, and that is debatable.

Also, the cited IDs co2-B-39 and retail-A-33 do not exist in those runs' feedback/findings.json files. co2-B has 32 findings and retail-A has 19. I found the cited material in each run's agent-notes.md instead.
verdicts.release_evidence:
- awb-init/assets/workbench/foundation/sources.md line 16, and the copy in awb-init/assets/awb_landing.py SOURCES_TEMPLATE at line 726: Relevance and fitness must begin with "from documentation" or "from landed records".
- awb-status/scripts/collect_status.py lines 305-310: a non-empty Relevance and fitness cell without that basis is marked uncertain.
- awb_landing.py lines 704-705 and the help text at line 992: Restrictions is left for human judgment by design.
- awb-init/SKILL.md step 3 and 3.1, and awb-scope/SKILL.md line 57: "Adapt" the templates; "instructional comments and example rows are guidance, not project facts".
- awb-init/assets/workbench/investigation/state.md lines 10-22: legend paragraphs.
- awb-init/assets/workbench/README.md lines 46-47: overtime examples. awb-init/references/repair.md step 3 reconciles "Asking for things" back to the template.
- Run evidence: retail-A/feedback/agent-notes.md turn 1 ("used transparent Not yet assessed wording") and turn 2 ("stripped them from initial artifact"); co2-A/feedback/agent-notes.md lines 28 and 30; co2-B/feedback/agent-notes.md line 13.
- In all six runs, project/README.md is identical to the template from "Where work belongs" onward.
verdicts.narrowed: Supported version: the source-register template, backed by awb-status's basis check, requires Relevance and fitness to open with "from documentation" or "from landed records". A candidate source registered at setup, before any documentation has been read, cannot honestly do that. retail-A had to hedge with "Not yet assessed", which awb-status flags as uncertain. Separately, "adapt" in awb-init and awb-scope does not say whether the legend paragraphs in state.md and sources.md belong in the project record, so agents handled them inconsistently (co2-A, retail-A and co2-B each did something different). Cut from the finding: hand-filling Restrictions is deliberate helper design, not a defect. The README's Q3 overtime examples appear verbatim in all six runs because the template is built that way, so they are a cosmetic template choice, not a result of how co2-B read "adapt".

verdicts.reasoning:
Only one part of C-41 is a real release defect. The other parts describe behavior the release intends.

What holds up:
- **Assessment basis at candidate stage.** awb-init step 3.4 creates the source register as soon as a source "becomes a real candidate". The template (foundation/sources.md line 16) says Relevance and fitness must begin with `from documentation` or `from landed records`. awb-status collect_status.py lines 305-309 flags any other non-empty wording as uncertain. A candidate registered during init has often had neither its documentation read nor any data landed, and the template gives no wording for that stage, so agents improvise.
  - retail-A agent-001 wrote "Not yet assessed; candidate supplied by user...", and its agent-notes Turn 1 names this exact gap.
  - co2-B agent-001 wrote "Named by the user as the source for all five questions; not yet assessed".
  - Both rows lack the basis prefix, so status would flag them until the data was assessed. The release causes this and a normal user would hit it.

What does not hold up:
- **Instruction paragraphs in records are intended.** awb_landing.py lines 707-740 (SOURCES_TEMPLATE, "foundation/sources.md as awb-init installs it") writes the full instruction prose into sources.md itself when the file is absent. The state helper (awb_provenance.py _Record/_State) edits state.md in place and keeps that prose. Agents were not forced to remove it:
  - state.md keeps it in taxi-A, taxi-B, co2-A and co2-B, partly in retail-B, and retail-A chose to strip it.
  - co2-A chose to strip the sources.md prose.
- **Restrictions is filled by hand by design.** Template line 28, the help text at awb_landing.py line 992, and workbench-guides/data.md line 29 all say plainly to fill it. The comment at line 705 says the helpers keep that column as entered. co2-A filled it and asked for a convenience argument. That is a feature request, not a defect.
- **The README examples are template-owned.** All six runs, not only co2-B, kept the "why overtime rose in Q3" examples. references/repair.md step 3 treats the **Asking for things** requests as template content that repair adds back and reconciles. Keeping them verbatim is therefore the intended result. co2-B's note shows it was unsure what "adapt" meant there, but the outcome is a generic example request in a user guide section. At most that is cosmetic.

The evidence IDs co2-B-39 and retail-A-33 are not in those runs' findings.json files (co2-B goes up to 32 and retail-A up to 19). I checked the facts directly in the relays, agent-notes and project files instead.
verdicts.release_evidence:
- awb-init/SKILL.md line 41 (step 3.4): create the source register "when a source becomes a real candidate".
- awb-init/assets/workbench/foundation/sources.md line 16: Relevance and fitness must begin with `from documentation` or `from landed records`; no option for the candidate stage.
- awb-status/scripts/collect_status.py lines 305-309: flags as uncertain any Relevance and fitness cell that does not begin with a basis.
- awb-init/assets/awb_landing.py lines 704-740: SOURCES_TEMPLATE writes the instruction prose into sources.md, and the comment says the helpers keep Restrictions as entered.
- awb-init/assets/awb_landing.py line 992 and workbench-guides/data.md line 29: explicit "fill Restrictions yourself".
- awb-init/references/repair.md step 3: reconciles the README's **Asking for things** requests with the template.
- Run evidence: retail-A relay agent-001 (row "Not yet assessed; candidate...") and agent-notes Turn 1; co2-B relay agent-001 ("...; not yet assessed | candidate"); co2-B agent-notes line 13 (copied the README verbatim, unsure about the overtime examples); the overtime examples are present in all six project READMEs; co2-A agent-notes line 30 (Restrictions filled by hand).
verdicts.narrowed: The source-register template requires Relevance and fitness to begin with `from documentation` or `from landed records`, and awb-status flags any other wording as uncertain. But awb-init creates the register as soon as a source is a candidate, when neither basis may exist yet, and the template offers no wording for that stage. In retail-A and co2-B the agents wrote "not yet assessed" without the prefix. Severity: minor. The instruction paragraphs, the Restrictions column filled by hand, and the generic README request examples are intended design; at most the README examples are cosmetic.

consolidated.title: Release reports restate every caveat, duplicate a headline, and can contradict START-HERE
consolidated.description: awb-release requires listing every open caveat, even when the user asked only for the release path (taxi-A, retail-A). Both users valued the list, so the evidence of harm is weak. open_caveats repeats the Limitations slide's headline beside its first bullet (taxi-B). taxi-B's release summary in chat called the outline and chart files 'For the board' and methodology.md 'internal only'. The released START-HERE sends all three to the deck builder, and only the finished deck and the note to the board.
consolidated.oct16_ref: new (START-HERE itself is fixed; see C-50 in fixed_since_oct16)
consolidated.caused_by_fix: no
consolidated.evidence: taxi-A-28: msg 9, reply 9; feedback/human.md section 6. retail-A-20: reply 9; awb-release/SKILL.md Report. taxi-B-28: reply 7. taxi-B-20: reply 7; storage/releases/airport-trips-and-tipping/board-briefing/001/START-HERE.md.

verdicts.reasoning:
None of the three parts traces to the harness, but only the START-HERE contradiction shows harm a user can see, and part of its wording overstates the evidence.

(1) Restating every caveat. awb-release/SKILL.md line 63 requires it ("List every `open_caveats` entry ... the headline and bullets of the deck's Limitations and open caveats ..."). The CHANGELOG states it as intended. The installed copies in agent-home are byte-identical to the release, so a real user on an interactive host would get the same list. The harness did shape the complaint, not the behavior. The harness note asks agents to log what is "too long" in instructions, and the only objections came from agent feedback (taxi-A agent.md section 2, retail-A agent.md rank 9). Both simulated users praised the list (taxi-A human.md section 6: "the caveats were listed"; retail-A: "useful closing list of caveats"). The lists were short: 5 bullets in taxi-A, 4 in retail-A. Product behavior, but harm is unsupported.

(2) Headline duplication. The release tool emits it by design. open_caveats() in awb_draft.py takes slide["headlines"][:1] plus the bullets. In taxi-B the raw output lists "Cash tips are not recorded, so tipping figures describe card payments only" and then a first bullet saying nearly the same thing. The duplication stays inside the tool's JSON output. The Claude agent presented the line as the slide's heading ("headed ..."), and the Codex agent in retail-A merged the headline into its first bullet. The cause is the product, the effect is cosmetic, and the user never saw it.

(3) START-HERE contradiction. This is real and the user saw it. In taxi-B reply 7, Claude wrote "For the board: the deck outline, the six chart files and the methodology note". The released START-HERE sends findings.md and the chart CSVs to the deck builder, and only the finished deck and methodology-note.md to the audience. The persona caught it (human.md pain point 7). Nothing in the harness caused it: the agent system prompt and relay say nothing about file roles, and the same model runs on a real host. The agent volunteered the breakdown. The awb-release Report section does not ask for one and never mentions START-HERE, and in that turn the agent only ran ls on the release folder. Across all of taxi-B's agent logs it never read START-HERE, so it guessed the categories. The finding overstates one detail. Calling methodology.md "internal only" agrees with START-HERE, whose part 3 marks the files part 2 attaches as internal and not for the audience. Only the outline and chart files being labeled "For the board" is a contradiction. This happened once, in one run.
verdicts.release_evidence: awb-release/SKILL.md lines 59-63 (Report): requires listing every open_caveats entry, "the headline and bullets" of the Limitations and Open questions slides, and never mentions START-HERE or file roles. awb-package/assets/awb_draft.py open_caveats() (around line 4997): builds the rows from slide["headlines"][:1] + slide["bullets"], so the headline is emitted by design. CHANGELOG.md line 46 states this as intended. taxi-B/relay/agent-007.jsonl: the release tool output shows the headline line and a near-duplicate first bullet. The release output has no file-role or start_here field. The agent's only file access that turn was ls on the release folder, and grep across agent-001..007 finds no read of START-HERE's content. taxi-B/storage/releases/airport-trips-and-tipping/board-briefing/001/START-HERE.md: part 1 sends the deck and methodology-note.md to the audience; part 2 attaches findings.md, charts, methodology.md and deck-rules.md for the builder; part 3 marks the part 2 files as internal. taxi-A and retail-A reply 9 plus human.md: both users rated the caveat list positively. The installed skills in each run's agent-home are byte-identical to the release.
verdicts.narrowed: Supported on its own is the START-HERE contradiction, and only for the outline and chart files. In taxi-B, the agent's awb-release completion message volunteered a breakdown of which files go to whom. awb-release's Report does not ask for one or point to START-HERE, and the agent never read that file. The breakdown labeled findings.md and the chart CSVs "For the board", while the released START-HERE sends them to the deck builder and only the finished deck and methodology-note.md to the board. This happened once and is minor. A fix would be for the awb-release Report to point to the release's START-HERE instead of leaving the agent to describe file roles. Labeling methodology.md "internal only" agrees with START-HERE part 3. The other two parts are not defects. The every-caveat list is behavior the release intends, and both users valued it; only agents, prompted by the harness's friction-log note, objected to its length. The repeated headline is by design inside the open_caveats JSON, cosmetic, and was not visibly duplicated in either agent's chat.

verdicts.reasoning:
The finding makes three claims, and I checked each one against the shipped files and the run logs.

(1) Listing every caveat on release. awb-release/SKILL.md, in its Report section, does require it: "List every `open_caveats` entry ... the headline and bullets of the deck's Limitations and open caveats and Open questions slides". CHANGELOG.md line 46 shows this was a deliberate choice. In all three runs, though, the user had asked for a release, not only the path. taxi-A msg 9 says "Release it, and give me the full path". retail-A msg 9 says "Use awb-release to mark the package delivered". taxi-B msg 7 asked for the caveats outright: "report the full destination path and the caveats carried into the release". Both users who did not ask for the list valued it. taxi-A human.md section 6 says "the caveats were listed". retail-A human.md line 54 calls it "a useful closing list of caveats", and in msg 10 that user picked out the IT caveat to chase. Only the agents' own notes complain about the length (taxi-A agent.md section 2, retail-A agent.md rank 9). The release causes the behaviour, but it works as designed and no user was harmed.

(2) Duplicated headline. open_caveats() in awb-package/assets/awb_draft.py (around line 4997) emits `slide["headlines"][:1] + slide["bullets"]` as rows of the same shape. Only position tells the headline apart: its `sub` is empty, but a bullet's can be empty too. In the taxi-B release output, the headline "Cash tips are not recorded, so tipping figures describe card payments only" is followed by the bullet "Cash tips are not in the data ... every tipping figure covers credit-card trips only." The same overlap appears in taxi-A and retail-A. However, the overlap comes from the deck's wording, and the repeat exists only in the raw JSON. In every run the agent's chat report handled it cleanly. taxi-B reply 7 presents the headline as the heading ("headed ...") and then lists the bullets. The taxi-A and retail-A replies merge the headline into the first bullet. No user ever saw a duplicate.

(3) Contradicting START-HERE. Part of this is true: taxi-B reply 7 put "the deck outline, the six chart files and the methodology note" under "For the board". The released START-HERE.md sends findings.md and the chart CSVs to the builder, and sends only the deck and methodology-note.md to the audience. The finding overstates the methodology.md part, though. The agent said "Internal only: the methodology reference and the manifest", which matches START-HERE part 3: "the files part 2 attaches ... your audience gets the deck instead". More importantly, nothing in the release caused the mix-up. awb-release's Report asks for no file listing by audience, and the release tool output contains no file roles; the agent made up the grouping after running only `ls -R`. Every shipped description of the roles is correct and consistent:
- START-HERE.md, generated by start_here() in awb_draft.py around line 2831
- package-contract.md line 22
- helpers.md line 38
- README.md lines 19 and 195
- awb-package/SKILL.md line 98
This was a one-off agent error in a single run. The agent's closing line still pointed the user to START-HERE, and the user then followed START-HERE correctly (taxi-B msg 8).

Net result: claim 1 is intended behaviour that users found useful, claim 2 never reached a user, and claim 3 was not caused by the release.
verdicts.release_evidence: awb-release/SKILL.md Report section (last paragraph): "List every `open_caveats` entry, those carried forward included: the headline and bullets of the deck's Limitations and open caveats and Open questions slides". CHANGELOG.md:46 documents the same design. awb-package/assets/awb_draft.py open_caveats() (~line 4997): `for block in slide["headlines"][:1] + slide["bullets"]` emits the headline as an unmarked row ahead of the bullets. The release epilog (~line 5220) describes the same. File roles are correct in every shipped place: start_here() in awb_draft.py ~2831-2853 (part 1 sends the deck and methodology-note.md to the audience; part 2 sends findings.md, the charts and methodology.md "for the builder only"; part 3 keeps the manifest and the part-2 files internal), plus package-contract.md:22, helpers.md:38, README.md:19 and :195, and awb-package/SKILL.md:98. awb-release asks for no audience or builder file listing. Run evidence: taxi-B relay/agent-007.jsonl release output shows the headline and first bullet overlapping. taxi-B transcript reply 7 has the "For the board" mislabel but presents the headline as a heading, with no duplicate. The taxi-A and retail-A reply 9 caveat lists contain no duplicates. taxi-A human.md section 6 and retail-A human.md line 54 show both users valued the caveat list.
verdicts.narrowed: Only a cosmetic version holds, and no user saw it. The release's open_caveats output emits the Limitations slide headline as a row shaped exactly like a bullet, ahead of the bullets. When a deck's headline restates its first bullet (taxi-B, and in effect taxi-A and retail-A), the raw JSON repeats that caveat. Agents had to fold the headline in themselves, and all three did so correctly in chat. A `kind: headline` field, or a separate `headline` key per slide, would remove the guesswork. The caveat listing on every release is intended and users valued it. The taxi-B "For the board" mislabel was the agent's own error, not caused by the release.

consolidated.title: Chart row selection and chart roles are too narrow for common charts
consolidated.description: @where accepts only one condition on one column, or @first. taxi-A's two-month top-10 charts therefore needed two new projection results during packaging, and taxi-B needed a label column and a rerun just to chart a NULL 'all hours' row. Chart specifications have no annotation role, so retail-A put counts, starting values and growth rates into category labels.
consolidated.caused_by_fix: no
consolidated.evidence: taxi-A-19: reply 7; awb-package/references/helpers.md:52. taxi-B-25: item 3; commit 9ccf132. retail-A-35: Data lines of charts 3 and 4 in release 001 findings.md.

verdicts.reasoning:
The two main limits are in the release. They are not artifacts of how the simulation was run.

1) The selection grammar is closed by design. In awb_draft.py, parse_chart and _select accept only `@first=<n>` or a single `@where=<column>=<value>[,<value>]`, and `_select` keeps the rows whose one column matches a listed value. helpers.md:52 documents the same thing. In taxi-A, q5-supported.csv holds 1026 rows (2 months x 2 scenarios). Taking `supported_rank` 1..10 returns 40 rows, ten for each (month, scenario) pair, because the without_review rows have ranks of their own. `@first` has no offset, so it cannot reach July either. Charting both months' primary top tens therefore needs `scenario='all' AND rank<=10`, which the grammar cannot say. The agent made board-rankings to get around this. board-airports also needed `scenario='all' AND cohort in (...)`. Nothing in the harness (codex exec, sandbox, auto-approved MCP, relay, persona) affects this: any interactive user's agent calling export would hit the same parser.

2) The bar, column and line forms in the release's deck-rules.md have no annotation or data-label role. Their roles are category, value(s) and series; only Scatter has `label`. retail-A put invoice and customer counts, and base revenue and growth, into `[values.<column>]` display labels: see the manifest `values` maps and the chart-3 and chart-4 CSVs. The persona did not prompt this. The agent's own notes call it a workaround for the fixed role schema.

The finding overstates its taxi-B example. Commit 9ccf132 added `hour_label` and reran tips-by-hour, but the exported chart uses `@where=hour_label=00..23`. So the chart leaves the NULL "All hours" row out; it does not chart it. Before the commit, the saved table wrote pickup_hour as 0..23 with the all-hours row blank. `@where=pickup_hour=0,1,...,23` would therefore have picked the same rows without a new column or a rerun. That rerun came from the agent misjudging what the grammar could do (model behavior), not from a release limit. taxi-B's own notes do record a real but harmless conjunction case: month='both months' AND a vendor list. The agent got around it by picking the 'both months' rows, at no cost.

The "two projection results" count in taxi-A is also partly inflated. board-airports also records a new airport/other median-fare ratio, which would need a recorded result anyway. board-rankings adds summary count columns as well.
verdicts.release_evidence:
- release awb-package/assets/awb_draft.py: parse_chart (around line 3472) accepts only first=<n> or where=<column>=<values>; _select (around line 3573) filters on that one column.
- release awb-package/references/helpers.md:52: the same closed grammar.
- release CHANGELOG: `@first`/`@where` added so that "a top-ten chart no longer needs a recorded result of its own".
- awb-package/SKILL.md step 4: tells the agent to select rows in --chart rather than record a new result.
- release deck-rules.md Chart forms table: Horizontal bar, Column and Line take category / value(s) / series; only Scatter takes `label`.
- taxi-A: q5-supported.csv has 10 rows each for supported_rank 1..10 in (Jan, all), (Jan, without_review), (Jul, all) and (Jul, without_review). The producers board-rankings.py and board-airports.py filter `scenario=='all'` & a second column; the latter also computes airport_median_fare_multiple.
- retail-A release 001: manifest.json charts[2] and charts[3] `values` maps embed counts, bases and growth rates in category labels.
- taxi-B: 9ccf132^ tips-by-hour.csv has pickup_hour 0..23 with blank all-hours rows. The export used `@where=hour_label=00..23`, which leaves the all-hours row out.
verdicts.narrowed: Chart row selection takes only one column's value list, or a leading @first block with no offset. So a chart that needs a two-column condition cannot be selected from an existing result. The clear case is one scenario's top ten in each of two months (taxi-A, board-rankings; board-airports also needed a new ratio regardless). The workaround is a new recorded result or a rerun with a helper column. Separately, the bar, column and line chart forms have no annotation or data-label role, so supporting figures such as counts, bases and growth rates end up in category value labels (retail-A). The taxi-B example does not support the finding. Its all-hours row was left out of the chart, not charted, and `@where=pickup_hour=0..23` on the original table would have worked; the label column and rerun were unnecessary agent choices.

verdicts.reasoning:
The shipped code and docs cause this. In awb-package/assets/awb_draft.py, parse_chart (around line 3472) accepts only `@first=<n>` or `@where=<column>=<value>[,<value>]`. That means one column, exact-match values only, no empty values, no conjunctions and no comparisons such as <=. helpers.md:52 and package-contract.md:53/71 state the same limit. Step 4 of awb-package/SKILL.md tells the agent to select rows in `--chart`, "rather than recording a new result", and the contract says rows are never selected by editing the file. So when a chart needs a filter the grammar cannot express, the only route left is a new recorded result. For chart roles, CHART_FORMS in awb_draft.py (around line 1904) gives Horizontal bar, Column and Line only category, value and series. Only Scatter takes `label`. check_charts (around line 2375) also refuses any file column that no Data role names. So a bar chart cannot carry a count or a growth rate as a separate annotation column. deck-rules.md says the same.

Evidence check. The cited finding IDs are wrong: taxi-A-19, taxi-B-25 and retail-A-35 are about other issues or do not exist. The relevant ones are taxi-A-12, taxi-B-18 and retail-A agent.md line 98. The content still holds, with one exception:
(1) taxi-A: in q5-supported.csv (1,026 rows), the needed rows (scenario='all' and supported_rank<=10) sit at positions 0-9 and 512-521. Neither @first nor a single-column @where can pick them. The agent recorded board-rankings in turn 7, and the manifest charts it with selection 'all'. board-airports has the same need (scenario='all' plus three cohorts from q2-airports), though it also added a new ratio column, so it was not purely a selection workaround.
(2) retail-A: release 001 chart-3.csv and chart-4.csv put invoice and customer counts, and base revenue and growth rate, into the category labels, e.g. "Australia (base £29,360; +367%)". The agent's feedback calls this a workaround for the fixed role schema.
(3) taxi-B: overstated. Before commit 9ccf132, tips-by-hour saved pickup_hour as the integers 0-23, with a blank cell for the all-hours row. The final chart excludes that row; it does not chart it. `@where=pickup_hour=0,1,...,23` would have excluded it with no rerun, and display.toml value labels could have zero-padded the hours. Adding the label column and rerunning was the agent's choice; the grammar did not force it. taxi-B's other complaint, that it could not combine month and vendor, cost nothing, because the agent just picked the 'both months' rows.

None of this depends on the harness. Any user on a normal host gets the same grammar and the same check-draft refusals. Severity minor is fair.
verdicts.release_evidence:
- awb-package/assets/awb_draft.py parse_chart (~line 3472): the closed grammar `RESULT[:COLUMNS][@first=<n>|@where=<column>=<value>[,<value>]]`, with "none may be empty" (so a NULL row cannot be selected).
- awb_draft.py CHART_FORMS (~line 1904): bar, line and column forms take only category, value and series; `label` exists only for Scatter.
- check_charts (~line 2375) refuses a column "named by no **Data:** role".
- awb-package/references/helpers.md:52 "Row selection" states the same grammar.
- awb-package/SKILL.md step 4.1: "select its rows in the `--chart`, such as `@first=10` for a top ten, rather than recording a new result".
- package-contract.md:53: the Data line must name "every column it holds", and rows are "selected with `--chart`, never by editing the file".
- deck-rules.md Chart forms table: the same role list.
verdicts.narrowed: Confirmed for two of the three runs. The single-column, exact-match `@where` grammar cannot express a conjunction such as scenario='all' AND rank<=10, so taxi-A had to record a new board-rankings projection result during packaging (board-airports was partly the same workaround, but it also added a new ratio). Separately, bar, column and line charts have no annotation or label role, and check-draft refuses any column without a role, so retail-A put counts, base revenue and growth rates into category labels. Drop the taxi-B example. Its NULL all-hours row could have been excluded with `@where=pickup_hour=0,...,23` without a rerun, and it was excluded from the chart, not charted. The grammar's inability to select an empty value was never actually needed in that run.

consolidated.title: Codex replies say everything twice: progress narration, then a full summary
consolidated.description: Codex agents narrate their progress ('I'll do X... now checking Y') and then summarize the same content, so the answers start halfway down: taxi-A replies 3, 5 and 8; co2-A r1, r3 and r5; retail-A replies 2-9. A live Codex user would see the interim messages too, but the relay delivers all of a turn's messages as one block, which makes the replies look longer. No release instruction drives the repetition. Tag: co2-A-06 is product; unclear is better supported, because the relay effect confounds the evidence.
consolidated.caused_by_fix: no
consolidated.evidence: taxi-A-36: replies 3, 5 and 8; human.md section 4. co2-A-06: transcript r1 lines 28-56; separate agent_message items in agent-001, -003 and -005. retail-A-03: interim items in relay/agent-00N.jsonl; human.md pain point 2.

verdicts.reasoning:
The repetition comes from the Codex host's own design, and the relay then removed the part of that design that keeps it from bothering a user. The release has nothing to do with it.

1. **The host tells the model to narrate and then summarize.** The base instructions in the agents' Codex rollouts (e.g. retail-A/agent-home/.codex/sessions/2026/10/17/rollout-2026-10-17T07-17-58-...jsonl, session_meta) say: "If the user's request requires calling tools, start with a message in the `commentary` channel... should not be left without a commentary update for more than 60 seconds." They also say: "The final answer must always be fully self-contained: users should never need to read earlier commentary updates, since they are collapsed after the final answer is shown to users." The skill announcements ("I'm using awb-clean...") come from the host too: "The first time in a conversation that you decide to apply a skill, inform the user in the commentary channel."

2. **The rollouts confirm the split.** The interim messages are tagged `phase: commentary` (retail-A main session: 30 commentary, 10 final_answer; co2-A: 22 commentary, 9 final_answer). Only the last message of each turn is `final_answer`.

3. **The relay erases that split.** relay.py `_codex_reply` takes every `agent_message` item from `codex exec --json` and joins them with blank lines. It also drops the tool-call cells that sat between them. It uses `<stem>.last.md`, the final message alone, only as a fallback. The user then receives the result under "The agent replied:" (e.g. retail-A/relay/human-005.in.md) with no marker where commentary ends and the answer begins. In a live Codex session the commentary appears between tool calls while the agent works and collapses once the final answer shows. So a user would not find the answer "starting halfway down." The co2-A user even guessed the mechanism: "felt like the narration stream and the final summary were concatenated" (co2-A/feedback/human.md #2).

4. **co2-A's "four questions twice" is an exec-mode rendering issue.** In co2-A agent-001, the third "message" was not commentary at all. It was a `request_user_input_async` call (rollout line 47, which returned `{"accepted":true}`). `codex exec` emitted it as an AgentMessage item, and the relay passed it on as reply text. The model then repeated the questions in its final answer. In an interactive session that call shows the host's question UI, not text inside the reply.

5. **The taxi-A evidence does not support the finding.** taxi-A human.md section 4 never mentions duplicated or narrated replies. The nearest item is orchestrator item 12: two interim messages in reply 5 contradicted each other. In a live session those would sit in collapsed commentary.

6. **The co2-A-06 citation is wrong.** That ID in co2-A findings.json is the awb-status-prose finding, not this one. The repetition evidence for co2-A is orchestrator item 5.

7. **Nothing in the release drives this.** AGENTS.md's Conversation section only governs plain terms, asking for decisions, and the single closing status line. awb-scope only governs how questions are paced. No skill asks for progress narration or a restated summary. The finding itself concedes "No release instruction drives the repetition."

What a live Codex user would still see is the host's intended progress commentary while a turn runs. That is the same for any task, the release does not cause it, and it is collapsed afterward.
verdicts.release_evidence:
There is none.
- **AGENTS.md (awb-init/assets/workbench/AGENTS.md):** has no instruction to narrate progress, announce skills, or restate results. "## Conversation" covers plain wording, asking for decisions, and one closing status line on turns that changed records.
- **awb-scope/SKILL.md:** only paces scoping questions (at most four per round, each with a recommendation).
- **Who causes it:** the Codex host prompt ("start with a message in the commentary channel", a self-contained final answer, commentary "collapsed after the final answer is shown") together with relay.py `_codex_reply`, which joins every agent_message into one block and uses the final-only `.last.md` only as a fallback.
verdicts.narrowed: At most: Codex's host-mandated commentary sometimes includes partial findings that its final answer restates. A live Codex user sees these as progress updates during a turn, and they collapse once the final answer appears. This is host and model behaviour, not a release defect. One secondary point applies only to the harness: codex exec renders request_user_input_async calls as agent messages, so the relay passed co2-A's scoping questions to the user twice.

verdicts.reasoning:
The release does not cause this. Most of what the simulated users saw comes from the relay and from how `codex exec` behaves.

1) The release has nothing that drives it, and nothing that prevents it. I searched every shipped SKILL.md, the references, README, workbench-guides and the AGENTS.md template (the project copy in taxi-A is identical to the shipped one). Nothing asks for progress narration, preambles or a restating summary. The only reply-shape rules are in AGENTS.md "Conversation": summarize helper output, ask for a plain decision in the message, and end a records-changing turn with one plain status line. None of these produce interim narration. The narration is Codex's own habit of posting short commentary before its tool calls. It shows in almost every Codex turn of all three runs (2 to 8 agent_message items per turn) and does not depend on which skill is running.

2) The relay makes it look much worse. relay.py `_codex_reply` collects every `agent_message` item in the turn and joins them with blank lines into one `.out.md`, with the command and MCP calls between them removed. On an interactive Codex host those messages stream one at a time between the tool calls, and the final answer comes last, after the work. So "the answers start halfway down" is mostly an effect of joining them.

3) The worst case is a `codex exec` effect. co2-A reply 1 shows the four scope questions twice. The first copy is not text the agent wrote: rollout 01a14995-3b8a ordinal 46 is a `request_user_input_async` call, ordinal 47 renders it as an AgentMessage, and ordinal 49 auto-returns `{"accepted":true}`. Without anything to answer it, the agent then asked the questions again in its final message. retail-A's rollout has the same single call. No release file mentions a structured question tool.

4) Evidence checked:
- **retail-A-03** matches the finding (human.md pain point 2) and is tagged unclear for the relay reason.
- **The co2-A-06 citation is wrong.** co2-A-06 is the awb-status prose finding. The repetition finding is co2-A-05, and its stated reason ("the relay shows interim messages as an interactive Codex session does") is inaccurate for the reasons in points 2 and 3.
- **taxi-A-36 does not exist.** The current taxi-A findings.json has 28 entries, and taxi-A's human.md section 4 has no complaint about repetition. It records only a self-contradiction between an interim message and the final one in reply 5 (orchestrator item 12).
- **The transcripts do show the overlap.** For example, taxi-A agent-003 has interim "All three files are now available... 6,041,527" and then the final "All three files are now fully loaded... 2,964,624 January", and agent-008 says "all five answered" twice.

What remains for a live user is some overlap between Codex's streamed commentary and its final summary. That is the host model's style, separated in the live UI by the tool activity between messages. It is not a release defect. At most, the release could add a one-line style rule to AGENTS.md as an improvement.
verdicts.release_evidence: No instruction causes it. Shipped awb-init/assets/workbench/AGENTS.md "## Conversation" (lines 26-34) has only these reply-shape rules: "Summarize helper output", "ask in that message for a plain decision", and the one-line end-of-turn status line. Nothing calls for progress narration or a restating summary. grep across all SKILL.md, references, README and workbench-guides finds no progress, narration, preamble, announce or request_user_input instruction. The amplifier is in the harness: kit/relay.py `_codex_reply` (texts.append for every agent_message, then `"\n\n".join(texts)`). The question-tool duplication is in co2-A rollout 01a14995-3b8a ordinals 46-49: a request_user_input_async call rendered as an AgentMessage and auto-answered `{"accepted":true}`.
verdicts.narrowed: On a live interactive host, Codex's streamed progress commentary partly overlaps its final summary. That is native Codex host and model style that the release neither causes nor addresses, so at most it is an optional AGENTS.md style improvement, not a release defect. The doubled blocks and "answers start halfway down" seen in the sims come from the relay joining all interim messages into one block, and from `codex exec` rendering request_user_input_async as text.

consolidated.title: Commit reminders: still repeated in one run, suppressed when needed in another
consolidated.description: co2-B suggested a first commit in A2 and again at release in A5, and volunteered Git status in A1 and A3, against the once-a-session rule. retail-A released 001 with uncommitted producer, query, review-rule and package-format changes. The manifest records them, but the release report said nothing, because a commit had already been suggested that session.
consolidated.caused_by_fix: partly: #102 (issue #86) added the once-a-session guard to the package and release reports, and that guard suppressed retail-A's mention of uncommitted release inputs.
consolidated.evidence: co2-B-25: A1; A2 ('I'd suggest a first commit now'); A3; A5 ('and commit, if you'd like that'); human/notes.md turn 6. retail-A-21: producing_uncommitted_changes and packaging_uncommitted_changes in release 001 manifest.json; provenance_gaps []; awb-release/SKILL.md Report.

verdicts.reasoning:
I looked for a harness cause and found none. The finding as written overstates what happened, so only a narrower version holds.

Harness causes ruled out:
- **Session continuity.** relay.py resumes each role by a fixed id: `claude -p --resume <sid>` for Claude and `codex exec resume <thread>` for Codex. "This session" therefore means the same thing it would in a real interactive chat.
- **Compaction (co2-B).** No compaction event appears in any co2-B agent log. Context grew steadily from 42K to 308K tokens by A5, so the A2 suggestion was still in context.
- **Rule in context.** awb-package was loaded through the Skill tool in A3. Its Report section, which says "Suggest no commit in this report when you already suggested a commit this session", was therefore in context when A5 was written.
- **Prompting.** Neither the appended harness note (a friction log) nor the agent system prompt mentions commits.
- **Persona.** The Codex persona never brought up commits before U6, when it said "No Git commit needed". It simply ignored the A2 suggestion, which a real user could also do.

co2-B:
- **The real violation is A5.** "...copy it to your releases folder, and commit, if you'd like that." This is a second commit suggestion, made in the package report after A2's "I'd suggest a first commit now". A real user with the same skills and model could get it, because the rule is a single clause at the end of a long Report paragraph.
- **A1, A3 and A6 are not violations.** The once-a-session rule limits suggestions, not mentions of Git status.
  - A1 is the init report saying the new repository has no commits yet.
  - A3 is the awb-status report the user asked for ("Nothing is committed to Git"). It correctly holds back the "Commit the current work" suggestion that awb-status line 68 forbids once one has been made.
  - A6 confirms the user's own "no commit" instruction.

retail-A:
- **The silence follows the release's own spec.** The `release` MCP output has no field for producing or packaging uncommitted changes. Its provenance_gaps is [] because the files have recorded checksums. awb-release's Report lists provenance_gaps and checkout_only_acquisitions but never uncommitted changes. So the agent had nothing it was told to report, and the same would happen on any host.
- **The causal claim is partly wrong.** The finding says the report was silent because a commit had already been suggested. The once-a-session cap did shape A5, where the agent's notes say the 23 uncommitted paths "will be disclosed without repeating the prior session commit suggestion". A5 did tell the user "This Q4 revision is uncommitted." The package-format templates, however, were installed in A6, after the last commit, and nothing at release mentioned them. That gap is a product design issue: release reports don't surface uncommitted producing or packaging code, and the cap also forbids a reminder there.
verdicts.release_evidence:
Release text:
- **awb-package/SKILL.md §7 Report:** "Suggest no commit in this report when you already suggested a commit this session."
- **awb-release/SKILL.md Report:** asks for provenance_gaps and checkout_only_acquisitions, and says "Suggest no commit in this report when you already suggested a commit this session." It has no item for producing_uncommitted_changes or packaging_uncommitted_changes.
- **awb-status/SKILL.md line 68:** the "Commit the current work" suggestion is gated by "unless you already suggested a commit this session."
- **AGENTS.md template:** "suggest one at most once a session while it is uncommitted."
- **CHANGELOG line 156:** the once-a-session cap in package and release reports is deliberate.

co2-B transcript:
- A2: "I'd suggest a first commit now."
- A5: "...and I'll freeze it as release 001, copy it to your releases folder, and commit, if you'd like that."

retail-A:
- The `release` tool result in relay/agent-009.jsonl has provenance_gaps [] and no uncommitted fields.
- released/001/manifest.json lists four untracked products-three-customers producer and query files under producing_uncommitted_changes, and six untracked package-format files under packaging_uncommitted_changes.
- The A5 agent-notes entry shows the cap applied deliberately.
- A9 says nothing about uncommitted state.
verdicts.narrowed: co2-B: in one continuous session (no compaction, awb-package's Report rule in context since A3), the A5 package report offered a commit even though A2 had already suggested one. That breaks awb-package's "suggest no commit when already suggested" clause. A1, A3 and A6 are status facts or a confirmation, not suggestions, so they are not violations. retail-A: the awb-release report never tells the user that a release was frozen from uncommitted producing or packaging code. The `release` output doesn't surface those manifest fields, and the Report lists only provenance_gaps, which are empty when checksums were recorded. The once-a-session cap also forbids a commit reminder at that point. As a result, the package-format files installed after the last commit went unmentioned at release 001. The A5 disclosure ("This Q4 revision is uncommitted") came four turns earlier. Severity: minor.

verdicts.reasoning:
The finding joins two separate problems. Only the retail-A one is caused by the release.

co2-B (over-suggesting): the release already forbids this, clearly and in several places. AGENTS.md line 50 says to "suggest one at most once a session while it is uncommitted". The user README (line 105) and the workbench README (line 56) say the same. The awb-package Report (SKILL.md line 96) says "Suggest no commit in this report when you already suggested a commit this session." awb-release line 61, the awb-status table row and the awb-init repair report carry the same guard, and CHANGELOG line 156 states the cap as design. All agent turns ran in one session (efe42f0e for every agent-00N.jsonl). The agent did suggest a commit in A2 ("I'd suggest a first commit now") and offered one again in A5, in an awb-package report ("...and commit, if you'd like that"). The user then said "No Git commit needed." That is one deviation from a clear instruction, not a repeated one. A1 ("new local Git repository (no commits yet)") restates what awb-init step 5 does. A3's "Nothing is committed to Git" is a line of status. Neither suggests a commit, so neither breaks the once-a-session rule. The human notes for turn 6 mention "offers to commit" as noise, which matches A2 and A5. This half is not a product defect.

retail-A (silent at release): the evidence holds up. In released/001/manifest.json, producing_uncommitted_changes lists four untracked files: the Q4 version-B producer and three queries. packaging_uncommitted_changes lists six package-format files. git status also shows foundation/review-rules.md untracked, plus modified products.sql, settings.toml and others. The release copy holds only findings, methodology, charts and the manifest, so those untracked queries are kept only as checksums and nowhere else. The A9 release reply says nothing about uncommitted code. The agent had suggested a commit in A3 of the same Codex thread (01a14995), and the user approved it in A4.

The release causes this silence in three ways:
(a) awb-release SKILL.md Report (line 61) ends "Suggest no commit in this report when you already suggested a commit this session."
(b) The same Report lists nothing about uncommitted producing or packaging changes. The `release` command's output (awb_draft.py around line 5195) doesn't return those fields at all.
(c) provenance_gaps (awb_draft.py line 5023) only counts {"unknown": ...} values, so uncommitted changes never appear as a gap.

The manifest template itself concedes the risk: "a SHA with uncommitted changes does not fully identify the producing code". So any on-request user who commits once early and releases after later changes freezes a release whose producing code exists only in the working tree, and nothing tells them at release.
