So a different agent model with the same release avoided the problem. This one comes from how the model behaved, not from the release.

One related gap stays unaddressed in what shipped. The released findings.md says the Monday average rose 13.3%, with no note that 2024-01-01 and 2024-01-15 (New Year's Day and MLK Day) were January Mondays. My read-only recount with the approved screens gives January Monday daily counts of 75,399, 77,654, 74,705, 82,977 and 82,029. Leaving out the two holidays gives 80,887, so the July rise is about 10.1% rather than 13.3%. The direction holds and the size changes only modestly, so this is at most a minor caveat. It is also an agent lapse, not something the release caused.
verdicts.release_evidence:
A search of all 57 shipped files for holiday, calendar, weekday or confound found no calendar-event guidance. Nothing instructs the agent to skip such checks either.

Release files:
- awb-init/assets/workbench/workbench-guides/analysis.md: the agent read this in taxi-A reply 4 (agent-004.jsonl). It lists mechanical checks, including a period-coverage count for sums, and says "Record a question the analysis raises, such as whether a dip is seasonal". It has no specific calendar or holiday prompt.
- awb-explore/SKILL.md, steps 3–4: asks for candidate explanations and a follow-up query for each one the question turns on. taxi-A never invoked awb-explore.

taxi-A run files:
- queries/q1-volume.sql: adjusts for how many times each weekday occurs in the month, but not for holidays.
- queries/q1-thursday.sql: added only after the user raised July 4.
- agent-002.jsonl: the brief the agent wrote names holidays as uncontrolled.
- released/001/findings.md, line 21: Monday +13.3% with no January holiday note.

taxi-B:
- transcript.md, line 104: the Claude agent raises the January and July holidays at intake, unprompted.
verdicts.narrowed: The release has no prompt to check holidays when comparing average volume per weekday across two periods. In one run (taxi-A, Codex agent), the agent reported a July Thursday decline that July 4 caused, until the user raised it. It also shipped a Monday +13.3% comparison without noting the two January Monday holidays, which shrink the rise to about +10% without changing its direction. This is a guidance gap worth an optional enhancement, such as one line in analysis.md asking whether one-off calendar days drive any per-weekday or per-day comparison. The release is not the cause. The same agent named holidays as uncontrolled in its own brief, and the taxi-B agent on the same release raised them unprompted.

consolidated.title: A near-tie at the top-N cut line is not flagged
consolidated.description: The #10 zone in taxi-A's released January ranking is effectively a tie. Briarwood/Jamaica Hills (371 trips, $93.4973/h) beats LaGuardia Airport (87,625 trips, $93.4970/h) by less than a tenth of a cent, and neither the slide nor its notes say so, though one of the board's decisions concerns airports. Neither the ranking validation nor the review checks for near-ties at the cut.
consolidated.caused_by_fix: no
consolidated.evidence: taxi-A-15: storage/releases/trip-pattern-comparison/board-brief/001/charts/chart-4.csv; referee/spotcheck3.py; brief.md:55 sets only zone-ID tie-breaking.

verdicts.reasoning:
The near-tie is real, and I could not trace it to the harness.

1. I checked the numbers at full precision in taxi-A/project/investigations/trip-pattern-comparison/results/q5-supported.csv. January, scenario "all": Briarwood/Jamaica Hills has 371 trips at 93.4972501290092 $/h and supported_rank 10. LaGuardia Airport has 87,625 trips at 93.4969666113598 $/h and supported_rank 11. The gap is about $0.0003 per hour. Chart-4.csv shows only the top ten, rounded to 93.50, so the board deck cannot reveal the tie.

2. The agent never saw it. I searched the agent relay logs (agent-001 to agent-010, Codex). The agent displayed only the top-ten rows. LaGuardia's rank-11 row and its rate never appear in any output it looked at, so nothing prompted it to notice the cut-line gap.

3. The release has no check that would have caught it.
   - workbench-guides/analysis.md asks only for "a stable total ORDER BY, with tie-breakers". That handles exact ties. It says nothing about closeness at a top-N cut or rank stability.
   - The agent's brief.md:55 ("stable zone-ID tie-breaking") follows that guidance.
   - refinement_validation.py is agent-written. It checks only that ranks are contiguous and that zones meet the support floor.
   - The package review brief (awb-package/references/review.md) is limited by design: narrative traceability, claim strength, revalidation-flag caveats, brief coverage, and a closed list of readability items. It never asks the reviewer to inspect underlying results for fragile cut lines.
   - A grep of the whole release for near-tie, cut line, margin and rank-stability guidance found nothing relevant.

4. Possible harness causes, each ruled out:
   - The ranking data, the release guidance and the review brief are the same on an interactive host.
   - Running codex exec non-interactively does not change whether the agent inspects rank 11.
   - The Codex sandbox, auto-approved MCP tools, the simulated home and the study disclosure have no bearing on a numeric ranking.
   - The persona accepted the 300-trip floor without asking about stability. A real user also sees only the top ten, so a real user would not catch it either.
   - The only factor outside the release is agent diligence. That varies by model and run and would vary the same way for real users.

5. The near-tie itself is a coincidence in this dataset; the gap is that nothing in the release prompts for it. In taxi-B (Claude as agent, months combined) the cut is different. That agent added a generic caveat that zones near the minimum can move in or out of the list, so this kind of caveat depends on the agent and the release does not require it.

6. Impact is limited, so minor severity fits. No slide claims anything that depends on LaGuardia being left out. "Both top tens have nine named Queens zones and Outside NYC" still holds if they swap, since LaGuardia is in Queens. The no-review sensitivity keeps LaGuardia at #11 (93.467), so "membership stable" is literally true. The Limitations slide carries a generic caveat: "The small-sample floor does not establish ranking precision". The finding's airport-relevance framing is somewhat overstated.
verdicts.release_evidence:
- release/analytics-workbench-skills/awb-init/assets/workbench/workbench-guides/analysis.md: the only tie guidance is "Result queries use a stable total ORDER BY, with tie-breakers". Nothing covers near-ties or rank stability at a top-N cut.
- release/analytics-workbench-skills/awb-package/references/review.md, Brief step 3: the review covers narrative consistency, traceability, claim strength, revalidation flags, brief coverage, and readability ("only these"). No step examines result fragility.
- A grep of the release for tie, near-tie, cut, threshold, margin, sensitivity and stability found no ranking-closeness guidance.
- taxi-A/project/investigations/trip-pattern-comparison/results/q5-supported.csv: January Briarwood 93.4972501 (rank 10) vs LaGuardia 93.4969666 (rank 11).
- taxi-A/project/investigations/trip-pattern-comparison/refinement_validation.py:45 checks only that ranks are contiguous.
- Agent relay logs show the agent displayed only the top-ten rows and never saw LaGuardia's rank-11 row.
verdicts.narrowed: The release prompts no near-tie check at a ranking cut line. analysis.md covers only exact ties, through a stable tie-breaker. The package review brief is limited to narrative and traceability checks and never examines result fragility. Whether a cut-line near-tie gets caveated therefore depends on the agent alone. In taxi-A the Codex agent missed one: January #10 Briarwood/Jamaica Hills leads #11 LaGuardia by about $0.0003/h. The released deck shows only the rounded top ten and does not flag it. Impact is minor. No released claim depends on the order of these two zones, the deck carries a generic caveat that ranking precision is not established, and the finding's claim that the tie matters for the airport decision is overstated.

verdicts.reasoning:
The data claim holds. I re-ran referee/spotcheck3.py read-only against the landed parquet. January Briarwood/Jamaica Hills comes out at 93.49725 $/h on 371 trips and LaGuardia Airport at 93.49697 on 87,625 trips, a gap of about $0.0003/h. The agent's own result table, results/q5-supported.csv rows 11-12, already showed this: Briarwood has supported_rank 10 and LaGuardia 11. The released chart-4.csv rounds to 2 decimals, so Briarwood shows as 93.50, which is also what LaGuardia would show. LaGuardia is dropped from the top ten even though the two values look the same at the deck's own precision. The ranking slide, its chart caveat and its notes (findings.md:74-91) never mention LaGuardia or a tie. The only robustness item is a sensitivity check: top-ten membership is unchanged when the 127 review records are removed.

Release causation. Nothing in the shipped files would have prevented this, and some of the guidance points away from catching it:
(1) workbench-guides/analysis.md:17 treats ties only as a determinism problem: "stable total ORDER BY, with tie-breakers". That is where the brief's "stable zone-ID tie-breaking" (brief.md:55) comes from.
(2) analysis.md:15 lays out a fixed validation list: four mechanical checks plus scope, metrics and values judgments. None of them asks for the margin at a ranking cut.
(3) awb-package/SKILL.md:69 recommends cutting a top N with "@first=10", and helpers.md:52 shows that @first just takes the first n rows with no boundary check.
(4) review.md step 3 is a fixed list of narrative checks (consistency, claim strength, verification citations, brief coverage, and a readability list marked "only these"). Ranking robustness or near-ties appear nowhere in it, so the reviewer had no basis to raise this.
I found no instruction about near-ties, fragile rankings or cut-line margins anywhere in the release (grep for tie, robust, fragile, margin, boundary). Nothing here depends on the host or the harness. A real user on a normal interactive host would get the same deck, because nothing in the workflow prompts for this check.

What tempers it: this is a gap in the guidance, not an instruction that actively causes the problem, and it only shows up when the data happens to tie at the cut. No stated claim is wrong because of it. The headline ("every named zone in both top tens is in Queens") still holds if the two zones swap, since LaGuardia is also in Queens. The slide makes no airport claim, and JFK already appears at #6. Severity minor is fair; the impact is close to cosmetic.
verdicts.release_evidence: release/analytics-workbench-skills/awb-init/assets/workbench/workbench-guides/analysis.md:17 ("Result queries use a stable total ORDER BY, with tie-breakers" - determinism only) and :15 (the fixed validation list has no cut-line margin check). awb-package/SKILL.md:69 ("@first=10 for a top ten"), with helpers.md:52 (@first takes the first n rows, no boundary check). awb-package/references/review.md:22-28 (fixed list of narrative checks; nothing on ranking robustness or ties). No near-tie or margin guidance anywhere in the release. Run evidence: taxi-A/project/investigations/trip-pattern-comparison/results/q5-supported.csv rows 11-12 (93.4972501 rank 10 vs 93.4969666 rank 11); taxi-A/storage/releases/trip-pattern-comparison/board-brief/001/charts/chart-4.csv (Briarwood 93.50 at #10); findings.md:74-91 (no tie disclosure). spotcheck3.py re-run reproduces 93.49725 vs 93.49697.
verdicts.narrowed: The shipped validation guidance (analysis.md), the top-N export selection (@first) and the package review checklist (review.md) contain no check for the margin at a ranking cut line. Ties are treated only as a deterministic-ordering issue. As a result, a top-N chart can silently drop an entry that is effectively tied, and indistinguishable at the deck's display precision. In taxi-A, LaGuardia sat #11, $0.0003/h behind #10, and both display as 93.50. No stated claim depended on the cut (the all-Queens headline holds either way), so the effect is a missing disclosure, not a wrong finding.

consolidated.title: Export with --no-datasets and no --chart deletes every chart
consolidated.description: A package export with --no-datasets and no --chart removed all five chart exports and their manifest entries. The call exited 1, the check-draft that followed failed, and a full re-export recovered the charts. SKILL.md says to omit --no-datasets for a provenance-only refresh, so the agent misused the flag, but the helper deletes everything with no guard or dry run.
consolidated.caused_by_fix: no
consolidated.evidence: taxi-A-18: agent-007 log (2 failed awb/package calls; 'ls .../draft/charts' failed with No such file or directory); awb-package/SKILL.md:72.

verdicts.reasoning:
The log supports the facts. In taxi-A agent-007 (Codex), call #2 to awb/package was `export trip-pattern-comparison board-brief --result` for all nine results plus `--no-datasets`, with no `--chart`. The helper returned `charts: []`, `export_checks.results: 0`, and five check_charts rows saying "no chart file for this specification", with exit status 1. check-draft then failed with the same five chart rows, plus unrelated numbers and claims rows. `ls draft/charts` failed with No such file or directory. A later full export with all five `--chart` flags restored the charts, and check-draft passed.

The code in awb-package/assets/awb_draft.py does exactly this. In export(), `full = bool(charts or datasets or no_datasets)`, and write_charts() with an empty list unlinks every chart-N.csv and removes the empty directory. The manifest then gets `record["charts"] = "none"`. The CLI has a guard in one direction only: `--chart` without `--dataset` or `--no-datasets` is refused. `--no-datasets` without `--chart` is accepted even when findings.md has Chart N specs. The helper detects that mismatch only after writing, through check_charts.

I could not tie the trigger to the harness:
(a) Auto-approved MCP tools: setup.sh sets `default_tools_approval_mode = "approve"`. An interactive approval prompt would have shown the same arguments, and a user would have had no reason to refuse them, so it would not have stopped the call.
(b) Sandbox, simulated home, relay, persona and study disclosure: none of these touches flag choice. The human turn only asked for wording fixes and a full draft.
(c) Context loss: no compaction occurred in the turn. The agent had read `help export` earlier in the same turn. That help says "Any --chart, --dataset, or --no-datasets replaces the whole chart set ... no --chart records charts none".
(d) The MCP server, awb-init/assets/awb_mcp.py, ships with the release and is registered the way the README says, so the tool path is the product path.

The agent ignored documented behavior (SKILL.md:72, the CLI epilog, and CHANGELOG line 198). The same mistake could happen on any interactive host. Across all six runs it happened in 1 of 26 export calls; the others used `--result` alone correctly.

The release's part is a missing pre-write guard, plus a flag named for datasets that also replaces the chart set. The deletion itself is not a bug: it is the documented, deterministic behavior. Impact is low. Chart CSVs are regenerated from saved results, the helper signals the problem loudly (exit 1 and check_charts rows), and one full re-export fixes it. The one real loss is the manifest's per-chart shaping specs, which must be rebuilt from findings.md and the pasted methodology_lines. This is a minor hardening issue, not a defect in what the helper is documented to do.
verdicts.release_evidence: awb-package/assets/awb_draft.py: export() sets `full = bool(charts or datasets or no_datasets)`. With no charts, write_charts() unlinks every chart-N.csv and rmdirs charts/, and `record["charts"] = ... or "none"`. cli_export refuses only `args.chart and not (args.dataset or args.no_datasets)`, with no reverse guard. check_charts runs only after the write. The CLI epilog documents the behavior: "Any --chart, --dataset, or --no-datasets replaces the whole chart set and dataset selection: no --chart records charts none." awb-package/SKILL.md:72 says to omit `--chart`, `--dataset`, and `--no-datasets` for a caveat-only revision. CHANGELOG.md:198 shows the trap was known and handled with documentation rather than a guard. The awb MCP server (awb-init/assets/awb_mcp.py) ships with the release. Run evidence: taxi-A/relay/agent-007.jsonl, package call #2 (exit 1, five check_charts rows), check-draft #3 failed, `ls` of draft/charts returned No such file or directory, and call #4 (full export) restored the charts. The same turn earlier read `help export`, which includes the warning.
verdicts.narrowed: The agent misused the documented flags, against SKILL.md:72 and the help text it had read in the same turn. When that happens, `export --no-datasets` with no `--chart` replaces the chart set with none. The five regenerable chart CSVs are deleted and their manifest specs are set to "none". This happens even though findings.md still has Chart N specifications. The helper detects the mismatch only after writing (check_charts, exit 1) and has no pre-write refusal or dry run. A flag named for datasets silently governs charts too. One full re-export recovers everything. This is a minor guard and naming gap on documented behavior. The helper itself does not malfunction, and the harness did not cause it.

verdicts.reasoning:
The run evidence is accurate. In taxi-A agent-007, after a narrative edit (finish_board_metadata.py), the agent called awb/package export with nine --result flags plus --no-datasets and no --chart. The result was charts: [], written: true, check_charts listing Chart 1-5 as "no chart file for this specification", and exit status 1. The check-draft that followed failed with the same five chart rows, and `ls .../draft/charts` returned No such file or directory. One full re-export with all five --chart specs restored everything and check-draft then passed.

The release documents this behavior and tells the agent not to do it:
- awb-package/SKILL.md:72 (step 4.4) says a caveat-only revision passes only --result and must "omit --chart, --dataset, and --no-datasets". It also says a charts row asking to rerun export needs the full export with every --chart.
- references/package-contract.md:71 says only a --result-only call leaves exported files untouched.
- The export CLI help text says: "Any --chart, --dataset, or --no-datasets replaces the whole chart set and dataset selection: no --chart records charts none. With only --result it records provenance and leaves exported files untouched."
- CHANGELOG.md:198 says the same.

The agent pulled `help export` over MCP earlier in the same turn, and the transcript shows that exact help text in the result, so it had the rule in front of it and broke it anyway.

The helper behaves as specified, in export() in awb_draft.py:
- `full = bool(charts or datasets or no_datasets)`
- write_charts with an empty list removes the chart files.

The helper also flags the result straight away: exit 1 plus check_charts naming every missing chart file. Nothing irreplaceable was lost. Chart CSVs and the manifest's charts entries are rebuilt from recorded results, and the other manifest fields (results, export_checks, flags, slugs) were kept.

The misuse happened once. In every other run, agents that did a provenance-only export used --result alone and got completed results: co2-A agent-006, retail-A agent-007 and agent-008, and retail-B agent-005. That suggests the instruction works in practice. The flag name --no-datasets does not hint that it also clears charts, but the help line beside it and SKILL.md say so outright. This was an agent error against a clear instruction, not something the release causes.
verdicts.release_evidence:
- release/analytics-workbench-skills/awb-package/SKILL.md:72: "For a revision that only adds caveats and keeps the exported files, pass only `--result`, once for every represented result; omit `--chart`, `--dataset`, and `--no-datasets`."
- awb-package/references/package-contract.md:71: "a call with only `--result` refreshes provenance and leaves exported files untouched".
- awb-package/assets/awb_draft.py, export(), from line 3762:
  - the docstring says "Any chart, dataset, or no_datasets makes a full export that replaces the chart set"
  - the code sets `full = bool(charts or datasets or no_datasets)`
- awb_draft.py write_charts(), line 2296: "none removes them".
- awb_draft.py cli_export help text, line 3946: "Any --chart, --dataset, or --no-datasets replaces the whole chart set and dataset selection: no --chart records charts none."
- awb_draft.py line 4048: exits 1 when check_charts is non-empty.
- CHANGELOG.md:198 says the same.
- taxi-A/relay/agent-007.jsonl:
  - an earlier awb/read help topic=export call returned that help text
  - the failed export args were "--result x9 --no-datasets" with no --chart
  - the result showed check_charts with five "no chart file" rows and "exit status 1"
  - a later full export with five --chart specs recovered
- Correct --result-only exports, all completed: co2-A agent-006, retail-A agent-007 and agent-008, retail-B agent-005.
verdicts.narrowed: Optional hardening only, not a release-caused defect. export already works out check_charts against findings.md after it writes. It could do that check before writing and refuse --no-datasets (or --dataset) without --chart while findings.md still has Chart N specifications. Today it deletes the regenerable chart files first and then reports exit 1. In this run the cost was one failed call, recovered by a single full re-export.

consolidated.title: Answered child questions stay open until linked by hand
consolidated.description: Analytical child questions created at scoping stayed 'open' after recorded results and their caveats had answered them. Before packaging, the agent linked results by hand to close Q-006, Q-007 and Q-010.
consolidated.caused_by_fix: no
consolidated.evidence: taxi-A-25: reply 6 turn; agent-notes line 68; agent.md section 2.

verdicts.reasoning:
The evidence matches the logs. In turn 2 (awb-scope), the Codex agent added Q-006 to Q-010 as must or should data questions under the user's roots. In turn 4 it read `questions --all` and declared `answers` for Q-008 and Q-009, but not for Q-006, Q-007 or Q-010. Turn 5 never mentions those three. In turn 6, after loading awb-package and the package contract, it edited the `answers` lists in settings.toml and ran `questions answer Q-006 --result q2-airports`, `Q-007 --result q3-standard` and `Q-010 --result q1-volume`. Its history and notes say the purpose was to keep these questions off the "Open questions" slide.

I looked for a harness cause and found none:
- Relay turns resume the same Codex thread (relay.py lines 141-150), so the agent did not lose context between turns.
- No sandbox failure, auto-approval, relay truncation or simulated-home issue touched this path.
- The study disclosure has no bearing on question linking.
- Persona front-loading shortened the interview. But Q-006 and Q-007 came from ordinary scoping answers in message 2 ("evidence gaps... worth flagging", "assess what the records can and can't support"), which a real user could easily give.

The release creates this situation:
- awb-scope says every material unknown left open becomes an open ledger question with its answerer, and that "a data question is answered only by a recorded result whose settings table declares it".
- The helper refuses a text answer for a data question (awb_provenance.py lines 2220-2221).
- Nothing in analysis.md asks the agent to go back over open child questions as results and caveats pile up.
- package-contract.md adds an Open questions slide whenever any unanswered must question exists.

So a question about limits, such as "what evidence is missing" or "which tipping claims are supportable", which caveats answer rather than a computed table, has no clean way to close. It stays open until packaging brings it up. Then the agent has to link a loosely related result; for example, it linked Q-010, a schema and join-key validation question, to q1-volume.

The finding's framing is overstated in two places:
1. Explicit linking through `answers` or `questions answer --result` is the release's intended design. Nothing ever closes a question automatically, so "linked by hand" alone is not a defect.
2. The problem depends on how the agent words its scoping questions. In co2-A and retail-A the Codex agents built dedicated audit results (entity-audit, coverage, intake-validation, revenue-reconciliation) for similar foundation child questions and linked them without trouble. A real Codex user on an interactive host could still hit this with the same release, so the verdict is product, minor, with the narrower scope below.
verdicts.release_evidence:
- **awb-scope/SKILL.md**, section 2: "every other material unknown is an open ledger question with its answerer". Section 3: "A data question is answered only by a recorded result whose settings table declares it."
- **awb-init/assets/awb_provenance.py:2220-2221**: `questions answer` raises "is a data question; only a recorded result answers it (--result)" when given --text.
- **awb-init/assets/workbench/workbench-guides/analysis.md:19**: linking is done explicitly through `answers` or `awb.py questions answer Q-NNN --result <id>`. There is no instruction to revisit open child questions.
- **awb-package/references/package-contract.md:38**: the Open questions slide is included "if and only if unanswered `must` questions... exist".
- **Run logs**:
  - taxi-A/relay/agent-002: Q-006 to Q-010 added at scope.
  - agent-004: after reading the question list, the agent linked only Q-008 and Q-009.
  - agent-006: settings `answers` edits plus `questions answer` for Q-006, Q-007 and Q-010 during awb-package.
- **Agent's own account**: taxi-A/feedback/agent-notes.md line 68 and agent.md section 2 ("Question linkage and scopes").
verdicts.narrowed: At scoping, the agent recorded questions about limits ("what evidence is missing", "which claims are supportable", "do schemas and joins support the grouping") as must data questions. The release closes a data question only by linking a recorded result; it refuses a text answer for data questions and has no "answered by caveats / not observable from these records" route. Nothing between analysis and packaging prompts a sweep of open child questions. As a result, three such questions in taxi-A stayed open until awb-package's Open-questions rule surfaced them. The agent then retro-linked loosely matching results (Q-010 to q1-volume, Q-006 to q2-airports, Q-007 to q3-standard). Explicit linking itself is intended behavior. The real friction is the missing route for answers that come from caveats, and the late surfacing. The problem depends on how the agent words its scoping questions; it did not occur in co2-A or retail-A.

verdicts.reasoning:
The run evidence matches the facts. Q-006, Q-007 and Q-010 were created as must-priority data children at scoping (agent-002). In the reply-6 turn (relay/agent-006.jsonl) the agent added them to the `answers` lists in settings.toml and called `questions answer Q-006 --result q2-airports`, `Q-007 --result q3-standard` and `Q-010 --result q1-volume`. agent-notes line 68 and agent.md section 2 describe this. What the evidence does not show is a release defect. Requiring an explicit link is the release's design, and the release tells the agent how to do it at the right time:
- workbench-guides/analysis.md, "Add a result": a result's settings table holds `answers = ["Q-NNN"]` "when it answers ledger data questions". The same section adds that `awb.py questions answer Q-NNN --result <id>` links one already recorded.
- The settings.toml template comment, the run.py docstring, the ledger header and the `questions` help all repeat this.
- awb-scope says: "A data question is answered only by a recorded result whose settings table declares it; workbench-guides/analysis.md says how."

The agent clearly understood the mechanism. It declared children at result time for Q-008, Q-009, Q-012, Q-013, Q-014 and Q-015, and in turn 5 it linked Q-009 and Q-012 through `questions answer --result`. Q-006, Q-007 and Q-010 stayed open because the agent decided at the time that no result answered them. These are limitation-type questions ("what evidence is missing", "which claims remain unsupported", "do schemas support the grouping"). The agent later decided the results' caveats and validation covered them. That is the agent's judgment, not a step the release skipped.

The release then caught the open questions as designed. package-contract.md "Ledger storyline" puts every unanswered `must` question on the Open questions slide, and that is exactly what prompted the agent to settle them before packaging ("removed artificial Open questions membership"). The fix took four MCP calls and one settings edit. Nothing reached the user: replies 4 to 6 report only root-question status, and the scoped review and check-draft later passed with zero open questions. Automatically closing a question because a caveat seems to cover it would be wrong, so "stays open until linked" is intended behaviour, not a bug.
verdicts.release_evidence:
Places where the release tells the agent to link, or catches unlinked questions:
- awb-init/assets/workbench/workbench-guides/analysis.md, "Add a result": "`answers = [\"Q-NNN\"]` when it answers ledger data questions". The same section: "`awb.py questions answer Q-NNN --result <id>` links one already recorded."
- awb-init/assets/workbench/investigation/settings.toml, template comment: "answers = [\"Q-004\"]  # optional: ledger data questions this result answers; run.py marks them answered."
- awb-init/assets/workbench/investigation/run.py docstring: the same rule.
- awb-init/assets/awb_provenance.py: _LEDGER_HEADER and the `questions` help say "A data question is answered only by a recorded result: its settings table declares answers ...".
- awb-scope/SKILL.md section 3: "A data question is answered only by a recorded result whose settings table declares it."
- awb-package/references/package-contract.md, "Ledger storyline": the Open questions slide is included "if and only if unanswered `must` questions ... exist". This is the check that brought these three questions up before packaging.

Run evidence:
- taxi-A project questions.json: Q-006, Q-007 and Q-010 have origin scope and priority must.
- settings.toml: answers were declared at result time for Q-008, Q-009, Q-012, Q-013, Q-014 and Q-015. Q-006, Q-007 and Q-010 were added later.
- relay/agent-006.jsonl: the `questions answer` calls for Q-006, Q-007 and Q-010.
- agent-notes.md line 68.
verdicts.narrowed: At most a guidance gap. Nothing in awb-scope or analysis.md shows how to close a scope-created data question whose answer is a limitation, for example "what evidence is missing" or "which claims cannot be supported". Such an answer lives in a result's caveats rather than in a computed figure, so the agent may not declare `answers` when it records the result. The question then stays open until the package's Open questions rule forces a decision. This is a minor documentation improvement, and nothing reached the user. The release did not fail to give the instruction, and it did not cause the omission.

consolidated.title: Rerunning a result only to record a check demotes a supported finding
consolidated.description: taxi-B reran a result only to add a check to a judgment's detail text, with the table unchanged. That demoted a user-approved supported finding to provisional, because the checks are part of the finding's baseline. The agent had to promote it again, and a history entry was written.
consolidated.caused_by_fix: no
consolidated.evidence: taxi-B-08: record_finding in awb-init/assets/awb_provenance.py; reply 6; commits 01b0aa8 and 188dfc2.

verdicts.reasoning:
The demotion comes from deterministic release code, not from how the simulation was run. In taxi-B agent turn 6 (relay/agent-006.jsonl), the persona asked for base fare to be described as "the recorded fare, including flat fares". The scoped review followed the release's awb-package/references/review.md, whose line 27 says a sentence about how a source builds a series must rest on a `reference:` or a recorded check. The review flagged findings.md:36 as unsupported (review-reports/agent-006-record01.txt). The agent edited the `metrics` judgment's detail in settings.toml (commit 01b0aa8) and reran airport-fares-durations through the awb MCP `run` tool. The run returned state "refreshed", status "provisional", history true, and the table was unchanged. Commit 188dfc2 shows that the only evidence changes were the metrics detail, the timestamps and the settings hash. It also shows the history entry "rerun: supported → provisional" followed by the agent's own "promoted to supported" entry.

The release code explains this exactly. `_baseline()` compares the table sha256, the full checks list including detail text, and the scoped settings. `record_finding()` keeps a row only when all three match. Any other rerun sets status to provisional and writes a history entry if the row was supported. The CHANGELOG and awb-init/references/provenance.md document this behavior. Judgments live in settings.toml and only reach the evidence through a run, so the release offers no way to add a check to an approved result without rerunning it, and that rerun always demotes.

Harness factors I tested, none of which caused it:
- Non-interactive `claude -p`: the code path is identical on an interactive host. If anything, a real host would make re-promotion costlier, because the state template asks for the user's approval again.
- Auto-approved MCP tools: they only made the agent's self-re-promotion frictionless. They did not cause the demotion.
- Simulated home, relay, and the study disclosure: not involved.
- Codex sandbox: not involved, since the agent role was Claude.
- Persona front-loading: the "flat fares" request is an ordinary edit for a domain user. The persona brief only gives background (RatecodeID 2 is the JFK flat fare).

The one real harness contributor is weak. The agent's system prompt allows only URLs the user gives, and agent-notes.md says it could not fetch the TLC fare page. A `reference:` might otherwise have satisfied the reviewer without a rerun. But the TLC dictionary the project retained defines fare_amount as the meter's time-and-distance fare, and a fare-page citation would not establish that fare_amount stores the $70. A recorded check is the natural route either way. The general trigger, adding a check after approval because the review demands checks for "exactly"/"checked" wording, is also routine in this release.

There is also a doc/code mismatch. The state template (awb-init/assets/workbench/investigation/state.md line 10) says "A rerun that changes a supported finding's result returns it to provisional". The code also demotes when only a check's detail text changes and the table is identical.

Caveats on the finding as written:
- Its evidence ID is wrong. The matching findings.json entry is taxi-B-05; taxi-B-08 is about threshold timing.
- "Only to add a check" understates the edit. The agent also reworded the judgment's definition text from "meter's time-and-distance fare" to "fare recorded for the trip, flat fares included". The checks changed in meaning, not only by an appended sentence.
- The demotion is intended, conservative behavior. This is design friction, not a malfunction, so "minor" fits.
verdicts.release_evidence:
- awb-init/assets/awb_provenance.py:1485-1487: `_baseline()` compares the table sha256, the full checks list including detail text, and the scoped settings.
- awb_provenance.py:1568-1581 (`record_finding`): a row is kept only when the baseline matches exactly. Otherwise status becomes provisional and a history entry is written if the row was supported.
- CHANGELOG.md:252 and awb-init/references/provenance.md:7 document that any rerun whose checks differ makes the row provisional.
- awb-init/assets/workbench/investigation/state.md:10 says a rerun "that changes a supported finding's result" returns it to provisional, to be re-promoted after the user approves. This is narrower than the code.
- awb-package/references/review.md:27 requires a reference or recorded check for how-a-source-builds-a-series wording.
- Sim evidence: taxi-B relay/agent-006.jsonl (the run returned status "provisional" with history true, followed by `records state finding --status supported`), review-reports/agent-006-record01.txt, project commits 01b0aa8 (settings.toml metrics detail) and 188dfc2 (evidence detail change plus the history entries "rerun: supported → provisional" and "promoted to supported").
verdicts.narrowed: When a result already approved as supported is rerun so that a check can be recorded, the release demotes it to provisional, and the agent or user must promote it again. Judgments live in settings.toml and reach the evidence only through run.py. The rerun baseline includes every check's detail text, so any judgment-text edit demotes the finding even when the table is byte-identical. In taxi-B the edit also reworded the judgment's definition, not only appended a check. The state template says a rerun demotes only when it "changes a supported finding's result", which does not match the code. This is intended conservative behavior that causes minor friction, not a malfunction. The correct findings.json ID is taxi-B-05, not taxi-B-08.

verdicts.reasoning:
The run evidence checks out. In turn 6 the user asked for base fare to be described as including flat fares. The reviewer (review-reports/agent-006-record01.txt, lines 2-4) then rejected the flat-fare sentence because no recorded check backed it. Commit 01b0aa8 changes one line, the `metrics` judgment's `detail` in settings.toml. The agent reran only airport-fares-durations through mcp__awb__run, which returned "state": "refreshed", "status": "provisional", "history": true. The agent then called `state finding --status supported` with the reason "Rerun only recorded the flat-fare check... table and finding text unchanged". Commit 188dfc2 shows that the evidence diff changes only recorded_at, producing_commit, the settings sha and the detail text. The table checksum is unchanged. history.md gained two entries: "rerun: supported → provisional" and "promoted to supported".

The release causes this directly. In the shipped awb_provenance.py, `_baseline()` (line 1485) is the table sha256 plus the full checks list plus the scoped settings. `record_finding()` (lines 1568-1581) keeps a row only on an exact match. Any other rerun sets the row to provisional and writes a history entry for a row that was supported. Because the judgment detail sits in both the checks and the settings content, a detail-only edit always fails the match.

The release also tells the agent to take exactly this path. The only documented way to record a check is in workbench-guides/analysis.md line 19 and in awb-init/references/provenance.md: "state the check ... in the detail of a passing `values` or `metrics` judgment ... and rerun". The documented order makes the collision normal. Findings are promoted at the headline preview, before the draft. The review in awb-package/references/review.md lines 26-27 comes later and demands recorded checks for "how a source builds a series" and "checked/verified" wording. So checks the review asks for usually arrive after promotion, and recording them demotes the finding.

The template is also inconsistent with the code. The state.md template (line 10) says only "A rerun that changes a supported finding's result returns it to provisional". Here the result did not change, yet the finding was demoted.

The agent did not ignore any instruction. It followed the documented path. A real user on an interactive host would hit this whenever a review asks for a check on a finding that is already supported. Minor severity fits: the cost is an extra promotion call and two noise entries in history. Under a strict reading of the template, it could also cost a round-trip to get the user's approval again.
verdicts.release_evidence:
- awb-init/assets/awb_provenance.py lines 1485-1487: `_baseline` returns {table sha256, full checks list, scoped settings}.
- awb-init/assets/awb_provenance.py lines 1568-1581: rows are kept only when the baseline matches exactly. Otherwise status becomes provisional and history gets `_rerun_entry` when the old status was supported.
- workbench-guides/analysis.md line 19: "a rerun with unchanged table, checks, and settings keeps its row; any other makes it provisional". The same line gives the way to record a check: "state the check ... in the detail of a passing values or metrics judgment ... and rerun".
- awb-init/references/provenance.md: the same instruction to record a check and rerun, and the same refresh semantics.
- CHANGELOG.md line 252: the same design.
- awb-init/assets/workbench/investigation/state.md line 10: says only "A rerun that changes a supported finding's result returns it to provisional", which understates the trigger.
- awb-package/references/review.md lines 26-27: the review requires a recorded check for sentences on how a source builds a series.
- Run evidence: taxi-B/relay/agent-006.jsonl (run result "state": "refreshed", "status": "provisional"); commits 01b0aa8 and 188dfc2. Note: the findings.json entry for this issue is taxi-B-05, not taxi-B-08. taxi-B-08 is the pre-landing inspection finding.
verdicts.narrowed: The demotion is designed and documented behaviour: any change to checks, including judgment detail text alone, makes a rerun non-exact. The defect is the interaction. The release's only documented way to record a check (edit a judgment's detail and rerun) always demotes a supported finding, even when the table is identical. The documented order (promote at headline preview, then a review that asks for recorded checks) makes that sequence routine. The state.md template says demotion follows a rerun that "changes a supported finding's result", which understates it. The cost is one re-promotion and two history entries. No numbers or data are harmed.

consolidated.title: Priority set by the agent decides which questions reach the main deck
consolidated.description: taxi-B gave Q1 and Q5 priority 'should' without asking, as awb-scope directs. It then cited 'your two should questions' as the reason to move them to the appendix, since the package contract sorts finding slides by priority.
consolidated.caused_by_fix: no. #103's --show flag took the Open questions slide off priority, but deck order still follows it.
consolidated.evidence: taxi-B-14: Q-001 and Q-005 in questions.md; reply 4; human/notes.md turn 5; awb-scope/SKILL.md; package-contract.md.

verdicts.reasoning:
None of the harness explanations hold up.

(1) The agent set the priorities because the release told it to. The installed awb-scope and awb-package skills are byte-identical to the release (diff -rq). The agent loaded awb-scope in agent turn 1. awb-scope says "Give each recorded question a priority and parent: must when the decision cannot be made without its answer ... should otherwise" and "Write the records without a separate confirmation round." Neither the skill's Report step nor the README mentions priorities. The user is never shown or asked about them, on any host. In agent-002.jsonl the agent records Q-001 and Q-005 with --priority should and Q-002/3/4 with must. That follows the rule exactly, given the two board decisions (airport study, tipping position).

(2) Persona front-loading changes nothing. The decisions are part of the persona's situation, and awb-scope's interview asks for "the decision it supports" anyway. The 8-slide length is something a real user would give, and awb-package collects it.

(3) The non-interactive relay did not stop the agent from asking. It asked several rounds of decisions; it skipped priorities only because the skill says not to ask. The agent system prompt says nothing about priorities and only discloses the study.

(4) Auto-approved MCP, the sandbox and the simulated home play no part.

(5) Packaging: the agent read package-contract.md (agent-004), which orders finding slides by ledger priority. awb-package tells it to "Propose the ledger-derived finding order" and to propose which slides move to the appendix when the main slides run past the agreed length. With 8 slides and 4 required ones, the agent proposed moving "your two 'should' questions, volumes (Q1) and top zones (Q5)." That pins on the user a ranking the agent made silently. The user objected to the label in notes.md turn 5 ("Calls volumes and rankings my two 'should' questions, although both are explicit descriptive questions").

The headline "decides which questions reach the main deck" goes too far. agent-004 asked the user to approve the appendix move and offered an alternative. human-005 accepted it ("Keep volumes and the zone ranking in the appendix"), and human.md calls it "an acceptable tradeoff." The release also never says to pick appendix slides by priority; that step was the agent's choice, guided by the priority-sorted ledger order. The words "your 'should' questions" are the agent's own, but they rest on a ledger field the release makes it fill silently and that the package then sorts by.
verdicts.release_evidence: awb-scope/SKILL.md section 2: "Give each recorded question a priority and parent: `must` when the decision cannot be made without its answer, `could` when the answer only refines it, `should` otherwise", plus "Write the records without a separate confirmation round." The skill's Report step does not mention priorities. awb-package/references/package-contract.md line 34 sorts finding slides by priority (must, should, could), main sequence and appendix alike. awb-package/SKILL.md line 54: "Propose the ledger-derived finding order" and "proposing which move to the appendix when the main slides exceed it." The README never mentions priorities. The installed copies in taxi-B/agent-home/.agents/skills match the release. agent-002.jsonl: questions add for Q-001 and Q-005 with --priority should. agent-004.out.md: "I propose moving your two 'should' questions, volumes (Q1) and top zones (Q5), to the appendix", followed by an approve-or-alternative decision. human-005.out.md accepts the move. human/notes.md turn 5 disputes the label.
verdicts.narrowed: awb-scope has the agent set must/should/could priorities without asking, and the README never mentions them. The package's ledger-derived slide order then sorts by those priorities. So when an agreed slide length forces appendix moves, the agent's default proposal moves the user's lower-priority questions, here Q1 and Q5, and justifies it with a label the user never set ("your two 'should' questions"). The user still approves at the headline checkpoint and did accept the move. Priority shapes the default proposal and how it is explained; it does not decide main-deck membership on its own.

verdicts.reasoning:
The release causes the mechanism; the finding overstates its effect.

How the release produces it:
- awb-scope/SKILL.md, step 2, has the agent give each question a priority itself: `must` when the decision cannot be made without the answer, `could` when it only refines it, `should` otherwise. The same step ends "Write the records without a separate confirmation round."
- Nothing tells the agent to confirm priority with the user or show it to them. The step 4 report lists settled items, records and open questions by answerer, but not priority. README.md never mentions question priority.
- package-contract.md, "Ledger storyline", sorts siblings and finding slides by priority (must, should, could). awb-package/SKILL.md tells the agent to "Propose the ledger-derived finding order" and to propose which slides go to the appendix when the main deck exceeds the recorded length. The lowest-priority finding slides fall at the end of the order, so they are the natural ones to move.

What the run shows:
- In agent-001.jsonl the agent recorded Q-001 (volumes) and Q-005 (top zones) with `--priority should` and the others as `must`. No reply before reply 4 mentions priority (grep of agent-001 to 003 .out.md).
- The two board decisions are the airport study and a tipping position. Neither needs Q1 or Q5, so the agent applied the scope rule faithfully. This is not agent error.
- In reply 4 (agent-004.out.md), with 8 main slides and 4 required slides, it proposed "moving your two 'should' questions, volumes (Q1) and top zones (Q5), to the appendix". That was the first time the user saw the label.
- human/notes.md turn 5 records the friction: "Calls volumes and rankings my two 'should' questions, although both are explicit descriptive questions."

Why "decides" is too strong:
- The agent asked the user directly ("is moving weekday volumes and top zones to the appendix acceptable?") and offered an alternative: keep both in the main deck and move How we know and Limitations to the appendix.
- The user approved the move in human-005.out.md.
- So priority sets the default proposal and its stated reason. The user still made the call at the headline checkpoint.
- Using the bare word "should" in chat also slips past AGENTS.md line 28 ("chat uses plain words"). That rule does not name priority, though, and the underlying behaviour comes from the skills.

Impact: a real user on a normal host would hit this whenever the deck has a length cap and some of their own questions don't bear on the decision. Severity minor.
verdicts.release_evidence:
- awb-scope/SKILL.md, step 2, "Give each recorded question a priority and parent": `must` / `could` / `should otherwise`. It is set by the agent; the step closes with "Write the records without a separate confirmation round."
- awb-scope/SKILL.md, step 4 Report: priority is not among the items reported.
- README.md: no mention of question priority.
- awb-package/references/package-contract.md, "Ledger storyline": "sorting siblings by priority in that order ... Order finding slides by that selected question's priority". This ledger-derived order is the default the headline checkpoint proposes.
- awb-package/SKILL.md, "The headline checkpoint": "Report the main slides ... against any recorded length, proposing which move to the appendix when the main slides exceed it. Propose the ledger-derived finding order".
- awb-init/assets/workbench/AGENTS.md line 28 ("chat uses plain words") does not name priority.
- Run evidence:
  - agent-001.jsonl: questions add for Q-001 and Q-005 with `--priority should`.
  - questions.md: Q-001 and Q-005 have Priority should.
  - agent-004.out.md: "moving your two 'should' questions ... to the appendix", with the alternative offered.
  - human-005.out.md: the user approves the move.
  - human/notes.md turn 5: friction over the label.
verdicts.narrowed: awb-scope has the agent assign question priority silently: no confirmation round, it is not in the scope report, and the README never mentions it. awb-package's ledger storyline orders finding slides by that priority. So when the deck exceeds the agreed length, the agent's default appendix proposal is the user's own lower-priority questions, explained with an internal label ("your two 'should' questions") the user never set or saw. The user still decides at the headline checkpoint. In taxi-B the agent asked directly, offered an alternative, and the user approved the move. Priority sets the default proposal and its stated reason, not the outcome.

consolidated.title: state.md goes stale after a release
consolidated.description: After release, taxi-B's state.md still listed 'Preview the slide headlines with Dana before drafting the package' as the next step. It also kept 'JFK trips mostly pay the $70 median fare', wording the reviewer had removed from the deck. Neither awb-release nor awb-status refreshes or flags state after a release.
consolidated.caused_by_fix: no. #97 added rewording a corrected finding with state finding --text; next steps and the release step are not covered.
consolidated.evidence: taxi-B-21: state.md lines 13 and 37; awb-release/SKILL.md has no step to refresh state.

verdicts.reasoning:
I tried to pin this on the harness and couldn't.

What the evidence shows:
- taxi-B's state.md (Last updated 07:58:01 EDT, i.e. 11:58Z) was last rendered during agent turn 6. The release ran in turn 7 (11:59:54 to 12:00:21Z) and changed nothing in state.md. Its Next steps still say "Preview the slide headlines with Dana before drafting the package".
- relay/agent-003.jsonl shows the agent added that step with `state next`. In turn 4 it dropped only item 1. Dana approved the headlines in message 5 and the agent drafted in turn 5, so the step was already stale from turn 5. It was stale inside awb-package, before the release, not because of it.

The release skills have no step for this:
- awb-release/SKILL.md has no step to update state.md or its Next steps.
- awb-package/SKILL.md never mentions Next steps. The only skill that does is awb-explore.
- AGENTS.md only says how to change next steps (`state next`), not when.
- awb-status reports `next_steps` verbatim. Its `git.state_status` check (collect_status.py) only looks at files under investigations/<slug>/. A release writes under deliveries/, so status would still call the state current and show the stale step. awb-status was not actually run after the release here; this part is inferred from the skill text and code.

Harness candidates I checked and rejected:
- The agent system prompt and the harness note only add a friction log. Nothing discourages record maintenance.
- claude -p resume per turn, auto-approved MCP and the simulated home don't affect whether the agent runs `state next`.
- The persona asked for the release in one message, which a real user could do.
- The run ended right after the release, but a real user stopping there sees the same file.
- Across runs, the Codex-agent runs taxi-A and co2-A did rewrite Next steps after release. The Claude agent in taxi-B didn't. That is model variance, not harness: a real user running either agent depends on the skills to prompt this, and they don't.

The JFK half of the finding has the wrong cause:
- awb-package/SKILL.md line 65 already says: "When a review or the user corrects a claim a finding's text states, also reword that finding with `python3 src/awb.py state finding <id> --text ...` in the same revision."
- The turn-5 review (review-reports/agent-005-record01.txt) flagged "JFK trips mostly show the flat fare". The agent took it out of the deck but never reworded the finding.
- In turn 6 it re-promoted airport-fares-durations with the reason "table and finding text unchanged". The check it added only covers To JFK (p25 = p75 = $70). From JFK has p25 = $52, so "mostly pay the $70 ... in either direction" is still unsupported.
- So this part comes from the agent not following an existing awb-package instruction during packaging. It is not something missing from awb-release or awb-status, and it is not specific to after a release.
verdicts.release_evidence:
- awb-release/SKILL.md (lines 1-63): steps 1-5 and Report never mention state.md or Next steps.
- awb-package/SKILL.md: never mentions Next steps. Line 52 promotes findings at the headline checkpoint. Line 65 requires rewording a finding's text when a review corrects it; the agent didn't follow this.
- AGENTS.md line 48 says how to change next steps (`state next`) but sets no trigger.
- awb-status/SKILL.md lines 30 and 70: reports `next_steps` verbatim.
- awb-status/scripts/collect_status.py `git_status`: the state-date check only covers investigations/<slug>/, so a release under deliveries/ never makes state "out of date".
- taxi-B/relay/agent-003.jsonl and agent-004.jsonl: the `state next` calls that added the step and then left it. agent-005.jsonl through agent-007.jsonl: no `state next` call.
- taxi-B/relay/agent-006.jsonl line 156: re-promoted with "finding text unchanged".
- results/airport-fares-durations.csv: From JFK p25_fare = 52.0.
- taxi-A and co2-A state.md: Next steps were rewritten after release.
verdicts.narrowed: Neither awb-package nor awb-release has a step to update state.md's Next steps at the headline approval, draft or release milestones. awb-status reports Next steps verbatim, and its state-currency check ignores the deliveries/ folder, so it would not flag them. In taxi-B, "Preview the slide headlines with Dana before drafting the package" went stale once Dana approved the headlines (turn 5). It stayed stale through drafting and release. The JFK "mostly pay the $70 median fare" wording should be dropped from this finding or recorded separately. awb-package line 65 already requires rewording a finding when a review corrects it, and the agent didn't do it during packaging. That is an agent miss of an existing instruction, not a gap in the release skills.

verdicts.reasoning:
The finding is half right.

**Next-step half: real, and the release causes it.** taxi-B's state.md shows "Last updated: 2026-10-17T07:58:01-04:00". Line 37 has one Next steps item: "Preview the slide headlines with Dana before drafting the package". Git history shows the item was added in commit 412d7d9 at 07:35. The headlines were approved at 07:42 in commit 8439222. That same commit edited the Unresolved issues list but kept the finished next step. The draft was written in agent-005, revised in agent-006 (state re-rendered at 07:58), and released in agent-007 at 08:00 (released/001). Through all of that the item stayed.

No shipped instruction tells the agent to remove a next step once the package workflow has done it:
- awb-release/SKILL.md (sections 1-5 and Report) never mentions state.md or next steps.
- awb-package/SKILL.md updates state only to promote findings behind approved headlines (line 52) and to reword findings (line 65). It never touches Next steps.
- The AGENTS.md template (line 48) says how to change next steps, not when.
- awb-explore line 48, by contrast, does say to replace superseded Next steps items. Package and release have no matching step.

awb-status doesn't catch it either:
- collect_status.py copies next_steps from state.md as written (line 267).
- Its state_status check only looks at changes under investigations/<slug>/ (line 948), so a release in deliveries/ never marks state out of date.
- A later status report would therefore show "Preview the slide headlines" as open work after the release.

Codex as the agent (taxi-A, co2-A) rewrote Next steps after releasing, unprompted. taxi-B's agent had cleared stale steps earlier in the run but not after this release. So whether this happens depends on the agent. No clear instruction was ignored; there is none to ignore. A real user would hit this some of the time. It is minor.

**JFK half: not caused by a missing release step.** The JFK wording on line 13 ("JFK trips mostly pay the $70 median fare") went stale during packaging, before the release. awb-package line 65 already covers it: "When a review or the user corrects a claim a finding's text states, also reword that finding with python3 src/awb.py state finding <id> --text ..." The agent did not apply that rule. The reviewer's objection (review-reports/agent-005-record01.txt) was that "mostly show the flat fare" lacked recorded support, not that it was false. In agent-006 the agent recorded a check on the airport result: "at least half of trips to JFK record the 70-dollar flat fare". So the state wording is now mostly backed by a recorded check. It is still slightly stronger than that check: "in either direction", while the check covers trips to JFK only.

**Framing.** "Goes stale after a release" is off. The next step went stale when the headlines were approved, and the package workflow and release both carried it forward.
verdicts.release_evidence: awb-release/SKILL.md: no step or line touches state.md or next steps. awb-package/SKILL.md line 52: state is updated only to promote findings. Line 65: an existing rule to reword a finding when a review corrects its claim, which covers the JFK half. awb-explore/SKILL.md line 48: the only skill that replaces superseded Next steps items. awb-init/assets/workbench/AGENTS.md line 48: says how to change next steps, not when. awb-init/assets/workbench/investigation/state.md line 22: describes Next steps, with no rule for when to update them. awb-status/scripts/collect_status.py line 267: copies next_steps as written; around line 948: prefix = f"investigations/{slug}/", so deliveries and releases are not counted for state_status. taxi-B evidence: state.md lines 3, 13, 37. In project git, 412d7d9 (07:35) adds the Preview step and 8439222 (07:42, "Approve headlines...") keeps it. released/001 is dated 08:00:07. relay/agent-007.out.md reports the release and tells the user in chat that the next step is to build the deck. review-reports/agent-005-record01.txt flags "JFK trips mostly show the flat fare". Evidence airport-fares-durations.json records the at-least-half $70 check. For comparison, taxi-A and co2-A state.md files were rewritten after release.
verdicts.narrowed: No step in awb-package or awb-release tells the agent to retire a state.md Next steps item that the package workflow has finished (headlines approved, draft written, release made). awb-status reports next steps as written, and its staleness check ignores deliveries/. So a finished step such as "Preview the slide headlines with Dana" can outlive the headline approval and the release, and status will list it as open work. The JFK finding wording is not part of this gap: awb-package already says to reword a finding the review corrects, and the agent later recorded a check that at least half of trips to JFK are $70.

consolidated.title: Status does not check references on rows assessed from landed records
consolidated.description: An agent edit to foundation/sources.md silently did nothing, so 'reference: not yet retained' stayed for two turns. Status checks for a reference only on rows assessed from documentation, so only the package reviewer caught it.
consolidated.caused_by_fix: no
consolidated.evidence: taxi-B-22: feedback/agent.md section 3; review-reports/agent-005-record01.txt; documentation_without_reference in awb-status/scripts/collect_status.py.

verdicts.reasoning:
I traced the chain in the taxi-B relay logs to see where the harness could be responsible.

1. Turn 2 (agent-002.jsonl). The agent wrote the nyc-tlc row with the basis "from landed records: ...; data dictionary not yet retained", Status `candidate`, and Notes `reference: not yet retained`. The harness played a part here. The simulation boundary only lets the agent read URLs the user gives it, so it had to ask before fetching the TLC dictionary (agent-002.out.md: "I can only read web addresses you give me"). On a normal host it might have fetched the dictionary right away and never written the placeholder. But the persona also said they "couldn't download the TLC data dictionary". Separately, the release's own template names `reference: not yet retained` as a spelling it expects to see. So a row with a pending reference is a realistic state on any host, not something only the harness produces.

2. `land` then changed Status from `candidate` to `acquired`. This is product behaviour (`_mark_source_acquired` in awb_landing.py), and the land output reports it as `source_status_changed`.

3. Turn 3 (agent-003.jsonl). The agent ran a Python `str.replace` through Bash, and its search string still contained `| candidate |`, so nothing matched and nothing changed. The only check it ran was `grep -c dictionary`, which returned 3 because the template text already contains that word, so it proved nothing. This was the agent's own mistake, not a harness constraint: Edit was in `--allowedTools` and nothing pushed it toward Bash.

4. Turn 4 (agent-004.jsonl). awb-status ran. The MCP tool truncated its output, but the `sources` block still came through: `{"count":1,"documentation_without_reference":[],...}`. At that moment the findings already cited the dictionary ("cash tips are not recorded (TLC data dictionary)"), quality.md linked it, and the PDF was in foundation/references/nyc-tlc/. Status still reported nothing, because `assessed` in collect_status.py only includes rows where `documentation_basis(row)` is true. That decision is fixed code and would come out the same on any host given the same sources.md.

5. Turn 5. The package reviewer flagged it (agent-005-record01.txt, findings.md:36 and methodology-note.md:17: "records no reference ('reference: not yet retained')").

Conclusion. The harness affected a precondition (why the placeholder existed in turn 2), and the edit that did nothing was agent error. Neither causes the status gap. Status trusts the basis label completely and never cross-checks it. I also ran the basis regex: a mixed label like the one the agent meant to write, "from landed records and documentation", is read as `landed records` and raises no uncertainty. So the reference check would be skipped there too, even though the template says to use `from documentation` whenever documentation settled the assessment.

Two things limit the finding. First, the check is narrow by design and the design is documented (awb-status SKILL.md, CHANGELOG). Second, the designed backstop worked: the package reviewer caught the problem before release. Severity minor is right. The finding's wording also blurs things a little: the edit "silently did nothing" because of the agent's own replace, not because of anything the release failed to do.
verdicts.release_evidence: awb-status/scripts/collect_status.py: `assessed = [... for row in registered or [] if documentation_basis(row)]`. Only those rows feed `documentation_without_reference`. `documentation_basis` matches `\s*`?from (documentation|landed records)\b`, so "from landed records and documentation" counts as landed records and raises no uncertainty (I tested the regex). awb-init/assets/workbench/foundation/sources.md says `reference: not yet retained` "counts as none", but only rows labelled from documentation are ever checked. awb-init/assets/awb_landing.py `_mark_source_acquired` rewrites Status in place. taxi-B relay/agent-004.jsonl: the status output shows `"sources":{"count":1,"documentation_without_reference":[],"documentation_access_notes":[]}` while the row still read `reference: not yet retained` and foundation/references/nyc-tlc/data_dictionary_trip_records_yellow.pdf existed. agent-003.jsonl: the replace's search string contains `| candidate |`, which land had already changed. Its only check was `grep -c dictionary` (3, matched by template text). review-reports/agent-005-record01.txt: the reviewer's catch.
verdicts.narrowed: awb-status decides whether to check a source's reference only from the basis label at the start of Relevance and fitness. A row labelled `from landed records` is never checked. That includes a mixed label like `from landed records and documentation`, which is read as landed records without raising an uncertainty. It holds even when the Notes contain the template's own named non-reference `reference: not yet retained` and a file sits in foundation/references/<source-id>/. So a basis label that is stale or mixed while findings rely on documentation gets a clean status report, and only the package reviewer catches it. In taxi-B the row was stale because of the agent's own replace, which matched nothing: land had already changed `candidate` to `acquired` and reported it. The simulation's URL boundary explains why the placeholder was written in the first place. Neither of those is a release defect. Severity minor, and the designed reviewer backstop worked.

verdicts.reasoning:
The run evidence matches the timeline the finding describes, but the release did not cause the problem.

Timeline. In turn 2 (agent-002) the agent wrote the nyc-tlc row by hand as "from landed records: ... data dictionary not yet retained | candidate | reference: not yet retained". The `land` call then flipped Status to acquired, and its JSON output said so: "source_status_changed": "Sources row nyc-tlc: Status candidate -> acquired" (agent-002.jsonl line 99). The help text the agent had read also says land "sets a candidate source to acquired".

In turn 3 (agent-003.jsonl line 25) the agent ran its own Python str.replace with an old-string that still contained "| candidate |". The string no longer matched, so the replace did nothing. The agent's only check was `grep -c "dictionary"`, which returned 3 because the template text in sources.md already contains the word "dictionary". That hid the failure.

In turn 4, awb-status reported `documentation_without_reference: []` (agent-004.jsonl line 70). In turn 5 the package reviewer flagged findings.md:36 and methodology-note.md:17 (agent-005-record01.txt). The agent's own feedback (section 3) admits that its str.replace silently did nothing because land had already changed the status.

What the release does. collect_status.py `documentation_basis()` only checks rows whose Relevance and fitness begins `from documentation`. That is the documented design:
- awb-status/SKILL.md says the check covers "a source assessed from documentation whose Notes record no reference".
- The sources.md template says to use `from documentation` when documentation or a schema settled the assessment, otherwise `from landed records`.

The stale row still claimed a landed-records basis, so status behaved exactly as specified. A row assessed from landed records needs no reference. Flagging every such row would be noise.

Two things caused the problem, and neither is in the release:
- The agent's own unchecked edit, which ignored land's explicit status-change message.
- A verification grep that matched template text.

The package reviewer gate, the check meant to catch claims about how a source builds a series, caught it as designed. A real user's agent would only hit this by botching an edit the same way. The suggested fix (flag `reference: not yet retained` once a file exists under foundation/references/<source-id>/) is a feature request, not the correction of a defect.

One side note, separate from this finding and not shown in the evidence: the basis regex `from (documentation|landed records)\b` also reads the agent's invented spelling "from landed records and documentation" as a landed-records basis, without recording any uncertainty. A mixed-basis row with no reference would therefore escape the check. In this run the final row has a valid form-1 reference, so it had no effect.
verdicts.release_evidence: awb-status/scripts/collect_status.py ~line 305: documentation_basis() matches only `from (documentation|landed records)` and returns True only for documentation; line ~465: `assessed = [... if documentation_basis(row)]`, so documentation_without_reference covers documentation-basis rows only, by design. awb-status/SKILL.md line 34 defines the entry as "a source assessed from documentation whose Notes record no reference". awb-init/assets/workbench/foundation/sources.md line 16 gives the basis rule (documentation vs landed records). awb-init/assets/awb_landing.py lines 809-835 and 895: land changes the Status from candidate to acquired and reports `source_status_changed` in its output, and its help text (line ~992) says so. Run: taxi-B relay agent-002.jsonl line 99 (land reported the status change); agent-003.jsonl line 25 (str.replace still keyed on "| candidate |", checked only with grep -c "dictionary" = 3); agent-004.jsonl line 70 (status: documentation_without_reference []); agent-005 review report caught it; feedback/agent.md section 3 admits the agent's own edit silently did nothing.
verdicts.narrowed: none. Separate latent issue, not shown in this run: the basis regex reads a nonstandard mixed basis such as "from landed records and documentation" as landed records without recording an uncertainty, so such a row would skip the reference check.

consolidated.title: reconcile() credits overlapping exclusions to the first rule
consolidated.description: reconcile() requires each excluded row to count under exactly one rule, so rows that broke several validity rules were credited to whichever rule came first. The per-rule counts shown to the user overlap: 2,433 trips over 65 mph in total, against 2,182 among trips that pass the other rules. The narrative's count-check sentence then read as if overlapping counts were added, and the user had to correct it.
consolidated.caused_by_fix: yes: #97 (issue #87) added reconcile() with its exclusive split.
consolidated.evidence: taxi-B-23: agent-notes turn 3; replies 2 and 3; third correction in msg 6; workbench-guides/analysis.md:15.

verdicts.reasoning:
I could not tie this to the harness. Nothing in the agent system prompt or the persona BRIEF raises overlap, double counting or how the count check should be worded. The persona's "without double counting" in msg 2 is ordinary analyst behaviour and did not plant the issue. Non-interactive claude -p, the Codex sandbox, the auto-approved MCP tools, the relay and the study disclosure have no plausible path to a sentence in the narrative.

What actually happened:
1. The release's reconcile() (awb-init/assets/awb_validate.py) fails the row_counts check unless before == after + sum(excluded). analysis.md:15 describes it as "rows in equal to rows kept plus rows excluded by each rule". With overlapping validity rules, a per-rule breakdown therefore has to be exclusive. The agent's helpers.filter_step credits each row to the first rule it fails. Its turn-3 notes flag this exclusive-split requirement as friction "worth documenting".
2. The result table invalid-records.sql counts each rule independently, so the counts overlap: speed 2,433, plus the vendor counts for bad_distance and bad_fare. The reconcile evidence records the first-rule split instead (implausible speed 2,182).
3. The draft findings.md (How-we-know slide, line 103) and methodology-note.md:24 said "At every step, the records kept plus the records excluded by each rule equal the records going in, exactly." That is the guide's reconcile wording, carried almost word for word into the user-facing text. It sat next to overlapping per-rule figures (2,433 on the data-quality slide), so it reads as if the displayed rule counts add up.
4. The package review flagged this sentence only for citation form. The repair kept "excluded by each rule" and made the claim more prominent ("An automatic count check in every result confirms..."). check-draft passed it. The user caught it in msg 6, third bullet.

A real user on a normal host, with the same skills, would get the same sentence. A less careful user would release it unchanged, which is worse. The Codex persona being a sharp reader affects only whether the defect was noticed, not whether it exists.

The finding is overstated in two places:
- The 2,433 vs 2,182 gap is not a defect. 2,433 is the correct independent count the user asked for. The 2,182 in reply 2 came from an exploration query (speed-distribution) before any result ran. It was not produced by reconcile(), though it equals the reconcile attribution.
- reconcile() does not strictly force first-rule-wins: a single "any rule" bucket would pass the check. It is the guide's "each rule" wording that pushes toward an exclusive per-rule split.
verdicts.release_evidence:
- awb-init/assets/awb_validate.py, _row_counts and reconcile(): the check fails unless before == after + sum(excluded.values()).
- awb-init/assets/workbench/workbench-guides/analysis.md:15: "every filtered population reconciled by `reconcile()`, rows in equal to rows kept plus rows excluded by each rule".
- awb-init/assets/workbench/investigation/run.py:76-87, the producer example: "validation fails unless they add up".
- awb-package/references/review.md:26: a reconciliation sentence is checked for citation form ("cites the recorded result or check"), not for whether its terms match the counts shown.
- taxi-B, agent-005.jsonl (package record report): the reviewer flagged findings.md:103 and methodology-note.md:24 ("records kept plus the records excluded by each rule equal the records going in, exactly") only for not naming the check.
- taxi-B evidence/invalid-records.json row_counts detail: "implausible speed 2182" (first-rule split). results/invalid-records.csv: implausible_speed 2433 (independent count).
- transcript msg 6, third bullet: the user's correction. Reply 6: the reworded sentence "valid records plus invalid records, each counted once ... individual rule counts can overlap".
- feedback/agent-notes.md, turn 3: "producer reconcile() requires an exclusive split; overlapping validity rules forced 'first rule wins' attribution ... worth documenting".
- No hint about overlap or the count-check wording appears in human/BRIEF.md or prompts/claude-agent-system.md.
verdicts.narrowed: reconcile() and its guide wording in analysis.md:15 ("rows in equal to rows kept plus rows excluded by each rule") describe an exclusive split by rule. The result table and the deck report independent, overlapping per-rule counts (2,433 over 65 mph in total; the reconcile evidence credits 2,182 to that rule). The agent carried the reconcile wording into the user-facing How-we-know slide and the methodology note as "records kept plus the records excluded by each rule equal the records going in, exactly". The package review flagged that sentence only for citation form, check-draft passed it, and the user had to correct it to "valid plus uniquely counted invalid records ... individual rule counts can overlap". The overlapping counts themselves are correct reporting, not a defect, and the 2,182 the user saw in reply 2 came from an exploration query, not from reconcile(). reconcile() does not strictly force first-rule-wins (a single any-rule bucket passes); the guide's "each rule" wording pushes toward it.

verdicts.reasoning:
The run evidence matches the finding. In taxi-B, the project's helpers.filter_step (investigations/airport-trips-and-tipping/helpers.py) gives each excluded record to the first rule it fails, because reconcile() fails unless before == after + sum(excluded). That makes the reconcile detail list "implausible speed 2182". The invalid-records result, which is what the deck shows, counts each rule independently, so the deck says "2,433 records showed implausible recorded speeds above 65 mph". The first draft's count-check sentence, found in the agent-005 relay log and review-reports/agent-005-record01.txt, read: "records kept plus records excluded by each rule equal the records going in, exactly". Next to the deck's overlapping per-rule figures, that reads as if those figures add up. The user corrected it as the third wording issue in message 6 ("sounds as though overlapping rule counts are added"), and the agent reworded it in reply 6. The agent's turn-3 notes flag the same friction: "reconcile() requires an exclusive split; overlapping validity rules forced 'first rule wins' attribution ... worth documenting."

Release cause: none of the shipped files says what to do when exclusion rules overlap.
