The contract in awb_validate.py (_row_counts and reconcile) requires a per-rule split where each row counts once, but every description calls it "rows excluded by each rule" or "the rows each exclusion rule removed": workbench-guides/analysis.md:15, references/validation.md:14, the reconcile docstring, the run.py comment, and the settings.toml comment. None says rules must be made exclusive, how to assign a row that fails several rules, or how to describe the check next to independently counted rule figures. A grep of the release for overlap, exclusive, "first rule" and "counted once" turns up nothing on this. The draft's sentence repeats the guide's phrase almost word for word. The package review (review.md "claims of checking") made the agent name the check, and it passed this wording without seeing the overlap. The agent ignored no clear instruction. A real user whose validity rules overlap, which is common, would hit the same ambiguity on a normal host. Nothing about it depends on the harness.

Caveats that narrow the finding: (1) The two sets of per-rule counts come partly from the agent's own design. It chose to report independent per-rule counts in invalid-records, and reconcile() did not force that. (2) The 2,182 shown in reply 2 was an exploration figure, correctly labelled "among those that pass your other rules", and it never appeared in the deck. Only 2,433 did. (3) The reconcile check itself was correct. The defect is the ambiguous wording of what it checks, plus the lack of overlap guidance. It took one user correction, in one run, so minor is right.
verdicts.release_evidence: awb-init/assets/awb_validate.py:96-132 (_row_counts fails unless before == after + sum(excluded.values()); the pass detail lists the exclusive per-rule counts) and :148-162 (reconcile docstring: "the rows each exclusion rule removed, as {rule: rows}", with no overlap guidance). awb-init/assets/workbench/workbench-guides/analysis.md:15 ("every filtered population reconciled by `reconcile()`, rows in equal to rows kept plus rows excluded by each rule"), echoed almost word for word in the draft sentence the user corrected. awb-init/references/validation.md:14 ("A step's `excluded` maps each exclusion rule to the rows it removed, and the check fails unless `before` equals `after` plus every excluded row"). awb-init/assets/workbench/investigation/run.py:76-87 and settings.toml:38-40 use the same wording. Grepping the release for overlap/exclusive/first rule/counted once finds no guidance on rules that overlap. awb-package/references/review.md:26 and package-contract.md:49 make a narrative name the check behind a "reconciles" claim, but say nothing about separating the exclusive reconcile counts from independently counted rule figures. Run evidence: taxi-B transcript.md:108 (2,182, reply 2), :194 (2,433, reply 3), :492 (user correction, msg 6), :520 (reworded sentence); relay/agent-005.jsonl and review-reports/agent-005-record01.txt:2-3 (original "records excluded by each rule" sentence); project helpers.py filter_step (first-rule attribution); feedback/agent-notes.md turn 3 friction line.
verdicts.narrowed: Nothing in the release covers exclusion rules that overlap. reconcile() and its check quietly require a per-rule split where each row counts once, while analysis.md:15, validation.md:14 and the reconcile docstring call it "rows excluded by each rule". So in taxi-B the agent gave each overlapping record to its first failed rule (speed 2,182) and showed independently counted figures elsewhere (speed 2,433). Its draft count-check sentence repeated the guide's "records kept plus records excluded by each rule equal the records going in". Next to the overlapping figures in the deck, that read as if those figures add up, and the user had to correct it once. Reporting overlapping per-rule figures was the agent's own design choice, and the 2,182 in reply 2 was a correctly labelled exploration figure that never reached the deck.

consolidated.title: MCP read profile cannot use an investigation's settings
consolidated.description: awb read profile rejects a 'settings' argument ('unknown arguments: settings'), so it cannot summarize an investigation-local view. sql now binds params and settings, but profile does not.
consolidated.caused_by_fix: no
consolidated.evidence: co2-A-12: agent-003 awb/read profile failure; awb_mcp.py lines 373-381.

verdicts.reasoning:
I looked for a harness cause and found none.

1. The refusal comes from the shipped server, not the host. In awb_mcp.py read_command (lines 373-374), `_check_keys` allows `settings` only when the command is `sql`; for `profile` it allows just `command`, `query` and `max_rows`. The relay log for co2-A agent-003 (item_31) shows the call reached the server and came back as a tool result: "unknown arguments: settings", status failed. No approval prompt, sandbox denial, relay step or timeout was involved. The MCP server, awb_validate.py and the CLI installed in the simulated home are byte-identical to the release (checked with diff), so the simulated home does not explain it either.

2. The gap is in the CLI too. `awb.py profile` in awb_validate.py cli_profile (around line 252) takes only `source`, `--out`, `--max-rows` and `--read-only`. It opens `landing.session(root)` without `investigation=`. `sql` (awb_landing.py cli_sql) is different: `--settings` binds the [parameters] and loads that investigation's views/*.sql. The profile error path even admits it: "profile binds no parameters". So neither the MCP read tool, the MCP data tool (which passes args straight to the same CLI) nor the CLI can profile an investigation-local view by name. The MCP refusal matches what the CLI can do; the root cause is the CLI's profile command.

3. The release itself points users here. The project AGENTS.md says to get "counts, nulls, and distinct values with `awb.py profile`", and analysis.md says to inspect values with profile. Investigations keep their own views (co2-A's country_data lives in investigations/emissions-and-country-focus/views/01_scope.sql). The read tool has one flat schema that lists `settings` next to `profile`, so any host's model could reasonably send it. That is not specific to Codex or a non-interactive run.

4. Nothing in the simulation setup is involved. The personas, the study disclosure and the human role had no part in this call; it was the agent's own step while building results.

Impact is small. The agent recovered in one call by copying the view's eligibility filter into a SELECT over the foundation view. That workaround duplicates the view logic, which can drift from it. Minor severity is right.
verdicts.release_evidence:
- release/analytics-workbench-skills/awb-init/assets/awb_mcp.py lines 373-381: `_check_keys` allows `settings`/`params` only for `sql`; `profile` gets `("command","query","max_rows")`. The read tool's flat inputSchema (around lines 142-150) lists `settings` and describes it as "sql: an investigation whose settings [parameters] the query binds and whose views/*.sql it loads".
- awb-init/assets/awb_validate.py cli_profile: no `--settings` or `--param`, and it calls `landing.session(root)` without `investigation`. Its error text says "profile binds no parameters".
- awb-init/assets/awb_landing.py cli_sql (around line 1692): `--settings INVESTIGATION` loads that investigation's views/*.sql through `session(root, ..., investigation=args.settings)`.
- CHANGELOG.md line 68: the read tool's `sql` takes `params` and `settings`; profile gets no matching change.
- awb-init/assets/workbench/AGENTS.md line 24 and workbench-guides/analysis.md line 15 tell users to inspect counts, nulls and distinct values with `awb.py profile`.
- Log: co2-A/relay/agent-003.jsonl item_31 has `{"command":"profile","settings":"emissions-and-country-focus","query":"country_data"}` and the result "unknown arguments: settings". item_33 is the successful retry with the filter copied in.
- The installed copies in co2-A/agent-home/.agents/skills are identical to the release.
verdicts.narrowed: The root cause is in the CLI, not only the MCP layer. Neither `awb.py profile` nor the MCP read or data profile can load an investigation's views/*.sql or bind its settings [parameters], while `sql --settings` can. The shared read-tool schema lists `settings` next to `profile`, which invites the failing call. Profiling an investigation-local view means copying its definition into the query (as the agent did) or getting counts through `sql` with settings. One failed call, recovered at once: minor.

verdicts.reasoning: The release causes this. Code: awb_mcp.py read_command (lines 372-383) allows only ("command", "query", "max_rows") for profile, so passing `settings` fails in _check_keys with "unknown arguments: settings". The CLI underneath cannot do it either. In awb_validate.py, cli_profile has no --settings or --param option, and it opens landing.session(root) without investigation=. That means profile only ever loads foundation/views and never investigations/<name>/views/*.sql. `sql` passes investigation=args.settings (awb_landing.py line 1712), so sql can see those views. MCP is not dropping something the CLI has. The profile helper itself cannot see investigation-local views at all. Docs: landing.md says "`profile` binds no parameters", which covers $name binding. No shipped text says profile cannot see an investigation's views/*.sql. Several things point the other way. The read tool describes profile as a summary "of a view". awb-explore is triggered by "profile this view". The flat read schema lists a `settings` property next to profile (its description does start "sql:"). The rejection also gives no route to profiling an investigation view. Evidence: co2-A agent-003, item_31 (jsonl line 63), is awb/read {command: profile, settings: emissions-and-country-focus, query: country_data}. It returned "unknown arguments: settings" with status failed. country_data is defined only in investigations/emissions-and-country-focus/views/01_scope.sql, so it really is an investigation-local view. The agent's own feedback (agent-notes.md line 42) records the failure. It worked around it by copying the scope filter into a SELECT against the foundation view, which succeeded. Nothing here is specific to the harness, since any host that profiles an investigation view hits it. The agent made one reasonable attempt and did not ignore any instruction. Impact is small: one rejected call, an immediate workaround, and a filter copied by hand that could drift from the view's definition. So the minor rating is right.
verdicts.release_evidence: awb-init/assets/awb_mcp.py lines 372-383: _check_keys allows only command/query/max_rows for profile, and settings/params are wired only `if command == "sql"`. awb-init/assets/awb_validate.py cli_profile (lines 252-326): there is no --settings or --param argument, it uses `landing.session(root, read_only=True)` without investigation=, and its comment says "landing's fix binds with sql's --param or --settings, which profile does not take". awb-init/assets/awb_landing.py line 1712: sql uses `session(root, read_only=..., investigation=args.settings)`, and session() is documented at lines 1243-1246 as loading investigations/<inv>/views/*.sql only when investigation is given. awb-init/references/landing.md line 45 says only that "`profile` binds no parameters" and does not mention investigation views. Run evidence: co2-A/relay/agent-003.jsonl item_31, "unknown arguments: settings", with country_data defined in co2-A/project/investigations/emissions-and-country-focus/views/01_scope.sql. co2-A/feedback/agent-notes.md line 42 records the failure and the workaround.
verdicts.narrowed: The gap is in the profile helper itself, not MCP parity. Both `awb.py profile` and the MCP read tool's profile load only foundation/views and bind no settings parameters. So neither can summarize a view defined in an investigation's views/*.sql, which sql --settings can see. The docs disclose only the missing parameter binding, and the "unknown arguments: settings" rejection gives no workaround. In co2-A this cost one rejected call and a scope filter copied by hand into a foundation SELECT. Minor.

consolidated.title: Status calls the state out of date when history is written a second after it
consolidated.description: co2-A's status called the investigation state out of date because history.md was written one second after state.md's stamp, though all evidence was current. The skills direct the agent to write history after state commands, which produces exactly this order.
consolidated.caused_by_fix: yes: #104 (issue #93) switched freshness to timestamps precise to the second. 'indeterminate at date precision' appears in no run, but this order of writes now reads as out of date.
consolidated.evidence: co2-A-15: agent-005; collect_status.py lines 1000-1031.

verdicts.reasoning:
The harness explanations don't hold up. The sequence in co2-A is the following.

1. agent-004 items 35 and 37 ran MCP `state finding` commands. These stamp state.md, and the tool also appends history.md itself in the same call (its result shows "history.md: ### 2026-10-17 — gdp-co2-thresholds reworded...").
2. Item 39 was `questions add`. Item 41 was an apply_patch to brief.md and analysis-results.md.
3. Item 43 was a `python3 -c` that appended a hand-written history.md entry about the Q2 5% threshold comparison and the Q4 aviation/shipping caveat.
4. In agent-005, the first status reported last_updated 07:32:49 and state_status "out of date", with latest_change history.md at 07:32:50.

The cause is in collect_status.py. Its `exempt` list (about line 951) holds only state.md, questions.json and questions.md. `order()` (lines 1000-1006) calls an exact-mtime change "after" when its whole second exceeds the state stamp. So any edit to history.md (or brief.md, analysis-results.md, and so on) a second or more after the last state command dates the state. The later status in the same turn shows the flip side: history.md and the state stamp were both at 07:36:39 there, so it reported "up to date".

The hand-written entry is something the release asks for. Installed AGENTS.md line 48 lists the state commands, then says "Write history by hand only when a scope, method, caveat, or data limitation changes understanding". The history template likewise says the state command appends some entries and the rest are written by hand. A Q2 method comparison plus a Q4 caveat clarification is exactly that case. state.md already reflected both, so "out of date" was a false positive. awb-status SKILL.md line 51 turns that status into a risk request for the user ("Update the investigation state").

Harness checks:
- **Timing (Codex exec, parallel tool calls, auto-approved MCP).** Items 35-43 landed within about 0.2 s, which is why the gap was only one second. On an interactive host each call waits for approval, so the gap would be seconds or minutes. The flag would then be certain rather than marginal: the harness made the bug less likely to show, not more.
- **Sandbox.** The heredoc failure only changed how the file was written (`python3 -c` instead of a heredoc), not its mtime or the write order.
- **No commits yet.** A real user's choice ("Commits: on request"). Uncommitted history.md is dated by its mtime either way.
- **Other factors.** The simulated home, relay, personas and study disclosure play no part in the collector's logic.
- **Prevalence.** It appears only in co2-A. retail-B's "out of date" came from settings.toml, a separate cause.

Corrections to the finding as written:
- The skills don't dictate the order; they sanction hand-written history entries, and writing one after the matching state command is the natural order.
- "Though all evidence was current" mislabels the check. The collector compares file mtimes against the state.md stamp, not against evidence.
- The one second is incidental, not the essence of the bug.
verdicts.release_evidence:
- **collect_status.py (release awb-status/scripts):**

- **co2-A relay agent-004:**

verdicts.narrowed: The status collector counts any edit to a non-exempt investigation file, history.md included, made a second or more after the last `state` command as dating state.md. The edit that triggered it here is a hand-written history entry, which AGENTS.md calls for when a method or caveat changes. Writing that entry after the matching state command makes status report "out of date" and offer the "Update the investigation state" risk request, even though state.md already reflects the change. The same applies to brief.md and analysis-results.md. On an interactive host the gap is longer and the false flag is certain, not a one-second edge case. The skills do not prescribe the order, and the check compares file mtimes against the state stamp, not evidence freshness.

verdicts.reasoning:
The run evidence matches the finding. In co2-A agent-005, the first awb `read status` call returned git.state_status "out of date", with latest_change being investigations/emissions-and-country-focus/history.md at 2026-10-17T07:32:50-04:00. state.md's Last updated was 07:32:49. `stale` in the same turn returned checked 9, stale 0.

The cause is in agent-004, the previous turn. The agent ran `state finding gdp-co2-thresholds --text/--claim/--reason` and `state finding historical-shares --caveat --reason`. Both commands stamp state.md, and the caveat-only change writes no history entry. About a second later, a `python3 -c` command (jsonl line 44) appended a hand-written "## 2026-10-17 — Accepted findings and requested Q2 threshold comparison" entry to history.md. That entry covers the Q2 comparison and the Q4 caveat change the state commands had already recorded.

The release directs this hand write and does nothing to keep it from dating the state:
1. AGENTS.md Record maintenance (line 48) says to change findings with `state finding`, then "Write history by hand only when a scope, method, caveat, or data limitation changes understanding". The history.md template says the same: the helpers append entries only for reruns and status or claim changes, and others are written by hand. A caveat change made with `state finding --caveat` writes no entry, so the agent must add one by hand after the state command. awb-scope's Rescope branch also orders it: revise the state, then write a history entry.
2. No `awb.py state` subcommand writes a free-form history entry or re-stamps Last updated. Nothing tells the agent to write history first or to refresh the state afterwards.
3. collect_status.py git_status (lines ~952-1031) exempts only state.md, questions.json and questions.md: "a record of its own that state.md does not hold". history.md is not exempt, so any history mtime in a later whole second than the stamp is ordered "after" and gives "out of date".
4. The helper avoids this only for history it writes itself. The _commit docstring and CHANGELOG line 186 say the state is "stamped after the findings and history files written with it", which shows history written alongside a state change is not meant to date the state. Hand-written history does not get that protection.
5. For "out of date", awb-status SKILL.md tells the agent to report latest_change without running `stale`. It also maps the status to the risk request "Update the investigation state". A real user on a normal host with Git would see a false out-of-date warning.

Mitigating facts: the co2-A agent ran `stale` anyway and did not pass the warning on to the user, so in this run nobody saw it; the agent logged it in feedback. Two hand edits sanctioned by awb-scope Sharpen in the same apply_patch, to brief.md and analysis-results.md, could also have landed in the :50 second. The "one second" in the finding is incidental. Because the comparison works in whole seconds, any later second triggers the warning, and a write within the same second does not. That is why the second status call in agent-005, where history and the stamp were both at 07:36:39, reported "up to date".

consolidated.title: The methods-note length line must stand alone in its exact form
consolidated.description: check-draft rejected 'Methods note length: about 500 words. The user requested about one page...', because the length line must stand alone, in the exact template form.
consolidated.caused_by_fix: yes: #101 (issue #85) added the length line, and the row it reports for a line in another form.
consolidated.evidence: retail-A-15: reply 7; awb/read failure for agent-007 in harness-log.md; awb-package/SKILL.md step 1 (Establish).

verdicts.reasoning:
Nothing about how the simulation was run explains this. In agent-006 the Codex agent edited investigations/marketing-budget/brief.md itself (file_change item_28) and wrote one line: "Methods note length: about 500 words. The user requested about one page, delivered beside the deck." The persona's request was ordinary ("I do want the methodology note, about one page"), not a front-loaded answer. None of these touched the edit: non-interactive exec, the sandbox (its zsh heredoc and cache failures hit other commands), auto-approved MCP, the simulated home, or the relay. The study note only asks for a separate friction log and does not ask for reasons to go into the brief. The same agent on an interactive host would write the same line and get the same result from the checker.

The cause is an agent slip that the release's strict parser catches on purpose:
- awb_draft.py note_length_problems runs `_NOTE_LENGTH.fullmatch(line.strip())` with `Methods note length: about ([0-9]+) words\.?`. Any line that starts like a length line but has trailing prose becomes a problem row.
- The release tells the agent to use the exact form in two places. The brief template says "a methods note length on its own line as `Methods note length: about <n> words`", and awb-package step 1 says "in the template's ... form". The agent read both (template in agent-002, SKILL.md in agent-006) and still added a sentence.
- In the other five runs the agent wrote the line correctly the first time.

The finding also overstates the effect. note_length is informational: `_structure_passed` leaves it out, and the docstring says "it never fails the check". check-draft did exit 1, but only because of the missing inventory and the unrecorded number 20261017. The agent fixed the line with one python -c replace in agent-007, and the user never saw it. What is real is design friction, not a rejection: strict Markdown-as-config parsing that a careless agent can trip over.
verdicts.release_evidence: awb-package/assets/awb_draft.py lines 2873-2906: `_NOTE_LENGTH` is fullmatched against each stripped brief line, and any other line that looks like a length line gets the "the methods note length is not written as `Methods note length: about <n> words`" row. The note_length_problems docstring says "Informational, like slides: it never fails the check." `_structure_passed` (line 2980) does not include note_length. awb-init/assets/workbench/investigation/brief.md line 19 says to write it "on its own line as `Methods note length: about <n> words`". awb-package/SKILL.md step 1 says "in the template's `Methods note length: about <n> words` form". helpers.md line 35 describes the deliberate flagging of variant forms. In the retail-A agent-007 log, check-draft item_25 shows note_length at brief.md line 43, while its errors list holds only the inventory error and its numbers list only 20261017. After the one-line split, item_30 shows note_length: []. The other five runs' briefs all have the line in the correct form.
verdicts.narrowed: When an agent appends explanatory prose to the brief's methods-note length line, check-draft reports an informational note_length row; it does not reject the draft or fail the check, which here failed for unrelated reasons (missing inventory, the number 20261017). Splitting the line fixes it in one edit. The release already documents the standalone form in the brief template and awb-package step 1, so this is an agent deviation caught by a strict, documented parser. It happened in 1 of 6 runs and had no visible effect on the user. At most it is a minor design-friction product issue: the parser could accept prose after the closing period.

verdicts.reasoning:
The release says what form the line takes, and the check behaved as designed.

(1) Shipped instructions. The brief template at awb-init/assets/workbench/investigation/brief.md, line 19, says to record "a methods note length on its own line as `Methods note length: about <n> words`". awb-package/SKILL.md step 1 says to record it "in the template's `Methods note length: about <n> words` form". awb-package/references/helpers.md, line 35, gives the exact parse and says a line written in another form "is reported rather than read as none". The agent read the template in agent-002 and SKILL.md in agent-001 and agent-006.

(2) What happened. In agent-006 the agent edited brief.md with apply_patch and wrote "Methods note length: about 500 words. The user requested about one page, delivered beside the deck." That is the exact form with prose added on the same line, which goes against "on its own line". In agent-007 the awb/read check-draft returned a note_length row naming brief.md line 43: "the methods note length is not written as ...". The agent split the line with one python replace, and the next check returned note_length [].

(3) "Rejected" overstates it. Per awb_draft.py note_length_problems and package-contract.md, note_length rows are informational and never fail the check. Both failed awb/read calls returned exit 1 because of errors ["manifest: manifest.json records no inventory list; run check-draft without --verify-only"]. That is the expected result of a verify-only precheck. The second call still failed after note_length was cleared. The later awb/package check-draft completed.

(4) Scope. The cost was one agent edit, the user never saw it, and the agent broke a clear template instruction once, not repeatedly. A loose parser that silently read prose-laden lines would go against the deliberate single-form design. Flagging the line rather than ignoring it is the intended behaviour.
verdicts.release_evidence: awb-init/assets/workbench/investigation/brief.md:19: "a methods note length on its own line as `Methods note length: about <n> words`". awb-package/SKILL.md:30: "a methods note length in the template's `Methods note length: about <n> words` form". awb-package/references/helpers.md:35: the exact parse (list marker and closing period allowed), with a line in any other form reported, and "Informational, like `slides`: it never fails the check". awb-package/assets/awb_draft.py:2876-2906: _NOTE_LENGTH matches the whole stripped line, and a near-match line becomes a row. package-contract.md:73: note_length is in the informational list. Run evidence: retail-A/relay/agent-006.jsonl item_28 (apply_patch to brief.md). agent-007.jsonl item_3 (the brief already holds the line with trailing prose). item_25 (note_length row; the exit 1 comes from the manifest inventory error). item_27 (one-edit fix). item_30 (note_length [], still exit 1 for the inventory). feedback/agent-notes.md:117 calls it "expected pre-final validation".
verdicts.narrowed: At most: awb-package/SKILL.md step 1 says the length goes in "the template's ... form" but does not repeat the template's "on its own line". At packaging time the investigation's brief.md no longer contains the template's guidance paragraph. So an agent that adds prose after the exact line gets an informational check-draft note_length row and has to split the line, a one-edit fix the user never sees. check-draft did not reject or fail on it.

consolidated.title: precision_warnings repeats for a value that genuinely has four decimals
consolidated.description: On every export, precision_warnings flagged 0.1875 (3/16), which genuinely has four decimal places. There is no way to confirm it and silence the warning.
consolidated.caused_by_fix: yes: #100 (issue #88) added precision_warnings with no confirmation key.
consolidated.evidence: retail-B-18: agent.md item 11 and section 3; awb-package/references/helpers.md.

verdicts.reasoning:
Nothing about how the simulation was run explains this warning. The cause is the release's export code, run deterministically on real data, and an interactive user would see the same output.

1. **The value really has four decimals.** The query `investigations/marketing-budget-evidence/queries/product-cancellation-rate.sql` computes `largest_cancellation_line / nullif(cancellation_value, 0)` and never rounds. Row 993 of `results/product-cancellation-rate.csv` (ALARM CLOCK BAKELIKE GREEN) is 45/240 = 0.1875, which a double stores exactly.

2. **The check only counts decimal places.** In `awb-package/assets/awb_draft.py` `_shape()` (around lines 3684-3691), every `[percent]` column shown to fewer than two places is checked. The warning fires if any selected cell has `_places(...) == 4`. It cannot tell a rounded query from a true fraction like k/16 or k/80, and the message wrongly says the query rounded it.

3. **There is no way to confirm the column.** `[confirmed]` is read only by `label_collisions`. The precision branch checks nothing like it. helpers.md line 54 documents no way to confirm either, and its advice to save at full precision cannot be followed because the result already is full precision.

4. **The only ways to clear it change the deliverable.** You can show the column to two places (`[round]` >= 2), or drop the column or row from the export. The run had `largest_line_share_of_cancellations = 1` with 1-place percents, a normal choice.

5. **It fired on every full export.** The full `product-cancellation-rate` dataset was exported with this column. The same warning, with example 0.1875, appears in relay logs agent-005 (three times) and agent-006 (twice).

**Harness explanations ruled out:** The warning is computed by the release's Python code from the CSV and display.toml, not by any host behaviour, so none of the suspects can produce it: claude -p, auto-approved MCP, the simulated home, the relay, the persona, or the study disclosure. The study disclosure may have made the agent more likely to report it, but the behaviour is real.

**Limits:** The warning does not block anything, since files are written and neither check-draft nor release gates on it. So the impact is repeated noise and a wrong diagnosis, which is consistent with "minor".
verdicts.release_evidence:
- **Warning logic:** `release/analytics-workbench-skills/awb-package/assets/awb_draft.py` lines 3684-3691 flag any `[percent]` column with places < 2 if any selected cell has exactly 4 decimal places. `_PRECISION` (line 3385) says "a sign the query rounded them". `[confirmed]` is used only by `label_collisions` (line 3830); the `notes["precision"]` path never checks it.
- **Docs:** `awb-package/references/helpers.md` line 54 says to "save the result at full precision and round only under [round]" and offers no way to confirm a column. CHANGELOG line 62 describes the same heuristic.
- **Run data:** in `retail-B/project`, `results/product-cancellation-rate.csv` row 993 has `largest_line_share_of_cancellations` = 0.1875 (240.0 cancelled, largest line 45). The SQL has no rounding. `foundation/display.toml` sets `[round] largest_line_share_of_cancellations = 1` and lists the column under `[percent]`.
- **Relay logs:** the warning appears in `retail-B/relay/agent-005.jsonl` and `agent-006.jsonl` export results.
verdicts.narrowed: Export's `precision_warnings` flags a percent column shown to fewer than two decimals whenever any of its selected fractions has exactly four decimal places. It does this even when the value genuinely has four, such as 45/240 = 0.1875, and says the query rounded it when it did not. No key confirms or silences the warning (`[confirmed]` covers only label warnings). It goes away only if the column is shown to two or more places or is dropped from the export. The warning does not block anything, so the cost is repeated noise and wrong advice on every full export, not a failure.

verdicts.reasoning:
The shipped helper causes this. In awb-package/assets/awb_draft.py, `_shape` (around lines 3684-3691) appends a precision note for every [percent] column whose [round] places are below 2 when any selected cell `_places(...) == 4`. That is purely a digit-count heuristic: it never asks whether the query actually rounded. `export` then reports these as `precision_warnings` (line 3832). There is no opt-out. `[confirmed]` is read only by `label_collisions` (line 3738), and `_DISPLAY_KEYS` has no precision-confirm key. helpers.md line 54 and package-contract.md line 71 describe the warning with no way to confirm it. The warning text (`_PRECISION`, line 3385) says "a sign the query rounded them" and tells the user to "save the result at full precision". Here the result already is at full precision, so the advice cannot be acted on.

The run evidence backs this up. The retail-B query queries/product-cancellation-rate.sql computes `largest_cancellation_line / nullif(cancellation_value, 0)` without rounding. Row 993 of results/product-cancellation-rate.csv holds 0.1875 (ALARM CLOCK BAKELIKE GREEN), which is 45/240 and genuinely exact. display.toml marks that column as a percent with [round] 1, which meets the trigger condition. The relay logs show the same `precision_warnings` entry for result_id product-cancellation-rate, column largest_line_share_of_cancellations, example "0.1875" on repeated exports (several in agent-005.jsonl, one in agent-006.jsonl). Ratios of small integer counts land on exactly four decimals often, so a real user with a ratio column shown at 0 or 1 place would hit this.

Mitigations, which keep the severity minor:
- It is only a warning. Files are written, and neither check-draft nor release gates on it.
- Setting the column's [round] places to 2 or more stops it. That changes what the slide shows, though, so it is not a confirmation.
verdicts.release_evidence: awb-package/assets/awb_draft.py lines 3684-3691: `for column in percent: if places.get(column) is not None and places[column] < 2: example = next((row[column] for row in selected if ... _places(row[column], scale.get(column)) == 4), None)`, which appends to notes["precision"]. Line 3385 `_PRECISION = "its fractions are saved to exactly four decimal places, a sign the query rounded them ... save the result at full precision and round only under [round]"`. Line 3832: report["precision_warnings"] with no filtering. Line 3738: `[confirmed]` is consulted only for label collisions. awb-package/references/helpers.md line 54 (Warnings) and package-contract.md line 71 offer no confirm or silence mechanism for precision_warnings. Run evidence: retail-B project results/product-cancellation-rate.csv line 993 has an unrounded 0.1875 from a query with no ROUND. foundation/display.toml sets `largest_line_share_of_cancellations = 1` under [round] and lists the column in [percent]. Relay logs agent-005.jsonl and agent-006.jsonl show repeated precision_warnings entries with example "0.1875". Feedback is in agent.md item 11 and section 3.
verdicts.narrowed: export's precision_warnings uses a digit-count heuristic. It flags any percent-column fraction saved to exactly four decimals, shown at fewer than two places, even when the query did not round it (here 45/240 = 0.1875). It has no confirm or opt-out key, and its advice to "save at full precision" is already met, so it repeats on every export. It is a non-blocking warning, and the only way to clear it is raising the column's [round] places to 2 or more, which changes what the slide shows.

consolidated.title: The EDA scan floods a wide panel with expected anomalies
consolidated.description: eda-scan reported 142 anomalies on co2-B's country-year panel. Almost all were extreme values or high null rates that country size and historical sparseness explain. It also listed [parameters] keys as 'not read by the scan'. The scan with an integer year column now works.
consolidated.caused_by_fix: no
consolidated.evidence: co2-B-14: eda-scan call in relay/agent-002.jsonl; exploration/eda/owid_co2.json records date_column 'year', with no cast error (Oct 16 failed with 'Unimplemented type for cast').

verdicts.reasoning:
I found nothing tying this to the harness. The scan output is deterministic code, and every claim in the finding holds.

1. The call matches the claim. relay/agent-002.jsonl has one mcp__awb__data eda-scan call on owid_co2 with --date-column year, --start 1850, --end 2024, --measure co2, --dimension entity_kind, --key country,year. It exited 0. The printout shows 15 anomaly rows, then "127 more anomalies in the full scan", so 142 in total. It also prints "settings keys not read by the scan: parameters.change_start_year, ... parameters.top_n".

2. The saved file matches the printout. exploration/eda/owid_co2.json has 80 columns and 142 anomalies: 74 extreme-values, 57 high-nulls, 7 null-shift and 4 rare-negatives. Its date_column is year, the year column is BIGINT, and there is no cast error. scope.settings_unused holds the six [parameters] keys.

3. The release code produces this on its own. The anomalies() function in awb-explore/scripts/eda_scan.py adds a high-nulls entry for any column at 20% null or more. It adds an extreme-values entry for any numeric column with at least one value beyond 3 IQR. Nothing accounts for skew, entity size, or how wide the table is. On an 80-column country-year panel with log-normal sizes and sparse early years, those two rules fire about twice per column.

4. The settings line is also release behavior. resolve_settings() treats [results] as run.py's alone but not [parameters]. Any [parameters] key that is not a start/end fallback gets listed as unused. The release's own awb-init settings.toml template tells users to put run.py's [parameters] in that same file, so anyone who follows the template sees this line.

5. The agent ran the released code unchanged. agent-home/.claude/skills/awb-explore/scripts/eda_scan.py is byte-identical to the release copy, and the .agents/skills/awb-explore tree matches the release tree.

6. No harness mechanism changes what the scan prints:
   - non-interactive claude -p
   - auto-approved MCP tools
   - the simulated home (the code is identical)
   - relay behavior
   - the persona, which supplied the question scope (1850 to 2024), something a real user would also give
   - the study disclosure, which only explains why the agent wrote it in feedback notes

   The OWID CO2 panel is a realistic public dataset that a real user could pick.

7. The Oct 16 context checks out. oct16-ref/proposed-issues.md and data.json contain the old "Unimplemented type for cast" error, which matches the "now works" note.

Two things soften the finding without making it a harness artifact:
- The printed summary is capped at 15 rows, and awb-explore/SKILL.md asks for a disposition only for printed anomalies. So the work it forces on the user is bounded, though all 15 printed rows were low-signal.
- The agent did not scope out aggregate rows such as World and the continents, which inflates the extreme-value counts. That is a reasonable user choice, and excluding the aggregates would not stop the per-column rules firing on country-size skew and historical sparseness.

Severity minor is appropriate.

verdicts.reasoning:
The evidence holds up. In co2-B/relay/agent-002.jsonl the agent made one mcp__awb__data eda-scan call on owid_co2 (--date-column year --start 1850 --end 2024 --measure co2 --dimension entity_kind --key country,year).
