claims.claim:
Issue area #93 (awb-status) persists, though the consolidator rates its items partly fixed.
- awb-status still counts findings that users cannot map to their questions: 'nine supported findings and two provisional reference calculations' in taxi-A, and 'seven supported and seven provisional' in retail-A, whose user asked 'What are the 14?'.
- It replied in prose instead of the promised per-question screen in taxi-A and co2-A.
- Large status outputs were truncated: taxi-B lost its questions section.
claims.oct16_ref: #93 / Oct 16 C-48 (taxi-A 'Nine findings', retail-A '11 supported findings'); verified C-30 and C-18
claims.evidence: SIMS/taxi-A/transcript.md line 426; SIMS/retail-A/transcript.md message 6; findings taxi-A-05, co2-A-06, retail-A-01, taxi-B-07 and retail-A-11

skeptics.reasoning:
The quotes and run attributions check out against the primary sources. The headline goes too far, and two details are off.

What checks out:
- taxi-A transcript line 426 (reply 8) reads "nine supported findings and two provisional reference calculations". The user says in human.md section 2 item 4 that they "couldn't map 11 results onto my 5 questions". That complaint is only in the post-session feedback, though. In chat the user never raised it and approved the release.
- retail-A reply 5 (line 338) reads "seven supported and seven provisional findings". Message 6 (line 351) asks "What are the 14?", and reply 6 spends a paragraph explaining.
- The taxi-A reply 8 and co2-A reply 5 status reports are prose paragraphs, with no per-question list and no "You can ask for" requests.
- The Oct 16 baseline matches: C-48 has taxi-A "Nine findings are supported" and retail-A "11 supported findings", and it is filed under #93.
- The consolidator rates C-30 partly_fixed.

What weakens it:
1. **The product fix landed. The agents did not render it.** The collector's full output (taxi-A overflow 20261017-081556-read-status-2bb6ed13.txt; retail-A overflow 20261017-075719-read-status-e9270bbe.txt) now includes questions.by_question, and it accounts for the totals exactly:
   - taxi-A: Q1 2 supported, Q2 2 supported, Q3 2 supported + 1 provisional, Q4 1 supported, Q5 2 supported + 1 provisional, which makes 9 + 2.
   - retail-A: Q1 2 + 4, Q2 1, Q3 2, Q4 3 provisional, Q5 2, which makes 7 + 7.
   awb-status/SKILL.md tells the agent to report each by_question entry with its findings by status. The retail-A agent read the full overflow file and still gave only the totals. So the counts the users could not map are an agent rendering failure, not missing data.
2. **"Issue area #93 persists" overstates it.** #93 covered five items: C-31, C-32, C-48, C-71 and C-85. C-31's "indeterminate at date precision" wording appears in none of the six runs' relay logs, and taxi-A's status reads "up to date". C-32's deferred edits did not recur. Instead, retail-A did the other request before the report. The release now has a row for provisional findings with no draft (C-85). Only the C-48 symptom clearly persists, so "partly fixed" is a defensible rating for the area.
3. **"Its items partly fixed" is wrong for C-18.** The consolidator rates C-18 "persists", and its Oct 16 reference is C-61 (rejected), not #93.
4. **"taxi-B lost its questions section" overstates the loss.** The 5,233 characters cut removed the ledger counts, the roots (the user's own questions), the must-answer sub-questions and the provisional list. The per-question finding counts for Q-001 to Q-005 survived in the visible tail. The truncation was also wider than taxi-B:
   - taxi-A's reply-8 status lost 1,054 characters, including the start of the questions section. This partly explains taxi-A's missing per-question view.
   - retail-A's status overflowed as well, and the agent recovered it from the cache file.
5. **The prose/no-layout problem is wider than taxi-A and co2-A.** The B-run status sections in taxi-B, co2-B and retail-B also lack the per-question findings and the suggested requests. No run in the transcripts shows a "You can ask for" section.
skeptics.corrected_claim: The findings-count part of #93 (Oct 16 C-48) persists for users. taxi-A's status gave "nine supported findings and two provisional reference calculations"; the user said only in post-session feedback that they could not map 11 results to 5 questions. retail-A's status gave "seven supported and seven provisional", and the user asked "What are the 14?". No run produced the promised one-screen per-question report with suggested requests: taxi-A and co2-A answered in prose, and the B runs also left out the per-question findings. The data for the mapping now exists. The collector's questions.by_question totals exactly 9+2 for taxi-A and 7+7 for retail-A, so the failure lies in how agents render the report. Other #93 items did not recur, notably the cryptic "indeterminate at date precision" freshness wording, which appears in no run. That makes "partly fixed" a defensible rating for the area as a whole. Separately, the MCP server's 16,000-character cap truncated status outputs in taxi-A (1,054 chars, including the start of the questions section), taxi-B (5,233 chars, losing the ledger counts, roots and provisional list but not the per-question counts) and retail-A (recovered from the overflow file).

skeptics.reasoning:
Only one of the claim's three bullets is a #93 symptom that persists. The other two are new, and confounds explain them at least as well as a missing fix does.

1. Counts (taxi-A, retail-A). This bullet holds as a recurrence, and model role does not explain why it stayed the same. Both studies had Codex as the agent in the A runs. The symptom appeared in the same two runs each time: Oct 16 taxi-A said "Nine findings are supported" and retail-A said "11 supported findings". The mechanism has changed, though. The collector now emits `questions.by_question`, and awb-status/SKILL.md asks for a per-question breakdown. In retail-A the agent printed by_question itself (retail-A/relay/agent-005.jsonl: Q-001 2 supported and 4 provisional, through Q-005) and still reported "seven supported and seven provisional". That is agent compliance, plus a skill that still puts `active.counts` first. In taxi-A the status MCP result was cut at the 16,000-character cap, which predates the fixes. The 1,054 characters cut included the questions section and the Q-001 and Q-002 entries (scratchpad/taxiA_status8.txt), and the agent never read the overflow file. Two parts of the symptom come from the fixes themselves:
   - The supported/provisional split comes from the new promotion model in #104 and #105.
   - The skill leading with `active.counts` comes from #104.

   The Claude-agent B runs reported status per question ("all five questions have answers, provisional until you approve") and showed no such confusion.

2. Prose instead of the screen (taxi-A, co2-A). This is new, not a persisting #93 item, and confounds shape it. In both runs Codex sent the status as an interim commentary message partway through the turn (taxi-A agent-008 item 7, co2-A agent-005 item 10), then did the other work bundled into the same message. That order is exactly what #93's new rule requires ("Carry out the message's other requests... after the report"). The persona brief makes "ask where things stand at least once" an end-point criterion, so users tack status onto work requests. The Oct 16 skeptic already flagged that as a harness effect. Under the old read-only rule, the same Codex agents on Oct 16 gave a bulleted status as their final message. The yardstick also changed. The taxi-A user quoted the new README promise ("each of your questions with its findings"), which the Oct 16 README did not make.

3. Truncation (taxi-B-07, retail-A-11). The referee tagged both items "unclear". The consolidator puts them in a separate cluster, C-18 (oct16_ref C-61, rejected), not in #93. The cap predates the fixes. taxi-B lost the questions section only because the sim's path boundary blocked the overflow file, and the agent rebuilt it from `questions list`. The consolidator says #93's additions to the payload likely pushed it over the cap, so this is a side effect of the fix, not persistence.

4. The other Oct 16 #93 items appear fixed:
   - "indeterminate at date precision" appears in no run (C-67).
   - Edits sent with a status request were carried out in the same turn, not deferred.
   - Caveats were listed.
   - retail-A used the new "Preview the slide headlines" row.

"Persists" overstates the evidence. "Partly fixed", with one residual symptom tied to the Codex agent, fits better. With three runs per cell, the 2-of-3 rate in the Codex cells is unchanged, so neither improvement nor regression can be resolved.
skeptics.corrected_claim: Issue area #93 is partly fixed, not persisting. One symptom recurs at the same rate in the same cells: Codex agents (taxi-A, retail-A) still report finding totals that users cannot map to their five questions ("nine supported and two provisional"; "seven supported and seven provisional", which led to "What are the 14?"). This happens even though the collector now emits a per-question breakdown and the skill asks for it. The residual product causes are critical, and they depend on the fixes themselves: the skill still puts `active.counts` before the per-question entries, and the new promotion model leaves supporting checks provisional. In taxi-A the MCP output cap also cut the first per-question entries. The prose-format replies (taxi-A, co2-A) are a new effect of #93's report-first order. Codex sends the status as an interim message while users bundle status with other work, which the persona brief encourages. The truncation items belong to a separate cluster (C-18) about the pre-existing MCP output cap. The other #93 items (freshness wording, edits deferred by status, hidden caveats, the provisional-findings row) did not recur.

claims.claim: Status freshness is still fragile: co2-A's status called the state out of date because history was written one second after it, although all evidence was current.
claims.oct16_ref: #93 / Oct 16 C-31 ('indeterminate at date precision'); verified C-67 (partly fixed)
claims.evidence: finding co2-A-15

skeptics.reasoning:
The event itself checks out against the primary sources, but the "unchanged" label and the "still fragile" framing claim more than one instance can carry.

Confirmed:
- co2-A/relay/agent-005.jsonl has two `read status` calls. In the first, active.last_updated is "2026-10-17T07:32:49-04:00" and git.state_status is "out of date" with days_after_state 0. Its latest_change is investigations/emissions-and-country-focus/history.md at "2026-10-17T07:32:50-04:00". At second precision, that is one second after the state.
- The `stale` call in the same turn returned {"checked": 9, "stale": 0}. "All evidence current" matches 9 of 9 results current.
- release/.../awb-status/scripts/collect_status.py (lines 998-1028) compares int(mtime) with the Last updated stamp. Any change one second later counts as "after", which matches the reported behaviour.

Nuances the claim leaves out:
1. The history write was the agent's own manual append, not one made by the tool. In agent-004.jsonl (its .ts file maps line by line, 52/52), the last `state finding` calls finished at 07:32:49.8 and 07:32:49.9. Both stamp state.md 07:32:49. A python `p.open("a").write(...)` call then appended the "## Accepted findings and requested Q2 threshold comparison" entry to history.md at about 07:32:50.0 (history.md line 107). The tool's own history entry (line 99) fell in the same second as the state write, so it was correctly not counted.
2. "One second" is a truncated second-precision difference. The actual gap was roughly 0.1-0.2 s across a second boundary.
3. history.md may not have been the only change counted as later. An apply_patch on brief.md and analysis-results.md (in the investigation folder, not exempt) finished at 07:32:49.9-50.0. Their sub-second mtimes can't be recovered because later turns rewrote both files.
4. The agent never showed "out of date" to the user. It reported "all nine saved results are current" from the stale check. The second status call in the same turn returned "up to date".

Why "unchanged" overstates:
- The Oct 16 defect (C-31) was that "indeterminate at date precision" appeared as the normal same-day result in 4 runs (data.json C-31).
- In this re-run, every status call I found returned plain-language values:
  - "up to date" in taxi-A (5 calls), taxi-B, co2-B (2), retail-A, and co2-A's second call.
  - "out of date" in retail-B, which looks genuine (settings.toml changed 52 s after the state).
  - "out of date" once in co2-A: the sub-second false positive above.
- No run produced "indeterminate". This is a narrow leftover edge case of a partly fixed issue, not the same issue unchanged.

I could not locate the "verified C-67 (partly fixed)" cross-reference. In oct16-ref data.json and the README, C-67 is the harness pre-approval finding, not freshness.
skeptics.corrected_claim: Status freshness still has an edge case, though the Oct 16 problem is partly fixed rather than unchanged. In one of roughly a dozen status calls across six runs, co2-A's collector reported the state "out of date" (days_after_state 0). The agent's own manual append to history.md landed at 07:32:50, about 0.1-0.2 s after its last state write, which stamped 07:32:49, but on the far side of a second boundary. brief.md and analysis-results.md were also edited in that window. A stale check in the same turn showed 9 of 9 results current, the agent did not pass the warning to the user, and the next status call returned "up to date". The Oct 16 failure, a cryptic "indeterminate at date precision" as the normal same-day result, did not recur: the other status calls returned plain "up to date", and retail-B's "out of date" appears genuine.

skeptics.reasoning:
The raw facts hold. In co2-A/relay/agent-005.jsonl the collector returned state_status "out of date", days_after_state 0, latest_change history.md at 07:32:50-04:00. state.md has Last updated 07:32:49. The stale check found 9 of 9 results current. The parts that do not hold are "unchanged" and the reading that this is a timestamp false alarm.

1. **A different, path-dependent mechanism, not the Oct 16 defect.** In the oct16-ref, C-31 was "indeterminate at date precision" in every same-day status call: 4 of 4 checked runs. The release (CHANGELOG line 186) moved Last updated to second precision. In this re-run, 10 of 12 collector outputs across the six runs read "up to date" and none read "indeterminate". The co2-A out-of-date reading comes from what the agent did. In agent-004 the Codex agent called `state finding` twice (07:32:49.8 and 49.9, which stamped the state). In the same tool batch it then hand-edited brief.md and analysis-results.md (49.9 to 50.0). It then appended a history.md entry with `python3 -c` at 07:32:50.0. collect_status.py treats any later change to a non-exempt investigation file as dating the state. history.md is not exempt, and the template AGENTS.md permits hand-written history. By the release's own rule, then, the history file really did change after the state. "One second" is just how quickly the agent issued its calls, not a precision artifact. An agent that writes history before its last state writer would never trigger it.

2. **Metric definition differs.** "All evidence was current" measures evidence freshness, which comes from the stale check. state_status measures whether any investigation record changed after the state was stamped. The claim treats the two as one metric. A clean stale check does not make the out-of-date reading wrong under the product's definition. Whether narrative edits should date the state is a design question, and that is the fix the agent itself proposed.

3. **The user never saw it.** The agent ran the stale check and told the user "all nine saved results are current" (agent-005.out.md and .last.md). The phrase "out of date" never reached the user. So "status called the state out of date" is true only of the raw collector JSON, not of the status report the user received.

4. **Model and persona variance, small n.** The only other out-of-date reading was retail-B, where Claude was the agent and settings.toml had changed after the state. That agent treated the signal as a prompt to update the state and raised no finding. co2-A-15 is a single minor finding, self-reported by the agent (source: agent).

5. **Where the claim has a point: the second boundary is fragile.** brief.md and analysis-results.md were edited after the state, in the same second, and counted as "before". history.md crossed into the next second and counted as "after". So the verdict depended on sub-second timing. That residual issue cuts both ways, missing real edits as well as flagging them, and it is narrower than the Oct 16 problem.

Evidence: co2-A/relay/agent-004.jsonl (items 34-43), agent-004.ts, agent-005.jsonl (item_5; item_28 later reads "up to date"), release awb-status/scripts/collect_status.py lines 950-1031, release awb-init/assets/workbench/AGENTS.md line 48.
skeptics.corrected_claim: The Oct 16 date-precision defect (#93/C-31, "indeterminate" in every same-day status) did not recur: 10 of 12 collector calls across six runs read "up to date". What remains is narrower. In co2-A the raw collector output read "out of date" because the agent hand-appended a history.md entry (and edited brief/analysis-results) about 0.1 s after its last state writer stamped Last updated (07:32:49 vs 07:32:50). The evidence was current (stale 9/9). This is how the release is designed: hand edits to history date the state, and the design does not separate narrative edits from evidence freshness. The second-boundary ordering is also timing-sensitive: edits in the same second are counted as earlier than the state. The agent caught it with a stale check and never told the user the state was out of date. It is one self-reported minor instance, so the status freshness issue is partly fixed, with a narrower residual design issue.

claims.claim: Issue area #94 (README) persists, though the consolidator rates it partly fixed. In 6 of 6 runs, users again called the README long, with admin material mixed into the analyst guide. Each also named a missing piece: the data stages (taxi-A), display precision (co2-A), a concrete example of how small an issue triggers the review stop (co2-B), what approval is for (retail-B), and the full path at release (retail-A).
claims.evidence: section 3 of SIMS/{taxi-A,taxi-B,co2-A,co2-B,retail-A,retail-B}/feedback/human.md; findings taxi-A-09, taxi-A-28, co2-A-21, co2-B-27 and retail-B-21

skeptics.reasoning:
I re-read section 3 of all six feedback/human.md files, the human/notes.md friction logs, findings.json, and the Oct 16 README and proposed-issues.md.

1. "In 6 of 6 runs, users again called the README long" is wrong. The true count is 4 of 6.
- taxi-B: "It is long for someone using the product for the first time"
- co2-A: "the README is long, and half of it is install/MCP admin material"
- co2-B: "long for a first-time analyst"
- retail-B: "long for a first-time commercial user"
- taxi-A did not call the README long. Its section 3 says only that one part is too dense ("What you will be asked", items 6-8). Its notes say "Install and administer" is "irrelevant to me but easy to skip".
- retail-A did not call it long either. It called item 7 on review problems dense and "How it works" too technical. Its "Length: too long" line is in section 4 and is about the agent's messages.
- None of the cited findings supports "6 of 6". taxi-A-28 says "dense", not long, and no README-length finding exists for taxi-A or retail-A.

2. "Admin material mixed into the analyst guide" is overstated.
- The four users who called it long all blamed install/admin content.
- But co2-A says outright the admin half is "clearly separated", which contradicts "mixed into".
- co2-B places the problem where "installation and host-specific material begin", that is, after the analyst part.
- The plainest "mixed in" complaint comes from retail-A: the analyst quick-start "also mentions commits and the MCP server". retail-A never said the README was long.

3. "Each also named a missing piece" is partly wrong.
- Four attributions check out: taxi-A (data states: landed, published, screened), co2-A (display precision), co2-B (a concrete example of how small an issue triggers the review stop) and retail-B ("what approval is for").
- retail-A's full-path item is listed under "Wrong in practice". It is a promise the README makes that the agent did not keep (finding retail-A-05), not a missing piece.
- retail-A's actual "Missing" items were different: findings counted per calculation rather than per question, how to name the source for the audience, and being asked IT-only questions.
- The claim lists five pieces for six runs and leaves out taxi-B. taxi-B asked for an example of which review decisions need analyst judgment, and an example of an observed pattern versus a supported explanation.
- Finding retail-B-21 covers only length and admin material, not approval.

4. What holds:
- All six users had README complaints, so issue area #94 does persist, as Oct 16 C-25 did (6/6).
- The release README is still about 4,718 words (wc -w), with Install and administer and How it works sections. That is consistent with "partly fixed".
- I could not find the consolidator's own rating on disk, so that part is unverified.
skeptics.corrected_claim: Issue area #94 (README) persists: all 6 users raised README complaints in section 3 of their feedback. In 4 of 6 runs (taxi-B, co2-A, co2-B, retail-B), users called the README long and pointed to installation/admin material, though co2-A said that half was "clearly separated". In the other two, users called specific sections dense: "What you will be asked" items 6-8 (taxi-A) and item 7 on review problems (retail-A). retail-A also said the analyst quick-start mentions commits and the MCP server. Missing pieces named: the data states, landed, published and screened (taxi-A); display precision (co2-A); a concrete example of how small an issue triggers the review stop (co2-B); what approval is for (retail-B); an example of which review decisions need analyst judgment (taxi-B); and per-calculation finding counts, source naming and IT-only questions (retail-A). retail-A also reported that the README promises the release copy's full path but it got a relative link, which is a broken promise rather than a gap.

skeptics.reasoning:
The core of the claim holds, and it is a product effect rather than a confound. The release README is 4,718 words, the same file the users received. The #94 commit (415d678) kept "Install and administer" in the README on purpose, because the archive carries no docs folder. It also lengthened the analyst quick-start, from about 1,905 to about 2,290 words, by adding the missing expectations. So a "still long, admin in the same file" complaint was a predictable result of the fix as shipped.

The claim's specific assertions are overstated, and parts of them come from the harness:

1. "6 of 6 called it long, with admin mixed in" is miscounted. In section 3 of feedback/human.md:
   - taxi-A says neither. It calls only "What you will be asked" items 6-8 too dense, and its turn-1 notes call the install section "irrelevant to me but easy to skip".
   - retail-A never calls the README long. It says the README is too technical and that the quick-start mentions commits and MCP.
   - "Long" appears in 4 of 6 runs (taxi-B, co2-A, co2-B, retail-B). Installation or admin material is named in 5 of 6.
   - "Mixed into the analyst guide" misdescribes co2-A, which says the admin material is "clearly separated". Most users objected to the admin material sharing the file, not to it being mixed into the quick-start.

2. Which model played the user predicts the "long" verdict. All three Codex-played users (the B runs) wrote nearly identical turn-1 notes: "README is long for a first-time analyst/commercial user". Only one of three Claude-played users (co2-A) called the whole README long. With three runs per cell and a fixed role assignment, the uniform "long" result cannot be separated from a stock Codex reaction to any document of about 4.7k words. The Oct 16 6/6 count used a broader union: "length, admin material or jargon" in notes.md. That metric is not the one this claim uses.

3. "Each also named a missing piece" is guaranteed by the harness. The end-of-run prompt in kit/relay.py (feedback()) asks every user for "(3) the README: what was missing, unclear, or wrong, and what you needed to know that it did not tell you". The prompt is the same in both studies, and the Oct 16 harness lens already said it inflated the missing-items list. So a 6/6 count carries no signal of persistence. The content shift points the other way:
   - None of Oct 16's named gaps recur in feedback: headline word limit, review rounds, release waiver, URL fetching, commits. The new README covers the headline limit (line 13) and URL fetching (line 54).
   - Display precision and the landed/published/screened data states were already missing from the Oct 16 README (old_README_1db6084.md), and nobody named them then. That looks like the prompt sampling different items from a standing pool of gaps, not like persistence.

4. Two of the listed missing pieces are mislabeled or incomplete:
   - retail-A's "full path at release" is filed under "Wrong in practice". The README states the full path is reported (line 31). The agent gave a relative link (retail-A-05), and co2-A's agent reported the full path as promised. This is run-level agent behavior, not a README gap.
   - taxi-B's missing piece is left out: an example of which review decisions need the analyst, close to co2-B's.

The README complaint is real and comes from the product, but the evidence fits "partly fixed with a narrower remaining gap" better than "unchanged". The 6/6 counts are inflated by miscounting, by the feedback prompt, and by the model-role split.
skeptics.corrected_claim: Issue area #94 (README) is partly fixed, not unchanged. The README is shorter: 4,718 words against about 5,345 on Oct 16, with install, admin and internal material down from about half to about a third. None of the Oct 16 gaps that #94 targeted came up again (headline limit, review rounds, URL fetching, release waiver). But the fix kept "Install and administer" in the same file and made the quick-start longer (about 1,905 to 2,290 words). In section 3 of the feedback, 4 of 6 users called the README long: all three users played by Codex and one of the three played by Claude. 5 of 6 wanted installation or admin material moved out. taxi-A raised neither; it called one section dense and said in its notes that the install section was easy to skip. Every user named a README gap, but the feedback prompt asks for exactly that, so this count does not show the issue persisting. The gaps named were new ones: data stages (taxi-A), display precision (co2-A), a concrete example of what triggers the review stop (co2-B, and much the same in taxi-B), and what approval is for (retail-B). retail-A's relative release link is an agent reporting slip against a README that is correct, not a README gap.

claims.claim: Across Oct 16's eleven issue areas: #84 is fixed; #85, #88, #89, #90, #91 and #92 are improved; #86, #87, #93 and #94 persist; none regressed. Four new defects came from the fixes themselves: C-12 (brief coverage), C-51 (imperative rule), C-24 (rule staleness) and the stop-rule gates in C-04.

skeptics.reasoning:
I checked the claim against the primary sources: reviewloop.py over all six runs, the six findings.json files, the review-reports, the oct16-ref data.json and proposed-issues.md, and a git comparison of 1db6084 against 1677d19. 1677d19 is the commit the release folder matches; I confirmed this for SKILL.md, review.md, awb-release/SKILL.md and awb_draft.py.

What holds:
- **The loop converges.** Every run had exactly one full review. Recorded reviews were 3, 4, 3, 5, 4 and 5 (taxi-A, taxi-B, co2-A, co2-B, retail-A, retail-B), and no request recorded more than 2. retail-A agent-007 shows 3 starts but only 2 records. On Oct 16 there were 21 full reviews in taxi-B, 38 in co2-B, 15 in retail-B, 4 in retail-A and 6 in co2-A.
- **The tally adds up.** 1 fixed, 6 improved and 4 persisting make 11 areas.
- **The four listed defects exist and trace to the fixes.** Brief coverage is taxi-A-03 (major); release review.md:27 adds the brief check. The imperative rule is retail-B-03 (major) and retail-A-13; review.md:28 is new text, and "imperative" appears 0 times at 1db6084 and once at 1677d19. Rule staleness is co2-B-06; the receipt's staleness list includes review-rules.md. The stop-rule gates are taxi-B-04, retail-B-04 and co2-B-03 (major), from review.md:43.
- **No area shows a clear rise in runs or severity.**

What does not hold:
1. **"Four new defects came from the fixes" undercounts.** At least five more defects in this run rest on code or text that is absent at 1db6084 and present at 1677d19:
   - **Hidden `.preview` folder** (taxi-A-06, co2-A-08). `.preview` appears 0 times before and 8 times after, added in #90 commits 7a6052c and 46dc388.
   - **Preview needs the draft folder before export creates it** (co2-B-11, retail-B-13). This comes from the same #90 change.
   - **Export's `[scale]` divisor text fails check-draft** (co2-B-10). This is the #88 `[scale]` feature: "divided by 1000000000" sits in methodology_lines, the numbers check rejects it, and the agent hand-edited allowed_numbers. Confirmed in co2-B agent-004.jsonl.
